        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Montelukast sodium, levocetirizine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Leukotriene Receptor Antagonists (LTRA)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of symptoms associated with seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 1 tab once daily. <b>Elderly</b>: Adjusted in accordance to renal function. <b>Childn and adolescents &ge;15 yrs</b>: 1 tab once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 10 mL/min). Infants &le;2 yrs. Childn 6-11 yrs with renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May impair ability to drive or operate machines.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, fatigue. <b>Montelukast:</b> Asthenia, fever, abdominal pain, trauma, dyspepsia, infectious gastroenteritis, dental pain, dizziness, nasal congestion, cough, flu, rash, increased ALT and AST, pyuria. <b>Levocetirizine:</b> Somnolence, dry mouth."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inducers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg/5 mg."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Cq6FfyDjvj2LxnkwvlQQwbC6wgNOQDy4N3mP4QubfQrtDCC9Yy.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/r25bhQBsXMDpwMkZGZf6BLkTJHDlNwblUBxXfli393wgFVfosH.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fluoxetine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD), obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), bulimia nervosa, panic disorder, and premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). In combination with olanzapine: Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults and treatment-resistant depression in adults (MDD in adults who do not respond to two separate trials of different antidepressants of adequate dose and duration in the current episode)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>MDD</b> - <b>Initial dose</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> 20 mg/day as single dose in the morning or in 2 divided doses in the morning and at noon. Max 80 mg/day; <b>Adolescents and childn 8-&lt;18 yrs:</b> 10 mg/day, may be increased to 20 mg/day after a week or if improvement is observed. <b>OCD</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> 20 mg/day as single dose in the morning or in 2 divided doses in the morning and at noon. Max 80 mg/day; <b>Adolescents and childn 7-&lt;18 yrs:</b> 10 mg/day, may be increased to 20 mg/day after 2 weeks or if improvement is observed. <b>Bulimia nervosa</b> - <b>Initial dose</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> 60 mg/day in the morning. <b>Maintenance, continuation, or extended treatment</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> 60 mg/day for up to 52 weeks. <b>Panic disorder</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> 10 mg/day, may be increased to 20 mg/day after a week, max 60 mg/day. <b>PMDD</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> 20 mg/day either every day of the menstrual cycle or 14 days before the expected onset of menstruation. <b>Bipolar I disorder depressive episodes, treatment-resistant depression</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> Fluoxetine 20 mg and olanzapine 5 mg once daily in the evening; <b>Special population (hypotensive, with hepatic impairment, sensitive to olanzapine):</b> Fluoxetine 20 mg and olanzapine 2.5-5 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients receiving MAOIs, thioridazine, pimozide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Clinical worsening and suicide risk. Bipolar disorder, patients with history of convulsive disorder or seizures, diabetic patients. Serotonin syndrome, risk of bleeding with concomitant use of aspirin, NSAIDs, warfarin, and other anti-coagulants. Hyponatremia. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn &lt;8 yrs with MDD, &lt;7 yrs with OCD, or with bulimia nervosa, panic disorder, and PMDD. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, fever flu syndrome, headache, vasodilation, anorexia, constipation, diarrhea, dry mouth, dyspepsia, flatulence, nausea, vomiting, weight loss, abnormal dreams and thinking, anxiety, decreased libido, dizziness, insomnia, nervousness, somnolence, tremor, pharyngitis, sinusitis, yawn, sweating, pruritus, rash, abnormal vision, abnormal ejaculation, impotence, agitation, hyperkinesias, menorrhagia, personality disorder, thirst, urinary frequency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "MAOIs, thioridazine, other antidepressants, antipsychotics, antiarrhythmics, ketoconazole, astemizole, midazolam, serotonergic drugs, tryptophan, triptans, warfarin, digoxin, NSAIDs, aspirin, CNS active drugs, TCAs, anticonvulsants, benzodiazepines, lithium, other drugs for MDD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 20 mg (P47.56)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Tirzepatide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Other Blood Glucose-Lowering Drugs, excluding Insulins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise in adults with insufficiently controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) as monotherapy when metformin is inappropriate due to intolerance or contraindications, or in addition to other antidiabetic drugs. Adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for weight management (e.g., weight loss and maintenance) in adults with an initial BMI of &ge;30 kg/m<sup>2</sup> or &ge;27 kg/m<sup>2</sup> to < 30 kg/m<sup>2</sup> with at least one weight-related comorbidity (e.g., hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, cardiovascular disease, prediabetes, or type 2 DM)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 2.5 mg once weekly, increased to 5 mg once weekly after 4 weeks. Dose may be increased in 2.5 mg increments after minimum of 4 weeks on current dose. Max 15 mg once weekly. SC inj in the abdomen, thigh, or upper arm at any time of day, with or without meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma. Multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid fluid depletion and electrolyte disturbances. Patients with severe hepatic or renal impairment and ESRD; history of pancreatitis; severe GI disease (e.g., severe gastroparesis); non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy requiring acute therapy, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or diabetic macular edema. Pulmonary aspiration in association with general anesthesia or deep sedation. Consider dose reduction of sulfonylurea or insulin when used in combination. Discontinue if pancreatitis is suspected; at least 1 month before a planned pregnancy. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly &ge;85 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia (when used with sulfonylurea or insulin), nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation. Hypersensitivity reactions, hypoglycemia (when used with metformin and SGLT2 inhibitors), decreased appetite, dizziness, hypotension, dyspepsia, abdominal distention, eructation, flatulence, GERD, hair loss, fatigue, injection site reactions. Increased heart rate, lipase, amylase, and blood calcitonin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for SC injection 2.5 mg/0.6 mL, 5 mg/0.6 mL, 7.5 mg/0.6 mL, 10 mg/0.6 mL, 12.5 mg/0.6 mL, 15 mg/0.6 mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Patients with history of asthma, bronchitis, emphysema, or other conditions where chronic and persistent cough occurs, HTN, toxic goiter, benign prostate hypertrophy, heart rate irregularity, glaucoma. Concomitant use with antihistamines and antidepressants. <b>Dextromethorphan:</b> Patients at risk of developing respiratory failure. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. 1st trimester of pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sleep disturbances, excitability, elevated BP, tachycardia, anginal attacks. <b>Chlorphenamine:</b> CNS depression (e.g. slight drowsiness to deep sleep, lassitude, dizziness, incoordination), exfoliative dermatitis. <b>Dextromethorphan HBr:</b> Dizziness, GI disturbances. <b>Guaifenesin:</b> GI discomfort, nausea, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Chlorphenamine maleate:</b> Calcium chloride, kanamycin sulfate, noradrenaline acid tartrate, phenobarbital, meglumine adipiodone. </b>Dextromethorphan HBr:</b> MAOIs, fluoxetine, lysergide. <b>Phenylpropanolamine HCl:</b> Amantadine, thioridacine, procyclidine, clemastine, zidovudine, indinavir, lamivudine, bromocriptine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 50 mg/10 mg/25 mg/ 2 mg (P14.40)."
          }
        ],

          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Secretolytic therapy in acute and chronic bronchopulmonary diseases associated with abnormal mucus secretion and impaired mucus transport."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - Adults: 1 tab thrice daily. Taken with liquid. <b>Syr 15 mg/5 mL</b> - Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs: 10 mL (2 tsp) thrice daily. Childn 6-12 yrs: 5 mL (1 tsp) 2-3 times daily; 2-5 yrs: 2.5 mL (&frac12; tsp) thrice daily; &lt;2 yrs: 2.5 mL (&frac12; tsp) twice daily. <b>Syr 30 mg/5 mL</b> - Adults and childn >12 yrs: 10 mL (2 tsp) twice daily.           },
          {

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Topical Antibacterials"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of primary (e.g. impetigo, folliculitis, furunculosis, ecthyma) and secondary bacterial skin infections (e.g. eczema, psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, herpes, epidermolysis bullosa, ichthyosis) infections caused by <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i> and <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i>; insect bites, infected minor traumatic lesions, small lacerations, sutured wounds, biopsy sites, and surgical incisions. Prevention of bacterial contamination and development of infection; permits wound healing in abrasions, minor cuts, and wounds."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply a small amount on affected areas thrice daily for up to 10 days. May be covered with gauze dressing if needed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Ophthalmic and intranasal use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For external use only. Do not mix with other topical products. Do not use at site of central venous cannulation; in conditions where large amounts of polyethylene glycol may be absorbed, particularly in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment. Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Burning sensation, stinging, pain, itching, swelling, redness, rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Salicylic acid 2%. Water-containing vehicles or formulations (e.g. Aquaphor, coal tar soln)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Respiratory pathogen infections (e.g. <i>S. pyogenes, S. pneumoniae, M. catarrhalis, C. trachomatis, Legionella</i> sp., <i>M. pneumoniae, S. aureus </i> and <i> H. influenza</i>), <i>C. pneumoniae</i> and <i>M. avium infection</i>, uncomplicated chlamydial urethritis, cervicitis or pharyngitis, alternative drug for multidrug-resistant <i>Salmonella typhi</i> infection outside the CNS."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Usual total dose for childn &ge;1 yr:</b> 30 mg/kg (as single daily dose of 10 mg/kg for 3 days. <b>Childn >2 yrs with pharyngitis or tonsillitis:</b> 12 mg/kg/day for 5 days. <b>>6 months with pneumonia or otitis media:</b> 10 mg/kg on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 5 mg/kg/day for further 4 days. <b>Acute otitis media:</b> 30 mg/kg single dose, or 10 mg/kg/day for 3 days. Shake well before use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pseudomembranous colitis. Observe for signs of superinfection with non-susceptible organisms. Patients with renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI reactions, hearing impairment, interstitial nephritis, acute renal failure, and abnormal liver function. Chest pain, melena, nephritis, vaginitis, headache, dizziness, convulsions, vertigo, somnolence and fatigue. Allergic and serious skin reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ergot derivatives. Antacids and cimetidine."
          },

  {
    "id": 2886,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2886,
        "brand_name": "Mycozole IV",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fluconazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of cryptococcal meningitis, coccidiomycosis, invasive candidiasis, mucosal candidiasis, including oropharyngeal, esophageal candidiasis, candiduria, and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, chronic oral atrophic candidiasis (denture soft mouth). Prophylaxis of relapse of cryptococcal meningitis in patients with high risk of recurrence, oropharyngeal or esophageal candidiasis in patients infected with HIV who are at high risk of experiencing relapse, candidal infections in patients with prolonged neutropenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Invasive candidiasis- Candidaemia:</b> 400-800 mg for 2 weeks. <b>Oropharyngeal candidiasis:</b> Initial dose of 200-400 mg followed by 100-200 mg daily for 7-21 days. <b>Esophageal candidiasis:</b> Initial dose of 200-400 mg followed by 100-200 mg daily for 14-30 days. <b>Candiduria:</b> 200-400 mg daily for 7-21 days. <b>Chronic atrophic candidiasis:</b> Initial dose of 200-400 mg followed by 50-100 mg daily for 14 days. <b>Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis:</b> 50-100 mg daily up to 28 days. <b>Prevention of relapse in patients infected with HIV who are at high risk of relapse:</b> 100-200 mg or 200 mg 3x weekly. <b>Treatment of cryptococcal meningitis:</b> Initial dose of 400 mg followed by 200-400 mg daily for 6-8 weeks. <b>Maintenance therapy to prevent relapse in patients with high risk of recurrence:</b> 200 mg daily. <b>Childn:</b> Max dose 400 mg daily. <b>Mucosal candidiasis:</b> Loading dose of 6 mg/kg followed by 3 mg/kg daily. <b>Invasive candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis:</b> 6-12mg/kg daily. <b>Maintenance therapy (prevent relapse) of Cryptococcal meningitis in childn with high-risk recurrence:</b> 6 mg/kg daily. <b>Prophylaxis of Candida in immunocompromised patients:</b> 3-12 mg/kg daily. <b>Infants &lt;2 weeks:</b> Max 12 mg/kg every 72 hrs. 3-4 weeks: 12 mg/kg- every 48 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Co-administration of terfenadine, cisapride, astemizole, pimozide, quinidine, and erythromycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with tinea capitis, cryptococcosis, deep endemic mycoses, renal or hepatic dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, and potentially proarrhythmic conditions. Concomitant use of halofantrine. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, rash, elevated alkaline phosphatase, ASAT and ALAT."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Amiodarone, rifampicin, HCTZ, alfentanil, amitriptyline, notriptyline, amphotericin B, anticoagulants, carbamazepine, CCBs, celecoxib, cyclophosphamide, fentanyl, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, ibrutinib, ivacaftor, olaparib, ciclosporin, everolimus, sirolimus, tacrolimus, losartan, lurasidone, methadone, NSAIDs, phenytoin, prednisone, rifabutin, saquinavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for intravenous infusion 200 mg/100 mL (P2,377.76)."
          }
        ],

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3131,
        "brand_name": "Mydfrin",

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,

          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Phenylephrine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Mydriatics/Cycloplegics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Vasoconstrictor, decongestant, and mydriatic on various ophthalmic conditions and procedures. Pupillary dilation in uveitis; ophthalmic surgical procedures, refraction without cycloplegia. Fundoscopy and other diagnostic procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Vasoconstriction and pupil dilation: </b >1 drop on upper limbus. May be repeated after 1 hr. <b>Uveitis - Posterior synechiae: </b>1 drop on the upper surface of cornea. Repeat when necessary but not exceeding 3 times. <b>Open-angle glaucoma:</b> Used in conjunction with miotic drugs. <b>Surgery:</b> Apply 30-60 mins before operation. <b>Refraction - Adults:</b> 1 drop in each eye 5 mins after a drop of preferred cycloplegic; <b>Childn:</b> May be combined with preferred rapid-acting cycloplegic. <b>Ophthalmoscopic examination:</b> 1 drop in each eye. Sufficient mydriasis is produced in 15-30 mins and lasts for 1-3 hrs. <b>Blanching test:</b> 1 or 2 drops applied to the injected eye. Nasolacrimal occlusion or gently closing the eyelid after administration is recommended."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with anatomically narrow angles or narrow-angle glaucoma. Newborn and infants with CV or cerebrovascular disease. Elderly with severe arteriosclerotic CV or cerebrovascular disease. Intraocular operative procedures when corneal epithelial barriers have been disturbed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for intraocular use. Remove contact lenses prior to application and reinsert after at least 15 mins. Avoid contact with soft contact lenses. Use in provocative test for angle closure glaucoma. Patients with sympathetic denervation e.g. patients with type 1 DM, orthostatic hypotension, HTN, hyperthyroidism. Concomitant use of MAOIs, TCAs, certain antihypertensives, or atropine. Contains sodium bisulfate and benzalkonium chloride. Geriatric patients with cardiac disease and infants with cardiac anomalies. Application to instrumented, traumatized, diseased or post-surgical eye or adnexa, patients with suppressed lacrimation. Rebound miosis. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Preterm and newborn infants. Childn and elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness. Eye pain, eye irritation, ocular hyperemia, conjunctivitis. Increase in BP, tachycardia, syncope, MI, arrhythmia, fatal subarachnoid hemorrhage. Pulmonary edema. Contact dermatitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "MAOIs, TCAs, guanethidine, reserpine, non-selective beta-blockers (e.g. propranolol), phenylephrine and atropine, inhalational anesthetics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Ophthalmic solution 25 mg/mL x 5 mL ."
          }
        ],

          "id": 431,
          "name": "Alcon Laboratories (Phils.), Inc."

  {
    "id": 4383,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4383,
        "brand_name": "Myox",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4uQcVLSeVEUhHmRFOkJxD4XPUZmYEDEsP5qig3Hs9b8ubuPQP8.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ZS58op3ikoTAcOIbPUHUWhkaVXUTnM5DtflhCJ7aOow1LfG4aF.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/zhYUgts3ImPP9FlumkP1DZhkFRldBCZdHUkInnTgQWiuwnLRnm.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Etoricoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For acute treatment of the signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA); treatment of ankylosing spondylitis; relief of acute pain caused by acute gouty arthritis, moderate to severe acute post-op pain associated with dental surgery or abdominal gynecological surgery,  primary dysmenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>OA</b>: 30 mg once daily; for patients with insufficient relief of symptoms from taking 30 mg once daily, dose may be increased to 60 mg once daily. Max 60 mg/day. <b>RA or ankylosing spondylitis</b>: 60 mg once daily; patients with insufficient relief of symptoms from taking 60 mg once daily, dose  may be increased to 90 mg once daily. Dose reduction to 60 mg may be appropriate once patient has clinically stabilized. Max 90 mg/day. <b>Acute pain</b>: 90 mg or 120 mg, Should only taken during the acute symptomatic period, max 8 days treatment. <b>Acute gouty arthritis</b>: 120 mg once daily for max 8 days. <b>Post-op dental surgery pain</b>: 90 once daily for max 3 days. <b>Primary dysmenorrhea</b>: Max 120 mg once daily. <b>Post-op gynecological pain</b>: 90 mg once daily. Max 120 mg once daily. <b>Hepatic impairment</b> - Mild (Child-Pugh scores 5-6): Max 60 mg. Moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9): Max 30 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to etoricoxib, other NSAIDs, or to any component of the product. Severe hepatic dysfunction (serum albumin &lt;25 g/L or Child-Pugh score &gt;10). Severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) or deteriorating renal disease. Patients who have history of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled  HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV). Patients who have experienced asthma, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps,  angioneurotic edema, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs, including other COX-2 specific inhibitors. Previous or active gastric, duodenal, or peptic ulcerations, or active GI bleeding, or IBD. Unstable or significant established IHD, PAD, and/or cerebrovascular disease. Patients who have undergone angioplasty. Use in peri-op in patients undergoing cardiac or  major vascular surgery. Childn and adolescents &lt;16 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of serious CV thrombotic events, Ml, and stroke; serious GI adverse events including bleeding, ulceration, and perforation of the stomach or intestines; which can be fatal. Patients with known CV disease, history of atherosclerotic CV disease, or significant risk factors for  CV events (e.g. HTN, hyperlipidemia, DM, a 1<sup>st</sup>-degree relative with IHD, cardiac failure, smoking). Risk of fluid retention and edema; patients with history of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, or HTN; pre existing edema. Renal papillary necrosis and other renal injury in long-term therapy. Patients with considerable dehydration. Elevation in ALT or AST (approx &gt;3x ULN).Patients with co morbid conditions e.g. coagulation disorders or concomitant use of drugs that increase risk of  bleeding. Not recommended in women attempting to conceive. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, HTN, dizziness, headache, ecchymosis, alveolar osteitis, edema, fluid retention, palpitations, arrhythmia, bronchospasm, constipation, flatulence, gastritis, dyspepsia, GERD, diarrhea, epigastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, esophagitis, pharyngitis, oral ulcer, asthenia, fatigue, influenza-like illness, and increased ALT and/or AST."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aspirin. Ciclosporin, tacrolimus. CYP inducers (e.g. rifampicin). CYP inhibitors (e.g.  ketoconazole). Digoxin. Diuretics, ARBs, and ACE inhibitors. Drugs metabolized by human  sulfotransferases (e.g. ethinylestradiol, oral salbutamol, minoxidil). HRT. Lithium. Methotrexate. Oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin). Oral contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 60 mg (P33.07), 90 mg (P37.20), 120 mg (P46.30)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 158,
          "name": "Westmont Pharmaceuticals, Inc."
        },

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Topical treatment of mild or moderate inflammatory forms of acne vulgaris (papulopustular acnes, grade I-II)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply as a thin layer using a swab to acne lesions twice daily, once in the morning and again before going to bed, after carefully cleaning and drying the affected areas. Duration of treatment: Up to 8 weeks but can be extended up to a max 12 weeks if considered as acceptable from a medical point of view."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn < 14 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid contact with eyes and other mucous membranes. Photosensitivity reactions in patients treated with other quinolones administered systemically. Avoid exposure to artificial UV radiation (UV lamps, solar beds, solarium) and avoid, when possible, exposure to sunlight. Do not apply to damaged skin (cuts and grazes) and during the nursing period. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin irritations, pruritus, burning sensation, erythema, contact dermatitis, urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Peeling agents, astringents, products containing irritant substances e.g. aromatic agents and alcohols."
          },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4bWXYKWD8E6iq1qDsJWu2MqEl8J3aYQe0S2BtaXsOXGeF14jb3.jpg",

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paracetamol, phenylpropanolamine HCl, chlorphenamine maleate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Nasal Decongestants, Antiallergics & Related Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of clogged nose, runny nose, postnasal drip, itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, headache, body aches, and fever associated with common cold, allergic rhinitis, sinusitis, flu, and other minor respiratory tract infections. Helps decongest sinus openings and passages."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: 1 tab every 6 hrs. Max 4 g/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with high BP or severe heart disease; anemia, renal or hepatic disease. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with high BP, toxic goiter, BPH, irregular heart rate, glaucoma, thyroid problems, diabetes, renal or hepatic disease. Concomitant use with antidepressants; warfarin. Should not be taken with &ge;3 alcoholic drinks. Reevaluate condition if fever worsens or persists >3 days. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. <b>Phenylpropanolamine:</b> Patients with heart disease, uncontrolled/untreated HTN.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Phenylpropanolamine:</b> Aggressiveness (particularly in young childn), anxiety, confusion, insomnia/sleep disturbance, nervousness; agitation, dizziness, restlessness, sudden persistent severe headache, tremor; blurred vision; chest tightness, palpitation; high BP; nausea; irritability. <b>Chlorpheniramine:</b> Insomnia/sleeplessness, nervousness; headache, tremor; blurred vision, visual disturbance; tinnitus; chest tightness; increased or decreased BP; constipation, diarrhea, GI discomfort, nausea, vomiting; muscle weakness; urination difficulties; mouth, nose, and throat dryness; irritability. <b>Paracetamol:</b> Skin redness, blisters, rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic agents (e.g. epinephrine), anesthetics (e.g. halothane), MAOIs (e.g. selegiline, moclobemide), TCAs (e.g. amitriptyline, imipramine), anxiolytics (e.g. alprazolam, diazepam), hypnotics (e.g. zolpidem). <b>Phenylpropanolamine:</b> Caffeine. <b>Paracetamol:</b> Warfarin, phenobarbital, phenytoin, metoclopramide, domperidone, cholestyramine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 325 mg/20 mg/1 mg (P8.50)."
          }
        ],

          },

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }

            "content": "Hematologic, CV, respiratory, neurologic, musculoskeletal, GI, dermatologic, hepatic, and injection site reactions."

            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: Allergic, vasomotor or other hyperactive nasal disorders, acute coryza.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - <b>Adults</b>: 1 tab twice daily. <b>Syr</b> - <b>Childn 5-12 yrs</b>: 5 mL; <b>3-4 yrs</b>: 3.75 mL; <b>Infants 7 months-2 yrs</b>: 2.5 mL; <b>1-6 months</b>: 1.25 mL. <b>Drops</b> - <b>Infants 7 months-2 yrs</b>: 1 mL; <b>Up to 6 months</b>: 0.5 mL.           {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Brain damage or epilepsy. Premature infants or neonates. Pregnancy and lactation."

Patients receiving antidepressants. May result to rebound congestion and rhinorrhea in excessive doses. Avoid alcoholic drinks. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.           },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Brompheniramine:</b> Antimuscarinic effects, sedation, hypotension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "MAOIs."
          },

            "content": "Tablet 15 mg/12 mg (P8.26). Syrup 12.5 mg/4 mg per 5 mL x 60 mL (P114.95). Oral drops 6.25 mg/2 mg per mL x 15 mL (P113.08)."

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antitussives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the relief of cough, clogged nose, postnasal drip, headache, body aches, and fever associated with the common cold, allergic rhinitis, sinusitis, flu, and other minor respiratory tract infections. It also helps decongest sinus openings and passages."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: 1 cap every 6 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe coronary disease or CV disease including MI, severe HTN and ventricular arrhythmia. Repeated administration in patients with anemia, cardiac, pulmonary, renal, or hepatic disease. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with high BP, toxic goiter, BPH, HR irregularity, glaucoma, and those taking antidepressants. Do not use with any other medicine containing dextromethorphan, phenylpropanolamine or paracetamol. Patients at risk of developing respiratory failure (e.g. chronic bronchitis, emphysema or during asthma attack); with persistent or chronic cough (e.g. cough lasting for &gt;3 weeks); when coughing is accompanied by excessive secretions. Liver or kidney disease. Concomitant use with warfarin. May impair ability to drive or operate machine.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Dextromethorphan</b>: Nausea, GI discomfort, dizziness, drowsiness, excitation, and mental confusion. <b>Phenylephrine</b>: Tremor, restlessness, anxiety, insomnia, nervousness, dizziness, increased BP, palpitation, arrhythmia, weakness, respiratory distress, and pallor. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Skin rashes, hypersensitivity, changes in the number of WBC and platelets, and minor stomach and GI disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Dextromethorphan:</b> MAOIs. <b>Phenylephrine:</b> Sympathomimetic agents, general anesthetics, antidepressants, adrenergic-blocking agents. <b>Paracetamol:</b> Warfarin or coumadin, phenothiazine, isoniazid, anticonvulsants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 325 mg/25 mg/10 mg (P9.73)."
          }

            "content": "For the relief of pain in common upper respiratory infections; runny nose, nasal congestion, allergic rhinitis and sinusitis. For fever reduction."

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 1 tab every 4 hrs. Childn 6-12 yrs: &frac12; tab every 4 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with high BP or severe heart disease, anemia, kidney or liver disease. Pregnancy and lactation."

            "content": "Patients with CV problems or DM. Withdraw medication if drowsiness, restlessness or nervousness occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.",

            "content": "<b>Paracetamol:</b> Changes in the number of WBC and platelets; allergic reactions; minor GI disturbances. <b>Phenylephrine:</b> Anxiety, insomnia, nervousness; dizziness, restlessness, tremor; arrhythmia, palpitation; increased BP, pallor; respiratory distress; weakness. <b>Chlorphenamine:</b> Sleepiness, drowsiness, nervousness; headache, tremor; blurred vision, visual disturbance; tinnitus; chest tightness; increased or decreased BP; constipation, diarrhea, GI discomfort, nausea, vomiting; muscle weakness; difficulty urinating; dryness of mouth, nose and throat; irritability."
          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paracetamol, phenylephrine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Nasal Decongestants, Antiallergics & Related Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of clogged nose, postnasal drip, headache, body aches, and fever associated with common cold, sinusitis, flu, and other minor respiratory tract infections. Helps decongest sinus openings and passages."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: 1 tab every 6 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. High BP or severe heart disease, anemia, kidney or liver disease. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Severe liver damage may occur if max daily amount of paracetamol (&gt;4 g) is consumed in 24 hrs; taken with other medicines containing paracetamol; consumption of &ge;3 alcoholic drinks every day. Liver disease. Use of warfarin.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Phenylephrine</b>: Tremor, restlessness, anxiety, insomnia/sleeplessness, nervousness, dizziness, increased BP, palpitation, arrhythmia, weakness, respiratory distress, and pallor. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Skin rashes and minor stomach and intestinal disturbance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic agents and general anesthetics. Antidepressants, adrenergic blocking agents, anticonvulsants, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 500 mg/25 mg (P8.50)."
          }
        ],

          },

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Nasal congestion due to common colds, headache, rhinitis, sinusitis associated with pain and fever."
          },

            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 1 cap every 8 hrs. <b>Childn 7-12 yrs</b>: 1 cap every 12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Coronary thrombosis, HTN, hyperthyroidism, closed-angle glaucoma, and acute liver failure. Concomitant use with MAOIs."

            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cardiac disease, angina, DM, prostatic enlargement. Patients receiving digitalis and antidepressants. Patients with G6PD deficiency. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C for phenylpropanolamine; Category B for paracetamol.",

                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Giddiness, nausea, vomiting, sweating, thirst, tachycardia, palpitations, precordial pain, difficulty in micturition, muscle weakness and tremors, anxiety, restlessness, insomnia."

            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs:</b> 2 sprays in each nostril once daily, preferably in the morning. Or 1 spray in each nostril twice daily. 2 sprays in each nostril twice daily may be necessary in some cases. Maintenance: 1 spray in each nostril once daily 4-7 days after initial therapy; Max 4 spray/nostril. <b>Childn 4-11 yrs:</b> 1 spray in each nostril once daily, preferably in the morning. 2 sprays in each nostril once daily or 1 spray in each nostril twice daily may be necessary in some patients. Max 2 sprays/nostril."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe allergies, clinical TB, asymptomatic <i>M. tuberculosis</i> RTI, untreated fungal and bacterial infections, ocular herpes simplex, untreated systemic viral infections. Reduction of growth velocity in childn; hypercorticism and suppression of HPA axis function; Cushing's syndrome. Withdrawal symptoms, acute adrenal insufficiency, or severe symptomatic exacerbation of asthma may occur when switching from systemic corticosteroids. Concomitant use with other inhaled steroids; immunosuppressants. Examine nasal passages periodically for mucosal changes and signs of candidiasis during prolonged use. Childn < 4 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Angioedema, rash, face and tongue edema, pruritus, urticaria, bronchospasm, wheezing, contact dermatitis, dyspnea, anaphylaxis/anaphylactoid reactions. Nasopharyngeal or respiratory, GI, and ocular effects. Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, lethargy, fatigue or arthralgia, fever, flu-like symptoms, menstrual cramps, aches and pains, growth suppression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other inhaled or systemic corticosteroids, potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir), ketoconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Nasal spray 50 mcg/spray x 120 sprays (P941.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/8nkjK5TGYz6T400gBoR3zUlJ7cPP6kEygDNGjv8IJu1R65g24M.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Mometasone furoate monohydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Nasal Decongestants, Antiallergics & Related Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of symptoms of seasonal or perennial rhinitis in adults, adolescents and childn 2-11 yrs. Prophylactic treatment in patients who have history of moderate to severe symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis. Treatment of nasal polyps and associated symptoms e.g. congestion and loss of smell in patients &ge;18 yrs. Treatment of symptoms associated with acute rhinosinusitis in patients &ge;12 yrs without signs and symptoms of severe bacterial infection. Adjunctive treatment to antibiotics for acute episodes of sinusitis in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Seasonal allergic or perennial rhinitis - Adults and adolescents</b>: 2 sprays/nostril once daily. Maintenance: 1 spray/nostril; Max 4 sprays/nostrils per day. <b>Childn 2-11 yrs</b>: 1 spray/nostril once daily. <b>Nasal polyposis - Adults and adolescents &ge;18 yrs</b>: 2 sprays/nostril twice daily. Once symptoms are adequately controlled, reduce to 2 sprays/nostril once daily. <b>Acute rhinosinusitis - Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs</b>: 2 sprays/nostril twice daily. <b>Adjunctive treatment of acute episodes of sinusitis - Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs</b>: 2 sprays/nostril twice daily. The dose may be increased to 4 sprays/nostril twice daily if symptoms are inadequately controlled."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue treatment if localized fungal infection of nose and pharynx develops. Patients with active or quiescent TB infections of respiratory tract, or in untreated fungal, bacterial, systemic viral infections or ocular herpes simplex. Patients transferred from long-term administration of systemically active corticosteroids to aqueous mometasone furoate nasal spray. Immunosuppressed patients. May cause visual disturbances, inhibition of wound healing. Treatment of symptoms of rhinosinusitis in childn &lt;12 yrs; nasal polyposis in childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, epistaxis, pharyngitis, nasal burning, nasal irritation, nasal ulceration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, cobicistat-containing products)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Aqueous nasal spray (500 mcg/g) 50 mcg per dose x 140 metered dose (P901.93), 60 metered dose (P487.20)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Substitute therapy for essential hypertension in patients already controlled with indapamide and amlodipine given concurrently at the same dose level."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab/day, preferably in the morning."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min), hepatic encephalopathy or severe liver impairment, hypokalemia, severe hypotension, shock including cardiogenic shock, obstruction of the outflow tract of left ventricle (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis), hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients in hypertensive crisis, with heart failure, hyperuricemia, galactose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, total lactase deficiency; choroidal effusion with visual field defect, transient myopia, and acute angle-closure glaucoma. Hepatic encephalopathy which can progress to hepatic coma, photosensitivity, hyponatremia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypercalcemia. Monitor blood glucose; plasma sodium, potassium, magnesium, and calcium levels regularly, even more frequent in elderly and cirrhotic patients. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypokalemia, somnolence, dizziness, headache, visual impairment, diplopia, palpitations, flushing, dyspnea, abdominal pain, nausea, dyspepsia, change of bowel habit, diarrhea, constipation, maculopapular rash, ankle swelling, muscle spasms, edema, fatigue, asthenia."
          },

            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Tacrolimus, ciclosporin. <b>Indapamide:</b> Lithium.           },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Septicemia, superficial suppurative disorder (phlegmone, lymphadenitis, perianal abscess), surgical and orthopedic infection (osteomyelitis, arthritis, wound infection), respiratory tract infections (pneumonia, circumtonsillar abscess, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, secondary infection of chronic respiratory disease, pulmonary abscess, empyema), urinary tract infections (nephropyelitis, complicated cystitis), gynecological infection (adnexitis, intrauterine infection, pelvic cavity infection, pelvis cellulitis), otorhinological infection (otitis media, nasosinusitis), bacterial meningitis (in childn from 3 months), febrile neutropenia, cystic fibrosis."
          },
          {

            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 500 mg-1 g twice to thrice daily IV infusion approx 30 mins. <b>Nosocomial pneumonia, peritonitis, febrile neutropenia, septicemia</b>: 1 g IV every 8 hrs; <b>Cystic fibrosis, meningitis</b>: 2 g IV every 8 hrs. <b>Childn 3 months-12 yrs - Bacterial meningitis</b>: 40 mg/kg IV every 8 hrs approx 30 mins depending on the type and severity of infection, known or suspected susceptibility of the pathogen(s) and patient's condition."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with valproic acid/sodium valproate. Do not use drugs that delay peristalsis (opiates and diphenoxylate with atropine)."

            "content": "Renal or hepatic impairment; epilepsy and CNS impairment, <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i> LRTI.         "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dsYGEAPs5voX4UIyQT1Z0WG8h9wbll96XUiZ7y9xKAyn4j8jOY.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/huqmUDZkfT9EmraIZ9O3ymt0QOwkkslV2Ft3IW3ILsXQ6pTUjH.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/t16DhKtKPpf3lZsSh6BSfqtDPHhauPliGpZAlbXcIFZXTgqLEj.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Vinorelbine tartrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vinca Alkaloids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "As a single agent and in combination chemotherapy in treatment of non-small cell lung cancer and metastatic breast cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy -</b> 1<sup>st</sup> 3 administrations: 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA once weekly; Subsequent administrations: Increase to 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once weekly; for patients whose neutrophil count dropped once below 500/mm<sup>3</sup> or more than once to between 500-1,000/mm<sup>3</sup> during the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 administrations, adjust dose. <b>Combination chemotherapy:</b> Dose and treatment regimen should be adjusted according to treatment protocol. <b>Hepatic insufficiency - Mild (bilirubin < 1.5x ULN, AST and/or ALT 1.5-2.5x ULN):</b> 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once weekly. <b>Moderate (bilirubin 1.5-3x ULN):</b> 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once weekly. Swallow with water without chewing or sucking the cap. Take after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe hepatic disorder, diseases significantly affecting absorption, history of significant surgical resection of stomach or small bowel, neutrophil count < 1,500/mm<sup>3</sup> or current or recent (within 2 weeks) severe infection, platelet count < 100,000/mm<sup>3</sup>. Patients requiring long-term oxygen therapy. In combination with yellow fever vaccine. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with fructose intolerance. Must undergo close hematological monitoring during treatment. Patients with history of IHD; poor performance status. Concomitant use with radiotherapy if the treatment field includes the liver; potent CYP3A4 inhibitors or inducers. Risk of irreversible infertility in men. Women of childbearing potential. Childn. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bacterial, viral, or fungal infections without neutropenia, bone marrow depression (resulting in neutropenia, leucopenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia), neurosensory disorders, GI disorders, alopecia, fatigue/malaise, weight loss."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Live attenuated vaccines (e.g yellow fever vaccine), phenytoin, fosphenytoin, vit K antagonists, macrolides, cobicistat, immunosuppressants, itraconazole, posaconazole, protease inhibitors, mitomycin-C, CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 20 mg (P7,440.47), 30 mg (P11,160.71)."
          }

          },

          },
          {

            "content": "Rx"

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) and stable mild and moderate congestive heart failure (CHF) in addition to standard therapies in elderly patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN - Adults</b>: 5 mg once daily. <b>In combination with HCTZ</b>: 5 mg plus HCTZ 12.5-25 mg. <b>Elderly &gt;65 yrs</b>: Initially 2.5 mg daily.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Liver insufficiency or impairment. Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock or episodes of heart failure decompensation.           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concomitant use with anesthetics. Untreated CHF, IHD. Increased sensitivity to allergens and severity of anaphylactic reactions. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Severe renal impairment. Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents. Elderly &gt;75 yrs.           {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Drugs for Hyperkalemia and Hyperphosphatemia"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of hyperphosphatemia in adult patients receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis, and adult patients with chronic kidney disease not on dialysis with serum phosphorus &gt;1.78 mmol/L."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Starting dose</b> – Serum phosphorus level 1.78-2.42 mmol/L (5.5-7.5 mg/dL): 2.4 g/day; >2.42 mmol/L (>7.5 mg/dL): 4.8 g/day. Total daily doses are taken in 3 divided doses with meals. Patients previously on phosphate binders (i.e. sevelamer HCl or calcium-based): Give on a gram-for-gram basis with monitoring of serum phosphorus levels. <b>Titration and maintenance</b>: Titrate dose every 2-4 weeks until acceptable serum phosphorus level is reached. Continue treatment based on the need to control serum phosphorus levels; the daily dose is approximately 6 g/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hypophosphatemia. Bowel obstruction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended in adult patients with CKD not on dialysis with serum phosphorus &lt;1.78 mmol/L. Patients with dysphagia, swallowing disorders, severe GI motility disorder (e.g. untreated or severe gastroparesis, retention of gastric contents and abnormal or irregular bowel motion), active IBD, major GIT surgery; rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Intestinal obstruction and ileus/subileus; patients who are constipated. Hypocalcemia/hypercalcemia, low levels of fat-soluble vits A, D, E and K; metabolic acidosis; peritonitis may develop. Folate deficiency during long-term treatment. Co-administration with anti-arrhythmic, anti-seizure medicinal products. Patients with hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Not indicated for the control of hyperparathyroidism. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, constipation. Diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciprofloxacin; ciclosporin, mycophenolate mofetil and tacrolimus; levothyroxine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 800 mg (P39.00)."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Nh5wODqeU4CczMMjq3uCBhGarc6xbnWO6Vtt94hNdJOtfpQHks.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Filgrastim",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Immunological Chemotherapeutic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Chemotherapy-induced neutropenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV/SC only. <b>Patients on low-dose chemotherapy or with non-serious marrow depression estimated damage</b>: 1.25 mcg/kg/day. <b>Patients with high-intensity chemotherapy or obvious decline of granulocytes</b>: 2.5 mcg/kg/day for 7 days. <b>Patients with neutrophilic granulocytes < 1x10<sup>9</sup>/L after chemotherapy</b>: 5 mcg/kg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to filgrastim, <i>E. coli</i>-derived proteins. Increased dose of cytotoxic chemotherapy beyond established dosage regimens. Severe congenital neutropenia (Kostmann’s syndrome) with abnormal cytogenetics. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not dilute using saline solutions. Obtain CBC and platelet count before instituting treatment. Concomitant use with cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiation therapy. Do not administer 24 hrs before to 24 hrs after cytotoxic chemotherapy. Patients with sickle cell disorders, chronic myeloid leukemia, myelodysplasia; preexisting cardiac conditions (MI, arrhythmia); infections causing myelosuppression. Risk for splenomegaly and splenic rupture, thrombocytopenia, leukocytosis, cutaneous vasculitis, ARDS, osteoporosis. May cause transient positive bone imaging changes. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Musculoskeletal pain. Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, mucosal inflammation, constipation and diarrhea. Sickle cell crisis. Leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia. Increased gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase, ALP, LDH, and uric acid. Headache, anorexia. Cough, pharyngolaryngeal pain. Alopecia, skin rash. Erythema, swelling or pruritus at site of injection. Fatigue and generalized weakness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that potentiate neutrophil release e.g. lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV/SC) 300 mcg/mL (P3,479.48)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Per 1 L: L-leucine 10.3 g, L-lysine monoacetate 10.01 g (equiv L-lysine 7.1 g), L-alanine 6.3 g, L-valine 6.2 g, L-isoleucine 5.1 g, L-arginine 4.9 g, L-threonine 4.8 g, L-serine 4.5 g, L-histidine 4.3 g, L-proline 4.3 g, L-phenylalanine 3.8 g, glycine 3.2 g, L-methionine 2.8 g, L-tryptophan 1.9 g, L-malic acid 1.5 g, glacial acetic acid 1.38 g, acetylcysteine 500 mg (equiv L-cysteine 370 mg)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Parenteral Nutritional Products"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For amino acid supply in severely impaired renal function and dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute and chronic renal insufficiency - Without dialysis treatment:</b> Up to 0.5 g amino acids/kg BW and day (= 500 mL/day at 70 kg BW). <b>Under dialysis treatment:</b> Up to 1 g amino acids/kg BW and day (= 1,000 mL/day at 70 kg BW). <b>Max:</b> 1.5 g amino acids/kg BW and day (= 1,500 mL/day at 70 kg BW), drop rate should be &le;20 drops/min. Administer calorie carriers either before or simultaneously by mouth or parenterally. <b>Duration</b> - Acute renal insufficiency: &le;2 weeks; Chronic renal insufficiency without dialysis treatment and acute and chronic renal insufficiency under hemodialysis, hemofiltration, or peritoneal dialysis: Until a sufficient oral supply of protein can be given."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Impaired amino acid metabolism, advanced functional impairment of the liver, severe cardiac insufficiency, hyperhydration, hypokalemia, hyponatremia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Regularly monitor blood electrolyte levels, water-electrolyte metabolism, acid-base status and serum urea. Supply sufficient potassium. Treat existing renal function reduction first. Increased production of gastric acid and stress ulcer. Do not mix with other drugs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs and other additives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 7% 500 mL (P737.00)."
          }

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pzcqzKZ6liEa1SwqpXRljxuG39kZOgFwEK7MVOVUarqkg4uX8u.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GWR6EvOfJGEluEPdR3zCx4sllPYTUd0eIcZRXVAIy7PuVZd3Yx.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GqOrFysTKJfUmgfzBl1KdMphvnw7RG1SO6GWqbPBhkqYd4CGmP.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pregabalin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunctive therapy in adults with partial seizures with or without secondary generalization. Treatment of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy</b>: Initially 150 mg/day as 2 or 3 divided doses, may be increased to 300 mg/day after an interval of 3-7 days. Max 600 mg/day after additional 7-day interval, if needed. <b>GAD</b>: Dose range is 150-600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. Initially 150 mg/day, may be increased to 450 mg/day. Max 600 mg/day after additional 7 days. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl &ge;60 mL/min: Initially 150 mg/day and max 600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses; &ge;30 to &lt;60 mL/min: Initially 75 mg/day and max 300 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses; &ge;15 to &lt;30 mL/min: Initially 25-50 mg/day and max 150 mg/day once daily or in 2 divided doses; &lt;15 mL/min: Initially 25 mg/day once daily. Max 75 mg/day once daily. Supplementary dose following hemodialysis: 25 mg as single dose. Max 100 mg. <b>Discontinuation</b>: Should be done gradually over a minimum of 1 week."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment, diabetes, CHF. Increased risk of suicidal thoughts or behavior. Monitor for emergence or worsening of depression and/or any unusual changes in mood or behavior. Increases the occurrence of accidental injury (fall) in elderly. Vision-related reactions. Withdrawal symptoms. May affect the ability to drive or operate machine. Childn &lt;12 yrs and adolescents 12-17 yrs. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased appetite. Euphoric mood, confusion, irritability, decreased libido, disorientation, insomnia. Dizziness, somnolence. Ataxia, abnormal coordination, tremor, dysarthria, memory impairment, attention disturbance, paresthesia, sedation, balance disorder, lethargy, amnesia. Blurred vision, diplopia. Vertigo. Vomiting, dry mouth, constipation, flatulence, abdominal distension. Erectile dysfunction. Gait abnormal, feeling drunk, fatigue, peripheral edema, edema. Increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ethanol, lorazepam, oxycodone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 75 mg (P28.96), 150 mg (P48.28)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pregabalin, methylcobalamin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of neuropathic pain associated with peripheral neuropathy, neuralgia, and fibromyalgia. Adjunct therapy for adults with partial onset of seizures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 1 cap twice daily. Patients previously on gabapentin will have a wash-out period of 1 week prior to start of dosing with pregabalin. <b>Renal impairment and hemodialysis</b>: Adjust dosing."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History or at risk of angioedema. Increased risk of suicidal behavior and ideation or unusual changes in mood or behavior. Use in treatment of central neuropathic pain due to spinal cord injury. Visual disturbance may occur. Reduced lower GI tract function when used in combination with opioid analgesics. History of substance abuse. Patients with conditions that may precipitate encephalopathy. CHF NYHA II or IV; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, and glucose-galactose malabsorption. Withdrawal symptoms. May cause weight gain; peripheral edema; creatine kinase elevations or myopathy; decreased platelet count; PR interval prolongation. Risk of male-mediated teratogenicity. Alcohol consumption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, somnolence, headache, ataxia, asthenia, dry mouth, constipation, edema, blurred vision, weight gain, and difficulty with concentration/attention."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CNS depressants, alcohol; antibiotics; cholestyramine, colchicine, colestipol; metformin, para-aminosalicylic acid, potassium chloride; nitrous oxide. Neomycin, ASA, H2-antagonists, omeprazole, colchicine, oral contraceptives, parenteral chloramphenicol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 75 mg/750 mcg (P33.00)."

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Ajt8uoJlNfs0mqNpOROCMmfP8xvuvag3GomOTqCiHN0NQ2Gfa6.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2LMA9C5iFp93TZnETcqwixPm4CIJpJIwLKb8KD5G7QZkLrkH5Y.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pregabalin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Indicated for the treatment of peripheral and central neuropathic pain in adults. Adjunctive therapy in adults with partial seizures with or without secondary generalization. Treatment of generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "150 mg- 600 mg/day given either 2-3 divided doses. <b>Neuropathic pain:</b> 150 mg/day given in 2-3 divided doses. May increased to 300 mg daily after 1 week. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>Epilepsy:</b> Initially 150 mg/day given in 2-3 divided doses. May increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week interval. <b>GAD:</b> 150-600 mg daily given in 2-3 divided doses. Initially 150 mg/day. May increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week. Following an additional week the dose may increase to 450 mg/day. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>Discontinuation:</b> Should be done gradually over a minimum of 1 week independent of the indication. <b>Renal impairment:</b> CrCl &ge; 60 mL/min:</b> 150 mg/day 2-3 divided doses. Max 600 mg/day; <b>&ge;30-&lt;60 mL/min:</b> 75 mg/day 2-3 divided doses. Max 300 mg/day; <b>&ge;15-&lt;30 mL/min:</b> 25-50 mg/day once daily or 2 divided doses. Max 150 mg; <b>&lt;15 mL/min:</b> 25 mg/day once daily. Max 75 mg/day. <b>Supplementary dosage hemodialysis:</b> 25 mg/day single dose. Max 100 mg/day single dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Diabetic patients. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema (e.g. facial, perioral, or upper airway swelling occur). Increase of occurrence of accidental injury in the elderly population. Vision-related effects. Renal failure. Withdrawal symptoms and concomitant anti-epileptic medicinal products. Patients with CHF. Treatment of central neuropathic pain due to spinal cord injury. Monitor for signs of suicidal ideation and behaviors. Reduced lower GIT function. Concomitant use with opioids. Monitor for misuse, abuse or dependence. Underlying conditions that may precipitate encephalopathy. May influence the ability to drive or use machines. Elderly. Childn &lt;12 and adolescents. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis. Increased appetite. Euphoric mood, confusion, irritability, disorientation, insomnia, libido decreased. Dizziness, somnolence, headache. Ataxia, abnormal coordination, tremor, dysarthria, amnesia, memory impairment, disturbance in attention, paresthesia, hypoesthesia, sedation, balance disorder, lethargy. Blurred vision, diplopia. Vertigo. Vomiting, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, abdominal distension, dry mouth. Muscle cramps, arthralgia, back pain, pain in limb, cervical spasm. Erectile dysfunction. Edema peripheral, edema, gait abnormal, fall, feeling drunk, feeling abnormal, fatigue. Increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproic acid, lamotrigine, gabapentin, lorazepam, oxycodone, ethanol. Lorazepam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 25 mg (P17.92), 75 mg (P32.00), 150 mg (P50.00)."
          }
        ],
