        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Vitamins E 100 IU, B<sub>1</sub> 300 mg, B<sub>6</sub> 100 mg, B<sub>12</sub> 1 mg",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vitamin B-Complex"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of deficiencies in vitamins B<sub>1</sub>, B<sub>6</sub>, B<sub>12</sub> and E manifested as: abnormal touch sensation (numbness, burning and pricking); muscle weakness and loss of reflexes in the extremities. Treatment of conditions responsive to high dose vitamins B<sub>1</sub>, B<sub>6</sub>, B<sub>12</sub> and E including polyneuropathy, diabetic neuropathy, neuralgia, neuritis, Wernicke’s disease, beri-beri, sideroblastic anemia, and pernicious anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab a day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to cobalt. Patients with early Leber’s disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients on warfarin therapy or at risk for Vit K deficiency (e.g. liver failure). Patients with inherited bleeding disorder or with history of hemorrhagic stroke, IDA, or hyperthyroidism.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Adverse neurologic effects (chronic administration of high vit B<sub>6</sub> doses). Anticoagulant effects, and stroke with bleeding (high dose vit E)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticonvulsants (phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine). <b>Vit B<sub>1</sub></b>: Neuromuscular blocking agents. <b>Vit B<sub>6</sub></b>: Cycloserine, hydralazine, INH, penicillamine; estrogen, theophylline. <b>Vit B<sub>12</sub></b>: Aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol, colchicine, extended-release potassium preparations, aminosalicylic acid and its salts, H2-receptor antagonists, metformin, methyldopa, cobalt irradiation of the small bowel; nitrous oxide; oral contraceptives, PPIs. <b>Vit E</b>: Digoxin, insulin, dietary fiber supplementation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet (P20.00)."
          }

  {
    "id": 3057,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3057,
        "brand_name": "Neurontin",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jK9utaFcQtHs96LAnJ2oEHqqt3JgXzQwCI5xAkQh8zlC03is59.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HygZN7dNbF3oMY19O4r0BYE7eCX0VpHqbZ38I5PZwhNLj4NWbY.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/C0eeY6O4XKkMkj0Y5hQEc8RSu08QHWCdS717oNjGXTlECvYo00.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gabapentin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "As monotherapy in the treatment of partial seizures with and without secondary generalization in adults and childn &ge;12 yrs. As adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial seizures with and without secondary generalization in adults and childn aged &ge;3 yrs. Treatment of neuropathic pain in adults aged &ge;18 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy - Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs:</b> 900-3,600 mg/day. Initially 300 mg three times a day on Day 1 or titrate the dose as follows: 300 mg once daily on Day 1, then 300 mg two times a day on Day 2, then 300 mg three times a day on Day 3. Thereafter, increase dose in 3 equally divided doses up to max 3,600 mg/day; <b>Childn 3-12 yrs:</b> Initially 10-15 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses, effective dose reached by upward titration over a period of approximately 3 days; &ge;5 yrs: 25-35 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses; <b>3-< 5 yrs:</b> 40 mg/kg/day in equally divided doses. <b>Neuropathic pain:</b> Initially 900 mg/day in 3 equally divided doses and increase if necessary up to max 3,600 mg/day. <b>Impaired renal function in patients with neuropathic pain or epilepsy – CrCl &ge;80 mL/min:</b> 900-3,600 mg/day; <b>50-79 mL/min:</b> 600-1,800 mg/day; <b>30-49 mL/min:</b> 300-900 mg/day; <b>12-29 mL/min:</b> 300 mg every other day to 600 mg/day; <b>< 15 mL/min:</b> 150 mg every other day to 300 mg/day. Patients undergoing hemodialysis who have never received gabapentin: Loading dose of 300-400 mg, then 200-300 mg following each 4 hrs of hemodialysis. Total daily doses should be administered in 3 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Abrupt withdrawal of anticonvulsants in epileptic patients may precipitate status epilepticus. Not considered effective in the treatment of absence seizures. Risk for dizziness and somnolence, which could increase the occurrence of accidental injury (fall); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms; risk for abuse and dependence. Concomitant use with opioids and other CNS depressants. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, back pain, fatigue, fever, headache, viral infection; vasodilation; constipation, dental abnormalities, diarrhea, dyspepsia, increased appetite, dry mouth or throat, nausea and/or vomiting; leukopenia, decreased WBC; peripheral edema, weight increase; fracture, myalgia; amnesia, ataxia, confusion, abnormal coordination, depression, dizziness, dysarthria, emotional lability, insomnia, nervousness, nystagmus, somnolence, thinking abnormal, tremor, twitching; coughing, pharyngitis, rhinitis, amblyopia, diplopia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids containing aluminum and magnesium; cimetidine. False positive readings in Ames N-Multistix SG dipstick test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P68.90), 300 mg (P75.97), 400 mg (P94.45). Tablet 600 mg (P134.75)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3917,

        },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Escitalopram oxalate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of major depressive episodes, panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder (SAD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dose. Taken once daily. <b>Adults - Major depressive disorder, GAD, SAD, and OCD:</b> 10 mg, may be increased to max 20 mg daily. <b>Treatment duration - SAD:</b> &ge;3 months; <b>Major depressive disorder, GAD:</b> 6 months; <b>OCD:</b> several months or longer; <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia:</b> Initially 5 mg, increased after a week to 10 mg daily. May further increase to max 20 mg daily for several months. <b>Elderly:</b> Initially &frac12; of recommended dose and lower max dose. <b>Hepatic impairment and poor metabolizers of CYP2C19:</b> Initially 5 mg daily for 1<sup>st</sup> 2 weeks, may be increased to 10 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with non-selective, irreversible MAOIs or pimozide. Unstable epilepsy. Rare hereditary galactose intolerance."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Gradually reduce dose over at least 1-2 weeks. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), history of mania/hypomania, cirrhosis, bleeding tendencies, controlled epilepsy. Coadministration with drug-induced hyponatremia or electroconvulsive therapy. Suicidal thoughts, attempt and behavior, hostility, paradoxical anxiety, akathisia, psychomotor restlessness, hyponatremia, cutaneous bleeding abnormalities. Discontinue if seizure develops for 1<sup>st</sup> time, increased seizure frequency; serotonin syndrome occurs; patient enters manic phase. May alter glycemic control. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, decreased/increased appetite, increased weight, anxiety, restlessness, abnormal dreams, decreased female libido, anorgasmia, insomnia, somnolence, dizziness, paresthesia, tremor, sinusitis, yawning, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, dry mouth, increased sweating, arthralgia, myalgia, ejaculation disorder, impotence, fatigue, pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Moclobemide, linezolid, selegiline, tramadol, sumatriptan, other triptans, TCAs, phenothiazines, thioxanthenes, butyrophenones, mefloquine, bupropion, lithium, tryptophan, St. John’s Wort, oral anticoagulants, NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P46.65), 20 mg (P71.62)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/R55ITBeWGTj1JRkD2ExOb5KoUz5Z8FiNc2Jwidt8MeF9E9pn5s.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7gWYfWvM5ZLSjHA9kmNj3pgS2DhwBAfYXOIQ8WOCMO2KtVVXTD.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Esomeprazole (IV: Sodium; Oral: magnesium trihydrate)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>IV/Tab</b> - Adult: Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis; long-term management for healed esophagitis to prevent relapse. Symptomatic treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Treatment of gastric ulcers and prevention of gastric and/or duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy. </b>IV:</b> Maintenance of hemostasis and prevention of rebleeding following therapeutic endoscopy for acute bleeding gastric or duodenal ulcers. Alternative therapy where oral administration is not appropriate; constitute only part of a full treatment period. Childn and adolescents 1-17 yrs: GERD with erosive reflux esophagitis and/or severe symptoms of reflux. <b>Tab:</b> Treatment of upper gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms associated with NSAID therapy. Prevention of gastric and/or duodenal ulcers associated with low-dose aspirin therapy. Following IV therapy, maintenance of hemostasis and prevention of rebleeding of gastric and/or duodenal ulcers. In combination with appropriate antibacterial regimen for <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> eradication, healing of <i>H. pylori</i>-associated duodenal ulcer and prevention of relapse of <i>H. pylori</i>-associated peptic ulcer. Pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. <b>Granules for oral susp:</b> GERD for childn 1-11 yrs. May also be used by patients having difficulty swallowing dispersed tabs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IV - Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis</b> – Adult and childn 12-17 yrs: 40 mg. Childn 1-11 yrs with < 20 kg BW: 10 mg; &ge;20 kg BW: 10 or 20 mg; 1-11 months: 1 mg/kg; 0-1 month: 0.5 mg/kg. <b>Long-term management of patients with healed esophagitis to prevent relapse</b> – Adult: 20 mg once daily. <b>Symptomatic treatment of GERD</b> – Adult: 20 mg in patients without esophagitis. Childn 12-17 yrs: 20 mg; 1-11 yrs: 10 mg; 1-11 months: 1 mg/kg; 0-1 month: 0.5 mg/kg. <b>Healing of gastric ulcer associated with NSAID therapy:</b> 20 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy:</b> 20 mg once daily. <b>Maintenance of hemostasis and prevention of rebleeding of ulcers:</b> 80 mg by bolus IV infusion over 30 minutes, followed by a continuous infusion of 8 mg/hr for 3 days. <b>Hepatic impairment – GERD</b>: Maximum of 20 mg daily dose; bleeding ulcer: 80 mg bolus followed by a continuous infusion dose of 4 mg/hr. <b>Tab/Granules for oral susp - GERD - Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis</b> - Adult and childn 12-18 yrs: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks, additional 4 weeks if esophagitis has not healed or with persistent symptoms. Childn 1-11 yrs with < 20 kg body weight: 10 mg once daily for 8 weeks; &ge;20 kg body weight: 10 or 20 mg once daily for 8 weeks. <b>Long-term management of patients with healed esophagitis to prevent relapse</b> - Adult and childn 12-18 yrs: 20 mg once daily. Childn 1-11 yrs: 10 mg once daily. <b>Symptomatic treatment of GERD</b>- Adult and childn 12-18 yrs: 20 mg once daily in patients without esophagitis. Childn 1-11 yrs: 10 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks. Childn 0-1 month with >2.5 kg BW: 2.5 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks; 1-11 months with 3-5 kg BW: 2.5 mg once daily for up to 6 weeks; >5-7.5 kg BW: 5 mg once daily for up to 6 weeks; >7.5-12 kg: 10 mg once daily for up to 6 weeks. <b>Tab: Treatment of upper GI symptoms associated with NSAID therapy:</b> 20 mg once daily. <b>Healing of gastric ulcer associated with NSAID therapy:</b> 20 or 40 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers or requiring continued low-dose aspirin therapy:</b> 20 or 40 mg once daily. <b>Maintenance of hemostasis and prevention of rebleeding of ulcers following IV therapy:</b> 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks. <b><i>H. pylori</i>-associated ulcer:</b> 20 mg with amoxicillin 1 g and clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Pathological hypersecretory conditions:</b> Initially 40 mg twice daily, then adjust or continue as indicated. Maximum 120 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation. <b>Granules for oral susp:</b> Patients with fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrose-isomaltase insufficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Exclude malignancy before treatment. Monitor patients on long-term treatment (>1 yr), at risk of osteoporosis and related fractures. Pregnancy. <b>Tab:</b> Possible drug interaction for all the components in the triple therapy for <i>H. pylori</i> eradication.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea, vomiting, constipation. <b>IV:</b> Injection site reaction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs with pH dependent absorption (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, erlotinib, digoxin), diazepam, phenytoin, warfarin and other coumarin derivatives, clopidogrel, cisapride, tacrolimus, methotrexate, antiretroviral drugs (e.g. atazanavir, nelfinavir, saquinavir, CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin) and inducers, CYP2C19 inhibitors and inducers, voriconazole, rifampicin, St. John’s wort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for solution for injection 40 mg (P1,159.00). Enteric-coated tablet 20 mg (P128.50), 40 mg (P141.00). Granules for oral suspension 10 mg (P131.50)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 20,
          "name": "AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals (Phils.), Inc."
        },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XWO1x4MbHochdJUNUqQUw4joQlSVeOAlRABZrsBeHFXYxTKbJD.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/sXpfefGNO5oXcIuv0clNbcdT1lr6vEpcVt69rQtkhVMc7G3rN8.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Esomeprazole (Tab: Magnesium; IV: Sodium)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis; long-term management of patients with healed esophagitis to prevent relapse; symptomatic treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy in patients at risk. Healing of <i>Helicobacter pylori</i>-associated duodenal ulcer; prevention of relapse of peptic ulcers in patients with <i>H. pylori</i>-associated ulcer disease. In combination with appropriate antibacterial regimens for <i>H. pylori</i> eradication, prevention of relapse of peptic ulcer with <i>H. pylori</i>-associated ulcer disease. <b>IV</b>: Treatment of peptic ulcer disease (PUD), NSAID-associated ulceration, GERD and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab - Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis</b>: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks. Additional 4 weeks for patients with esophagitis that has not healed or with persistent symptoms. <b>Long-term management of healed esophagitis to prevent relapse</b>: 20 mg once daily. <b>Symptomatic treatment of GERD without esophagitis</b>: 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks. <b>Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy in patients at risk</b>: 20 mg or 40 mg once daily. <b><i>H. pylori</i> eradication or prevention of relapse of peptic ulcers with <i>H. pylori</i>-associated ulcer disease</b>: 20 mg esomeprazole + 1 g amoxicillin + 500 mg clarithromycin, twice daily for 7 days. <b>Severe liver impairment</b>: Max 20 mg daily. Tabs may be dispersed in half a glass of non-carbonated water. Stir until tabs disintegrate and drink immediately or within 30 mins. <b>IV – Adults</b>: 20 mg or 40 mg IV injection (not &lt;3 min) or IV infusion (10-13 min) once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to esomeprazole or substituted benzimidazoles. Concomitant administration with atazanavir and nelfinavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "In the presence of any alarm symptoms (e.g. significant unintentional weight loss, recurrent vomiting, dysphagia, hematemesis or melena) and when gastric ulcer is suspected or present, malignancy should be excluded. Long-term treatment (&gt;1 yr). Slightly increased risk of GI infections e.g. Salmonella and Campylobacter. Concomitant use of atazanavir. Severe renal insufficiency. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>IV</b>: Concomitant use of an imidazole antifungal.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache; abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea/vomiting. Dry mouth; gas; pain, swelling or redness at injection site."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole and itraconazole; diazepam; phenytoin; warfarin; clarithromycin. Saquinavir; methotrexate; tacrolimus; erlotinib, digoxin; citalopram, imipramine, clomipramine; voriconazole; cilostazol; cisapride; warfarin; clopidogrel; rifampicin and St. John’s wort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 20 mg (P50.00), 40 mg (P70.00). Powder for injection (IV)  40 mg (P944.00)."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QQWBGR9rr4KGVklKuQxsOA4i0lEYi52oViU7F4JjLIjQzFugNY.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/P41Czc3xon5ILtx8Zvke8ux6elGfBnHtSXT9Is0s2L1jm6pmXQ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Nicardipine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute life-threatening hypertension (HTN); malignant arterial HTN or hypertensive encephalopathy; aortic dissection when short-acting beta-blocker therapy is not suitable or in combination with beta-blocker; severe preeclampsia when other IV antihypertensive agents are contraindicated; post-op HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Unless given by central venous line, dilute to a concentration of 0.1-0.2 mg/mL before use. <b>Adults</b> - <b>Initial:</b> 3-5 mg/hr for 15 mins, may be increased in increments of 0.5 mg or 1 mg every 15 mins. Infusion rate should not be &gt;15 mg/hr. <b>Maintenance:</b> 2-4 mg/hr. Transition to oral antihypertensive - 20 mg cap: 60 mg/day in 3 divided doses; 50 mg ER tab: 100 mg/day in 2 divided doses. <b>Elderly and pregnancy:</b> Initially 1-5 mg/hr, may be increased or decreased by 0.5 mg/hr after 30 mins, depending on BP and clinical situation. Dose should not be &gt;4 mg/hr, rate not &gt;15 mg/hr (treatment of preeclampsia). <b>Childn</b> - <b>Initial:</b> 0.5-5 mcg/kg/min. <b>Maintenance:</b> 1-4 mcg/kg/min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe aortic stenosis, compensatory HTN (e.g. arteriovenous shunt or aortic coarctation), unstable angina; within 8 days after MI. Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Continuous IV infusion only. Decrease dose by half or discontinue infusion when systemic hypotension and reflex tachycardia occur. Patients with CHF or pulmonary edema, suspected coronary ischemia, history of hepatic dysfunction or hepatic impairment, portal HTN, pre-existing elevated intracranial pressure, acute cerebral infarction, and renal impairment. Concomitant use with beta-blockers, magnesium sulfate. Infants and childn. Childn with renal impairment. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dizziness, peripheral edema, palpitations, flushing. Hypotension, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, nausea, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Beta-blockers, CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors, alpha-blockers, TCAs, neuroleptics, opioids, amifostine, dantrolene, magnesium sulfate, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus, digoxin, baclofen, corticosteroids, tetracosactide, inhalational anesthetics, vecuronium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 1 mg/mL x 10 mL (P550.00)."
          }

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3677,
        "brand_name": "Ninlaro",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tQM4WZ84UtADgbHGWDkSwm82YKMr44MxP5ZAdizkZSRjUBVC62.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/FvYCneF9WJSXlJBipyUiqnULiBX7iKyEApVqqZoPwTtNAhQALV.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dh0tQhzji6mThZBjbhauzzirmxwmyVT6pkOnGVDKe9PUb1VLV6.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ixazomib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proteasome Inhibitor"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of multiple myeloma in combination with lenalidomide and dexamethasone in adults who have received at least one prior therapy. Maintenance of multiple myeloma following autologous stem cell treatment (ASCT) and for those who had not been treated with stem cell transplantation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Multiple myeloma in adults who have received at least one prior therapy -</b> Initial ixazomib dose: 4 mg once a week on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle; Initial lenalidomide dose: 25 mg once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle; Initial dexamethasone dose: 40 mg once a week on days 1, 8, 15, and 22 of a 28-day cycle. <b>Patients with moderate/severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, or ESRD requiring dialysis:</b> Reduce ixazomib dose to 3 mg. <b>Maintenance of multiple myeloma following ASCT and those who had not been treated with stem cell transplantation -</b> Cycles 1-4: 3 mg; Cycle 5 onwards: 4 mg; All doses taken in a fasted state once a week on days 1, 8, and 15 of a 28-day cycle, then the cycle is repeated. <b>Patients with moderate/severe hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment, or ESRD requiring dialysis:</b> Reduce to 2.3 mg for cycles 1-4 and 3 mg for cycle 5 onwards. Take doses at approx the same time each day at least 1 hr before or 2 hrs after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Consider antiviral prophylaxis and thromboprophylaxis. Thrombocytopenia; Monitor platelet counts at least monthly during treatment and more frequent monitoring should be considered during the 1<sup>st</sup> three cycles. GI toxicities, peripheral neuropathy and edema, cutaneous reactions, thrombotic microangiopathy including TTP; PRES. Hepatotoxicity. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A inducers. Men and women of childbearing potential should use contraception during and for 90 days after stopping treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, bronchitis; thrombocytopenia, neutropenia; peripheral neuropathies; diarrhea, constipation, nausea and vomiting; rash; back pain; peripheral edema. Herpes zoster."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, St. John’s Wort). Oral contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 3 mg (P102,858.00), 4 mg (P102,858.00)."
          }
        ],

    "id": 1323,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1323,
        "brand_name": "Nirva",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2UjF8vYTqq3Cupqcv5P6oaM5bjurbj5ja8PVSyGFD9tvS0VKeR.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2UjF8vYTqq3Cupqcv5P6oaM5bjurbj5ja8PVSyGFD9tvS0VKeR.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0Bu0xZzHLb13Yx93lu3xwbUXPmmFNVuPXJwtxIxeCVRexqWYlG.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clozapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of treatment-resistant schizophrenia. For reducing risk of recurrent suicidal behavior or schizoaffective disorder who are considered to be at chronic risk for reexperiencing suicidal behavior. For psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson’s disease, in cases where standard treatment has failed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Treatment-resistant schizophrenia - Initial dose:</b> 12.5 mg once or twice daily on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, continue with daily dosage increments of 25-50 mg/day to achieve target dose of 300-450 mg/day by the end of 2 weeks. Subsequent dose increments not &gt;100 mg made once or twice weekly; <b>Therapeutic dose:</b> 300-450 mg/day in divided doses (may be divided unevenly, larger portion at bedtime). Max 900 mg/day; <b>Maintenance dose:</b> Carefully down titrate after achieving max therapeutic benefit. Treatment should be maintained for at least 6 months. If dose is &lt;200 mg, give once a day in the evening. <b>Discontinuation therapy:</b> Gradual dose reduction over a 1- to 2-week period. <b>Psychotic disorders occurring during the course of Parkinson's disease where standard treatment has failed - Initial dose:</b> 12.5 mg in the evening. Subsequent dose increments by 12.5 mg with max 2 increments/week up to max 50 mg; <b>Mean effective dose:</b> 25-37.5 mg/day, increase by increments of 12.5 mg/week up to max 100 mg/day; <b>Ending therapy:</b> Gradual dose reduction by 12.5 mg over a period of at least 1 week (preferably 2 weeks). <b>Patients with history of seizures or suffering from renal or CV disorders:</b> 12.5 mg once daily on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, increase dose slowly and in small increments. <b>Elderly:</b> 12.5 mg once daily on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, with subsequent dose increments of 25 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Myeloproliferative disorders, uncontrolled epilepsy, paralytic ileus, history of clozapine-induced agranulocytosis or severe granulocytopenia, unable to undergo regular blood tests, history of toxic or idiosyncratic granulocytopenia or agranulocytosis, impaired bone marrow function, alcoholic and other toxic psychoses, drug intoxication, comatose conditions, circulatory collapse and/or CNS depression of any cause, severe renal or cardiac disorders, liver disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of agranulocytosis, fatal myocarditis, history of seizures or other predisposing factors. Concomitant use with benzodiazepines or other psychotropic drug. Not for dementia-related psychosis. CV and/or pulmonary disease, DM, recurrences of NMS, tardive dyskinesia (particularly in elderly women), transient temp elevations >38<sup>o</sup>C with peak incidence within the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 weeks of treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fever, chills, hypothermia, fatigue, weakness; central and autonomic nervous systems, CV, GI, endocrine and metabolic, hepatic, respiratory, genitourinary/reproductive, hemic and lymphatic system, dermatologic and sensitivity, and musculoskeletal effects; visual disturbance, narrow-angle glaucoma, mydriasis, eyelid and ear disorder, bloodshot eyes, nystagmus, periorbital edema, numb/sore tongue, bitter taste, nosebleed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Bone marrow suppressants, sulfonamides, pyrazolone analgesics, azapropazone, penicillamine, cytotoxic agents and long-acting depot injection of antipsychotics. Ritonavir, benzodiazepines, alcohol, antihistamines, MAOIs, CNS depressants including narcotics, anticholinergics, antihypertensives, type 1C antiarrhythmics, highly protein-bound drugs, TCAs and antimuscarinics, caffeine, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline, venlafaxine, ciprofloxacin and amprenavir, omeprazole, rifampicin, lithium, phenytoin, cimetidine, citalopram, erythromycin, nicotine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mg (P16.51), 100 mg (P54.89)."
          }
        ],

      "success": true,

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Nebivolol HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) and stable mild and moderate chronic heart failure (CHF) in addition to standard therapies in elderly patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN - Adults:</b> 5 mg once daily. <b>In combination with HCTZ:</b> 5 mg plus HCTZ 12.5-25 mg. <b>Patients with renal insufficiency:</b> 2.5 mg daily. May be increased to 5 mg. <b>Elderly >65 yrs:</b> Initially 2.5 mg daily. May be increased to 5 mg daily. <b>CHF:</b> Initially 1.25 mg once daily, increase at interval of 1-2 weeks based on patient's tolerability to 2.5, 5, and 10 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Liver insufficiency or impairment. Acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock or episodes of heart failure decompensation. Sick sinus syndrome including SA block; 2nd and 3rd degree heart block (without a pacemaker); history of bronchospasm and bronchial asthma; untreated pheochromocytoma; metabolic acidosis; bradycardia (HR < 60 bpm); hypotension (systolic BP < 90 mmHg); severe peripheral circulatory disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concomitant use with anesthetics. Untreated CHF, IHD.           },

            "content": "<b>Phenylpropanolamine</b>: Aggressiveness (particularly in childn), anxiety, confusion, insomnia/sleep disturbances, nervousness; agitation, dizziness, restlessness, severe headache, tremor; blurred vision; chest tightness, palpitation; HTN; nausea; irritability. <b>Paracetamol (in high doses)</b>: Changes in the number of WBC and platelets; allergic reactions; minor stomach and intestinal disturbances; rare cases of skin reactions."
          },

            "content": "1-2 tabs three times a day. Or as prescribed."
          },

            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Glaucoma, myasthenia gravis; prostatic hypertrophy or bladder neck obstruction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cardiac arrhythmias, tachycardia, cardiac decompensation, coronary insufficiency. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Pregnancy. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C for orphenadrine; Category B for paracetamol.",

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "As monotherapy or in combination with metformin or insulin for type 2 diabetes mellitus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Initial dose:</b> 1-2 mg once daily with breakfast or the 1st main meal. Max 2 mg. <b>Maintenance dose:</b> 1-4 mg once daily. After 2 mg dose, increments should not be >2 mg at 1-2 weeks intervals based on the patient’s glucose response. Max 8 mg once daily. May also be combined with metformin. <b>In combination with insulin:</b> 8 mg once daily with the 1st main meal; start with low-dose insulin and adjust weekly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Type 1 DM, diabetic ketoacidosis. Severe renal or hepatic insufficiency. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of CV mortality. Hypoglycemia especially in the elderly, debilitated or malnourished patients and those with adrenal or pituitary, liver, or kidney dysfunction.             "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of non-insulin-dependent (type 2) diabetes mellitus (DM), particularly in obese and juvenile diabetics when diet alone failed as monotherapy. Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with type 2 DM."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Usual dose: 500 mg once daily, may be increased in increments of 500 mg weekly up to max 2,000 mg once daily. A trial of 1,000 mg twice daily should be considered."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Renal or hepatic failure, alcoholism, NIDDM complicated by severe ketosis and acidosis. Diabetic precoma and coma. Patients undergoing surgery, after severe trauma or during infections, COPD, CHD, cardiac failure, PVD, hypocalcemia. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Elderly. Lactation.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, gastric pain, constipation, vomiting, metallic taste in the mouth. Rash, pruritus, urticaria, erythema and flushing. Headache, dizziness. Impaired GI absorption of vit B<sub>12</sub> and folic acid (long-term use)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenprocoumon, hyperglycemic agents e.g. thiazides, corticosteroids. Alcohol.             "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of traveler’s diarrhea, hepatic encephalopathy, small intestine bacterial overgrowth, irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), diverticular disease and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and children &ge;12 yrs - Traveler’s diarrhea</b>: 600 mg (one 200 mg tab every 8 hrs) to 800 mg (two 200 mg tabs every 12 hrs) per day for 3 days. <b>Hepatic encephalopathy</b>: 1,200 mg per day for 7-10 days. <b>Diverticular disease</b>: 800 mg per day (two 200 mg tabs every 12 hrs) for 7-10 days. In cases where repeated courses of treatment are required, cyclic treatments of 1 week per month are recommended."
          },
          {

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Infectious or traveler’s diarrhea complicated with fever and/or presence of blood in stool; intestinal obstruction. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."

          {

            "content": "Patients with impaired renal function and kidney dysfunction. May impair ability to operate machinery.",

          },

            "content": "Dizziness, headache, wind abdominal bloating, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, urgency to evacuate feces, nausea, involuntary and painful or ineffective straining, vomiting, fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 601,
        "brand_name": "Norplus",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Imidapril HCl, hydrochlorothiazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once daily. Individualize dosage according to patient response."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to imidapril and other ACE inhibitors, and HCTZ and other sulfonamide derivatives. Patients with history of ACE inhibitor-associated angioneurotic edema, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, renal failure, anuria. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM, renal impairment (GFR &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), hyperkalemia, and CHF with hypotension. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Childn. <b>Imidapril</b>: Patients with vol depletion, heart failure, IHD, cerebrovascular disease, renovascular HTN, unilateral or bilateral renal artery stenosis, renal impairment (CrCl 30-80 mL/min), psoriasis, left ventricular valvular and outflow tract obstruction, collagen vascular disease, risk factors for hyperkalemia, diabetes; who recently underwent kidney transplantation or are undergoing hemodialysis or major surgery. Use during anesthesia. Concomitant use with immunosuppressants, allopurinol, and procainamide. Increased risk of severe hypotension, renal impairment or failure, cholestatic jaundice progressing in fulminant hepatic necrosis and sometimes death, angioneurotic edema, neutropenia/agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, anemia, persistent nonproductive cough, and hyperkalemia may occur. Monitor renal function during therapy. <b>HCTZ</b>: Patients with brisk diuresis, liver cirrhosis, edema, renal or hepatic disease. Fluid and electrolyte imbalance, hypersensitivity reactions, exacerbation or activation of SLE; metabolic, endocrine, and CV effects; acute myopia, secondary angle-closure glaucoma, and increased risk of NMSC may occur. Monitor serum electrolytes regularly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood and lymphatic, metabolism and nutrition, psychiatric, nervous system, cardiac, vascular, respiratory, thoracic, mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, renal, and urinary disorders. Impotence, asthenia, fever, weakness. <b>Imidapril</b>: Viral infection, blurred vision, tinnitus, chest discomfort or pain, joint or peripheral edema, fatigue, malaise, numbness, limb pain, weariness. Increased blood amylase, BUN, plasma creatinine, serum potassium, liver enzymes, AST, ALT, ALP, LDH, gamma-GTP, serum bilirubin, CPK, eosinophil. Decreased albumin, serum protein, erythrocyte, thrombocyte, leukocyte, Hgb, Hct, platelets, WBC count. <b>HCTZ</b>: NMSC, hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, worsening of diabetes. Increased total cholesterol, LDL-C, VLDL-C, triglycerides."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs (e.g. COX-2 inhibitors, aspirin &gt;3 g/day), lithium, antidiabetics (e.g. insulin, hypoglycemic agents), other antihypertensives and vasodilators (e.g. nitroglycerin, nitrates). <b>Imidapril</b>: Non-potassium- and potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements and salt substitutes, aliskiren, TCAs, neuroleptics, rifampicin, antacids, sympathomimetics, sodium aurothiomalate, NEP inhibitors (e.g. sacubitril, racecadotril). <b>HCTZ</b>: Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, amantadine, aminoglycosides, anticholinergics (e.g. atropine, biperidine), diazoxide, antigout drugs (e.g. probenecid, sulfinpyrasone, allopurinol), calcium salts, vit D supplements, carbamazepine, digitalis, cholestyramine, ACTH, amphotericin B (parenteral), stimulant laxatives, glycyrrhizin, cyclophosphamide, methotrexate, ciclosporin, epinephrine, tubocurarine, SSRIs, topiramate, iodinated contrast media."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg/12.5 mg (P26.88)."
          }

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment of hypertension (HTN) and can be used as the sole agent to control BP. May be used in combination with thiazide diuretics, alpha-blockers, beta-adrenoreceptor-blocking agents, or an ACE inhibitor. Reduce risk of fatal coronary heart disease (CHD) and non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and stroke; coronary revascularization and the need for hospitalization due to angina in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). 1<sup>st</sup>-line for and myocardial ischemia, whether due to fixed obstruction (stable angina) and/or vasospasm/vasoconstriction (Prinzmetal’s or variant angina) of coronary vasculature; may be used alone or in combination with other anti-anginal drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b> - Adults: 2.5-10 mg once daily, depending on patient’s BP level; Childn 6-17 yrs: 2.5-5 mg once daily. <b>Angina</b>: Initial dose 5 mg once daily, may be increased to max of 10 mg. <b>CAD</b>: 5-10 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to dihydropyridines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for pulmonary edema in patients with NYHA Class III and IV heart failure of non-ischemic etiology. Patients with impaired hepatic function. Concomitant use of ciclosporin in renal transplant patients. Childn &lt;6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headaches, dizziness, somnolence, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, nausea, edema, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Simvastatin (with 20 mg daily doses of amlodipine). CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. diltiazem, clarithromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir). CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, <i>Hypericum perforatum</i>). Tacrolimus. mTOR inhibitors (e.g. sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 2.5 mg (P8.90), 5 mg (P19.96), 10 mg (P33.64)."
          }

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dCwkOlta0xvOtTwzxpq8wMEeLn9nJAG8ubqf6fJ7rpLBmDvDva.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Eq9SX928r69PIlR66dZm9KUSUb74QDVPBMb83ntZmXHD8xwk8K.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ny3b04pxhY5Rl0gBMqJPAyLrshBAHkqhRVfvXQhH1nKoK9JRma.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Amlodipine besilate, atorvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "1<sup>st</sup> line treatment of hypertension (HTN) and can be used as sole agent to control BP in the majority of patients. Reduce risk of coronary revascularization procedures and need for hospitalization due to angina in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment of myocardial ischemia, whether due to fixed obstruction (stable angina) and/or vasospasm/vasoconstriction (Prinzmetal’s or variant angina) of coronary vasculature; may be used alone or in combination with other anti-anginal drugs for angina refractory to nitrates and/or adequate doses of beta-blockers. As adjunct to diet for treatment of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and nonfamilial hypercholesterolemia), combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson Types IIa and IIb), elevated triglyceride levels (Fredrickson Type IV), and in patients with dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson Type III) who do not respond adequately to diet."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "5 mg/10 mg to a max of 10 mg/20 mg once daily. Starting and maintenance dose should be individualized in the treatment of HTN/angina and dyslipidemia. Doses may be taken at any time of day with or without food. <b>Concomitant administration of atorvastatin with cyclosporine, telaprevir, tipranavir/ritonavir, or glecaprevir/pibrentasvir</b>: Atorvastatin should not exceed 10 mg. <b>Childn 6-17 yrs – HTN</b>: Amlodipine 2.5-5 mg once daily. <b>Childn &ge;10 yrs – Severe dyslipidemias</b>: Atorvastatin 10 mg/day, may be increased to 80 mg based on response and tolerability."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to dihydropyridines, amlodipine, atorvastatin or any ingredient in the product. Patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases &gt;3x ULN. Women of childbearing potential who are not using adequate contraceptive measures. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concomitant administration of atorvastatin with letermovir and cycloporin. Risk for pulmonary edema in patients with NYHA class III-IV heart failure, serum transaminases elevations of &gt;3x ULN. Liver function tests should be performed before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Patients who consume substantial quantities of alcohol and/or have history of liver disease. Patients with risk factor predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis Risk for myopathy; hemorrhagic stroke in patients who had stroke or TIA in past 6 months; increased HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Concurrent administration of cyclosporine, fibric acid derivatives, erythromycin, niacin, azole antifungals, colchicine, telaprevir, boceprevir or the combination of tipranavir/ritonavir. Temporary suspend atorvastatin during fusidic acid therapy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea. <b>Amlodipine</b>: Headaches, dizziness, somnolence, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, edema, fatigue. <b>Atorvastatin</b>: Nasopharyngitis, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, arthralgia, pain in extremities, musculoskeletal pain/spasms, joint swelling."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Amlodipine</b>: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir), clarithromycin, CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, <i>Hypercicum perforatum</i>), mTOR inhibitors (e.g. sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus), tacrolimus. <b>Atorvastatin</b>: Fibric acid derivatives, lipid-modifying doses of niacin, CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. erythromycin, clarithromycin, azole antifungals) and inducers (e.g. efavirenz, rifampin), OATP1B1 inhibitors (e.g., cyclosporine), protease inhibitors, glecaprevir, pibrentasvir, letermovir, elbasvir, grazoprevir, diltiazem, itraconazole, grapefruit juice, antacids containing magnesium and aluminum hydroxides, colestipol, digoxin, oral contraceptives containing norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol, fusidic acid, colchicine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 5 mg/10 mg (P22.54), 5 mg/20 mg (P29.26), 10 mg/10 mg (P34.98), 10 mg/20 mg (P40.78)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 699,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 699,
        "brand_name": "NovoSeven RT",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Eptacog alfa (activated)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hemostatics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of bleeding episodes and peri-op management in adults and childn with hemophilia A or B with inhibitors, congenital Factor VII (FVII) deficiency, and Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia with refractoriness to platelet transfusions, with or without antibodies to platelets. Treatment of bleeding episodes and peri-op management in adults with acquired hemophilia. Treatment of severe postpartum hemorrhage when uterotonics are insufficient to achieve hemostasis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Congenital hemophilia A or B with inhibitors - Acute bleeding episodes</b> - Hemostatic: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs, adjust until hemostasis is achieved; Post-hemostatic: 90 mcg/kg every 3-6 hrs for severe bleeds until hemostasis is achieved. <b>Peri-op management</b> - Minor surgery - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the surgery.  Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs for 48 hrs then every 2-6 hrs until healing occurs. Major surgery - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the surgery, additional bolus doses can be given. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2 hrs for 5 days then every 4 hrs or by continuous infusion at 50 mcg/ kg/hr until healing occurs. <b>Acquired Hemophilia - Acute bleeding episodes</b>: 70-90 mcg/kg every 2-3 hrs until hemostasis is achieved. <b>Peri-op management</b>: 70-90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2-3 hrs for the duration of the surgery and until hemostasis is achieved. <b>Congenital Factor VII Deficiency - Acute bleeding episodes</b>: 15-30 mcg/kg every 4-6 hours until hemostasis is achieved. <b>Peri-op management</b>: 15-30 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 4-6 hrs for the duration of the surgery and until hemostasis is achieved. <b>Glanzmann’s thrombasthenia - Acute bleeding episodes</b>: 90 mcg/kg every 2-6 hrs until hemostasis is achieved. Severe postpartum hemorrhage: 60-90 mcg/kg BW IV bolus; in case of insufficient hemostatic response, 2<sup>nd</sup> dose can be administered after 30 mins. <b>Peri-op management</b> - Initial: 90 mcg/kg immediately before surgery and repeat every 2 hrs for the duration of the procedure. Post-surgical: 90 mcg/kg every 2-6 hrs to prevent post-op bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May cause serious arterial and venous thrombotic events. Monitor signs or symptoms of activation of coagulation system or thrombosis. Patients with known hypersensitivity to mouse, hamster, or bovine proteins; with congenital hemophilia receiving concomitant treatment with aPCCs; older patients with acquired hemophilia and receiving other hemostatic agents; with a history of cardiac, vascular disease or predisposed to thrombotic events.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thrombotic events e.g. VTE, DVT; anaphylactic shock, rash, pruritus, urticaria; pyrexia, headache, nausea, dyspnea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Prothrombin complex concentrates (activated or not). Antifibrinolytics; rFXIII."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder and solvent for solution for injection (powder vial + solvent vial) 1 mg."
          }
        ],

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Enoxaparin sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), ischemic complications of unstable angina, and non-Q-wave myocardial infarction (MI). Treatment of acute DVT and acute ST-segment elevation MI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Abdominal surgery:</b> 40 mg SC once/day with the initial dose given 2 hrs prior to surgery. Duration of administration: 7-10 days, up to 12 days. <b>Hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> 30 mg SC every 12 hrs with the initial dose given 12-24 hrs after surgery. Hip replacement surgery: 40 mg SC once a day given initially 12 hrs prior to surgery. The initial phase of thromboprophylaxis in hip replacement surgery patients, continued prophylaxis with 40 mg once a day for 3 weeks. Duration of administration: 7-10 days up to 14 days. <b>Patients at risk of thromboembolic complications due to severely restricted mobility during acute illness:</b> 40 mg SC once a day. Duration of administration: 6-11 days, up to 14 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active major bleeding, thrombocytopenia associated with positive in vitro test for anti-platelet antibody."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not administer by IM injection. Do not mix with other injections for infusion. Patients with bleeding diathesis, uncontrolled arterial HTN or history of recent GI ulceration, diabetic retinopathy, and increased risk of hemorrhage. History of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Major hemorrhages e.g. retroperitoneal and intracranial bleeding. Low-weight patients (< 57 kg). Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hemorrhage; mild to moderate thrombocytopenia; mild local irritation, pain, hematoma, ecchymosis, and erythema. Non-hemorrhagic, primarily injection site ecchymoses and hematomas."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, platelet inhibitors i.e. aspirin, salicylates, NSAIDs (e.g. ketorolac, tromethamine), dipyridamole, or sulfinpyrazone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) 4,000 IU (equiv to 40 mg)/0.4 mL in 1 mL pre-filled syringe, 6,000 IU (equiv to 60 mg)/0.6 mL in 1 mL pre-filled syringe."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Doxorubicin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anthracycline Antibiotics in Chemotherapy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of ovarian cancer which has progressed or recurred after platinum-based chemotherapy; AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma after failure of, or intolerance to, prior systemic chemotherapy; multiple myeloma in combination with bortezomib for patients who have previously been treated with bortezomib and have received at least one prior therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Ovarian cancer</b>: 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 60 mins every 28 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. <b>AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma</b>: 20 mg/ m<sup>2</sup> IV over 60 mins every 21 days until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. <b>Multiple myeloma</b>: 30 mg/ m<sup>2</sup> IV over 60 mins on day 4 of each 21-day cycle for 8 cycles or until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester)."
          },

            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the relief and prophylaxis of reversible bronchospasm associated with bronchial asthma, bronchitis, emphysema and related conditions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 250 mg; may be gradually increased or decreased by half if therapeutic effect is not achieved or if side effects occur. <b>Childn &gt;25 kg BW</b>: 250 mg; <b>12-25 kg BW (2-7 yrs)</b>: 125 mg. All doses are to be taken every 12 hrs. Swallow tab whole; should not be crushed or chewed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant therapy with other xanthine medications. Acute asthma requiring prompt treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor theophylline plasma levels in individual patients. Concomitant therapy with sympathomimetic agents. Patients with reduced thyroid function, CHF, acute pulmonary edema, COPD, severe hypoxia, pneumonia, acute febrile episodes, acute viral infection; impaired liver function e.g. hepatic cirrhosis; cardiac arrhythmias, CAD, unstable angina, cardiomyopathy, severe hypertension; peptic ulcer, GERD. Elderly. Childn &lt;2 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Gastric irritation, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, epigastric pain, reactivation of peptic ulcer, GERD, hematemesis, tachycardia, palpitation, headache, CNS stimulation, reflex hyperexcitability, insomnia, tremor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Tobacco or marijuana smoking, xanthine-containing beverages, cimetidine, high-dose allopurinol, propranolol, macrolides (e.g. erythromycin, clarithromycin), quinolones (e.g. ciprofloxacin, enoxacin), alcohol, oral contraceptives, mexilitene, tacrine, thiabendazole, disulfiram, Interferon-alpha, verapamil, phenobarbitone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, St. John’s wort, halothane, ketamine, lithium, adrenaline and other sympathomimetic amines, beta-adrenergic agonists, ranitidine, diltiazem, nifedipine, isoniazid, furosemide, influenza vaccine, corticosteroids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sustained-release tablet 125 mg (P22.84)."

  {
    "id": 1999,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1999,
        "brand_name": "Oestrogel",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4x80VuFpcVVzBlcI8eDT4T9skdVhTCpD3GiQFlvqB5lkipbjlh.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/BjGmPOUyMW4Sp8mDlrVUa1qIBLaCng8wrvXXhEfa1JCgeJZvGp.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YU1epOguIQtSKs27LtQbUc7k3TSXsr4Cg2XTGaHfaxJdAeN2aS.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Estradiol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for estrogen deficiency symptoms in post-menopausal women. Prevention of osteoporosis in post-menopausal women at high risk of future fractures who are intolerant of or contraindicated for other medications approved for the prevention of osteoporosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initiate therapy at once in women who are not currently taking HRT. For women currently taking HRT, initiate therapy after completion of current HRT. In women with intact uterus the recommended dose of a\nprogestogen should be administered for at least 12 days of each month together with Oestrogel.<b>Menopausal symptoms:</b> Initially 2.5 g gel once daily, may be increased to max 5 g after one month if relief is not obtained. <b>Prevention of osteoporosis:</b> 2.5 g once daily. Apply gel to clean, dry, intact areas of skin (e.g. abdomen, arms, shoulders, inner thighs) in the morning or evening. Area of application should be as large as possible. Allow gel to dry for 2 mins before covering with clothing."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with known, past, or suspected breast cancer; known or suspected estrogen-dependent malignant tumors (e.g. endometrial cancer); undiagnosed genital bleeding; untreated endometrial hyperplasia; previous idiopathic or current VTE (e.g. DVT, pulmonary embolism); active or recent arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g. angina, MI, stroke); acute or history of liver disease as long as LFTs have failed to return to normal; porphyria. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Must not be applied to the breasts or mucous surfaces (e.g. vulval region). Patients with existing or history of leiomyoma (uterine fibroids), endometriosis; risk factors for thromboembolic disorders or estrogen-dependent tumors (e.g. 1<sup>st</sup>-degree heredity for breast cancer); HTN; liver disorder (e.g. liver adenoma); DM with or without vascular involvement; cholelithiasis; migraine or severe headache; SLE; history of endometrial hyperplasia; epilepsy; asthma; otosclerosis. Increased risk of CV morbidity in the 1<sup>st</sup> yr of use, VTE and pulmonary embolism; breast, endometrial (e.g. endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma), and ovarian cancer; abnormal vaginal bleeding; growth, pain, or tenderness of pre-existing uterine leiomyoma; photosensitivity/photoallergy. Concomitant use with sunscreen, CYP3A4 inducers or inhibitors. May aggravate symptoms and physical findings associated with previous endometriosis; consider the addition of progestin in patients with residual endometriosis post-hysterectomy. Initiate treatment only if post-menopausal symptoms adversely affect quality of life. Periodic check-ups are recommended of a frequency and nature adapted to the individual woman. Discontinue treatment if jaundice or deterioration of liver function, significant increase in BP, or new onset of severe migraine-type headache develops.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin irritation, redness, mild and transient erythema; headache, migraine, mood changes; nausea; growth of uterine fibromyomata, excessive production of cervical mucus; pain, enlargement, or secretion of breast; CHD; ischemic stroke; VTE; pulmonary embolus; breast, endometrial, or ovarian cancer; dementia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Transdermal estrogens might be less affected than oral hormones by enzyme inducers. CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. St. John’s Wort preparations, phenobarbital, carbamazepine, efavirenz, rifampicin) or inhibitors (e.g. erythromycin, clarithromycin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, grapefruit juice)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Transdermal gel 600 mcg/g x 80 g (P906.50)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WDMTwmEHIdFnAqtRbWACZAv5THuZwGzOYL5auMqqWcR9w820NV.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Nintedanib esilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Protein Kinase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with docetaxel for treatment of adults with locally advanced, metastatic or recurrent non small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) of adenocarcinoma tumor histology after failure of 1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy.  Treatment of adults with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), other chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) with a progressive phenotype, systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses taken 2x daily. <b>NSCLC:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs on days 2-21 of a standard 21-day docetaxel treatment cycle. Max 400 mg daily. <b>IPF, other chronic fibrosing ILDs with progressive phenotype and SSc-ILD:</b> 150 mg every 12 hrs. Max 300 mg daily; <b>Mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A):</b> 100  mg every 12 hrs. See product insert for dose adjustments for adverse reactions. Taken with food or teaspoonful of cold or room temperature soft food. Swallowed whole; do not crush or chew."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to nintedanib, peanut or soya. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30mL/min); females, asians, age, low BW; risk of bleeding; higher CV risk; history of abdominal surgery, hollow organ perforation, peptic ulceration, or diverticular disease, concomitant corticosteroids or NSAIDs. May induce neutropenia and sepsis in combination with docetaxel; arterial or venous thromboembolic events; GI perforations; nephrotic syndrome; posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. May impair wound healing. Not recommended for patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment; recent pulmonary bleeding (>2.5 mL of RBC)  and centrally located tumors with radiographic evidence of local invasion of major blood vessels or of cavitary or necrotic tumors; active brain metastasis. Discontinue in persistent severe diarrhea despite symptomatic treatment, nausea and vomiting; liver changes and injury; life-threatening VTE. In combination with docetaxel, monitor CBC at beginning of each cycle, during, and after therapy;  transaminase, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin levels. Assess liver function tests prior initiation of therapy, regularly during 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months and periodically. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents. Women of childbearing potential.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, increased liver enzyme values, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, decreased weight and  appetite."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "P-gp inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, erythromycin) and inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine,  phenytoin, St. John's wort)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P1,244.05), 150 mg (P1,857.89)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3568,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3568,
        "brand_name": "Olandus ODT",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/i73BSyT4Nw3aslKIIkHhza6olu3RgB08FxQ9ycTOehM2oKPxB1.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/i73BSyT4Nw3aslKIIkHhza6olu3RgB08FxQ9ycTOehM2oKPxB1.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mQjYAV5o9lt7R8Z1vBsmbIkKqNt8qXPVHvSQ8NEavDNrBRKr9E.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Olanzapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment and management of schizophrenia. <b>5 mg or 10 mg</b>: Treatment of moderate to severe mania associated with bipolar disorder. <b>15 mg</b>: Short-term treatment of acute manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder. Prevention of recurrence in patients with bipolar disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>5 mg or 10 mg – Schizophrenia – Adults</b>: Initially 5-10 mg once a day with target dose of 10 mg/day within several days. Debilitated patients predispose to hypotensive reactions, non-smoking female &ge;65 yrs: Initially 5 mg; <b>Adolescents</b>: Initially 2.5-5 mg once a day with target dose of 10 mg/day. Dose increments/decrements of 2.5 or 5 mg daily when adjustments are necessary. <b>Bipolar I disorders (manic or mixed episodes) – Adults</b>: Initially 10 or 15 mg once a day, maintenance of 5-20 mg/day. Dosage adjustments occur at intervals of not &lt;24 hrs. If in combination with lithium or valproate, initially 10 mg once a day. Adolescents: Initially 2.5-5 mg once a day with target dose of 10 mg/day. Dosage adjustments occur at intervals of not &lt;24 hrs. Max: 20 mg/day. <b>15 mg – Schizophrenia and related disorders</b>: Initially 5-10 mg/day, may be adjusted on the basis of clinical status within the range 5-20 mg daily. <b>Acute mania associated with bipolar disorder</b>: Initially 10-15 mg once a day as monotherapy or 10 mg once daily in combination therapy with lithium or valproate. Dosage adjustments occur at intervals of not &lt;24 hrs. Dose increments/decrements of 5 mg daily when adjustments are necessary. Max: 20 mg/day. <b>Preventing recurrence in bipolar disorder</b>: Initially 10 mg once a day, may be adjusted on the basis clinical status within a range 5-20 mg/day. <b>Elderly &ge;65 yrs</b>: Initially 5 mg/day. Tabs should be placed in the mouth and allowed to completely dissolve before swallowing the saliva, may be followed with water. Alternatively, may be dispersed in a full glass of water immediately before administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of overdose or suicide attempt. Not for treatment of dementia-related psychosis and/or behavioral disturbances, dopamine agonist associated psychosis in patients with Parkinson’s disease. Patients with prostatic hypertrophy, narrow-angle glaucoma, paralytic ileus and related conditions, elevated ALT and/or AST, hepatic impairment, pre-existing conditions associated with limited hepatic functional reserve, low leukocyte and/or neutrophil counts, history of drug-induced bone marrow depression/toxicity, bone marrow depression caused by concomitant illness, radiation therapy or chemotherapy, hypereosinophilic conditions or myeloproliferative disease, history of seizures, factors which may lower seizure threshold. May induce hyperglycemia, undesirable lipid alterations, weight gain, NMS, postural hypotension in elderly, sudden cardiac death, disruption of body temp regulation, esophageal dysmotility and aspiration, tardive dyskinesia, hyperprolactinemia. Concomitant use with hepatotoxic drugs. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Weight gain, constipation, dry mouth, dizziness. <b>5 mg or 10 mg</b>: Drowsiness, restlessness, unusual behavior, depression, difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep, weakness, difficulty walking, pain in arms, legs, back or joints, breast enlargement or discharge, late or missed menstrual periods, decreased sexual ability. <b>15 mg</b>: Somnolence, increased prolactin, total cholesterol, triglycerides, glucose; orthostatic hypotension, increased appetite, peripheral edema, increased ALT, AST, eosinophilia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Centrally acting drugs, alcohol (e.g. ethanol), dopamine agonists, charcoal, fluoxetine, carbamazepine, fluvoxamine. <b>5 mg or 10 mg</b>: Diazepam, omeprazole and rifampin, antihypertensive agents, levodopa."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Orodispersible tablet 5 mg (P52.00), 10 mg (P52.00). Orally disintegrating tablet 15 mg (P133.93)."
          }
        ],
