          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pzDd20c9EDfLyFJbUt3rHePOByVTDSSJda6Nei2CWbrVXOaWIA.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/osZEmlPQAMNSqbnRRPJru3qcpNKTv9CzVKIHbaZZdNNu40ACsV.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4sZnAlb2NqucUSBazvGOXeskAoXXy7VH7QsWwg0tATHyjFUaiU.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Baricitinib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Disease-Modifying Anti-Rheumatic Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of moderate to severe active rheumatoid arthritis in adults who have responded inadequately to, or who are intolerant to &ge;1 DMARDs, as monotherapy or in combination with methotrexate; moderate to severe atopic dermatitis in adults; severe alopecia areata in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 4 mg once daily. May be tapered to 2 mg once daily if sustained control of disease activity is achieved and is eligible for dose tapering. <b>Elderly &ge;75 yrs, patients with history of chronic or recurrent infections, co-administration with OAT3 inhibitors, renal impairment (CrCl 30-60 mL/min):</b> 2 mg once daily. Take with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active TB. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic and renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min); live, attenuated vaccines during or immediately prior to therapy; combination with biologic DMARDs, biologic immunomodulators, or other Janus kinase inhibitors; ciclosporin or other potent immunosuppressants (atopic dermatitis and alopecia areata). Patients with active, chronic or recurrent infections. Diverticulitis and GI perforations, risk of malignancies. Consider anti-TB therapy prior to initiation of treatment in patients with previously untreated latent TB. Do not initiate or temporarily interrupt in patients with absolute neutrophil count < 1 x 10<sup>9</sup> cells/L, absolute lymphocyte count <0.5 x 10<sup>9</sup> cells/L, or Hgb < 8 g/dL; herpes zoster; increased in ALT or AST and suspected drug-induced liver injury; DVT/PE. Screen for viral hepatitis prior to initiation of treatment. Assess lipid parameters approx 12 weeks following initiation of therapy and thereafter. Elderly. Childn and adolescents &le;18 yrs. Use effective contraception during and &ge;1 week after therapy in women.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, hypercholesterolemia, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, gastroenteritis, UTI, pneumonia, folliculitis, thrombocytosis( >600 x 10<sup>9</sup> cells/L), headache, nausea, abdominal pain, increased ALT (&ge;3 x ULN), rash, acne, increased creatine phosphokinase (>5 x ULN)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Azathioprine, tacrolimus, ciclosporin, probenecid, leflunomide, teriflunomide. Ibuprofen, diclofenac."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2 mg, 4 mg."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Conditions where inhibition of gastric acid secretion may be beneficial including aspiration syndromes, dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease and the Zollinger-Ellison syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acid-related dyspepsia</b>: 10-20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>GERD</b>: 20 mg daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>Peptic ulcer</b>: 20 mg daily, or 40 mg in severe cases, 4 weeks for duodenal ulcer, and 8 weeks for gastric ulcer. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 60 mg daily, or 20-120 mg daily, up to 120 mg three times daily. <b>Acid aspiration</b>: 40 mg at night before surgery, further 40 mg up to 6 hrs pre-op."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, skin rash, pruritus, urticaria, headache, paresthesia, dizziness, light-headedness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Atazanavir, cilostazol, diazepam, phenytoin, anticoagulants, disulfiram, cyclosporine, ampicillin, azole antifungals, iron supplements, other drugs metabolized by CYP450 and drugs which absorption is pH-dependent."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 20 mg (P32.29)."
          }

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Omeprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Cap – 20 mg</b>: Short-term treatment and symptomatic relief of heartburn that occurs &ge;2 days/week. <b>40 mg</b>: Short-term and maintenance treatment of duodenal and gastric ulcers, pathological hypersecretory conditions (e.g. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, multiple endocrine adenomas, systemic mastocytosis), gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and associated symptoms, NSAID-associated gastric and duodenal ulcers or erosions, acid-related dyspepsia, erosive esophagitis, <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> eradication in peptic ulcer disease (PUD). Prophylaxis of acid aspiration during general anesthesia. <b>IV</b>: Short-term treatment of duodenal and gastric ulcers, ulcerative esophagitis, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, GERD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap – Adults</b>: 20 mg once a day 30 mins-1 hr before breakfast for 14 days. <b>Duodenal ulcer</b>: 20 mg once daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>Gastric ulcer</b>: 40 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>Pathological hypersecretory conditions</b>: Initially 60 mg once daily. May be administered up to 120 mg 3 times daily. GERD and other symptoms associated with the disease, <b>NSAID-associated gastric and duodenal ulcers or erosions</b>: 20 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks. Additional 4 weeks for patients who have not healed after 4-week treatment. <b>Acid-related dyspepsia</b>: 10-20 mg once daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>Erosive esophagitis</b>: 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>Prophylaxis of acid aspiration</b>: 40 mg on the evening before surgery, followed by 40 mg 2-6 hrs pre-op. <b><i>H. pylori</i> eradication in PUD</b> - Dual therapy: 40 mg once daily in the morning + clarithromycin for 14 days. Triple therapy: 40 mg once daily + amoxicillin + metronidazole for 7 days. Or, 20 mg twice daily (morning and evening) + clarithromycin + amoxicillin for 10 days. Or, 20 mg twice daily + clarithromycin + metronidazole (or tinidazole) for 7 days. <b>Childn 1-16 yrs - GERD and other acid-related disorders (erosive esophagitis) - BW &ge;20 kg</b>: 20 mg; 10-&lt;20 kg: 10 mg; 5-&lt;10 kg: 5 mg. Patients with hepatic impairment, elderly: Daily dose to not exceed 20 mg. Caps may be opened and contents swallowed directly or mixed with a slightly acidic fluid (e.g. fruit juice, yogurt, non-carbonated water). <b>IV</b>: 40 mg once daily by slow IV injection (not &lt;2.5 mins) at a rate of not &gt;4 mL/min."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Cap</b>: Trouble or pain in swallowing food, vomiting with blood, or bloody or black stools. Not for the immediate relief of heartburn symptoms or prevention of occasional heartburn due to consumption of certain food or drinks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Gastric malignancy should be excluded prior to treatment. Hepatic impairment. Asian. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C. <b>20 mg cap</b>: Heartburn for &gt;3 months or with lightheadedness, sweating or dizziness. Chest or shoulder pain with lightheadedness, shortness of breath, sweating, or pain spreading to the arms, neck, or shoulders. Frequent chest pain and wheezing related to heartburn. <b>40 mg cap/IV</b>: Risk of atrophic gastritis, CAP.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nervous system, GI, musculoskeletal, dermatologic and sensitivity, genitourinary tract, hepatic, respiratory, CV hematologic, ocular effects. Fever, tinnitus, weight gain, acute gout, hypophosphatemia, hypocalcemia, fluid overload, hyperglycemia, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia, sweating, hyponatremia, otitis media. Edema, gynecomastia, oral candidiasis, candidal infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin or other vit K antagonists, phenytoin, diazepam, digoxin, saquinavir, tacrolimus, cilostazol. Ampicillin, iron salts, dasatinib, ketoconazole, itraconazole. Voriconazole, rifampicin, St. John’s wort, atazanavir, nelfinavir. Clopidogrel, ciclosporin, disulfiram, benzodiazepine, clarithromycin, cyanocobalamin, tacrolimus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 20 mg (P41.32). Delayed-release capsule 40 mg (Rx) (P61.35). Powder for injection (IV) 40 mg (Rx) (P657.14)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ovq0gVn4sxiCD1tvvCwk9DGbmUxvRIVWTgwyqc749v8Wo22W6x.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/PodvKfUjJt6al2twFME4QwClyJVVYXwmZUnPm81ECvzwAixpmT.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/r2MTuoacfiaz4hZeumrNu1SBokzriMuVutuj4yZoCX61lRV358.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ondansetron",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiemetic/Antivertigo"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of nausea and vomiting induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Prevention and treatment of post-op nausea and vomiting (PONV). Management of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) in childn &ge;6 months, and for the prevention and treatment of PONV in childn &ge;1 month."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Chemotherapy and radiotherapy induced nausea and vomiting (CINV and RINV) - Adults - Emotogenic chemotherapy and radiotherapy:</b> 8 mg administered as a slow IV inj (in not &lt;30 secs) or IM inj, immediately before treatment, followed by 8 mg orally every 12 hrs. <b>Highly emetogenic chemotherapy:</b> A single dose of 8 mg by slow IV inj (in not &lt;30 secs) or IM inj immediately before chemotherapy, then followed by 2 further IV inj or IM doses of 8 mg, 4 hrs apart, or by a constant infusion of 1 mg/hr for up to 24 hrs. Max initial IV dose of 16 mg diluted in 50-100 mL of saline or other compatible infusion fluid and infused over &lt;15 mins immediately before chemotherapy. May be enhanced by addition of single IV dose of dexamethasone sodium phosphate, 20 mg administered prior to chemotherapy. <b>Childn &ge;6 months and adolescents - CINV:</b> Given by IV infusion diluted in 25-50 mL of saline or other compatible infusion fluid and infused over < 15 mins. Should be diluted in 5% dextrose or 0.9% NaCl. . <b>Dosing by BSA:</b> &le;0.6 m<sup>2</sup>: 5 mg/m<sup>2</sup> + 2 mg syr every 12 hrs on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 2 mg syr every 12 hrs on 2<sup>nd</sup>-6<sup>th</sup> day; 0.6 m<sup>2</sup> to 1.2 m<sup>2</sup>: 5 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV + 4 mg syr or tab after 12 hrs on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 4 mg syr or tab every 12 hrs on 2<sup>nd</sup>-6<sup>th</sup> day; &gt;1.2 m<sup>2</sup>: 5 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV + 8 mg syr or tab after 12 hrs on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 8 mg syr or tab every 12 hrs. The IV dose must not exceed 8 mg. Total dose over 24 hrs (given as divided dose) must not exceed 32 mg. <b>Dosing by BW:</b> &le;10 kg: Up to 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg IV every 4 hrs on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 2 mg syr every 12 hrs on 2<sup>nd</sup>-6<sup>th</sup> day; &gt;10 kg: Up to 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg IV every 4 hrs on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 4 mg syr or tab every 12 hrs on 2<sup>nd</sup>-6<sup>th</sup> day. The IV dose must not exceed 8 mg. Total dose over 24 hrs (given as divided dose) must not exceed 32 mg. <b>Post-operative nausea and vomiting - Adults:</b> May be administered as a single dose of 4 mg given by IM or slow IV inj at induction of anesthesia. <b>Childn &ge;1 month and adolescents:</b> For prevention and treatment after surgery, a single dose may be administered by slow IV (not < 30 secs) at dose 0.1 mg/kg up to max of 4 mg either prior to, at or after induction of anesthesia. <b>Patients with hepatic impairment:</b> Max dose of 8 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with apomorphine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to other selective 5HT<sub>3</sub>  receptor antagonists. Patients with congenital long QT syndrome, who have or may develop prolongation of QT, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, bradyarrhythmias, are taking medicinal products that lead QT prolongation or electrolyte abnormalities, with sub-acute intestinal obstruction, with adenotonsillar surgery prevention of nausea and vomiting. Concomitant use with serotonergic drugs. Childn receiving ondansetron with hepatotoxic chemotherapeutic agents. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, constipation, sensation of warmth or flushing, local IV injection site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, tramadol, apomorphine, SSRIs, SNRIs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IM/IV) 2 mg/mL x 2 mL, 4 mL."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1619,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1619,
        "brand_name": "Onzet",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ondansetron HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiemetic/Antivertigo"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of nausea and vomiting induced by cytotoxic chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Prevention and treatment of post-op nausea and vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 8 mg given up to 2 hrs before treatment, followed by 8 mg 12 hrs later, then 8 mg twice daily for up to 5 days after the end of chemotherapy to protect against delayed emesis. Prevention and treatment of post-op nausea and vomiting: 16 mg 1 hr before anesthesia or 8 mg 1 hr before anesthesia, followed by 2 further doses of 8 mg at 8-hr intervals. <b>Childn 4-11 yrs:</b> 4 mg given 30 mins before chemotherapy, with subsequent 4 mg doses given 4 and 8 hrs thereafter. May give 4 mg thrice daily for 1-2 days after the end of chemotherapy. <b>Renal or hepatic impairment:</b> Max 8 mg. <b>IV/IM</b> - <b>Prevention of nausea and vomiting associated with emetogenic chemotherapy</b> - Adults and childn 6 months-18 yrs: Dilute in 50 mL of 5% dextrose or 0.9% sodium chloride before administration. 3 doses of 0.15 mg/kg infused over 15 mins beginning 30 mins before the start of chemotherapy for the 1<sup>st</sup> dose, then administer subsequent doses 4 and 8 hrs after the 1<sup>st</sup> dose. Alternatively for adults, 32 mg IV single dose infused over 15 mins beginning 30 mins before the start of chemotherapy. <b>Prevention of post-op nausea and vomiting</b> - Adults: 2 mg IV or 4 mg IM as single dose. Childn 1 month-12 yrs (weighing &gt;40 kg): 4 mg as single dose; &le;40 kg: 0.1 mg/kg as single dose. Administer IV doses in not &lt;30 secs, preferably over 2-5 mins, immediately before induction of anesthesia or post-op if patients did not receive prophylactic antiemetics and experiences nausea and vomiting after surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of apomorphine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe hepatic impairment. Patients with signs of subacute intestinal obstruction or ileus. Concomitant use of drugs that prolong QT interval or cause electrolyte abnormalities. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>IM/IV:</b> May mask a progressive ileus and gastric distention.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, sensation of warmth or flushing, hiccups, constipation, dizziness, and blurred vision."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cardiotoxic drugs, antibiotics, antifungal, antiarrhythmics, beta-blockers, serotonergic drugs, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin. <b>Incompatibilities:</b> Alkaline solns."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 8 mg (P243.87). Solution for injection (IM/IV) 2 mg/mL x 4 mL (P596.40)."
          }
        ],

        "id": 1781,
        "brand_name": "Operol",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/CK1UevhOJWCZSITF6UtTShlTmxtjrJolAp1Itn2PNa4oCqBlhf.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/CK1UevhOJWCZSITF6UtTShlTmxtjrJolAp1Itn2PNa4oCqBlhf.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yAAKNeZ2zoqWT6RPY0mfFGo5qClNd9yjLxWE5lAevicOHo3uot.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Propofol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Parenteral Anesthetics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "General anesthesia, monitored anesthesia care, ICU sedation in intubated and mechanically ventilated patient."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>General anesthesia induction - Adults &lt;55 yrs</b>: 40 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (2-2.5 mg/kg). <b>Elderly, debilitated or ASA-PS III or IV patients</b>: 20 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (1-1.5 mg/kg). <b>Cardiac anesthesia</b>: 20 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (0.5-1.5 mg/kg). <b>Neurosurgical patients</b>: 20 mg every 10 secs until induction onset (1-2 mg/kg). <b>Childn 3-16 yrs</b>: 2.5-3.5 mg/kg administered over 20-30 secs. <b>General anesthesia maintenance: Infusion - Adults &lt;55 yrs and neurosurgical patients</b>: 100-200 mcg/kg/min. <b>Elderly, debilitated, ASA-PS III or IV patients</b>: 50-100 mcg/kg/min. <b>Cardiac anesthesia</b>: 100-150 mcg/kg/min (with secondary opioid), 50-100 mcg/kg/min (with primary opioid). <b>Childn 2 months-16 yrs</b>: 125-300 mcg/kg/min. <b>Intermittent bolus - Adults &lt;55 yrs</b>: Increments of 20-50 mg, as needed. <b>Monitored anesthesia care (MAC) sedation initiation - Adults &lt;55 yrs</b>: Slow infusion of 100-150 mcg/kg/min for 3-5 mins or slow injection of 0.5 mg/kg for 3-5 mins followed immediately by a maintenance infusion. <b>Elderly, debilitated, neurosurgical, ASA-PS III or IV patients</b>: Same with adult dose. Avoid rapid boluses. <b>MAC sedation maintenance - Adults &lt;55 yrs</b>: Infusion of 25-75 mcg/kg/min or incremental bolus doses of 10 mg or 20 mg. <b>Elderly, debilitated, neurosurgical, ASA-PS III or IV patients</b>: Same with adult dose. Avoid rapid bolus. <b>Initiation and maintenance of ICU sedation in intubated, mechanically ventilated – Adults</b>: Initial infusion of 5 mcg/kg/min for at least 5 mins. Subsequent increments 5-10 mcg/kg/min for 5-10 mins. Maintenance 5-50 mcg/kg/min or higher may be required. Clinical effect evaluation and CNS function assessment should be carried out daily throughout the maintenance to determine minimum dose required for sedation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to propofol and its component, egg and soy products. Epilepsy, seizure. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor patient for signs of hypertension and/or bradycardia. Lipid metabolism disorder (e.g. primary hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipemia, pancreatitis). Epileptic patient.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nodal tachycardia, hypotension, decreased cardiac output, agitation, apnea, rash, hypersalivation, diplopia, ear and eye pain, nystagmus, taste perversion, tinnitus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Narcotics, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, chloral hydrate, droperidol, nitrous oxide, opioids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Emulsion for injection 10 mg/mL x 20 mL (P500.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Bisphosphonates"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of skeletal-related events (pathological features, spinal compression, radiation or surgery to bone, or tumor-induced hypercalcemia) in adults with advanced malignancies involving bone. Treatment of tumor-induced hypercalcemia in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered as IV infusion only. <b>Prevention of skeletal-related events in adults with advanced malignancies involving bone</b>: 4 mg given over not &lt;15 mins every 3-4 weeks. <b>Hypercalcemia of malignancy (albumin-corrected serum calcium &gt;12 mg/dL [3 mmol/L])</b>: 4 mg over not < 15 mins following standard rehydration procedures. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl &gt;60 mL/min: 4 mg; 50-60 mL/min: 3.5 mg; 40-49 mL/min: 3.3 mg; 30-39 mL/min: 3 mg. Doses are given every 3-4 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Give oral supplementation of calcium 500 mg and vit D 400 IU per day. Maintain proper hydration. Patients with or at risk for renal deterioration. Patients with asthma. Risk for hypocalcemia, musculoskeletal pain, ONJ, atypical fractures of femur, ocular disturbances. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn 1-17 yrs. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fever and flu-like syndrome, fatigue, chills, rigors, malaise, flushing. CV, CNS, GI, hematologic, lymphatic effects. Moniliasis. Hypophosphatemia, hypomagnesemia, hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, hypernatremia. Increased creatinine, BUN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Loop diuretics, aminoglycosides, nephrotoxic drugs (e.g. aminoglycosides, other antineoplastic agents, aspirin, NSAIDs) or drugs that significantly impact renal function (e.g. diuretics, ACE inhibitors), thalidomide. <b>Incompatibilities</b>: Calcium or other divalent cation-containing infusion solutions (e.g. Lactated Ringer’s solution)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 4 mg/5 mL (P11,562.08)."
          }

    "detail": {
      "success": true,

        "id": 1250,
        "brand_name": "Oxalee",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/H6EYg6J3kqAUJoPVL0SbSgdBlGQ1CtilHJZoParOBnYVX14Ch4.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/FnnleOJfr6tlOxrQ7R382ysiURHvzdiuydblTiTgzc9mJtA7wq.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gX8DAcaUSMHt24J4GFGQIkHSS37z3fYNsx5L8MQcopEcb8Grol.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Oxaliplatin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Platinum Complexes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of advanced colorectal cancer in combination with infusional 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and leucovorin; adjuvant treatment of stage III colon cancer in patients who have undergone complete resection of the primary tumor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer before fluoropyrimidines. Antiemetics should be given before and after therapy with oxaliplatin. <b>Treatment of patients with advanced colorectal cancer - Day 1</b>: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m<sup>2</sup> (as IV infusion diluted in 250-500 mL of 5% dextrose soln) and leucovorin 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> (by IV infusion in 5% dextrose soln), both given over 120 mins at the same time in different bags using a Y-line, followed by 5-FU 400 mg/m<sup>2</sup> by IV bolus given over 2-4 mins, followed by 5-FU 600 mg/m<sup>2</sup> (diluted in 500 mL 5% dextrose soln) as a 22-hr continuous IV infusion. <b>Day 2</b>: Leucovorin 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> in IV infusion over 120 mins, followed by 5-FU 400 mg/m<sup>2</sup> by IV bolus over 2-4 mins, followed by 5-FU 600 mg/m<sup>2</sup> diluted in 500 mL 5% dextrose solution as a 22-hr continuous IV infusion. Treatment may be repeated every 2 weeks. <b>Adjuvant treatment in patients with stage III colon cancer after complete resection of primary tumor</b>: Recommended for a total of 6 months (i.e. 12 cycles), given every 2 weeks according to the dose schedule described for the treatment of advanced colorectal cancer. Postpone next dose until hematological values return to acceptable levels (neutrophils &ge;1.5x10<sup>9</sup>/L and platelets &ge;75x10<sup>9</sup>/L)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to oxaliplatin or other platinum compounds (cisplatin, carboplatin). Patients with peripheral sensory neuropathy with functional impairment prior to first course; severe impairment renal function (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min); myelosuppression prior to starting first course with baseline neutrophils &lt;1.5x10<sup>9</sup>/L and/or platelet count < 75x10<sup>9</sup>/L. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid cold foods and drinks and cover skin before cold exposure during and within 48 hrs after administration. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Fertility impairment. Elderly. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Acute and peripheral neuropathies, sensory disturbance, pulmonary fibrosis, hematologic effects, GI effects, dermatologic reactions, hepatotoxicity (elevation of transaminases, alkaline phosphatase), renal toxicity (creatinine elevation), musculoskeletal effects, thromboembolism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Nephrotoxic drugs; antineoplastic drugs (irinotecan, topotecan); protein-bound drugs (erythromycin, salicylate, sodium valproate, granisetron, paclitaxel); drugs affecting CYP450 enzymes. <b>Incompatibilities</b>: Sodium chloride or other chloride-containing solutions, aluminum, alkaline compounds or media."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for IV infusion 50 mg (P9,316.59), 100 mg (P16,164.33)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WrPnjKelwKvoKutrEpiuICWBokQneteFZuwY7bBAtR0pUDdGc5.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Fet5YWoc8dgpmWlAeMOcseENVTDkSQGaRbQmGvbm7EBl9KfdeA.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paclitaxel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Taxanes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Palliative treatment of stage 3 or 4 advanced local carcinoma of the ovary after surgical resection, in combination with cisplatin; management of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of 1<sup>st</sup> line or subsequent chemotherapy; advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in patients who are not candidates for potentially curative surgery and/or radiation. Palliative treatment of advanced or refractory AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma in patients who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy. Treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the breast after failure of combination therapy or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy. For initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an anthracycline in patients for whom anthracycline therapy is suitable, or with trastuzumab in patients who over-express HER-2 at a 3+ level and for whom anthracycline is not suitable."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Premedicate all patients with corticosteroids (e.g. oral dexamethasone), antihistamines (e.g. IV diphenhydramine), and H<sub>2</sub> antagonists (e.g. IV cimetidine or ranitidine) prior to paclitaxel administration. <b>Ovarian cancer - Primary treatment</b>: 135 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 24 hrs, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, every 3 weeks. Alternatively, 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, every 3 weeks. <b>Secondary treatment after failure of 1<sup>st</sup> line or subsequent chemotherapy</b>: 135 or 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hrs every 3 weeks. <b>Palliative treatment of advanced NSCLC</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hours, followed by a platinum compound, with a 3-week interval between courses; 135 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 24 hrs followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, given every 3 weeks; or 175mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hrs followed by cisplatin 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, given every 3 weeks. <b>Breast cancer - Adjuvant treatment of node-positive breast cancer</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks for 4 courses administered sequentially to doxorubicin-containing combination therapy. <b>Treatment of breast cancer after failure of initial chemotherapy for metastatic disease or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks. <b>HER-2 overexpressing breast cancer</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks for 6 cycles. Administer trastuzumab 2 mg/kg IV once a week until progression of disease after an initial loading dose of 4 mg/kg. <b>AIDS-related Kaposi’s sacrcoma</b>: 135 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered over 3 hrs, every 3 weeks. Alternatively, 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, every 2 weeks (dose intensify 45-50 mg/m<sup>2</sup> per week)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to products containing polyoxyethylated castor oil (cremophor EL). Patients with solid tumors who have baseline neutrophil count &lt;1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>; AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma with neutrophil count &lt;1,000 cells/mm<sup>3</sup> and those with concurrent, serious, uncontrolled infections; hepatic dysfunction, alcoholism, and epilepsy. Childn. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Undiluted paclitaxel should not come in contact with PVC equipment or devices. Contains ethyl alcohol. Narrow therapeutic index. Patients with preexisting or at risk for bone marrow suppression, severe cardiac conduction abnormalities, peripheral neuropathy. Risk for embryotoxicity and mutagenicity. Vaccine administration. Postpone oral poliovirus vaccine in people in close contact with patients undergoing paclitaxel therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Women of childbearing potential. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tingling and numbness of hands and feet, neutropenia, bone and muscle aches, hair loss, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, mild diarrhea, mucositis, amenorrhea, changes in nails. Infectious complications."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antineoplastic agents, myelosuppressive agents, drugs affecting CYP450 isoenzymes CYP2C8 and CYP3A4, CNS depressants, vaccines. <b>Incompatibilities</b>: Amphotericin B, chlorpromazine HCl, hydroxyzine HCl, methylprednisolone, sodium succinate, and mitoxantrone HCl."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 6 mg/mL x 5 mL (P4,045.86), 16.67 mL (P9,866.99), 43.4 mL (P19,000.00)."
          }
        ],

    "id": 4813,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4813,
        "brand_name": "Paclisun",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paclitaxel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Taxanes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of breast cancer after failure of combination chemotherapy for metastatic disease or relapse within 6 months of adjuvant chemotherapy; combination with carboplatin is the 1<sup>st</sup>-line for locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer for patients not candidates for curative surgery or radiation therapy; combination with gemcitabine is 1<sup>st</sup>-line for metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion. <b>Metastatic breast cancer (MBC):</b> 260 mg/m<sup>2</sup> or 295 mg/m<sup>2</sup> for 30 mins every 3 weeks. <b>Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC):</b> 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 30 mins on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 21-day cycle, administered immediately after with carboplatin on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. <b>Adenocarcinoma of the pancreas:</b> 125 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 30-40 mins on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle, administered immediately after with gemcitabine on the same days. <b>Hepatic impairment - MBC</b> – AST < 10 x ULN and bilirubin >1.5-&le;5 x ULN: 200 mg/m<sup>2b</sup>. <b>NSCLC</b> - AST < 10 x ULN and bilirubin >1.5-&le;5 x ULN: 80 mg/m<sup>2b</sup>. The dose increases in subsequent courses if the reduced dose for two cycles are tolerated. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and preparation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Baseline neutrophil counts of < 1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with total bilirubin >5 x ULN or AST >10 x ULN; metastatic adenocarcinoma of the pancreas with moderate to severe hepatic impairment; biliary obstruction or presence of stent; pneumonitis. May induce severe myelosuppression; severe neuropathy; sepsis; febrile neutropenia; severe or fatal hypersensitivity reactions and cross-hypersensitivity. Perform CBC frequently, prior to dosing on day 1 (for MBC) and days 1, 8, and 15 (for NSCLC and for pancreatic cancer). Childn. Elderly. Use contraception during and at least 6 months after treatment. Avoid fathering a child during treatment and at least 3 months after last dose. Women of child bearing potential. Breastfeeding should be avoided for 2 weeks after last dose. May impair fertility in males and females of reproductive age.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Alopecia, neutropenia, sensory neuropathy, abnormal ECG, fatigue/asthenia, myalgia/arthralgia, AST elevation, alkaline phosphatase elevation, anemia, nausea, vomiting, infections, diarrhea, pneumonia, peripheral edema, pyrexia, decreased appetite, rash, dehydration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP2C8 and CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 100 mg/0.91 mL x 2 mL (P9,000.00), 300 mg/2.73 mL x 5 mL (P25,000.00)."
          }

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Triptorelin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hormones and Antagonists in Chemotherapy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Palliative treatment of locally advanced non-metastatic hormone-dependent prostate cancer, as an alternative to surgical castration. Treatment of metastatic hormone-dependent prostate cancer. Adjuvant treatment to radiotherapy in patients with high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate cancer. <b>3.75 mg</b>: In combination with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor as adjuvant treatment of HR-positive early-stage breast cancer in premenopausal women at high risk of recurrence after completion of chemotherapy. For the pituitary down-regulation in assisted reproduction technology. <b>3.75 mg and 11.25 mg</b>: Treatment of endometriosis. <b>22.5 mg</b>: Treatment of central precocious puberty (CPP) in childn &ge;2 yrs with onset before 8 yrs in girls and 10 yrs in boys."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered as single injection. <b>Prostate cancer - Duration - 3.75 mg (IM/SC)</b>: Every month (4 weeks); <b>11.25 mg (IM)</b>: Every 3 months (12 weeks); <b>22.5 mg (IM)</b>: Every 6 months (24 weeks). <b>Breast cancer (3.75 mg IM only)</b>: Every 4 weeks in combination with tamoxifen or an aromatase inhibitor. Commence after completion of chemotherapy, once premenopausal status is confirmed. Initiate 6-8 weeks (minimum of 2 injections with 2-week interval) before starting aromatase inhibitor treatment. <b>Pituitary down-regulation in assisted reproduction (3.75 mg only) - Long protocol</b>: Single injection prior to induction of stimulation with exogenous gonadotropins. <b>Short protocol</b>: Single injection induced at the same time as or every shortly before stimulation with exogenous gonadotropins. <b>Endometriosis in women &ge;18 yrs (3.75 mg and 11.25 mg only)</b>: 3.75 mg IM/SC every 28 days, to be initiated in the first 5 days of the menstrual cycle. Max duration of treatment: 6 months. <b>CPP (22.5 mg only)</b>: Administer in a regular six-monthly (24 weekly) period. Discontinue around physiological age of puberty and bone maturation (12-13 yrs for girls, 13-14 yrs for boys)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to triptorelin, GnRH, GnRH agonists analogs. Intravascular injection. Women with undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding. Patients with spinal cord compression secondary to prostate cancer metastases. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for transient increase in serum testosterone levels, temporary amenorrhea or permanent loss of ovarian function, bone mineral density loss, hypogonadism, anemia, increased lymphocyte count, pituitary apoplexy, ovarian hyperstimulation. Patients with preexisting or at risk for hyperglycemia, metastatic vertebral lesions and/or upper or lower urinary tract obstruction, CV diseases (HTN, hyperlipidemia), QT/QTc prolongation, seizures, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, CNS anomalies, depressive disorders. Concomitant use of drugs associated with QT-prolongation, induce convulsion (e.g. bupropion, SSRIs). Patients with renal and hepatic impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },

                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Men</b>: Induced variation in serum testosterone levels. <b>Women</b>: Hot flushes, vaginal dryness, amenorrhea. Local, CV, nervous, endocrine, GI, hepatic, musculoskeletal, respiratory, dermatologic, genitourinary, and sensory effects. Asthenia, fatigue, and bruising. Decreased Hgb, RBC. Increased glucose, BUN, AST, ALT, ALP levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Should not be mixed with medicinal products. Drugs affecting pituitary secretion of gonadotropins; drugs that induce hyperprolactinemia e.g. antipsychotic agents (chlorpromazine, haloperidol, molindone, olanzapine, prochlorperazine, risperidone), methyldopa, metoclopramide, reserpine); drugs that prolong QTc interval and induce Torsades de pointes. Anticoagulants, antihypertensives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection (IM/SC) 3.75 mg (P7,087.50), (IM) 11.25 mg (P18,573.48), (IM) 22.5 mg (P30,870.65)."

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefoxitin sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of intra-abdominal and pelvic infections including endometritis (prophylaxis at caesarian section), pelvic inflammatory disease; gonorrhea, urinary tract infections (UTI). Prophylaxis for surgical infections when contamination with anaerobes is likely for having greater activity against anaerobic bacteria including <i>Bacteroides fragilis</i>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via IM injection, IV injection, or IV infusion (intermittent or continuous). Usual dosage - Adults: 1-2 g IM/IV every 8 hrs, up to 12 g daily in severe infections; Childn and infants >4 weeks: 20-40 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs, up to 200 mg/kg/day in severe infections. Max 12 g daily; Infants 1-4 weeks: 20-40 mg/kg every 8 hrs; < 1 week: 20-40 mg/kg every 12 hrs. <b>Post-op surgical infections prophylaxis - Adults:</b> 2 g IV when inducing anesthesia, followed by 1-2 g injection every 2 hrs until the skin has closed up. Treatment duration: Limited to post-op period, sometimes up to 24 hrs but must never exceed 48 hrs. For appendectomy, a single dose is sufficient; <b>Childn and infants:</b> 30-40 mg/kg every 6 hrs; <b>Neonates:</b> 30-40 mg/kg every 8-12 hrs. <b>Uncomplicated UTI:</b> 1 g IM twice daily. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 2 g IM + probenecid 1 g orally. <b>Caesarian section:</b> 2 g IV as soon as the umbilical cord is clamped. <b>Adults with renal impairment -</b> CrCl 30-50 mL/min: 1-2 g every 8-12 hrs; 10-29 mL/min: 1-2 g every 12-24 hrs; 5-9 mL/min: Initially 1-2 g, then 0.5-1 g every 12-24 hrs; < 5 mL/min: Initially 1-2 g, then 0.5-1 g every 24-48 hrs. Adults undergoing dialysis: Additional loading dose of 1-2 g after each dialysis session."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with penicillins and other cephalosporins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with known histories of allergy and renal impairment. Monitor renal and hematological status especially during prolonged and high-dose therapy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions, acute renal tubular necrosis or interstitial nephritis. Convulsions or other CNS toxicities. Injection site pain, thrombophlebitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potentially nephrotoxic antibiotics, especially aminoglycosides; diuretics (e.g. furosemide, ethacrynic acid). False positive Coomb’s test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 1 g (P874.50)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, complicated urinary tract infections (UTI) including pyelonephritis, soft tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, wound infections), and intra-abdominal infections in adults and childn, including neonates (from birth). Prophylaxis against gastrointestinal (GI) (including esophageal), orthopedic, cardiovascular (CV), and gynecological surgery (including caesarian section) infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via deep IM injection, IV injection for 3-5 mins, or IV drip or infusion for 30-60 mins. <b>Adults and childn &ge;40 kg - CAP, acute exacerbations or chronic bronchitis, soft tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, wound infections):</b> 750 mg IV or IM every 8 hrs; <b>Complicated UTI including pyelonephritis:</b> 1.5 g every 8 hrs IV or IM; Severe infections: 750 mg IV every 6 hrs or 1.5 g IV every 8 hrs; <b>Surgical prophylaxis for GI, gynecological surgery (including caesarian section), and orthopedic operations:</b> 1.5 g with induction of anesthesia, may be supplemented with 750 mg IM after 8 hrs and 16 hrs; <b>Surgical prophylaxis for CV and esophageal operations:</b> 1.5 g with induction of anesthesia, followed by 750 mg IM every 8 hrs for 24 hrs. <b>CAP, complicated UTI including pyelonephritis, soft tissue infections (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, wound infections), intra-abdominal infections - Childn < 40 kg, toddlers, and infants >3 weeks:</b> 30-100 mg/kg/day IV in 3-4 divided doses. 60 mg/kg/day is appropriate for most infections; <b>Infants 0-3 weeks:</b> 30-100 mg/kg/day IV in 2-3 divided doses. <b>Patients with renal impairment -</b> CrCl 10-20 mL/min, renal failure on continuous arteriovenous hemodialysis in intensive therapy units: 750 mg twice daily; < 10 mL/min: 750 mg once daily. In patients on hemodialysis: Additional 750 mg IV or IM after each dialysis session. Can be incorporated into the peritoneal dialysis fluid (usually 250 mg for every 2 L of dialysis fluid)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g. penicillins, monobactams, carbapenems)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated for infections caused by G(-) non-fermenting bacteria. Patients with renal impairment, history of non-severe hypersensitivity to other beta-lactam antibiotics; on a controlled sodium diet. Concomitant use with potent diuretics (e.g. furosemide) or aminoglycosides. Antibiotic-associated pseudomembranous colitis may develop. Overgrowth of <i>Candida</i> or other non-susceptible organisms during prolonged use. Monitor renal function of elderly patients and those with pre-existing renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neutropenia, eosinophilia, decreased Hgb; transient rise in liver enzymes; injection site reactions (e.g. pain, thrombophlebitis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Estrogen, oral contraceptives; probenecid; potent diuretics (e.g. furosemide), aminoglycosides; oral anticoagulants. False positive Coomb’s test. May interfere with copper reduction methods (e.g. Benedict’s and Fehling’s soln, Clinitest). False negative ferricyanide test."

            "content": "Treatment of severe bacterial infections sensitive to cefotaxime, especially septicemia, endocarditis, and meningitis, except those due to <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>. Prophylaxis of endoscopic prostate resection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via deep IM injection, IV injection, or IV infusion for 20-60 mins. <b>Adults -</b> Usual dose: 3 g/day, may be increased up to 12 g depending on the severity of infection; <b>Urinary tract infections:</b> 2 g/day; <b>Prophylaxis of endoscopic prostate resection:</b> 1 g IV on anesthetic induction; <b>Meningitis:</b> 200-300 mg/kg/day. Max 24 g/day. <b>Childn, infants, and full-term neonates:</b> 50 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses via IV injection, may be increased up to 200 mg/kg/day depending on the severity of infection. <b>Premature neonates:</b> 50 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses via IV injection, may be increased to 100 mg/kg/day in severe infections. <b>Pneumococcal meningitis -</b> Adults, childn, and infants >3 months: 50-75 mg/kg IV infusion for 20 mins every 6 hrs within first 48-72 hrs (i.e. 200-300 mg/kg/day), followed by vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV infusion for 60 mins (i.e. 60 mg/kg/day) in adults in case of signs of severity or in the presence of reduced-penicillin sensitivity pneumococcus risk factors.             "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of multidrug-resistant G(-) infections due to organisms proven or suspected to be susceptible to piperacillin-tazobactam except CNS infections; polymicrobial infections (e.g. mixed aerobic and anaerobic infections) except infections in which other agents have insufficient activity or are contraindicated due to toxic potential."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 4 g/500 mg every 8 hrs, may be increased up to 4 g/500 mg every 6 hrs. <b>Childn >12 yrs:</b> 240 mg/30 mg to 320 mg/40 mg per kg/day in 3-4 divided doses. <b>Patients with renal impairment -</b> CrCl 20-40 mL/min: 4 g/500 mg every 8 hrs; < 20 mL/min and on hemodialysis:4 g/500 mg every 12 hrs. Administer an additional 2 g/250 mg or 4 g/500 mg dose after each dialysis session. All doses given via IV infusion for 30 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics (e.g. penicillins, cephalosporins) and beta-lactamase inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of sensitivity to multiple allergens, renal impairment or undergoing hemodialysis, herpes virus infections, infectious mononucleosis. Concomitant use with aminoglycosides, potassium-depleting agents. Anaphylactic/anaphylactoid reactions (including shock), antibiotic-induced pseudomembranous colitis, bleeding abnormalities (e.g. prothrombin time, bleeding time); leukopenia and neutropenia during prolonged use. Perform CBC periodically. Take into account sodium content of product. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting; rash, erythema, cutaneous hypersensitivity reactions, pruritus, urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Methotrexate; oral anticoagulants, fluoroquinolones, macrolides, cyclins, co-trimoxazole, cephalosporins. False positive glycosuria using copper-reduction method; Platelia Aspergillus EIA test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for solution for IV infusion 2 g/250 mg (P720.50), 4 g/500 mg (P1,248.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 160,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 160,
        "brand_name": "Pantoloc",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pantoprazole sodium sesquihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab: 20 mg – Adults:</b> Prevention of NSAID-induced gastroduodenal ulcers in patients at risk with a need for continuous NSAID treatment. <b>Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs:</b> Symptomatic improvement (e.g. heartburn, acid regurgitation, pain in swallowing) and healing of mild reflux esophagitis; long-term management and prevention of relapse in reflux esophagitis. <b>Childn 5-11 yrs:</b> Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and reflux esophagitis. <b>40 mg – Adults:</b> Treatment of moderate and severe reflux esophagitis, gastric and duodenal ulcer, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other pathological hypersecretory conditions, and in combination with 2 appropriate antibiotics for eradication of H. pylori in patients with peptic ulcers to reduce recurrence of duodenal and gastric ulcer. <b>Childn 5-17 yrs:</b> Treatment of reflux esophagitis. <b>IV:</b> Treatment of duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, moderate and severe reflux esophagitis, bleeding peptic ulcer (and prevention of re-bleeding), Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other conditions associated with pathological overproduction of gastric acid. Prophylaxis of acute bleeding stress ulcer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken 1 hr before breakfast. <b>Tab - Adults - Prevention of NSAID-induced gastroduodenal ulcers:</b> 20 mg daily; <b>Moderate and severe reflux esophagitis, gastric and duodenal ulcer:</b> 40 mg daily, may be doubled when there is no response to other treatment; <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other pathological hypersecretory conditions:</b> Initially 80 mg per day, titrated up or down as needed. For dose >80 mg, give in 2 divided doses; <b>Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i> with 2 appropriate antibiotics:</b> Take second pantoprazole tab before evening meal. Treatment duration: 7 days, max 2 weeks. Twice daily doses. (a) 40 mg pantoprazole + 1,000 mg amoxicillin + 500 mg clarithromycin, (b) 40 mg pantoprazole + 500 mg metronidazole + 500 mg clarithromycin, (c) 40 mg pantoprazole  + 1,000 mg amoxicillin + 500 mg metronidazole. <b>Symptomatic improvement and healing of mild reflux esophagitis: Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs -</b> 20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks, recurring symptoms can be controlled with 20 mg once daily, when required. Treatment duration: &ge;4 weeks. <b>Long-term management and prevention of reflux esophagitis relapse: Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs</b> - 20 mg maintenance dose daily, increased to 40 mg daily if relapse occurs, can be reduced again to 20 mg after healing of the relapse. <b>Symptomatic GERD: Childn 5-11 yrs -</b> 20 mg daily, further investigation is recommended if symptom control has not been achieved after 4 weeks. <b>Treatment of reflux esophagitis – Childn 5-17 yrs: >35 kg BW:</b> 40 mg; <b>19-35 kg:</b> 20 mg. Treatment duration: 4-8 weeks. <b>Severe hepatic impairment:</b> Max 20 mg daily or 40 mg every other day. <b>Renal impairment:</b> &le;40 mg. <b>IV inj- Duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, and severe reflux esophagitis:</b> 40 mg/day; <b>Long-term management of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other hypersecretory conditions:</b> Initially 80 mg/day, can be titrated up or down as needed. For dose >80 mg, give in 2 divided doses; If rapid acid control is required: Initially 2 x 80 mg to manage decrease of acid output into target range (< 10 mEq/h) within 1 hr; <b>Upper digestive hemorrhage (complimentary to endoscopic therapy) and prevention of re-bleeding:</b> 80 mg bolus, followed by 8 mg/hr infusion for 72 hrs; <b>Prophylaxis of acute bleeding due to stress ulcer:</b> 40-80 mg once to twice daily. May be given as bolus (&ge;2 mins) or infusion. <b>Severe hepatic impairment:</b> Max 20 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Combination treatment for eradication of <i>H. pylori</i> in patients with moderate to severe hepatic or renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for mild GI complaints. Restrict use of therapy as preventive of NSAID-induced gastroduodenal ulcers to patients requiring continued NSAID treatment and with increased risks for GI complications. Co-administration with HIV protease inhibitors (acidic intragastric pH dependent) is not recommended. May increase risk of GI infections or bone fractures. May masks symptoms of gastric malignancy. Severe hypomagnesemia, subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus. Vit B<sub>12</sub> malabsorption on prolonged use. Discontinue for at least 5 days prior CgA measurements. Monitor liver enzymes regularly in patients with severe liver impairment; long-term treatment (&ge;1 yr); magnesium levels prior to and periodically during treatment on patients requiring long-term treatment or who use drug-induced hypomagnesemia. Tab: Childn < 5 yrs.  IV: Childn < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fundic gland polyps (benign). IV: injection site thrombophlebitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole, erlotinib, HIV protease inhibitors (e.g. atazanavir), warfarin or phenprocoumon, methotrexate, fluvoxamine, CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 (e.g. rifampicin, St. John’s wort)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 20 mg, 40 mg. Lyophilized powder for injection (IV) 40 mg."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 221,
          "name": "Zuellig Pharma Corp."
        },

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2984,
        "brand_name": "Pantopraz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/daHSpZ9di4pUQzKauZfcIgHfaBwKaxf8h5xlAcDbmz0mupKFEM.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/fn69oUNlz6PqJ5uBUnN2T6vhVWJ6rjSmdHdjXGsAN8Xa5pgTdz.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4V7GkwCLpgS8piF36Qvc9vPO0ck5RNvc0PFlQ5UeBXwf1EHQPe.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pantoprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: Peptic ulcer disease (PUD). Moderate and severe gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). Combination therapy with suitable antibiotics for the eradication of <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> in patients with gastric ulcers. Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. <b>IV</b>: Short-term treatment of GERD associated with a history of erosive esophagitis. Treatment of pathologic secretion conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – PUD</b>: 40 mg once daily. <b>Benign gastric ulceration</b>: 40 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 80 mg once daily. <b>GERD</b>: 40 mg once daily. <b><i>H. pylori</i> infection</b>: 40 mg twice daily with clarithromycin and either amoxicillin or metronidazole. <b>Severe hepatic insufficiency</b>: Reduced to 40 mg every other day. <b>Renal impairment and elderly</b>: Max 40 mg daily (except when used for eradication of <i>H. pylori</i>, elderly patients should receive 40 mg twice daily). <b>IV – Reflux esophagitis, gastric and duodenal ulcer</b>: 40 mg IV infusion once daily for 7-10 days. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other related hypersecretion conditions</b>: Initially 80 mg daily given in 2 divided doses. Dose can be adjusted as needed based on the gastric acid secretion. For rapid acid control, starting dose 80 mg twice daily. A temporary dose increase &gt;160 mg should not be applied longer than required for adequate acid control. <b>Severe hepatic impairment</b>: Max 20 mg daily. <b>Renal impairment and elderly</b>: Max 50 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Tab</b>: Not to be used in combination therapy for the eradication of <i>H. pylori</i> in patients with moderately severe hepatic or renal impairment. <b>IV</b>: Patients using atazanavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "<b>IV</b>: <i>C. difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Increased risk of osteoporosis-related fractures of the hip, wrist or spine especially in high doses. Symptomatic response to pantoprazole treatment does not preclude the presence of gastric malignancy. Zinc supplementation should be considered in patients who are prone to zinc deficiency. Discontinue treatment once acute interstitial nephritis develops.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, diarrhea. <b>IV</b>: Injection site reaction, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, flatulence, dizziness, arthralgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs with pH-dependent bioavailability (e.g. ketoconazole). <b>Tab</b>: Drugs metabolized by CYP450. <b>IV</b>: Atazanavir, nelfinavir, warfarin, clopidogrel, methotrexate. False positive in urine tests for THC."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 40mg (P58.00). Lyophilized powder for injection (IV) 40 mg (P680.00)."
          }

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily, with or without meal. <b>Duodenal ulcer:</b> 40 mg in the morning for 2 weeks, continued for 2 weeks further if not fully healed. <b>Benign gastric ulcer, GERD:</b> 40 mg in the morning for 4 weeks, continued for 4 weeks further if not fully healed. <b>Elderly, renal impairment:</b> Max 40 mg daily. <b>Hepatic impairment due to cirrhosis:</b> 40 mg every other day. <b><i>H. pylori</i> eradication:</b> Twice daily doses for 7 days, continued for 7 days further if not fully healed; a) 40 mg pantoprazole + 500 mg clarithromycin + 1,000 mg amoxicillin; b) 40 mg pantoprazole + 400 mg metronidazole + 500 mg clarithromycin; (c) 40 mg pantoprazole + 1,000 mg amoxicillin + 500 mg metronidazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment. Monitor liver function regularly. Avoid smoking and foods that may upset stomach (e.g. alcohol, citrus fruits, caffeine, tomatoes, spicy food). >16 weeks of treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, skin rash, headache, CNS effects (e.g. reversible confusional state in severely ill patients)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, ampicillin esters, iron salts, drugs for indigestion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 40 mg (P67.50)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>Short-term treatment of erosive esophagitis associated with GERD – Adults</b>: 40 mg once daily up to 8 weeks. An additional 8 weeks may be considered if not yet healed.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of atazanavir and nelfinavir."
          },

            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Treatment does not preclude presence of gastric malignancy. Discontinue if acute interstitial nephritis occur. Patients at risk for osteoporosis-related fractures.           },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections caused by susceptible organisms, including chancroid, endocarditis, gastroenteritis (e.g. invasive salmonellosis, shigellosis), gonorrhea, meningitis (including prophylaxis against meningococcal meningitis, except those due to <i>Listeria monocytogenes</i>), septicemia, syphilis, typhoid fever, and Whipple’s disease; Lyme disease disseminated during early stage of meningitis (secondary stage) or delayed stage with neurological and articular systemic manifestations (tertiary stage). Surgical infection prophylaxis for prostate transurethral resection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via IM injection, IV injection for 2-4 mins, or IV infusion for 30 mins. <b>Adults and elderly:</b> 1-2 g/day as single injection. <b>Childn and newborns:</b> 50 mg/kg/day as single injection. <b>Lyme disease -</b> Adults and elderly: 2 g/day as single injection for 14-21 days; Childn: 50-100 mg/kg/day as single injection for 14-21 days. <b>Meningitis -</b> Childn: 50-100 mg/kg/day as single injection. 100 mg/kg is only justified as attack treatment; for infants 3-12 months, administer every 12 hrs. <b>Acute otitis media -</b> Childn: 50 mg/kg/day for 3 days in case of therapeutic failure; or 50 mg/kg as a single dose as alternative to oral therapy. <b>Surgical infection prophylaxis -</b> Adults and elderly: 1 g as single IM/IV injection when inducing anesthesia. Duration is limited to pre-op period over 24-48 hrs. <b>Susceptibility to purpura fulminans -</b> Adults and elderly: 1-2 g IV for the 1<sup>st</sup> dose; Childn: 50-100 mg/kg IV on the 1<sup>st</sup> dose. Max 1 g."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Cross-sensitivity with penicillins and other cephalosporins. Use of lidocaine (for IM injections) in patients with allergy to lidocaine or other amide local anesthetics, porphyria, unapplianced AV block, and cardiogenic shock."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe renal or hepatic impairment; on a strict low sodium diet. Concomitant use with calcium-containing products; oral anticoagulants. Perform echography in case of pain at right side of hypochondrium. Regular control of blood formula during prolonged use.Lidocaine may cause false positive anti-doping tests. Neonates with hyperbilirubinemia. Premature infants. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions. Skin, digestive, digestive, hepatobiliary, pancreatic, hematological, renal, and CNS disorders. Injection site pain, local phlebitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "False positive Coomb’s test, galactosemia, glycosuria when non-enzymatic methods are used. <b>Incompatibilities:</b> Calcium-containing solns (e.g. Hartmann’s or Ringer’s soln). Amsacrine, vancomycin, fluconazole, aminoglycosides."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",
