          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of active duodenal ulcer, active benign gastric ulcer, anastomotic ulcer, erosive or ulcerative gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), GERD maintenance, symptomatic GERD, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other pathological hypersecretory conditions. In combination therapy eradication of <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> in patients with peptic ulcer disease. Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcer recurrences associated with low-dose aspirin therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Active duodenal ulcer, active benign gastric ulcer and anastomotic ulcer</b>: 10 mg or 20 mg once daily in morning. Treatment duration of 4 weeks for active duodenal ulcer and 6 weeks for active benign gastric ulcer. <b>Erosive or ulcerative GERD</b>: 10 mg or 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. For reflux esophagitis doses of 10 mg or 20 mg (for severe mucosal injury) twice daily may be given for another 8 weeks if not responding to the usual dose of PPIs. Short-term treatment of GERD in childn &ge;12 yrs: 20 mg once daily for up to 8 weeks. <b>Long-term GERD maintenance</b>: 10 mg or 20 mg once daily depending on patient response. May be increased to 10 mg twice daily. <b>Symptomatic GERD without esophagitis</b>: 10 mg once daily. For subsequent symptom control, 10 mg once daily may be given as needed. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome and other pathological hypersecretory conditions</b>: 60 mg once daily up to 100 mg once daily, or 60 mg twice daily. <b>For prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcer recurrences associated with low-dose aspirin therapy</b>: 10 mg once daily. <b>Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i></b>: 10 mg or 20 mg twice daily + clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily + amoxicillin 1 g twice daily. Take doses in the morning, before meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Exclude possibility of gastric or esophageal malignancy prior to treatment. Patients with hepatic dysfunction, or on long-term of PPI use. Patients at risk for osteoporosis-related fracture, <i>Clostridium difficile</i> infection, SCLE, fundic gland polyps. Concomitant use of methotrexate and drugs that may cause hypomagnesemia. Childn < 12 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, asthenia, flatulence, rash and dry mouth. Insomnia, infection, dizziness, cough, pharyngitis, rhinitis, vomiting, nausea, constipation, non-specific pain, back pain, and flu-like syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, itraconazole, atazanavir, methotrexate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg (P79.00), 20 mg (P105.00)."
          }

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of Parkinson's disease and syndrome; manage associated tremor, dysphagia, sialorrhea, and postural instability; relieve many symptoms of parkinsonism (e.g. rigidity and bradykinesia). Alternative to levodopa when signs and symptoms of Parkinson’s disease are not evenly controlled throughout the day. Treatment of patients with Parkinsonism who are taking vitamin preparations containing vit B<sub>6</sub>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Initial dose:</b> 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg 3x daily, may be increased by 1 tab every day or every other day. Max 8 tabs/day. Alternatively, a starting dose of 1 tab of 250 mg/25 mg once daily may be used, can be increased using a combination of 100 mg/125 mg and 250 mg/125 mg tabs until optimal response is reached. <b>From levodopa:</b> Discontinue levodopa at least 12 or 24 hrs for slow preparations, prior to initiation of therapy. Give approximately 20% of previous levodopa daily dose; <b>< 1,500 mg levodopa/day:</b> 1 tab of 100 mg/25 mg 3-4x daily; <b>>1,500 mg levodopa/day:</b> 1 tab of 250 mg/25 mg 3-4x daily. <b>Maintenance:</b> Individualized dosage. At least 70-100 mg of carbidopa/day. When more levodopa is required, 250 mg/25 mg tab should be substituted for 100 mg/25 mg tab, then may increase by 1 tab every day or every other day. Max 8 tabs daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with narrow-angle glaucoma, suspicious undiagnosed skin lesion, or history of melanoma. Concomitant use with MAOIs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for drug-induced EPS. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with past or current psychoses; severe CV or pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, renal, hepatic, or endocrine disease, history of PUD, MI who have residual atrial, nodal, or ventricular arrhythmia; chronic wide-angle glaucoma; Concomitant use with psychoactive drugs. Dyskinesia, involuntary movements and mental disturbances, somnolence and sudden sleep onset, melanoma, impulse control disorders. Evaluate hepatic, hematopoietic, CV, and renal function periodically. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dyskinesias including choreiform, dystonia, and other involuntary movements; nausea. Muscle twitching and blepharospasm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antihypertensives, TCAs, ferrous sulfate or gluconate, D2 receptor antagonists (e.g. phenothiazines, butyrophenones, risperidone), isoniazid, dopamine-depleting agents (e.g. reserpine, tetrabenazine), selegiline. High protein diet."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg/25 mg x 50s (P1,801.80), 250 mg/25 mg x 50s (P2,893.80)."
          }

        "content": "Nirmatrelvir, ritonavir",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in adults who do not require supplemental oxygen and at increased risk for progressing to severe COVID-19."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Co-administer 300 mg nirmatrelvir (two 150 mg tabs) with 100 mg ritonavir every 12 hrs for 5 days. Should be administered as soon as possible after diagnosis of COVID-19 has been made and within 5 days of symptom onset. <b>Renal impairment - Moderate (eGFR &ge;30-< 60 mL/min):</b> 150 mg nirmatrelvir with 100 mg ritonavir every 12 hrs for 5 days. May be take with or without food. Tabs should be swallowed whole and not chewed, broken or crushed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal (eGFR &lt;30 mL/min, including patients with ESRD under hemodialysis) and hepatic (Child-Pugh Class C) impairment. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Concomitant use with alfuzosin, ranolazine, amiodarone, dronedarone, flecainide, propafenone, quinidine, fusidic acid, neratinib, venetoclax, colchicine, terfenadine, clozapine, lurasidone, pimozide, quetiapine, silodosin, eplerenone, ivabradine, ergot derivatives, cisapride, voclosporin, lovastatin, simvastatin, lomitapide, eletriptan, avanafil, sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, clorazepate, diazepam, estazolam, flurazepam, oral midazolam, triazolam, tolvaptan; rifampicin, apalutamide, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, St. John’s wort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Consider potential interactions with other medicinal products before and during therapy, review concomitant medicinal products during therapy, and monitor patients for adverse reactions. Concomitant use of CYP3A inhibitors or inducers, CYP2D6 and P-gp substrates. Patients with preexisting liver disease, liver enzyme abnormalities or hepatitis. Patients with uncontrolled or undiagnosed HIV-1 infection are at risk of developing resistance to HIV protease inhibitors. Women of childbearing potential not using contraception. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },

            "content": "<b>Tab - Adults:</b> 1 tab. <b>Childn 6-12 yrs:</b> &frac12;-1 tab; <b>2-6 yrs:</b> &frac12; tab. <b>Syrup - Adults:</b> 10 mL. <b>Childn < 6 yrs:</b> 5 mL. <b>6-12 yrs:</b> 5 -10 mL. All doses to be taken 3x a day."

          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hyperthyroidism, DM, serious CV disorders, HTN and peptic ulcers. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C for salbutamol and guaifenesin.",

              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of ear, nose, and throat (ENT) and genitourinary tract (GUT) infections; uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections; acute otitis media; lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Infants >3 months and childn < 40 kg - Recommended dose:</b> 25-50 mg/kg/day in 2-3 divided doses; <b>ENT, GUT, or skin and skin structure infections -</b> Mild to moderate: 25 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses or 20 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses; Severe: 45 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses or 40 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses; <b>Acute otitis media:</b> Mild, moderate, or severe: 80-90 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses; <b>LRTI:</b> Mild, moderate, or severe: 45 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. <b>Neonates and infants < 3 months:</b> 20-30 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. <b>Usual duration:</b> 5-14 days depending on severity and type of infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with infectious mononucleosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cross-sensitivity with cephalosporins. CDAD and colitis. Maintain adequate fluid intake. Patients with renal impairment. Periodic assessment of organ system functions and overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms during prolonged therapy. May interfere with protein testing when colorimetric methods are used. Infants &le;3 months. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dermatologic; GI; nervous, hemic, and lymphatic system; hepatic; and renal effects. <b>Childn:</b> Tooth discoloration (brown, yellow, or gray)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Allopurinol, anticoagulants, bacteriostatic agents, beta-lactam inhibitors, digoxin, methotrexate, oral contraceptives, probenecid. False positive Clinitest and Benedict’s soln. May interfere with protein testing (colorimetric methods)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P149.00), 105 mL (P165.00). Powder for suspension (oral drops) 100 mg/mL x 10 mL (P89.00)."
          }

            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Pneumonia, lung abscess, otitis media, pharyngitis, tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, scarlet fever, peritonitis, intra-abdominal abscess, endometritis, tubo-ovarian abscess, furunculosis, skin abscess, impetigo, acne pustule, cellulitis, wound infections. <b>Cap</b>: Empyema. Erysipelas, nail wall infections. Osteomyelitis and septic arthritis. Salpingitis, cervical area infections, pelvic inflammatory disease in combination with an antibiotic, cervicitis caused by <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>. Periodontal abscess and periodontitis. <b>IM/IV</b>: Pelvic cellulitis, post-op vaginal cuff infection, septicemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap - Adults and adolescents &gt;14 yrs</b>: 600-1,800 mg/day in 3-4 equal doses. <b>Childn and adolescents</b>: 8-25 mg/kg/day depending on location and severity of infection. Treatment should last for at least 10 days in infections due to beta-hemolytic streptococci. <b>IM/IV - Serious infections</b> - Adults: 600-1,200 mg/day divided in 2-4 equal doses; Childn &gt;1 month: 15-25 mg/kg/day in 3-4 equal doses. <b>More severe infections</b> - Adults: 1,200-2,700 mg/day in 2-4 equal doses; Childn &gt;1 month: 25-40 mg/kg/day in 3-4 equal doses; Neonates &lt;1 month: 15-20 mg/kg/day in 3-4 equal doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic or renal impairment. History of GI disease especially colitis. Atopic individuals. Dysphagia. Not to be used in the treatment of meningitis. Consider allergic cross-reaction between clindamycin and penicillin. Pregnancy. <b>Cap</b>: <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. <b>IM/IV</b>: Not to be injected direct rapid IV. Neonates and immature fetus. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pseudomembranous colitis, diarrhea, maculopapular rash, abnormal liver function test, eosinophilia. <b>IM/IV</b>: Pain, insensibility and sterile abscess, thrombophlebitis; nausea, vomiting, anorexia, glossitis, stomatitis, abdominal pain and esophagitis; urticaria and edema; SJS, Lyell’s syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis; erythema multiforme; azotemia, oliguria, proteinuria; neutropenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenic purpura, aplastic anemia; tinnitus, dizziness; facial blush, bitter taste, fever, headache, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Neuromuscular blocking agents, erythromycin, CYP3A4 and CYP3A5 inhibitors, vit K antagonists."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 300 mg (P34.00). Solution for injection (IM/IV) 150 mg/mL x 2 mL (P334.20), 4 mL (P501.30)."
          }

  {

      "data": {

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/PzQmv9To9FE0nbtWF6Axxx271rGUbjsTvJrHNhcbPlH3x2acis.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ekpGpsIjXIHBgI915NOOozFkTKn43ZmyJFThkoxlI2nWMzjmKQ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cKk8LTDi8o2ZiVSLnx5JaSTRXLpRsSAgyzzwlt5syuugUPby9a.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Esomeprazole (Cap: as magnesium dihydrate; IV: as sodium)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), <i>H. pylori</i>-associated ulcers, NSAID-associated ulcers, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. <b>Cap</b>: Prolonged treatment after IV-induced prevention of rebleeding of peptic ulcers. <b>IV</b>: Prevention of rebleeding following therapeutic endoscopy for acute bleeding gastric or duodenal ulcers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap - Adults and adolescents from 12 yrs - Treatment of erosive reflux esophagitis</b>: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks; <b>Long-term management of patients with healed esophagitis to prevent relapse</b>: 20 mg once daily; <b>Symptomatic treatment of GERD</b>: 20 mg once daily in patients without esophagitis, subsequently 20 mg for symptom control. Adults - <b>Treatment and prevention of <i>H. pylori</i>-associated ulcers</b>: 20 mg esomeprazole with 1 g amoxicillin and 500 mg clarithromycin, all twice daily for 7 days. <b>Healing of gastric ulcers associated with NSAID therapy</b>: 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>Prevention of gastric and duodenal ulcers associated with NSAID therapy in patients at risk</b>: 20 mg once daily; <b>Prevention of re-bleeding of peptic ulcers</b>: 20 mg once daily. <b>Prolonged treatment after IV-induced prevention of re-bleeding of peptic ulcers</b>: 40 mg once daily for 4 weeks. <b>Treatment of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: Initially 40 mg twice daily. Max 80-160 mg daily. Doses &gt;80 mg daily should be divided and given twice daily. <b>Severe hepatic impairment</b>: Max dose 20 mg should not be exceeded. <b>IV - Adults - Gastric antisecretory treatment</b>: 20-40 mg once daily; <b>Reflux esophagitis</b>: 40 mg once daily; <b>Symptomatic treatment of reflux disease, healing of gastric ulcers associated with NSAID therapy</b>: 20 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of re-bleeding of gastric and duodenal ulcers</b>: Following therapeutic endoscopy, 80 mg as bolus infusion over 30 mins followed by continuous IV infusion 8 mg/hr over 72 hrs. <b>Severe liver impairment</b> - GERD: Max 20 mg. Bleeding ulcers: Initial bolus infusion dose of 80 mg then continuous IV infusion of 4 mg/hr for 71.5 hrs. <b>Childn 12-18 yrs - Erosive reflux esophagitis</b>: 40 mg once daily; <b>GERD</b>: 20 mg once daily. <b>1-11 yrs - Erosive reflux esophagitis</b> - &ge;20 kg: 10-20 mg once daily; &lt;20 kg: 10 mg once daily. <b>GERD</b>: 10 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with nelfinavir. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild to moderate liver dysfunction or severe renal dysfunction. Long-term treatment (&gt;1 yr). Fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency. Contains parahydroxybenzoates. Co-administration of atazanavir. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Pregnancy. <b>IV</b>: Hypomagnesemia, risk of hip, wrist and spine fracture, reduced vit B<sub>12</sub> absorption.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache. Abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea/vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole and itraconazole. Diazepam, citalopram, imipramine, clomipramine, phenytoin. Warfarin. Cisapride. Clarithromycin. Digoxin, rifampicin, St. John’s wort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Delayed-release capsule 20 mg (P36.33), 40 mg (P50.12). Powder for solution for injection (IV) 40 mg (P572.90)."
          }

  {
    "id": 4460,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4460,
        "brand_name": "Pexitas 500",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pemetrexed",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Folic Acid Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of chemotherapy-naive patients with unresectable malignant pleural mesothelioma in combination with cisplatin. Treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer other than predominantly squamous cell histology: (1) 1<sup>st</sup>-line in combination with cisplatin, (2) maintenance as monotherapy in patients whose disease has not progressed immediately following platinum-based chemotherapy, and (3) 2<sup>nd</sup>-line as monotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses given via IV infusion over 10 mins on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. Reconstitute and dilute with preservative-free normal saline inj. <b>In combination with cisplatin:</b> 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> before 2 hrs infusion of 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> cisplatin. Antiemetics and appropriate hydration must be given prior and/or after receiving cisplatin. <b>Monotherapy:</b> 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. <b>Pre-medication regimen:</b> Give corticosteroid (4 mg oral dexamethasone 2x daily) prior to, the same day and day after each dose; oral folic acid or multivitamin containing 350-1,000 mcg folic acid daily, at least 5 doses for 7 days prior to 1<sup>st</sup> dose of treatment, continued throughout therapy and on day 21 after last dose; 1,000 mcg vit B<sub>12</sub> IM 1 week prior to 1<sup>st</sup> dose of treatment and once on the same day every 3 cycles. Prior to start of any cycle, patient should have ANC &ge;1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup> and platelets &ge;100,000 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>; total bilirubin &le;1.5x ULN; alkaline phosphate, AST/SGOT, and ALT/SGPT &le;3x ULN or &le;5x ULN if liver has tumor involvement. See complete product insert for preparation method and dose modifications during toxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with yellow fever vaccine. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Contact on skin and mucous membranes. Patients with renal (CrCl < 45 mL/min) or hepatic (bilirubin >1.5x ULN, aminotransferase >3x ULN without hepatic metastases or >5x ULN with hepatic metastases) impairment; risk factors for the development of renal events (e.g. dehydration, preexisting HTN or diabetes) and CV disease; pleural effusion or ascites; on a controlled sodium diet. Bone marrow suppression; myelosuppression; skin reactions; serious renal events including acute renal failure; severe dehydration; serious CV events including MI and cerebrovascular events; immunodepression; radiation pneumonitis or recall. Concomitant use with NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen, aspirin >1.3 g daily) or radiotherapy. Incompatibility with calcium containing (e.g. Lactated Ringer’s and Ringer’s inj). Monitor CBC including differential WBC and platelet count and evaluate renal and hepatic function using blood chemistry tests prior each dose. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Irreversible men infertility. Use contraception and avoid fathering a child during and 6 months after treatment. Women of childbearing potential.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Decreased neutrophils/granulocytes, leucocytes, Hgb, platelets; sensory neuropathy; diarrhea, vomiting, stomatitis/pharyngitis, nausea, anorexia, constipation; rash, alopecia; elevated creatinine, decreased CrCl; fatigue. Dehydration; taste disturbance; conjunctivitis; dyspepsia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, platinum compounds, ciclosporin; probenecid, penicillin; high doses of NSAIDs (e.g. ibuprofen >1.6 g/day, aspirin &ge;1.3 g/day; piroxicam, rofecoxib; oral anticoagulants; live attenuated vaccines. Incompatibility with calcium-containing diluents (e.g. Lactated Ringer’s and Ringer’s inj)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for IV infusion 500 mg (P17,857.14)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4654,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4654,
        "brand_name": "Philcort-16",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OB0cZPp1K1HDkkXvduWHaIgRCkG2w4dEEbUBp7yNfX7HgCKOTP.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TBUC4VU8cTYpz2KzmFfQ8jVayP6GD8IacsmjGo974wFAHbONqp.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/W2p3pTOpViQig8OOkTQsODKCAOt2Kybww47GhJN0furNcrluyo.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Methylprednisolone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Endocrine (primary or secondary adrenocortical insufficiency); adjunct therapy for short-term administration of rheumatic disorders; exacerbation or as maintenance therapy in selected cases of collagen diseases; dermatologic diseases; control of severe or incapacitating allergic conditions; severe acute or chronic allergic and inflammatory processes involving the eye and its adnexa; gastrointestinal, respiratory, hematologic diseases/disorders; palliative management of neoplastic diseases; edematous states (induce diuresis or remission of proteinuria in nephrotic syndrome, without uremia, of the idiopathic type or that due to lupus erythematosus); acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis, and management of edema associated with brain tumor; organ transplantation; tuberculosis meningitis with subarachnoid block or impending block; trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially, 4-48 mg/day depending on the specific disease. <b>Cerebral edema</b>: 200-1,000 mg/day. Organ transplantation: up to 7 mg/kg/day. Acute exacerbations of multiple sclerosis: 500 mg/day for 5 days or 1000 mg/day for 3 days. Maintenance dose should be determined by decreasing dose in small decrements. Discontinue treatment gradually after long-term therapy. <b>Alternate day therapy</b>: Twice the usual daily dose is administered every other morning to provide patient requiring long-term dose treatment while minimizing certain undesirable effects including pituitary-adrenal suppression, Cushingoid state, corticoid withdrawal symptoms, and growth suppression in childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with systemic infections, unless specific anti-infective therapy is given. Administration of live or live attenuated vaccines. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with known or suspected parasitic infections, active tuberculosis, hypersensitivity, Cushing’s disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes mellitus, seizure disorders, myasthenia gravis, Duchenne’s muscular dystrophy, ocular herpes simplex, thromboembolic disorders, HTN, hepatic failure, osteoporosis, steroid myopathy, systemic sclerosis. Childn. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infections and infestations, leukocytosis, steroid withdrawal syndrome, metabolic acidosis, psychiatric, nervous system, eye, ear and labyrinth, cardiac, vascular, respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, skin and SC tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, reproductive system, and breast problems."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, antiemetics, ciclosporin, macrolide antibacterials, indinavir, ritonavir, diltiazem, isoniazid, oral contraceptives, grapefruit juice), inducers (e.g. phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine, primidone, rifampicin, rifabutin), and substrates (e.g. cyclophosphamide, tacrolimus). Antacids, antidiabetic agents, anticholinergics, anticholinesterases, oral anticoagulants, aromatase inhibitors, cardiac glycosides, diuretics and other potassium depleting agents, mifepristone, NSAIDs, somatropin, sympathomimetics, vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 16 mg (P31.00)."

  {
    "id": 3473,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3473,
        "brand_name": "Piozone",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pioglitazone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Thiazolidinediones (Glitazones)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus as monotherapy or in combination with a sulfonylurea, metformin, or insulin when adequate glycemic control is not achieved by diet and exercise."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy:</b> Dose may be titrated in increments of 15 mg up to max 45 mg daily. <b>Patients without congestive heart failure (CHF):</b> Initially 15 or 30 mg once daily taken with or without meals. <b>Patients with CHF NYHA Class I or II:</b> Initially 15 mg once daily. <b>Combination therapy</b> – With metformin: Initially 15 or 30 mg once daily; continue current metformin dose. With sulfonylureas: Initially 15 or 30 mg once daily; continue current sulfonylurea dose. Decrease sulfonylurea dose in case of hypoglycemia. With insulin: Continue current insulin dose. Decrease insulin dose by 10-25% in case of hypoglycemia or FBS < 100 mg/dL. Individualize further adjustments based on glucose-lowering response. <b>Coadministration with strong CYP2C8 inhibitors:</b> Max 15 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. CHF NYHA Class III or IV. Severe hepatic impairment, ALT >2.5x ULN, or active liver disease. Type 1 DM, diabetic ketoacidosis. Active bladder cancer. Dialysis patients. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with existing edema or heart failure. History of CAD, CABG, MI. Use the lowest dose for patients with at least one risk factor for CHF. History of bladder cancer. Increased risk of fractures in women. Hypoglycemia. May cause ovulation in anovulatory premenopausal women with insulin resistance. Decreases in hemoglobin and hematocrit. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Undesirable effects on respiratory, endocrine, CV, CNS, musculoskeletal, hepatic, hematologic, renal, eye, and GI systems. Tumors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral contraceptives e.g. norethindrone/ethinylestradiol, insulin, insulin secretagogues e.g. sulfonylureas, midazolam, strong CYP2C8 inhibitors e.g. gemfibrozil, CYP2C8 inducers e.g. rifampicin, CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g.ketoconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 15 mg (P20.00), 30 mg (P29.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3335,
          "name": "LRI Therapharma"
        },

  {
    "id": 784,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 784,
        "brand_name": "Piptaz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/naDG14SKoxiuRoydmSxAUhObyCaO6UbWNHD0Aa6Wr2QII6Nq8n.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tvqwviPBVM101S8CLFdp2DZbKwdOWHuPeJb1BkgKTiVuFleRjp.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6MmrxJrOC5hshEqmf3DFBDxPYJO63m6vrtTlvSfV9Q5HF2tO2H.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Piperacillin, tazobactam",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of multidrug-resistant G(-) infections due to organisms with known or suspected susceptibility to Piperacillin/Tazobactam except CNS infections; polymicrobial infections (e.g. mixed aerobic and anaerobic infections in which other agents have insufficient activity or are contraindicated due to toxic potential)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered via IV infusion over 30 min. <b>Adults:</b> 3 g/375 mg every 6 hrs; <b>Nosocomial pneumonia:</b> Initially 4 g/500 mg. <b>Renal impairment - All indications except nosocomial pneumonia:</b> CrCl 20-40 mL/min: 2 g/250 mg every 6 hrs; < 20 mL/min: 2 g/250 mg every 8 hrs; Hemodialysis: 2 g/250 mg mg every 12 hrs, with additional dose of 0.75 g after each session; CAPD: 2 g/250 mg every 12 hrs; <b>Nosocomial pneumonia:</b> CrCl 20-40 mL/min: 3 g/375 mg every 6 hrs; < 20 mL/min: 2 g/250 mg every 6 hrs; Hemodialysis: 2 g/250 mg every 8 hrs, with additional dose of 0.75 g after each session; CAPD: 2 g/250 mg every 8 hrs. <b>Childn weighing >40 kg:</b> 3 g/375 mg every 6 hrs with aminoglycoside or 4 g/500 mg every 6 hrs; <b>Childn &ge;9 months weighing up to 40 kg:</b> 100 mg/12.5 mg per kg BW every 8 hrs; <b>2-9 months:</b> 80 mg/10 mg per kg BW every 8 hrs. <b>Treatment duration -</b> Usual: 7-10 days; Nosocomial pneumonia: 7-14 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, beta-lactam antibiotics, tetracyclines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with cystic fibrosis, bowel inflammation, bleeding problems, CHF, renal impairment, history of severe diarrhea or bowel problems due to antibiotics, low blood potasssium levels. Patients on dialysis or salt-restricted diet. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Agitation, constipation, diarrhea, dizziness, headache, indigestion, nausea, pain; swelling, redness, or inflammation at injection site; sleeplessness, vomiting, severe allergic reactions, bloody stools, chest pain, decreased urination, depression, fainting; fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat; fever, chills, sore throat, hallucination, prolonged muscle relaxation; red, swollen, or blistered skin; seizure, severe diarrhea, vomiting, stomach pain, shortness of breath; hand, feet, or ankle swelling; unusual tiredness or weakness, vaginal irritation or discharge, vein inflammation or tenderness, yellow of eyes or skin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminoglycosides (e.g. tobramycin), oral contraceptives; anticoagulants, diuretics (e.g. furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide); heparin, methotrexate, nondepolarizing muscle relaxants (e.g. vecuronium); probenecid; tetracyclines (e.g. doxycycline)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 2 g/250 mg (P822.69), 4 g/500 mg (P1,430.94)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 217,
          "name": "United American Pharmaceuticals, Inc."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pitavastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunctive therapy to diet to reduce elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, triglycerides, and to increase HDL-C in adult patients with primary hyperlipidemia or mixed dyslipidemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 2 mg/day. Max 4 mg. <b>Moderate and severe renal impairment and ESRD patients receiving hemodialysis:</b> 1 mg once daily. Max 2 mg once daily. <b>Patients taking erythromycin:</b> Max 1 mg once daily; <b>rifampicin:</b> Max 2 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease, including unexplained persistent elevations of hepatic transaminase levels. Coadministration with ciclosporin. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with predisposing factors for myopathy; impaired renal function; taking fibrates or lipid-modifying doses of niacin, colchicine. Temporarily withhold treatment in patients with an acute, serious condition suggestive of myopathy or predisposing to development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Liver enzyme abnormalities. Alcohol consumption. Increase in HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuria, acute renal failure, and myopathy. Arthralgia, headache, influenza, nasopharyngitis. Elevated creatine phosphokinase, hepatic transaminases, alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and glucose. Rash, pruritus, urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, erythromycin, rifampin, gemfibrozil and other fibrates, niacin, colchicine, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2 mg (P32.86), 4 mg (P38.08)."
          }
        ],

        "id": 4308,
        "brand_name": "Pixab",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tB0YpZzwrhXVrQTxsbHsSFYu3KqCMGhwpK4tT7Cax6r9VRH7gt.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hbzUxoVINaujju5JCoyK6SDAMnB1SurVOeQvcOnf44tJ0T5jC4.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/oMdIPc00WJu8liBUGRfwHJlcEWRBNLwKVJGU9BMwJHt6sQHF6Q.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in adults who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery. To reduce the risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and death in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with &ge;1 risk factors, including patients unsuitable for warfarin. Treatment and prevention of (recurrent) deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of VTE in elective hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> Initially 2.5 mg twice daily taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Duration of treatment: 32-38 days for hip replacement surgery; 10-14 days for knee replacement surgery.<b> Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism, patients with NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily. <b>Patients with at least 2 risk factors (&ge;80 yrs, &le;60 kg BW, or serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL [133 mmol/L]):</b> 2.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for 7 days followed by 5 mg twice daily. Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: 2.5 mg twice daily after 6 months of treatment. <b>Surgery and invasive procedures, patients not previously treated with anticoagulants:</b> At least 5 doses of 5 mg twice daily (2.5 mg twice daily if for dose reduction) twice daily before cardioversion. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of Apixaban: 10 mg loading dose, followed by 5 mg twice daily, may be reduced to 5 mg loading dose followed by 2.5 mg twice daily. Loading dose should be given at least 2 hrs before cardioversion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Clinically significant active bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Conditions with increased risk of hemorrhage. Patients with hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk; undergoing hip fracture surgery; prosthetic heart valves with or without atrial fibrillation. Temporarily discontinue for active bleeding, elective surgery, or invasive procedures; avoid lapses in therapy and restart as soon as possible. Risk of developing spinal or epidural hematoma during spinal/epidural anesthesia or puncture which can result in long-term or permanent paralysis. Indwelling epidural or intrathecal catheters must be removed at least 5 hrs prior to the 1<sup>st</sup> dose. Monitor for signs and symptoms of neurological impairment. Patients with history of thrombosis who are diagnosed with antiphospholipid syndrome. Patients with CrCl < 15 mL/min or those undergoing dialysis or with severe hepatic impairment. Mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B). Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, hemorrhage, hematoma, epistaxis. Nausea, GI hemorrhage, hematuria, contusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole. Diltiazem, naproxen, clarithromycin, amiodarone, verapamil, quinidine. Rifampin. Phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John’s wort. Enoxaparin, NSAIDs, aspirin, P2Y12 inhibitors. Agents associated with serious bleeding e.g. unfractionated heparin and heparin derivatives (LMWH), FXa inhibiting oligosaccharides e.g. fondaparinux, direct thrombin II inhibitors e.g. desirudin, thrombolytic agents, GPIIb/IIa receptor antagonists, dipyridamole, dextran, sulfinpyrazone, vit K antagonist, and other oral anticoagulants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg (P25.00), 5 mg (P36.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Piperacillin sodium, tazobactam sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly</b>: Treatment of lower respiratory tract infection, complicated and uncomplicated UTI, skin and skin structure infections, bacterial septicemia, and bacterial infections in neutropenic adults in combination with aminoglycosides. <b>Childn</b>: Bacterial infections in neutropenic childn in combination with aminoglycosides, appendicitis complicated by rupture with peritonitis and/or abscess formation in childn 2-12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer via slow IV injection (over at least 3-5 minutes or slow IV infusion (&gt;20-30 minutes). <b>Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: 4.5 g every 8 hrs. Total daily dose: 2-25 g-4.5 g every 6-8 hrs. <b>Neutropenia</b>: 4.5 g every 6 hrs in combination with aminoglycosides. <b>Renal insufficiency</b> – CrCl 20-80 mL/min: 4.5 g every 8 hrs; &lt;20 mL/min and hemodialysis: 4.5 g every 12 hrs. Administer additional 2.25 g each dialysis period. <b>Childn &lt;12 yrs – Neutropenia</b>: 90 mg/kg every 6 hrs in combination with aminoglycoside; max 4.5 g every 6 hrs. <b>Childn 2-12 yrs – Complicated appendicitis</b>: 112.5 mg/kg every 8 hrs, not exceeding 4.5 g every 8 hrs; for minimum 5 days to max 14 days. <b>Renal insufficiency</b> – CrCl 20-39 mL/min: 90 mg/kg every 8 hrs, not exceeding 13.5 g/days; &lt;20 mL/min: 90 mg/kg every 12 hrs, not exceeding 9 g/day. For childn &lt;50 kg on hemodialysis: 45 mg/kg every 8 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, or lactamase inhibitors. Patients with <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For single use. Patients with renal failure, history of allergic reactions to any penicillins, cephalosporins, lactamase inhibitors. Discontinue use if allergic reaction occurs. Patients requiring restricted salt intake. Perform periodic electrolyte determination in patients with low potassium reserves. Discontinue if CDAD is suspected or confirmed, and bleeding manifestation occur. Patients may experience neuromuscular excitability or convulsions if higher doses are given IV. Evaluate patients with gonorrhea for syphilis. Childn &lt;2 months. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Candidal superinfection. Leucopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia. Headache, insomnia. Hypotension, phlebitis, thrombophlebitis. Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting. Increase in ALT and AST. Rash, pruritus, urticaria, erythema, increase in blood creatinine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, tobramycin, heparin, oral anticoagulants, and other drugs that affect the blood coagulation system or thrombocyte functions. Methotrexate. False positive reaction for glucose in the urine using copper-reduction method."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IV) 4.5 g."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4899,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4899,
        "brand_name": "PK-Merz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Amantadine sulphate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of symptoms of Parkinson’s disease (e.g. stiffness, trembling, and diminished movement or motionless) and movement disorders similar to Parkinson’s disease caused by certain drugs (neuroleptics and drugs with similar mechanism of action), and extrapyramidal symptoms (e.g. early dyskinesia, akathisia, and parkinsonism)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 100 mg once daily for first 4-7 days, followed by once-weekly increase until maintenance dose is reached. Usual effective dose: 200-600 mg once daily. <b>Elderly - States of agitation and confusion or delirious syndromes:</b> Lower dose. <b>Previously treated with amantadine infusion soln:</b> Can start with higher dose. <b>Renal impairment – GFR 80-60 mL/min:</b> 100 mg every 12 hrs; <b>60-50 mL/min:</b> 200 mg and 100 mg (alternate days); <b>50-30 mL/min:</b> 100 mg once daily; <b>30-20 mL/min:</b> 200 mg twice a week; <b>20-10 mL/min:</b> 100 mg thrice a week; <b>< 10 and hemodialysis patients:</b> 200 mg and 100 mg once a week or once every 2 weeks. Taken with little liquid in the morning and afternoon. Do not take the last daily dose later than 4 pm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe decompensated heart failure (NYHA class IV). Cardiomyopathies. Myocarditis. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Existing bradycardia < 55 beats/min. Known prolonged QT interval (Bazett QTc >420 ms) or discernible U-waves or congenital QT syndrome in the family anamnesis. History of serious ventricular arrhythmias (e.g. torsade de pointes). Influenza virus A infection. Rare hereditary galactose intolerance. Coadministration with budipine or other QT prolonging drugs. Reduced levels of potassium or magnesium in blood."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Patients with renal insufficiency, prostatic hypertrophy, narrow-angle glaucoma, risks of electrolyte imbalances, cardiac pacemakers. Record ECG (50 mm/s) prior and 1 and 3 weeks after administration, prior and 2 weeks after any subsequent dose increase, and at least once a year. Manually determine the Bazett frequency-corrected QT time. Discontinue in patients with baseline >420 msQTc values, increase of >60 ms or >480 ms QTc during treatment, and discernible U waves; palpitations, dizziness, or syncope. Give amantadine infusion if acute worsening of parkinsonian symptoms (e.g. akinetic crisis) occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Planning of pregnancy. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, sleep disturbances, motor and psychiatric agitation, paranoid exogenous psychoses accompanied by visual hallucinations (elderly), urinary retention in case of prostatic hypertrophy, livedo reticularis sometimes associated with lower-leg and ankle edema, nausea, dry mouth, orthostatic dysregulation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "QT prolonging drugs, anticholinergics, indirectly CNS -active sympathomimetics, alcohol, memantine, triamterene/HCTZ diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 100 mg."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduction of atherothrombotic events in patients with recent myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, or established peripheral arterial disease (PAD), and acute coronary syndrome ACS."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>ACS:</b> Administered in conjunction with aspirin. 300 mg loading dose then continue at 75 mg daily. Recent MI, stroke, or established <b>PAD:</b> 75 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment and active pathological bleeding e.g. peptic ulcer or intracranial hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Diminished antiplatelet activity in patients with CYP2C19 function. General risk of bleeding. Discontinuation of clopidogrel increases the risk of CV events. Risk of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). Cross-reactivity among thienopyridines. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bleeding, GI hemorrhage. Chest pain, accidental/inflicted injury, influenza-like symptoms. Headache, dizziness, pain, fatigue. Edema, HTN. Abdominal pain, dyspepsia, diarrhea, nausea. Hypercholesterolemia. Arthralgia, back pain. Bruise, epistaxis. Depression. URTI, dyspnea, rhinitis, bronchitis, coughing, rash, pruritus. UTI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole or esomeprazole). NSAIDs, warfarin, SSRIs and SNRIs, repaglinide."
          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of atherosclerotic events in patients with history of recent myocardial infarction (MI) (within a few days until < 35 days from occurrence), recent ischemic stroke (from 7 days until < 6 months) or established peripheral artery disease (PAD), and patients with non-ST segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (ACS) (unstable angina/non-Q wave MI) including patients who are managed medically with percutaneous coronary intervention (with or without stent) or coronary artery bypass graft. Prophylaxis as an alternative to aspirin in patients at risk of thromboembolic disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Recent MI, stroke, established PAD, or as prophylaxis of thromboembolic events:</b> 75 mg once daily. <b>Non-ST segment elevation ACS:</b> 300 mg single loading dose; continue at 75 mg once daily in combination with aspirin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Presence of any pathological bleeding or coagulation disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cases of thrombocytopenic purpura. Patients with platelet disorders and/or at increased risk of bleeding, severe hepatic or renal impairment. Consider discontinuation 5 days prior elective surgery except in patients with cardiac stents that have not completed dual antiplatelet therapy. Patients < 21 yrs.             "content": "Immunization against pneumococcal disease caused by pneumococcal types included in the vaccine. Vaccination with Pneumovax 23 is recommended in selected immunocompetent and immunocompromised individuals. <b>(1) Immunocompetent persons:</b> (a) Routine vaccination for persons &ge;50 yrs; (b) Persons &ge;2 yrs with chronic cardiovascular disease (e.g. congestive heart failure and cardiomyopathies), chronic pulmonary disease (e.g. chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and emphysema), or diabetes mellitus; (c) Persons &ge;2 yrs with alcoholism, chronic liver disease (e.g. cirrhosis) or cerebrospinal fluid leaks; (d) Persons &ge;2 yrs with functional or anatomic asplenia (e.g. sickle cell disease and splenectomy); (e) Persons &ge;2 yrs living in special environments or social settings (e.g. Alaskan Natives and certain American Indian populations). <b>(2) Immunocompromised persons:</b> (a) Persons &ge;2 yrs, including those with HIV infection, leukemia, lymphoma, Hodgkin’s disease, multiple myeloma, generalized malignancy, chronic renal failure or nephrotic syndrome; (b) Those receiving immunosuppressive chemotherapy (e.g. corticosteroids); (c) Those who have received an organ or bone marrow transplant."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "0.5 mL single dose, SC or IM (preferably in the deltoid muscle or lateral mid-thigh)."
          },

            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Persons receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Intradermal administration may cause severe local reactions. Patients with severely compromised CV and/or pulmonary function.             "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Vit C:</b> High doses: Stomach upset and diarrhea; formation of oxalate stones; disturbed water and electrolyte balance, increased hemolysis, increased calcium in the kidneys and suppression of cobalamine (vit B12) activity; hemolysis in patients with G6PD deficiency; painful urination or pink/bloody urine; rebound scurvy. <b>Zinc:</b> >40 mg/day elemental zinc: GI effects e.g. nausea, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Vit C:</b> Iron, aspirin, paracetamol, aminophylline, bleomycin, erythromycin, lactobionate, nafcillin, sodium nitrofurantoin, conjugated estrogens, sodium bicarbonate, sulfafurazole, diethanolamine, chloramphenicol, sodium succinate, chlorothiazide sodium, and hydrocortisone sodium succinate. Alcohol or tobacco."

            "content": "<b>Vit C:</b> >2 g/day: Stomach upset and diarrhea.             "content": "Fluid retention.             "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."

                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }

            }
          },

    "detail": {

      "data": {
        "id": 1026,
        "brand_name": "Pradaxa",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/g9kHD8G12HbYw3lOqt4uSouCFNnGCuPFLr4CxlhL5FCwj8nJrr.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/H358FMKUDopNYUrp5ItMeno8eqlD20nP0fZRYAsfZDQykO8QAZ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wXvfPuEuz0HuSWPJdFECDUcxCApnTm1SgHSGveKPiZpKV6kMRN.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dabigatran etexilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and/or pulmonary embolism (PE) and prevention of related deaths. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism and reduction of vascular mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation; venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients who have undergone major orthopedic surgery; recurrent DVT and/or PE and related deaths."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Primary Prevention of VTE in patients who have undergone major orthopedic surgery:</b> 220 mg once daily; moderate renal impairment: 150 mg once daily (2 caps of 75 mg); <b>following knee or hip replacement surgery:</b> Initially 1 cap of 110 mg (mild to moderate renal impairment: 75 mg) within 1-4 hrs of completed surgery, continued with 2 caps of 110 mg (mild to moderate renal impairment: 2 caps of 75 mg) once daily for 10 days (knee replacement surgery) or 28 -35 days (hip replacement surgery) total. For both surgeries, if hemostasis is not secured, delay initiation of treatment. If treatment is not started on the day of surgery, initiate with 2 caps once daily. <b>Prevention of stroke, systemic embolism, and reduction of vascular mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation:</b> 150 mg or 110 mg (elderly &ge;80 yrs or with &ge;1 of risk factors of bleeding) 2x daily for life -long. Assess renal function in patients with CrCl 30-50 mL/min at least once a yr. <b>Treatment of acute DVT and/or PE and prevention of related death:</b> 150 mg 2x daily following parenteral anticoagulant for &ge;5 days, continued to max 6 months. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and/or PE and related death:</b> 150 mg 2x daily, may continue for life-long depending on individual patient risk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Hemorrhagic manifestations, bleeding diathesis, spontaneous or pharmacological impairment of hemostasis. Organ lesions at risk of clinically significant bleeding including hemorrhagic stroke within the last 6 months. Concomitant treatment with systemic ketoconazole. Prosthetic heart valve replacement."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with recent biopsy or major trauma and receiving treatments liable to increase the hemorrhagic risk, bacterial endocarditis, renal insufficiency, spinal/epidural anesthesia and lumbar puncture. Concomitant use with dronedarone. May cause false positive INR elevations. Discontinue treatment if acute renal failure develops; &ge;24 hrs prior surgical interventions. Assess renal function prior and during treatment and certain clinical situations when renal function is suspected to decline or deteriorate (e.g. hypovolemia, dehydration, comedications, etc.). Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >75 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bleeding or signs of bleeding, e.g. anemia and wound discharge. Abnormal hepatic function."

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1337,

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,

          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dexmedetomidine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Alpha-2 Selective Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Sedation of initially intubated and mechanically ventilated patients during treatment in an intensive care setting. Sedation/anxiolysis of non-intubated patients prior to and/or during surgical and other procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion. I<b>nitiation of ICU sedation - Adults:</b> Loading infusion of 1 mcg/kg over 10 mins; <b>Patients >65 yrs, and patients with impaired hepatic and renal function:</b> Consider dose reduction. <b>Maintenance of ICU sedation - Adults:</b> 0.2-0.7 mcg/kg/hr. Adjust rate of maintenance infusion to achieve desired level of sedation; <b>Patients >65 yrs and patients with impaired hepatic function:</b> Consider dose reduction. <b>Initiation of procedural sedation - Adults and for awake fiberoptic intubation patients:</b> Loading infusion of 1 mcg/kg over 10 mins; <b>For less invasive procedures (e.g. ophthalmic surgery), and patients >65 yrs:</b> Loading infusion of 0.5 mcg/kg over 10 mins; <b>Patients with impaired hepatic function:</b> Consider dose reduction. <b>Maintenance of procedural sedation - Adults:</b> 0.6 mcg/kg/hr and titrated to achieve desired clinical effect with doses ranging from 0.2-1 mcg/kg/hr. Adjust rate of maintenance infusion to achieve desired level of sedation; <b>For awake fiberoptic intubation patients:</b> 0.7 mcg/kg/hr until endotracheal tube is secured; <b>Patients >65 yrs and patients with impaired hepatic and renal function:</b> Consider dose reduction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not give infusions >24 hrs. Hypotension, bradycardia, sinus arrest. Transient HTN. Arousal and alertness. Patients with advanced heart block and/or severe ventricular dysfunction, hypovolemia, DM or chronic HTN. Concomitant use with vasodilators or negative chronotropic agents. Do not co-administered through the same IV catheter with blood or plasma. Discontinue when drug-related hyperthermia or pyrexia occurs. Monitor patients until body temp normalizes. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypotension, bradycardia, sinus arrest, transient HTN, dry mouth, fever, nausea, vomiting, hypoxia, tachycardia, anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sevoflurane, isoflurane, propofol, alfentanil, and midazolam. Incompatibility: Amphotericin B, diazepam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate solution for IV infusion 100 mcg/mL x 2 mL."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used in physiological doses for replacement therapy in adrenal insufficiency. Pharmacological doses are used when palliative anti-inflammatory or immunosuppressant effects are required."

            "content": "5-60 mg daily in divided doses, as a single daily dose after breakfast, as double dose on alternate days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Acute adrenal insufficiency may occur during prolonged treatment. Growth retardation in childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Cushingoid symptoms: moon face, hirsutism, buffalo hump, flushing, increased bruising, ecchymoses, striae, acne. Amenorrhea, hyperhidrosis, skin thinning, ocular changes, mental and neurological disturbances"
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

          }

            "content": "Primary and secondary adrenal insufficiency, congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Rheumatoid arthritis (RA), juvenile chronic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis. Allergic diseases including severe seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, drug hypersensitivity reactions, serum sickness, allergic contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma. Ophthalmic disease e.g. anterior and posterior uveitis, optic neuritis. Pulmonary sarcoid, fulminating or disseminated tuberculosis (with appropriate anti-TB chemotherapy), aspiration of gastric contents. Hematological disorders e.g. idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, autoimmue hemolytic anemia. Leukemia, malignant lymphoma. Ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease.             "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Recommended daily doses may be given as single dose or in divided doses, except alternate-day therapy (i.e. doubled minimum effective daily dose given every other day at 8 AM). <b>RA</b> - Severe: 12-16 mg; Moderately severe: 8-12 mg; Moderate and in childn: 4-8 mg. <b>Systemic dermatomyositis</b>: 48 mg. <b>SLE</b>: 20-100 mg. <b>Acute rheumatic fever</b>: 48 mg until ESR normal for 1 week. <b>Allergic diseases</b>: 12-40 mg. <b>Bronchial asthma</b>: Up to 64 mg single dose or alternate day up to max 100 mg. <b>Ophthalmic diseases</b>: 12-40 mg. <b>Hematological disorders and leukemias, malignant lymphoma</b>: 16-100 mg. <b>Ulcerative colitis</b>: 16-60 mg. <b>Crohn’s disease</b>: Up to 48 mg/day in acute episodes. <b>Organ transplantation</b>: Up to 3.6 mg/kg/day. <b>Pulmonary sarcoid</b>: 32-48 mg on alternate days. <b>GCA, PMR</b>: 64 mg. <b>Pemphigus vulgaris</b>: 80-360 mg."
          },
          {

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections, systemic infections unless specific anti-infective therapy is employed."

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>1<sup>st</sup> course</b>: 50 mg once daily for 5 days. Treatment may be started at any time in patients who have had no recent uterine bleeding. If progestin-induced bleeding is planned or spontaneous bleeding occurs prior to therapy, start at about the 5<sup>th</sup>  day of menstrual cycle. If ovulation do not occur, <b>2<sup>nd</sup> course</b>: 100 mg (two 50 mg tabs) once daily for 5 days. Start as early as 30 days after previous course. Do not increase dose or duration beyond 100 mg/day for 5 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or history of liver dysfunction. Hormone-dependent tumors or abnormal uterine bleeding of undetermined origin. Uncontrolled thyroid or adrenal dysfunction. Pituitary or ovarian tumors. Ovarian cysts (other than in association with PCOS) and pre-existing endometriosis. Childn and elderly. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May cause ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, occasional abdominal ovarian enlargement, PCOS, ovarian cyst formation, pain in the pelvic or abdominal area; visual symptoms e.g. spots or flashes (scintillating scotomata), diplopia, phosphenes, or photophobia; anovulatory disorders and tendency to develop endometrial carcinoma; ovarian cancer, pregnancy wastage, multiple pregnancy (simultaneous bilateral tubal pregnancy with chorionic gonadotropin), and ectopic pregnancy. Patients with uterine fibroids, hepatic impairment, pre-existing mental depression or thrombophlebitis, preexisting or family history of hyperlipidemia. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Benign, malignant, and unspecified neoplasms (e.g. cysts and polyps); metabolism and nutrition, psychiatric, nervous system, eye, cardiac and vascular, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, reproductive system and breast, congenital, familial and genetic disorders; pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal conditions; leukocytosis, thyroid disorder, tinnitus, increased urinary frequency or vol, fatigue, fever, weakness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Liver function test with sulfobromophthalein."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 50 mg (P150.50)."
          }
        ],
