        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LV28DEFbsX7jG0Z06BYC8uid0gngKv6cuN1VDXymUYjkxFF1MB.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/r9S0EgufHTuumTUy22EUzbjiS8suWVbZF6QfpACvMi6SHWHJTS.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/PdgCZbiWO5kavmLHfgZp38bmYEZwDmIIHf97wfXhWBCSVKA2x0.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pregabalin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gamma Amino Acids and Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of peripheral and central neuropathic pain and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in adults. Adjunct therapy in adults with partial seizures with or without secondary generalization."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "150-600 mg/day taken with or without food. All doses are given in 2-3 divided doses daily. <b>Neuropathic pain:</b> Initially 150 mg, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 3-7 days, to max 600 mg after another 7-day interval. <b>Epilepsy:</b> Initially 150 mg, may be increased to 300 mg after 1 week. Max 600 mg achieved after another week. <b>GAD:</b> Initially 150 mg, may be increased to 300 mg after 1 week, then increased to 450 mg after another week. Max 600 mg achieved after an additional week.  <b>Elderly:</b> dose reduction. <b>Renal impairment on hemodialysis - CrCl &ge;60 mL/min:</b> 150 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses, up to max 600 mg; <b>30-60 mL/min:</b> 75 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses, up to max 300 mg; <b>15-30 mL/min:</b> 25-50 mg/day in 1-2 divided doses, up to max 150 mg; <b>< 15 mL/min:</b> 25 mg as a single dose, max 75 mg. A single additional dose should be given immediately after every 4-hr hemodialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with diabetes, history of substance abuse, galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption, history of substance abuse. Concomitant use with anti-spasticity agents, opioids. May increase occurrence of accidental injury (fall) in the elderly. Loss of consciousness, confusion, mental impairment; loss or blurred vision, visual acuity and field changes; renal failure; CHF; CNS adverse reactions (e.g. somnolence) in the treatment of central neuropathic pain; suicidal ideation and behavior; intestinal obstruction, paralytic ileus; encephalopathy. Discontinue if symptoms of angioedema occur (e.g. facial, perioral, or upper airway swelling). Monitor for symptoms of misuse, abuse, or dependence. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 12 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, somnolence, headache; nasopharyngitis; increased appetite; confusion, irritability, insomnia, decreased libido; ataxia, abnormal coordination, tremor, dysarthria, amnesia, memory impairment, attention disturbances, paresthesia, hypoesthesia, sedation, balance disorder, lethargy; vertigo; vomiting, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, abdominal distension, dry mouth; muscle cramps, arthralgia, back and limb pain, cervical spasms; erectile dysfunction; peripheral edema, abnormal gait, fall, drunk or abnormal feeling, fatigue; increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 75 mg (P25.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Centrally-Acting Antihypertensives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of mild, moderate or severe hypertension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Initially 250 mg 2-3x a day for 2 days, then adjust every 2 days until adequate response is obtained. Start dose increase in the evening to minimize sedation. Max 3 g/day. <b>Elderly</b>: Initially 125 mg 2x a day then increase slowly. Max 2 g/day. <b>Childn < 12 yrs</b>: Initially 10 mg/kg in 2-4 divided doses. Max 65 mg/kg or 3 g/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active hepatic disease (e.g. acute hepatitis and active cirrhosis), phaeochromocytoma or paraganglioma. Depression. Porphyria.  Concomitant use with MAOIs. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue in presence of hemolytic anemia. May develop a positive Coombs test. History of previous liver disease or dysfunction. Renal impairment. Use of anesthesia. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sialadenitis. Blood and lymphatic system disorders. Hyperprolactinemia. Reversible mild psychoses or depression, decreased libido. Sedation, headache, dizziness, mental impairment. Orthostatic hypotension. Nasal congestion. GI disorders. Liver disorders including hepatitis, jaundice. Rash, TEN, angioedema, urticaria. Lupus-like syndrome, mild arthralgia, myalgia, breast enlargement, gynecomastia, amenorrhea, lactation disorder, erectile dysfunction, ejaculation failure, asthenia, edema (and weight gain)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, alprostadil, beta-blockers, CCB, diuretics, moxisylyte, nitrates, muscle relaxants, antidepressants, antihypertensives, antipsychotics, dopaminergics. Iron. Lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 250 mg."
          }
        ],

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1685,
        "brand_name": "Primigyn",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dinoprostone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Uterotonics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For ripening and dilatation of an unfavorable cervix in at-term pregnant women for labor induction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer entire contents into the endocervical canal (i.e. below the level of internal os/orifice of the uterus) using the catheter. Patients should remain recumbent or lying down on one side for 30 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to prostaglandins. History of cesarean section or major uterine surgery, difficult labor and/or traumatic delivery. Cephalopelvic disproportion is present. Grand multiparity with 6 or more previous pregnancy cases. Hyperactive or hypertonic uterine patterns. Fetal distress where delivery is not imminent. Patients in whom surgical intervention is warranted. Situations where vaginal delivery is not indicated as those with genital herpes, vasa previa or placenta previa, or unexplained vaginal bleeding during pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with glaucoma or raised IOP, asthma or history of asthma, pelvic infections, cardiac and lung diseases, renal and hepatic impairment.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, vaginal irritations, abdominal or back pain, headache, dizziness, uterine contractile abnormalities with or without fetal distress and intrapartum fetal bradycardia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Cervical gel 0.5 mg/3 g in syringe with catheter (P950.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3657,

      "data": {
        "id": 5047,

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients undergoing elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with one or more risk factors. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and for the prevention of recurrent DVT and PE."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of VTE after hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily starting 12-24 hours after surgery. <b>Treatment duration</b>- Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. <b>Hip replacement surgery:</b> 32-38 days. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily; elderly &ge;80 yrs, BW &le;60 kg, serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL: 2.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment. Taken with or without food. Tabs may be crushed and suspended in water, D5W, or apple juice or mixed with applesauce and promptly administered orally."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of bleeding including serious and potentially fatal hemorrhage. Patients with severe hepatic impairment, hepatic disease; associated with coagulopathy; renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min) or undergoing dialysis. Discontinue prior surgery or invasive procedure and restarted once adequate hemostasis is achieved. Patients with prosthetic heart valve or antiphospholipid syndrome. Switching from to or from other anticoagulants. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, hemorrhage, nausea, confusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir), inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St. John’s wort). Anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg (P33.75)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 414,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 414,

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7nB8QR4DwVmNZhDD7TabKLX9zcCAWYQFObwTkozGSEmiYcRBpx.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7nB8QR4DwVmNZhDD7TabKLX9zcCAWYQFObwTkozGSEmiYcRBpx.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5QOJE2GDhQv6nUqCCcs4c4Y4CbCMYqD8FOAjIheQI8DQGKaiKa.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefuroxime sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prophylaxis against infection to abdominal, pelvic, orthopedic, cardiac, pulmonary, esophageal, and vascular surgery where there is increased risk of infection. Treatment of respiratory (e.g. acute and chronic bronchitis, infected bronchiectasis, bacterial pneumonia, lung abscesses, and post-op chest infections), urinary tract (e.g. acute or chronic pyelonephritis, cystitis), ear, nose, and throat (e.g. sinusitis, tonsillitis, and pharyngitis), soft tissue (e.g. cellulitis, erysipelas, peritonitis), and bone and joint infections (e.g. osteomyelitis, septic arthritis), obstetric and gynecologic infection, pelvic inflammatory diseases, gonorrhea and other infections including septicemia and meningitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 750 mg IM/IV injection every 8 hrs. Severe infections: 1.5 g IV every 8 hrs. The frequency of IM/IV injection can be increased to every 6 hrs if necessary, giving a total dose of 3-6 g daily. <b>Childn:</b> 30-100 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 divided doses. Most infections: 60 mg/kg/day. <b>Neonates:</b> 30-100 mg/kg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>Prophylaxis</b> - <b>Abdominal, pelvic, and orthopedic surgeries:</b> 1.5 g IV with induction of anesthesia, but may be supplemented with two 750 mg IM doses 8 and 16 hrs later. <b>Cardiac, pulmonary, esophageal, and vascular surgeries:</b> 1.5 g IV with induction of anesthesia continuing with 750 mg IM every 8 hrs for a further 24-48 hrs. <b>Total joint replacement:</b> 1.5 g cefuroxime powder may be mixed dry with each pack of methylmethacrylate cement monomer before adding the liquid monomer. <b>Gonorrhea:</b> 1.5 g given as a single dose. May be given as two 750-mg injection into different sites, e.g. each buttock. <b>Renal impairment</b> - Moderate (GFR 20-50 mL/min): 750 mg every 8 hrs; Marked impairment (GFR 10-20 mL/min): 750 mg every 12 hrs; Severe (GFR &lt;10 mL/min): 750 mg once a day, a further 750 mg dose should be given at the end of each dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concurrent administration with potent diuretics. Patients who have experienced an anaphylactic reaction to penicillin. Pregnancy. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rashes, GI disturbances, and <i>Candida</i> intertrigo."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, diuretics, aminoglycosides, estrogens, progestins. May cause false negative reactions in the ferricyanide test. <b>Incompatibilities:</b> Sodium bicarbonate injection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 750 mg (P377.44)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1453,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1453,
        "brand_name": "Proglin Met",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Vildagliptin, metformin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM); as adjunct to diet and exercise in patients whose diabetes is not adequately controlled on metformin or vildagliptin alone or who are already treated with the combination of both as separate tabs;  as combination therapy - in combination with other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes, including insulin, when these do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Naive patients:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg once daily gradually titrated to max 50 mg/1 g twice daily. <b>Inadequately controlled - on vildagliptin monotherapy:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg twice daily. <b>On metformin monotherapy:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1 g twice daily, based on the current dose of metformin. <b>Switching from combination therapy of vildagliptin + metformin as separate tab:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1 g twice daily, based on vildagliptin or metformin already being taken. <b>In combination with a sulfonylurea or insulin:</b> Vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily and the metformin dose already being taken. <b>Patients with renal impairment - GFR 60-89 mL/min:</b> Max 3,000 mg/day metformin, 100 mg/day vildagliptin. Consider dose reduction if renal function declines. <b>45-59 mL/min:</b> Should not be >1,000 mg metformin as starting dose. Max 2,000 mg/day metformin, 50 mg/day vildagliptin. <b>30-44 mL/min:</b> Should not be >500 mg metformin as starting dose. Max 1,000 mg/day metformin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min), CHF, metabolic acidosis including lactic acidosis or diabetic ketoacidosis (with or without coma).Type 1 DM. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic impairment, ALT or AST >2.5x ULN; CHF NYHA class IV. Discontinue at the time of intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents or surgery under general, spinal or epidural anesthesia (except minor procedures not associated with restricted intake of food and fluids) and not restarted until 48 hrs after procedure and reinstituted only after renal function has been re-evaluated. Hypoxic states. Alcohol. Decreased serum vitamin B<sub>12</sub> levels. Stressed conditions (e.g., fever, trauma, infection, surgery). Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tremor, dizziness, headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Furosemide, nifedipine, ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine; NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid, alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P30.00), 50 mg/850 mg (P30.00), 50 mg/1 g (P30.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Denosumab",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Other Bone Metabolism-Affecting Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high-risk for fracture, multiple risk factors for fracture, who have failed or are intolerant to other osteoporosis therapy; to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis; glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis; bone loss in men receiving androgen deprivation therapy for nonmetastatic prostate cancer; bone loss in women receiving adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy for breast cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "60 mg as single SC inj in the abdomen, upper arm or thigh, once every 6 months. Give 1,000 mg calcium daily and at least 400 IU vit D daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hypocalcemia. Childn. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or receiving dialysis; risk factors for osteonecrosis of the jaw. Concomitant use of calcimimetic drugs. Atypical subtrochanteric and diaphyseal femoral fractures; increased fracture risk including multiple vertebral fractures following discontinuation of treatment; endocarditis, UTI, skin, abdomen, and ear infections; suppression of bone turnover; dermatologic adverse reactions; hypercalcemia in childn with osteogenesis imperfecta. Correct preexisting hypocalcemia prior to initiation of therapy. Monitor calcium and mineral levels within 14 days of therapy in patients predispose to hypocalcemia and disturbances of mineral metabolism. Perform pregnancy testing in females of reproductive potential prior initiation of therapy. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Back pain, pain in extremity, musculoskeletal pain, hypercholesterolemia, cystitis. Arthralgia, nasopharyngitis. HTN, bronchitis, headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) 60 mg/mL."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 221,
          "name": "Zuellig Pharma Corp."
        },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MY6qpMQod4mPyn9W0tNXrcU9VAHNOnuEovcWP5say30mvM1xDZ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ymKg8RycXv73uUplWhPjuGJWsbE10HidZQr3Gvg7vsFRVqit6z.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Prednisone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Wide variety of clinical circumstances or disorders affecting the endocrine, nervous, cardiovascular, renal (e.g. nephrotic syndrome), GI, skin and integumentary systems, ocular and respiratory systems of inflammatory and allergic origin (e.g. bronchial asthma and skin allergies)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "5-60 mg daily in divided doses or as a single dose after breakfast or as a double dose on alternate days. <b>As immunosuppressive</b>: 10-100 mg daily. <b>Primary and secondary adrenocortical insufficiency</b>: 5-25 mg daily in divided doses. <b>Adrenogenital syndrome</b>: 10-20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA, daily in divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute infections uncontrolled by appropriate antimicrobial therapy. Systemic fungal infections, glaucoma, gastric and duodenal ulcer, certain viral infections, and severe psychoneuroses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Heart disease, HTN, renal dysfunction, peptic ulcer, systemic fungal infection, history of psychotic disorders, DM, epilepsy, TB, osteoporosis, glaucoma, hypothyroidism, myasthenia gravis, hepatic failure, diverticulitis, colitis, herpes. Contraceptive failure. Sickle cell crisis. Childn. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C but D in 1<sup>st</sup> trimester.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Adrenal suppression. GI distress, nausea, peptic ulcer, behavioral disturbances, fluid and electrolyte imbalance, visual disturbances, growth retardation, skin and muscle atrophy, moon facie, hirsutism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticonvulsants, phenobarbital, phenytoin, antihistamines, barbiturates, ephedrine, primidone and rifampicin. Hypoglycemics, diuretics, salicylates, anticholinesterases. Aspirin, estrogen. Ciclosporin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 20 mg (P7.50). Suspension 10 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P175.00)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Rabeprazole sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of active duodenal ulcer, active benign gastric ulcer, symptomatic erosive or ulcerative gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and <i>>H. pylori</i>-positive duodenal ulcers. Maintenance for healed erosive or ulcerative."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Severe (erosive or ulcerative) GERD:</b> 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks or longer for healing erosive esophagitis. Maintenance: 10 or 20 mg daily. Symptomatic disease without erosive or ulcerative esophagitis: 10 or 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks. <b>Active peptic ulcer disease:</b> 20 mg daily for 4-8 weeks for duodenal ulcer and 6-12 weeks for gastric ulcer. <b>Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i>:</b> Twice daily doses. 20 mg rabeprazole combined with clarithromycin 500 mg and amoxicillin 1 g, or combined with clarithromycin 250 mg and metronidazole 400 mg. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome:</b> Initially 60 mg once daily, may be adjusted up to 120 mg daily. Give doses >100 mg daily in two divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended in childn. Patients with severe hepatic dysfunction. Exclude possibility of gastric or esophageal malignancy prior to initiation of therapy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, diarrhea, nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Measles, Mumps, Rubella Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Vaccination against measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella in individuals 12 months-12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "0.5 mL SC in the deltoid region of the upper arm or higher anterolateral area of the thigh. <b>Childn 1-12 yrs:</b> Single dose. If the 1<sup>st</sup> dose is given at 6-12 months of age, another (2<sup>nd</sup>) dose should be given at >1 yr. 3<sup>rd</sup> dose can be administered if warranted by official recommendations. At least 1 month should elapse between administration of doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Anaphylactoid reaction to neomycin. Malignant neoplasms affecting the bone marrow or lymphatic systems (e.g. blood dyscrasias, leukemia, lymphoma of any type). Immunosuppressive therapy (including high-dose corticosteroids; except those receiving corticosteroids as replacement therapy, e.g. Addison's disease). Primary and acquired immunodeficiency states, including immunosuppressed patients with HIV or AIDS, cellular immune deficiencies, hypogammaglobulinemia and dysgammaglobulinemia. Active untreated TB; active febrile illness (>38.5°C). Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to eggs. Patients with history of convulsions, cerebral injury or any other condition in which stress due to fever should be avoided. Individuals with HIV; thrombocytopenia and/or coagulation disorders. Risk of transmission of virus from vaccine recipients to susceptible high-risk individuals which include: Immunocompromised individuals, pregnant women and/or newborn infants of mothers without documented history of chickenpox or laboratory evidence of prior infection. Tuberculin test. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, irritability, diarrhea, vomiting, measles-like rash, rash, varicella-like rash, fever >38.9°C, erythema, pain or tenderness or soreness, swelling (ecchymosis), rash at injection site."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "M-M-R II, Attenuvax, Immune globulins (Ig), varicella zoster immune globulin (VZIG), salicylates."
          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Omeprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Duodenal ulcer, gastric ulcer, NSAID-associated complications, peptic ulcer associated with <I>Helicobacter pylori</I>, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), acid reflux disease, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Prevention of acid aspiration syndrome, acid-related dyspepsia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>NSAID-associated complications:</b> 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks if not fully healed. <b>Prophylaxis in patients with history of NSAID-associated complications who require continued NSAID treatment:</b> 20 mg once daily. <b>Peptic ulcer associated with <i>H. pylori</i>:</b> Omeprazole 40 mg once daily + clarithromycin 500 mg twice daily + amoxicillin 1 g twice daily for 1 week. <b>Acid-related dyspepsia:</b> 10-20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>GERD:</b> 20-40 mg daily for 4-12 weeks. Maintenance: 20 mg daily; Childn: 0.7-1.4 mg/kg BW daily up to max 40 mg daily for 4-12 weeks. <b>PUD:</b> 20 or 40 mg in severe cases, once daily; Duodenal ulcer: for 4 weeks; Gastric ulcer: 8 weeks. Maintenance: 10-20 mg daily. <b>Prophylaxis of acid aspiration:</b> 40 mg the evening before surgery, then 40 mg on the day of surgery 2-6 hrs pre-op. Taken before meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Gastric malignancy. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Exclude the possibility of malignancy before treatment if gastric ulcer is suspected. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Reversible confusional states, agitation, depression, hallucinations on severely ill patients. Arthralgia, paresthesia, aggression, blurred vision, taste disturbances, peripheral edema, hyponatremia, agranulocytosis, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, interstitial nephritis, hepatotoxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diazepam, phenytoin, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 20 mg (P30.25)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Travoprost",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiglaucoma Preparations and Miotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used to decrease the elevated intraocular pressure in patients with ocular hypertension, open-angle glaucoma, or pediatric glaucoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly:</b> 1 drop in the conjunctival sac of the affected eye(s) once daily. Gently close the eyelid after administration. Do not administer more than once daily. If >1 topical ophthalmic drug is being used, administer at least 5 mins apart."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For ocular use only. Contains propylene glycol, polyoxyethylene hydrogenated castor oil 40. May gradually change the eye color. Increase length, thickness, pigmentation, and/or number of lashes. Periorbital and lid changes including deepening of the eyelid sulcus. Patients with active intraocular inflammation, known risk factors for iritis/uveitis or macular edema; aphakic and pseudophakic patients with torn posterior lens capsule or anterior chamber lenses. Avoid contact with skin. Remove contact lenses prior to application and wait at least 15 mins before reinsertion. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Infants < 2 months. Women of child-bearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Iris hyperpigmentation, eye pain, ocular discomfort, dry eye, eye pruritus, eye irritation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Ophthalmic solution 40 mcg/mL (0.004% w/v) x 3 mL."

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For contraception and treatment of menstrual disorders (e.g. dysmenorrhea, premenstrual syndrome, and menorrhagia)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Take 1 pill daily, beginning on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual bleeding or any day, considering the patient is not pregnant. Use back-up method (e.g. condom) for the next seven days. The interval between 2 pills should be 24 hrs. Start a new pack after finishing. Do not skip any dose regardless of whether menstrual bleeding has stopped or there is a brief pause from sexual activity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Liver and clotting disorders. Breast and cervical cancer. Sickle cell anemia. Hormone-active tumors. Hyperlipidemia. Severe CV diseases. Previous or existing thromboembolic diseases. Idiopathic jaundice.  Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with DM, high BP, varicose veins, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, migraine, ophthalmological problems, tetany, diarrhea, and vomiting. If decided to discontinue, stop taking the pill only after a pack is finished.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, gastric upsets, nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, changes in appetite, BW, and libido,  breast tenderness, depressive moods, interference with liver functions."
          },
          {

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metronidazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-protozoals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab:</b> Anaerobic protozoal infections e.g. amebiasis, giardiasis or trichomoniasis, balantidiasis, blastocystis, and dientamebiasis. Treatment of bacterial infections including <i>Bacteroides fragilis</i> and <i>Clostridium tetani</i>. <b>IV:</b> Treatment of infections caused by <i>Bacteroides</i>; intra-abdominal, gynecological and obstetrical, respiratory, and central nervous system infections, septicemia, gas gangrene, osteomyelitis; prevention of post-op infections due to anaerobic bacteria and treatment of amebic abscess of the liver and in moribund or toxic cases of fulminating intestinal infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - <b>Amebiasis</b> - In susceptible patients: 2 tabs thrice daily for 5 days or 5 tabs as single dose for 3 days. In less susceptible patients, chronic amebic hepatitis: 1 tab thrice daily for 5-10 days or 5 tabs as single dose for 2 days. <b>Amebic liver abscess, other extraintestinal amebiasis:</b> 1 tab thrice daily for 5 days or 5 tabs as single dose for 2 days. <b>Urogenital trichomoniasis:</b> 1 tab at morning and night for 7 days or 5 tabs as single dose. When reinfections are likely, the partner should be treated concurrently. <b>Acute ulcerative gingivitis:</b> 1 tab twice daily for 3 days. <b>Giardiasis:</b> 5 tabs as single dose for 3 days. A 2<sup>nd</sup> course may be necessary 2 weeks after the 1<sup>st</sup> course. <b>Anaerobic infections</b> - <b>Treatment</b> - Adults: 500 mg thrice daily; Childn and infants: 7 mg/kg thrice daily. <b>Prevention</b> - Adults: 400 mg every 8 hrs for 3-4 days up to 1 g. <b>IV</b> - Adults and childn >12 yrs: 500 mg (100 mL); Childn < 12 yrs: 7.5 mg/kg. Doses infused over 20 mins at a rate of 5 mL/min repeated every 8 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with blood dyscrasias or with active disease of CNS. <b>IV:</b> Admixture of 10% glucose, penicillin G, potassium and Lactated Ringer's soln or with any other drug."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid alcohol intake. Carry out total differential leucocyte count before, during, and after treatment. Bone marrow depression and peripheral neuropathy (intensive and prolonged treatment). Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [

                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",

            "content": "Anorexia, nausea, abdominal pain, vomiting, vertigo, tiredness, and dark coloration of urine."

            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Dissolution of cholesterol gallstones in patients with a high risk for surgery and in patients after lithotripsy. Primary biliary cirrhosis stage I and II. Primary sclerosing cholangitis. Hepatitis of various etiologies with cholestatic syndrome. Reactive gastritis in duodenogastric reflux. <b>Childn 6-&lt;18 yrs</b>: Hepatobiliary disorder associated with cystic fibrosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Dissolution of cholesterol gallstones</b>: 10mg/kg/day taken as single dose in the evening before bedtime. BW &gt;100 kg: 5 caps; 81-100 kg: 4 caps; 61-80 kg: 3 caps; Up to 60 kg: 2 caps. <b>Primary biliary cirrhosis stage I and II and other conditions associated with intrahepatic cholestasis</b>: 10–15 mg/kg/day (i.e. 2-6 caps) taken in 2-3 divided doses. <b>Reactive gastritis in duodenogastric reflux</b>: 1 cap daily taken in the evening before bedtime for 10-14 days. <b>Childn &gt;2 yrs – Reactive gastritis in duodenogastric reflux</b>: 10-20 mg/kg/day. <b>Adolescents and childn – Cystic fibrosis</b>: 20 mg/kg/day in 2-3 divided doses, with a further increase to 30 mg/kg/day if necessary."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute inflammation of gallbladder or bile ducts. Occlusion of extrahepatic bile ducts (choledochus duct or cystic duct). Frequent episodes of biliary colics. Radiopaque calcified gallstones. Impaired contractility of gallbladder. Unsuccessful portoenterostomy in childn or childn with biliary atresia without good bile flow. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver enzyme levels (AST, ALT, gamma-GT) every 4 weeks during the first 3 months of treatment and every 3 months thereafter. Should not be used if gallbladder cannot be imaged using radiography or in case of calcification of gallstones. Women of childbearing potential should use effective non-hormonal contraception substitutes during treatment. Childn &lt;6 yrs. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Loose stools or diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cholestyramine, colestipol or antacids containing aluminum hydroxide and/or smectite (aluminum oxide), ciclosporin, ciprofloxacin, rosuvastatin, nitrendipine, dapsone, estrogenic hormones and blood cholesterol-lowering agents e.g. clofibrate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 250 mg (P45.00)."
          }

          {

            "content": "Treatment of the functional symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia including bladder outlet obstruction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>200 mcg</b>: 1 cap once daily. <b>400 mcg</b> - Adults: 400 mcg once daily, about 30 mins after the same meal each day. If discontinued or interrupted (either at 400 mcg or 800 mcg): Restart at 400 mcg once daily. Swallow cap whole; do not open, chew or crush."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic insufficiency, history of orthostatic hypotension. Childn. Women. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Orthostatic hypotension, priapism, ejaculation disorders may occur. Rule out prostate cancer prior to treatment.         "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pituitary Hormones & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>For female</b>: Sterility due to absence of follicle-ripening or ovulation. In combination with FSH or human menopausal gonadotropin, promotion of controlled superovulation in medically assisted reproduction programs. <b>For male</b>: Hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism. Delayed puberty associated with insufficient gonadotrophic pituitary function. Sterility in selected cases of deficient spermatogenesis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>In females</b>: Individualized dosage. One injection of 5,000-10,000 IU on 12<sup>th</sup> day of menstrual cycle or when the Graafian follicle attains a size &ge;18 mm. <b>In males</b>: 5,000 IU twice weekly for 12 weeks and may have to continue up to 1 yr to improve semen quality."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Precocious puberty, prostatic carcinoma or other androgen-dependent neoplasia, prior allergic reaction to chorionic gonadotropin. Presence of uncontrolled non-gonadal endocrinopathies (e.g. thyroid, adrenal or pituitary disorders). Breast, uterine, ovarian, and testicular tumors. Vaginal bleeding of unknown cause. Known or suspected androgen-dependent tumors, carcinoma of the prostate or mammary carcinoma in males."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Ovarian enlargement, ascites, with or without pain and/or pleural effusion, rupture ovarian cysts with resultant hemoperitoneum. Multiple births. Arterial thromboembolism. Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. May induce precocious puberty in patients for cryptorchidism. Discontinue therapy if signs of precocious puberty occur. Patients with epilepsy, migraine, asthma, cardiac or renal disease.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, irritability, edema, restlessness, depression, tiredness, precocious puberty, gynecomastia and pain at the injection site."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection (IM) 5,000 IU."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Individualized dosage. Recommended air-flow rate of 6-8 L/min. Suitable fill volume: 2-4 mL. <b>Childn < 12 yrs:</b> Max 2 mg/day, should only be considered with severe asthma and during limited period."

          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },

            "content": "Not intended for the rapid relief of acute asthma. Patients with active or quiescent pulmonary TB, fungal or viral infections in the airways, reduced liver function, COPD.     "id": 194,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 194,
        "brand_name": "Purinase",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Allopurinol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antigout Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of patients with primary and secondary gout; leukemia, lymphoma, and solid tumor malignancies who are undergoing chemotherapy expected to result in tumor lysis and subsequent hyperuricemia and hyperuricosuria; recurrent calcium oxalate renal calculi in patients whose urinary urate excretion is &gt;800 mg (males) or &gt;750 mg (females) daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses taken after meals. <b>Shifting from uricosuric agent to allopurinol</b>: Gradually reduce dose of uricosuric agent over several weeks and gradually increase dose of allopurinol to the required dose. <b>Intercritical and chronic tophaceous gout</b>: Initially 100 mg/day for 2 weeks after the pain and swelling of acute gouty arthritis have subsided. Titrate by 50-100 mg/day every 2-4 weeks to achieve serum uric acid &lt;6 mg/dL. Max 300 mg/day. <b>Leukemia, lymphoma, and solid tumor malignancies</b>: 600-800 mg/day in divided doses for 2-3 days. <b>Recurrent calcium oxalate renal calculi</b>: Initially 200-300 mg/day as single dose or in divided doses. May be increased/decreased depending on control or hyperuricosuria assessed by 24-hr urinary urate excretion determination. <b>Patients with renal impairment - Initial Dose</b>: CrCl 10-20 mL/min: 200 mg/day or below; &lt;10 mL/min: 100 mg/day or below, or 100 mg at intervals of &gt;1 day; <b>Maintenance dose</b>: CrCl 80 mL/min: 250 mg/day; 60 mL/min: 200 mg/day; 40 mL/min: 150 mg/day; 20 mL/min: 100 mg/day; 10 mL/min: 100 mg every 2 days; &lt;10 mL/min: 100 mg every 3 days. <b>Patients undergoing dialysis</b>: 300-400 mg immediately after each dialysis session."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with asymptomatic hyperuricemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Ensure adequate fluid intake (2 L/day). Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, conditions with increased rate of urate formation (neoplastic disease, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome), preexisting renal disease or poor urate clearance, CV disorders (e.g. HTN, cardiac insufficiency), impaired thyroid function, abnormal iron storage including hemochromatosis. Concomitant use with antineoplastics, diuretics, ACE inhibitors. May precipitate acute gout attacks. Monitor serum uric acid and creatinine periodically. Perform LFTs in patients with preexisting liver disease prior to and during early stages of therapy, then periodically thereafter. Perform renal function tests prior to and periodically during therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Patients with HLA-B*5801 allele (e.g. Han Chinese, Koreans, Japanese, and Europeans). Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin and subcutaneous reactions (e.g. angioedema). Macolopapular, pruritic, or purpuric rashes. Exfoliative rashes, SJS, TEN, DRESS. Acute gout attacks. GI effects (e.g. diarrhea, nausea). Increased liver enzymes and serum alkaline phosphatase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ampicillin, amoxicillin, ACE inhibitors (e.g. captopril), antacids (e.g. aluminum hydroxide), anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, other coumarin derivatives), chlorpropamide, cyclophosphamide and other cytotoxic agents (e.g. doxorubicin, bleomycin, procarbazine, mechlorethamine, bendamustine), ciclosporin, didanosine, diuretics, pyrazinamide, diazoxide, alcohol, mecylamine, mercaptopurine, azathioprine, phenytoin, theophylline, uricosurics and salicylates, vidarabine (adenine arabinoside)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg (P11.54), 300 mg (P32.50)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Saxagliptin HCl, dapagliflozin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once daily at any time of the day, with or without food. Swallowed whole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 45 mL/min/1.73m<sup>2</sup> MDRD). ESRD. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM. Patients with renal and severe hepatic impairment; predisposing factors to ketoacidosis include low beta-cell function reserve resulting from pancreatic disorders (e.g. type 1 diabetes, history of pancreatitis or pancreatic surgery), insulin dose reduction, reduced caloric intake or increased insulin requirements due to infections, illness, or surgery and alcohol abuse; known risk factors of hospitalization for heart failure or moderate-severe renal impairment. May induce joint pain; increases rate of hospitalization for heart failure. Assess signs and symptoms of ketoacidosis including nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, malaise and shortness of breath, blood glucose levels < 14 mmol/L (250 mg/dL). Inform patients of the symptoms of acute pancreatitis (persistent, severe abdominal pain). Advise patients to seek medical attention if symptoms of pain, tenderness, erythema, or swelling in the genital or perineal area, with fever or malaise are experienced. Discontinue or temporary interrupt treatment if ketoacidosis is suspected; hypersensitivity, pancreatitis, or Fournier’s gangrene occurs; develop blisters or erosions and bullous pemphigoid is suspected. Evaluate renal function prior to initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. Elderly. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, UTI, genital infection, gastroenteritis; diarrhea, vomiting; back pain, arthralgia; headache, dyslipidemia; polyuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lithium. 1,5-anhydroglucitol assay."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg/10 mg (P75.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3103,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3103,
        "brand_name": "Qtipine",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mrwlxHA1Ufn7A2RgosD0TiY4nhKfFasDNwBrFZTfnzBifvWnTk.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cWNSgcqtDvKUWPQoKOZEO27bGPzsWJb5pmuLrw1EiitK89f6v1.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5d2h3NMI3OOoDAMjSFmebZGyvQbRXq8dYt5z4M7Ss870Rd2eNA.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Quetiapine fumarate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia, manic and depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder, and to prevent recurrence in bipolar disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – Schizophrenia</b>: Initially 25 mg on Day 1, 50 mg on Day 2, 100 mg on Day 3, 150 mg on Day 4. All doses should be taken twice daily. May be adjusted to 300 mg-450 mg daily given in 2 or 3 divided doses. Max of 750 mg daily. <b>Manic episodes in bipolar disorder</b>: Initially 50 mg on Day 1, 100 mg on Day 2, 150 mg on Day 3, 200 mg on Day 4. All doses should be taken twice daily. May be adjusted to 400 mg-800 mg, increments should be &gt;200 mg daily. All doses should be taken twice daily. <b>Major depressive episodes in bipolar disorder</b>: Total daily doses of 50 mg on Day 1, 100 mg on Day 2, 200 mg on Day 3, 300 mg on Day 4, may be adjusted to 400 mg on Day 5 up to 600 mg on Day 8. <b>Recurrence in bipolar disorder</b>: 300 mg-800 mg once daily. <b>Childn and adolescents 13-17 yrs – Schizophrenia</b>: Total daily doses of 50 mg on Day 1, 100 mg on Day 2, 200 mg on Day 3, 300 mg on Day 4, 400 mg on Day 5, may be adjusted to 400 mg-800 mg after Day 5, increments should be &gt;100 mg daily. All doses should be taken in 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>10-17 yrs - Manic episodes</b>: Total daily dose of 50 mg on Day 1, 100 mg on Day 2, 200 mg on Day 3, 300 mg on Day 4, 400 mg on Day 5, may be adjusted to 400 mg-800 mg. All doses should be taken in 2 or 3 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. HIV-protease inhibitors, azole antifungals, erythromycin, clarithromycin, nefazodone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Withdrawal symptoms. Suicide/suicidal thoughts. Patients with history of seizures; known CV disease, cerebrovascular disease, or other conditions predisposing to hypotension; history of QT prolongation; suspected cardiomyopathy or myocarditis; DM or risk factors for DM; at risk for aspiration pneumonia; intestinal obstruction/ileus. Assess metabolic parameters e.g. change in weight, blood glucose and lipid at the time of treatment, changes should be controlled. EPS, tardive dyskinesia, NMS may develop. Not for treatment of dementia-related psychosis. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Decreased hemoglobin, elevations in serum triglyceride levels, total cholesterol (LDL), decreases in HDL. Dizziness, somnolence, headache, EPS. Dry mouth. Leucopenia, decreased neutrophil count, increased eosinophils. Hyperprolactinemia, decrease in T4, free T4, total T3, increase in TSH. Increased appetite, blood glucose, hyperglycemic levels. Abnormal dreams, nightmares, suicidal ideation/behavior. Dysarthria, tachycardia, palpitations. Blurred vision, orthostatic hypotension, dyspnea. Constipation, dyspepsia, vomiting. Elevations in ALT, gamma-GT levels. Mild asthenia, peripheral edema, irritability, pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbamazepine, phenytoin, ketoconazole, grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 25 mg (P29.46), 300 mg (P118.13)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9upJsKJxWxcH4XDJw3eBIU9Z5JBTuBn8XvplAloDfV1YZt6H5u.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5ymFXpOJfpb6FS3UWVKsNBSIsb8c2f8K1bbNUhVgfWnMIf3tgs.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Quetiapine fumarate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder including manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder, major depressive episodes in bipolar disorder, and preventing recurrence in bipolar disorder in patients whose manic, mixed or depressive episode has responded to quetiapine treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 25 mg twice daily, with increases of 25-50 mg twice to thrice daily to a target dose range of 300-400 mg a day, given in 2-3 divided doses daily, by the 4<sup>th</sup> or 7<sup>th</sup> day. Further dosage adjustments may be made in increments or decrements of 25-50 mg twice a day at intervals of 2 days. Some patients may require 150 mg a day. <b>Elderly and patients with hepatic impairment, predisposition to hypotension, or other debilitation</b>: Slower rate of dosage and lower target dosage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Alzheimer’s dementia, history of breast cancer, CV disease, hypotension, hypovolemia or dehydration, history of drug abuse or dependence, hepatic or severe renal impairment, hypothyroidism, seizure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with predisposition to hypotension or other debilitation. Elderly. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dysarthria; dyspnea, EPS, parkinsonian, flu-like symptoms, leukopenia, orthostatic hypotension, peripheral edema, skin rash. Constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, dry mouth, dyspepsia, increases weight, abdominal pain, abnormal vision, anorexia asthenia, headache, hypertonia, increased sweating, palpitation, pharyngitis, rhinitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol or CNS depressants, antihypertensive agents, cimetidine, CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin, diltiazem, erythromycin, fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone, verapamil), dopamine agonists or levodopa, CYP inducers (e.g. phenytoin), lorazepam, thioridazine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 25 mg (P40.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4405,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4405,
        "brand_name": "Qvex",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/iUjBLJjL2bEo2BJpBH9oi7csgkAgbE4BND3yIESwAuENDqhv4S.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wjlixkdmvybHfvhgZ7OHJEtKxNBybJHswGCiLx6H4Jyru6sH4v.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/daFwnTmgJT4p9thv40HRUDHBpaNHAgN4oJOGoQSMPIC113pi7B.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Quetiapine fumarate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia and bipolar disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia:</b> Initially 50 mg given in 2 divided doses on day 1, increased in increments of 50-150 mg on days 2 and 3, to a target of 300-400 mg daily by day 4, given in 3 divided doses. Daily dose may further be adjusted in steps of 50-100 mg at intervals not &lt;2 days. Max 750 mg/day. <b>Bipolar disorder</b> - <b>Acute manic episode:</b> Initially 50 mg twice daily on day 1, 100 mg twice daily on day 2, 150 mg twice daily on day 3, and 200 mg twice daily on day 4. Dose may then be adjusted to 400-800 mg/day if needed; <b>Depressive phase:</b> Initially 50 mg once daily at bedtime, increased to 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, 300 mg on day 4, may further be increased to 400 mg on day 5, and 600 mg on day 8, if necessary. Maintenance treatment as adjunct to lithium or valproate: Continue dose that controlled intial symptoms. <b>Elderly, patients with hepatic and renal impairment:</b> Initially 25 mg, may be increased daily in increments of 25-50 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. HIV-protease inhibitors, azole antifungal agents, erythromycin, clarithromycin, and nefazodone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Long-term treatment. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with hepatic or renal impairment, CV disease or other conditions predisposing to hypotension, cerebrovascular disease, history of seizures or conditions that lower seizure threshold. Monitor patients during early therapy for depressive phase in bipolar disorder. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, dizziness, mild asthenia, anxiety, fever, rhinitis, peripheral edema, constipation, dyspepsia, dry mouth, raised liver enzyme values."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CNS depressants, alcohol. Antihypertensives or drugs that prolong QT interval. Levodopa. CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. erythromycin, fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole. Carbamazepine, phenytoin, thioridazine. Antibacterials, antipsychotics e.g. risperidone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 25 mg, 100 mg, 300 mg."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kM6u4uLFhSaA86EOX81PkbTKy3NcErOQwkNpGXRV55REfnKYe1.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/c94OBXnVlnrtoCEzmJxWyatnlxXkPXsD179h8TPJxj3TmKk5xv.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pramipexole HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of Parkinson’s disease either alone or as an adjunct to levodopa therapy to reduce \"end-of-dose\" or \"on-off\" fluctuations in response."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Starting dose of 0.375 mg/day in 3 divided doses, should not increase more frequently than every 5-7 days. <b>Ascending dosage schedule</b> – Week 1: 0.125 mg; Week 2: 0.25 mg; Week 3: 0.5 mg; Week 4: 0.75 mg; Week 5: 1 mg; Week 6: 1.25 mg; Week 7: 1.5 mg. All doses given 3 times a day. Maintenance: 1.5-4.5 mg/day in equally divided doses 3 times per day. <b>Renal impairment – CrCl &gt;50 mL/min</b>: Initially 0.125 mg 3 times a day. Max 1.5 mg 3 times a day; <b>30-50 mL/min</b>: Initially 0.125 mg twice a day. Max 0.75 mg 3 times a day; <b>15-&lt;30 mL/min</b>: Initially 0.125 mg once daily. Max 1.5 mg once daily. <b>Discontinuation of treatment</b>: Tapered off at a rate of 0.75 mg/day, thereafter reduced to 0.375 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Symptomatic orthostatic hypotension, impulse control/compulsive behaviors; hallucinations and psychotic-like behavior, visual abnormalities, melanoma may occur. Patients with major psychotic disorder, preexisting dyskinesias, renal impairment. Abrupt withdrawal may cause NMS. Regular ophthalmologic monitoring. Sudden onset of sleep. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, dyskinesia, somnolence; hypotension; nausea. Abnormal dreams, behavioral symptoms of impulse control disorders and compulsion, confusion, hallucinations, insomnia, restlessness; amnesia, headache; visual disturbance including blurred vision and reduced visual acuity; constipation, vomiting; fatigue, peripheral edema; decreased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cimetidine; ranitidine, diltiazem, triamterene, verapamil, quinidine and quinine; cephalosporins, penicillins, indomethacin, HCTZ, chlorpropamide; cisplatin, procainamide; amantadine; other sedating drugs or alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 250 mcg (P38.00), 1 mg (P85.00)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "As add-on therapy for the symptomatic treatment of patients with stable angina pectoris who are inadequately controlled or intolerant to 1st-line antianginal therapies (e.g. beta-blockers and/or calcium antagonists)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy in adults with idiopathic Parkinson's disease. Adjunct therapy with levodopa in patients with end of dose fluctuations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy or adjunct in patients not taking levodopa:</b> Initially 1 mg once daily. <b>Concomitant levodopa with or without other Parkinson’s disease drugs:</b> Initially 500 mcg once daily, may be increased to 1 mg daily if clinical response is not achieved. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Max 500 mcg once daily. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Moderate to severe hepatic impairment. Co-administration with meperidine, tramadol, methadone, propoxyphene, St. John’s wort, cyclobenzaprine, dextromethorphan."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Exacerbation of HTN; new or worsening mental status and behavioral changes; compulsive behavior, uncontrollable intense urges; withdrawal-emergent hyperpyrexia and confusion; somnolence; high risk for skin cancer. Potentiation of dopaminergic side effects and exacerbation of preexisting dyskinesia on concomitant use with levodopa. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neck pain. <b>Monotherapy:</b> Influenza, skin carcinoma, leucopenia, allergy, depression, hallucinations, conjunctivitis, vertigo, angina pectoris, rhinitis, dermatitis, musculoskeletal pain, arthritis, urinary urgency, fever, malaise. <b>Adjunct:</b> Skin melanoma, decreased appetite, hallucinations, abnormal dreams, dystonia, carpal tunnel syndrome, balance disorder, orthostatic hypotension, abdominal pain, constipation, nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, rash, arthralgia, decreased weight, fall."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other MAOIs, St. John’s wort, pethidine, meperidine, sympathomimetics, dextromethorphan, antidepressants, ciprofloxacin, other CYP1A2 inhibitors, entacapone, antipsychotics, metoclopramide. Smoking. Tyramine-rich foods."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 500 mcg (P75.00), 1 mg (P140.00)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Complementary symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhea in infants (&gt;3 months) and in childn together with oral rehydration and the usual support measures, when these measures alone are insufficient to control the clinical condition, and when causal treatment is not possible. If causal treatment is possible, it can be administered as complementary treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1.5 mg/kg per dose (1-2 sachets), thrice daily at regular intervals. <b>Childn &gt;27 kg:</b> 2 sachets thrice daily; <b>13 kg-27 kg:</b> 1 sachet thrice daily. Taken with oral rehydration. Duration of treatment: 5 days or until two normal stools are recorded. Max 7 days. Granules can be added to food, dispersed in a glass of water or in the feeding-bottle."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome or saccharase-isomaltase deficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do a rehydration regimen and consider route based on age and BW of patient, the stage and severity of condition. Consider IV rehydration for serious or prolonged diarrhea with vomiting or lack of appetite. Presence of bloody or purulent stools and fever. Antibiotic-associated diarrhea. Chronic diarrhea. Diabetic patients (contains sucrose). Infants &lt;3 months. Childn with renal or liver impairment. Prolonged or uncontrolled vomiting. Lactation.",
