          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DErRbGbGod9f8oh665dIC5huuYfTSQsYkoQpm1GeMK9lxMT7GS.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ranitidine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "H2-Receptor Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of duodenal and gastric ulcer associated with <i>Helicobacter pylori</i>, NSAID-associated peptic ulcer, post-op ulcer, acute reflux esophagitis, Zollinger-Ellison syndrome, chronic episodic dyspepsia. Symptomatic relief of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and prophylaxis of Mendelson’s syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults including elderly</b>: The usual dose is 150 mg twice daily. <b>Duodenal and gastric ulcer</b>: 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg at night for 4 weeks. May be given for a further 4 weeks if not yet fully healed. <b>Ulcer following NSAID therapy or associated with continued NSAIDs</b>: 8 weeks treatment. <b>Prevention of NSAID-associated duodenal ulcer</b>: 150 mg twice daily. 300 mg twice daily for 4 weeks may be given. <b>Duodenal ulcers associated with <i>H. pylori</i> infection</b>: 300 mg at bedtime or 150 mg twice daily, may be given with oral amoxicillin 750 mg three times a day and metronidazole 500 mg three times a day for 2 weeks. Maintenance dose: 150 mg at bedtime. <b>Symptomatic relief of GERD</b>: 150 mg twice daily for 2 weeks. <b>Esophageal reflux disease</b>: 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg at bedtime up to 8-12 weeks. <b>Moderate to severe esophagitis</b>: Dose may be increased to 150 mg 4 times daily up to 12 weeks. <b>Healed esophagitis</b>: 150 mg twice daily. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 150 mg three times daily. Dose may be increased up to 6 g per day. <b>Chronic episodic dyspepsia</b>: 150 mg twice daily for up to 6 weeks. <b>Prophylaxis of hemorrhage from stress ulceration in seriously ill patients or recurrent hemorrhage from peptic ulceration</b>: 150 mg twice daily. <b>Prophylaxis of acid aspiration (Mendelson’s syndrome)</b>: 150 mg given 2 hrs before anesthesia, and preferably 150 mg the previous evening. <b>Obstetric patients in labor</b>: 150 mg every 6 hrs. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl &lt;50 mL/min)</b>: 150 mg daily at night for 4-8 weeks. May be increased to 150 mg twice daily. Maintenance dose: 150 mg at night. <b>Childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: Adult dose. <b> Childn - Peptic ulcer</b>: 4-8 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. Max 300 mg daily for 4 weeks; <b>GERD</b>: 5-10 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses. Max 600 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Malignancy. Renal impairment. History of acute porphyria. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, dizziness, tiredness, headache, and rashes. Reversible confusional states. Hypersensitivity. Fever, arthralgia, myalgia, agranulocytosis, or neutropenia and thrombocytopenia. Interstitial nephritis, hepatotoxicity. CV disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sucralfate (high dosage)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 150 mg (P18.42). Film-coated tablet 300 mg (P28.94)."
          }
        ],

          {

            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia and depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adult patients. Acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adult patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Schizophrenia:</b> Initially 1.5 mg once daily, can be increased slowly in 1.5 mg increments to max 6 mg/day. <b>Manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder:</b> Initially 1.5 mg, increased to 3 mg on day 2. May be adjusted to 1.5 mg or 3 mg increments. Max 6 mg daily. <b>Depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder:</b> Initially 1.5 mg once daily, can be increased to max 3 mg once daily on day 15. Taken once daily at same time of the day, with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with symptoms of akathisia; Parkinson’s disease; history of seizures or conditions that can lower the seizure threshold; risk factors for stroke or VTE; CV disease predispose to BP changes; history of QT prolongation, treated with QT prolonging drugs; known or at risk for DM. Not recommended in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) and hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score: 10-15); elderly with dementia. Suicidal ideation, attempt, and completed suicide, akathisia, restlessness, worsening of Parkinson’s disease, ocular symptoms/cataract, orthostatic hypotension, HTN, VTE. Consider discontinuation if tardive dyskinesia occurs. Immediately discontinue if NMS or unexplained fever without manifestation of NMS develops. Monitor BP and serum glucose levels. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Childn < 18 yrs. Use effective contraception for at least 10 weeks after the last dose. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Akathisia, Parkinsonism, dyslipidemia, increased weight, increased/decreased appetite, blurred vision, sleep disorders, fatigue, anxiety, sedation, dizziness, headache, dystonia, other EPS and abnormal movement disorders, tachyarrhythmia, HTN, vomiting, nausea, constipation, vomiting, dyspepsia, dry mouth, increased hepatic enzymes, increased blood creatine phosphokinase, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., boceprevir, clarithromycin, cobicistat, indinavir, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone, nelfinavir, posaconazole, ritonavir, saquinavir, telaprevir, telithromycin, voriconazole, diltiazem, erythromycin, fluconazole, verapamil)  or inducers (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampicin, St. John’s Wort, bosentan, efavirenz, etravirine, modafinil, nafcillin), P-glycoprotein substrates (e.g., dabigatran, digoxin), centrally acting drugs, alcohol."
          },
          {

            "content": "Monotherapy and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of partial seizures with and without secondary generalization. Treatment of neuropathic pain in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy</b> - <b>Adults and adolescents &gt;12 yrs</b> - Initially 300 mg thrice daily on day 1 or titrate dose as 300 mg once a day on day 1, 300 mg every 12 hrs on day 2 and 300 mg every 8 hrs on day 3. Increase dose further by 300 mg/day increments every 2-3 days up to max 3,600 mg/da. Effective dose: 900-3,600 mg/day given in 3 divided doses; <b>Childn 5-12 yrs:</b> Initially 10-15 mg/kg/day given in 3 divided doses. Effective dose: 25-35 mg/kg/day given in 3 divided doses. <b>3-4 yrs:</b> Initially 10-15 mg/kg/day given in 3 divided doses. Effective dose: 40 mg/kg/day given in 3 divided doses. <b>Peripheral neuropathic pain</b> - <b>Adults:</b> Initially 900 mg/day given in 3 divided doses or titrated as with epilepsy titration doses. Thereafter may be increased to 300 mg/day increments every 2-3 days up to max 3,600 mg/day. <b>Impaired renal function</b> - CrCl &ge;80 mL/min: 900-3,600 mg/day; 50-79 mL/min: 600-1,800 mg/day; 30-49 mL/min: 300-900 mg/day; 15-29 mL/min: 150 mg (administered as 300 mg every other day) to 600 mg/day; &lt;15 mL/min: 150 mg (administered as 300 mg every other day) to 300 mg/day; Hemodialysis: An additional 200-300 mg dose following each 4-hr hemodialysis. For anuric patients undergoing hemodialysis who have never received gabapentin: 300-400 mg loading doses, then 200-300 mg following each 4-hr hemodialysis. Give daily doses in 3 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinuation of therapy should be done gradually over a minimum of 1 week to avoid possibility of seizures. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rabeprazole sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux (GERD), duodenal ulcers, and used in combination with antibiotics to treat <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> bacterial infections in the stomach. IV: As step-up from oral rabeprazole when patient is temporarily unable to take oral medication. Gastric ulcer, prevention of acid aspiration, stress-induced mucosal injury in critical care."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - <b>GERD, duodenal ulcers:</b> 20 mg once daily for 4-8 weeks. <b>In combination with antibiotics to treat <i>H. pylori</i> bacterial infections in the stomach:</b> 20 mg twice a day for 7 days in combination with clarithromycin 500 mg and amoxicillin 1 g. <b>IV:</b> 1 vial (20 mg) once daily. IV injection: Contents of the vial needs to be reconstituted with 5 mL sterile water for injection, given slowly over 5-15 mins. IV infusion: Reconstituted soln should be further diluted and administered as short-term infusion over 15-30 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to rabeprazole or to substituted benzimidazoles."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Exclude malignancy when gastric ulcer is suspected. Rabeprazole IV is compatible with sterile water for injection and 0.9% sodium chloride injection. No other solvent or infusion fluid must be used for administration. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, diarrhea, and skin rashes. Pruritus, dizziness, fatigue, constipation, nausea and vomiting, flatulence, abdominal pain, arthralgia and myalgia, urticaria, and dry mouth."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP450 inhibitor or inducer. Dasatinib, ketoconazole, and itraconazole. Voriconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 20 mg (P26.04). Lyophilized powder for injection (IV) 20 mg (in vial) + sterilized water for injection 5 mL (ampule) (P784.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3413,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3413,
        "brand_name": "Renogen 10,000 IU",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/W9ex1fTjopI8XgLGsXoPqNurDyRUTRWhvRvSqNQNWL18SqEGQv.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/I3Frg0IfkjhcjyDZzozTqIpErLbo3lXFklBH4VheorokeDLCV6.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/aFnlQNeJgS4M08uJsAN07wLqJzcZuf7kArvMPbc3dn23cTu13O.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Epoetin alfa (recombinant human erythropoietin)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hematopoietic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of anemia in patients with non-myeloid malignancies where anemia is due to the effect of concomitantly administered chemotherapy. Treatment of anemia related to therapy with zidovudine in HIV-infected patients. Treatment of anemic patients (Hgb &gt;10-&le;13 g/dL) scheduled to undergo elective, noncardiac, nonvascular surgery to reduce need for allogenic blood transfusions; indicated for patients at high risk of peri-op transfusions with significant, anticipated blood loss."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cancer patients on chemotherapy</b>: 150-300 IU/kg by SC injection thrice a week or 40,000 IU by SC injection once a week. <b>Zidovudine-treated HIV-infected patients</b>: Prior to transfusion, endogenous serum erythropoietin level should be determined; &gt;500 mUnits/mL level is unlikely to respond to erythropoietin therapy. <b>Surgery patients</b>: 300 IU/kg/day by SC injection for 10 days before the surgery, on the day of the surgery and for 4 days after the surgery; alternate dose schedule: 600 IU/kg by SC injection once weekly (21, 14, and 7 days before surgery) plus 4<sup>th</sup> dose on the day of surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to mammalian cell-derived products and albumin. Uncontrolled HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Treatment of cancer patients with grossly elevated serum erythropoietin levels (e.g. &gt;200 mUnits/mL) is not recommended. Patients with history of seizure disorder or underlying hematologic diseases. Patients with known porphyria, chronic renal failure, and patients undergoing dialysis. Iron status including transferrin saturation and serum ferritin should be evaluated prior and during therapy. All patients will eventually require supplemental iron therapy. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "HTN, headache, arthralgia, nausea, edema, fatigue, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, chest pain, skin reaction at the injection site, asthenia, dizziness, clotted access, pyrexia, DVT."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV/SC) 10,000 IU/mL in pre-filled syringe (P2,869.56)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wNcZi89jexurO2Q0aYJbUJ4sbDgc3REOGsdaEBrcTfZPgoGOPS.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/SLJzbhnnL7IzJfWCmloVW0Im1x8jse5OcL0B9yK3cILZZTvbch.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Epoetin alfa (recombinant human erythropoietin)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hematopoietic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of anemia in patients with renal insufficiency or chronic renal failure (CRF); in zidovudine-treated HIV-infected patients; in cancer patients on chemotherapy. Reduction of allogenic blood transfusion in adult surgery patients. Increases the yield of autologous blood from adult surgery patients in a pre-donation program."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>CRF patients – Adults</b>: 50-100 IU/kg IV or SC injection thrice a week. Maintenance: Individually titrate to achieve and maintain lowest Hgb level sufficient to avoid need for RBC transfusion and not exceed 12 g/dL. Increases should not be made more than once a month. <b>Childn on hemodialysis</b>: 50 IU/kg IV or SC injection thrice a week. Maintenance: Adjust dose to maintain Hgb between 9.5-11 g/dL. Generally, childn under 30 kg require higher maintenance doses. <b>Zidovudine-treated HIV-infected patients (serum erythropoietin &le;500 mU/mL who are receiving zidovudine &le;4,200 mg/week)</b>: 100 IU/kg IV or SC injection thrice a week. <B>Cancer patients on chemotherapy – Adults</b>: 150 IU/kg BW by SC injection thrice a week; or 40,000 IU by SC injection once a week. <b>Childn</b>: 600 IU/kg BW by IV injection once a week. Max 40,000 IU. <b>Adult surgery patients</b> (Hgb level &gt;10-&le;13 g/dL) - <b>To reduce allogenic blood transfusion</b>: 600 IU/kg BW by SC injection once a week (days 21, 14, and 7 days before surgery) plus a 4<sup>th</sup> dose on the day of surgery; or 300 IU/kg/day BW by SC injection daily for 10 days before surgery, on the day of surgery and 4 days immediately thereafter. <b>In an autologous pre-donation program</b>: 600 IU/kg BW by IV injection twice a week for 3 weeks before surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to epoetin alfa or mammalian cell-derived products or albumin (human). Uncontrolled HTN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not shake container. Patients with chronic renal failure and with insufficient response to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents (ESA). Patients with advanced head and neck cancer receiving radiation therapy, receiving chemotherapy for metastatic cancer or lymphoid malignancy, with NSCLC or various malignancies not receiving chemo- or radiotherapy, with IHD or CHF, with pre-existing CV disease or history of HTN, with history of seizure or underlying hematologic disease, with known porphyria. May induce PRCA and severe anemia (with or without cytopenias) associated with neutralizing antibodies to erythropoietin, seizures, absolute or functional iron deficiency. Monitor and control BP. If patients fails to respond or maintain a response, consider the following: iron deficiency; underlying infectious, inflammatory, or malignant processes; occult blood loss; underlying hematologic diseases; folic acid or vit B<sub>12</sub> deficiencies; hemolysis, aluminum intoxication; osteitis fibrosa cystica; PRCA or anti-erythropoietin antibody-assciated anemia. May affect ability to drive and operate machines. Infants and childn &lt;1 month. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Immunogenicity. HTN, headache, arthralgia, nausea, edema, fatigue, diarrhea, vomiting, chest pain, administration site reaction, asthenia, dizziness, clotted access, tachycardia, shortness of breath, hyperkalemia, pyrexia, cough, rash, respiratory congestion, paresthesia, URTI, trunk pain, constipation, skin pain, pruritus, insomnia, UTI, DVT, dyspepsia, and anxiety."
          },

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YdEG8aX3l38zvzJl6Dc1UcDd9mtd3LfaN4dz3kRYzexSQWy4Cr.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/K8MIHRJ3yHFqZbv8pWeD6I0iebLLsMpPv4sALn6RQyG1PVeJRz.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ohEmB460BZwK6C98bHyzgHBTytRNSck0moh4rjk33GgvDJqx7z.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Calcitriol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vitamins A, D, & E"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Correction of calcium abnormalities and phosphate metabolism in renal osteodystrophy. Treatment of established postmenopausal osteoporosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Renal osteodystrophy:</b> Initially 0.25 mcg/day. In patients with normal or only slightly reduced calcium levels: 0.25 mcg every other day. If no satisfactory response within 2-4 weeks of therapy: Increase dose by 0.25 mcg at 2-4 week intervals. <b>Patients with osteodystrophy refractory to continuous therapy:</b> Pulse therapy of 0.1 mcg/kg/week divided into 2-3 equal doses given at the end of dialysis. Max 12 mcg/week. <b>Postmenopausal osteoporosis:</b> 0.25 mcg twice a day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with diseases associated with hypercalcemia, evidence of metastatic calcification, and vit D toxicity. Other products containing vit D."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Abrupt increase of calcium intake. Immobilized patients (e.g. undergone recent surgery). Discontinue if serum calcium rise by 1 mg/100 mL (250 micromol/L) above normal (i.e. 9-11 mg/100 mL or 2,250-2,750 micromol/L) and serum creatinine levels to >120 micromol/L. Patients with renal failure and vit D-resistant rickets taking oral phosphate; fructose intolerance. Monitor serum phosphate levels. Avoid dehydration. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypercalcemia, headache, abdominal pain, nausea, rash, and UTI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other calcium-containing preparations, thiazide diuretics, digitalis, corticosteroids, magnesium-containing drugs (e.g. antacids), phosphate-binding agents, and bile acid sequestrants (i.e. cholestyramine and sevelamer)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 0.25 mcg."
          }
        ],

        },

  {
    "id": 1100,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1100,
        "brand_name": "Renuvie",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qiCRzP6KscLCZ1DLVtdbRB3PHeLRUTjfneq7vR67Pu2HORWWaf.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jkKiIWmKS2F0Vyu42Hfq9dgYrgCKOrHupSHRsazqIDA2m95fSM.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/1YnCayjB8SoFGiI2vJ5uuXqH0MX8ud5UuUzOpIkBJhwvR7ECLL.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Risperidone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Schizophrenia in adolescents 13-17 yrs and as acute and maintenance treatment in adults. Bipolar mania: Short-term treatment of acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs as monotherapy or in adults in combination with lithium or valproate; treatment of moderate to severe manic episodes associated with bipolar disorders in adults. Conduct and other disruptive behavior disorders: Short-term symptomatic treatment (up to 6 weeks) of conduct and other disruptive behavior disorders in childn (&gt;5 yrs), adolescents and adults with subaverage intellectual functioning or mental retardation, or average IQ. Irritability associated with autistic disorders in childn and adolescents 5-16 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia - Adults:</b> 2 mg once or twice daily, increase in increments of 1-2 mg/day to recommended dose of 4-8 mg/day; <b>Adolescents 13-17 yrs:</b> 0.5 mg once daily, either in the morning or evening, adjust in increments of 0.5-1 mg/day to recommended dose of 3 mg/day. <b>Bipolar mania - Adults:</b> 2-3 mg once daily, increase in increments of 1 mg/day to recommended dose of 1-6 mg/day; <b>Childn 10-17 yrs:</b> 0.5 mg once daily, either in the morning or evening, adjust at intervals of not &lt;24 hrs in increments of 0.5-1 mg/day to recommended dose of 2.5 mg/day. <b>Conduct and other disruptive behavior disorders in childn and adolescents 5-18 yrs</b> - BW &ge;50 kg: Initially, 0.5 mg/day. Optimum dose: 1 mg/day. &lt;50 kg: Initially, 0.25 mg once a day. Optimum dose: 0.5 mg/day. <b>Autism:</b> Individualized dosing. <b>Adolescents and childn 5-16 yrs and BW &ge;20 kg:</b> 0.5 mg/day, may be increased on day 4 by 0.5 mg; <b>&lt;20 kg:</b> 0.25 mg/day, may be increased on day 4 by 0.25 mg. Maintain recommended dose for minimum of 14 days, consider dose increase at &ge;2-week intervals in increments of 0.25 mg for patients &lt;20 kg or 0.5 mg in patients &ge;20 kg; <b>Elderly or debilitated patients, patients with severe hepatic or renal impairment, patients either predisposed to hypotension or in whom hypotension would pose a risk:</b> 0.5 mg daily, may be increased in increments of not &gt;0.5 mg twice daily, an increase dose of &gt;1.5 mg should occur at intervals of &ge;1 week."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Elderly with dementia-related psychosis, NMS, risk of tardive dyskinesia, presence of risk factors for VTE. Patients with history of seizures and other conditions that lower seizure threshold, cardiac arrhythmias, and in patients with congenital long QT syndrome or using drugs known to prolong QT interval, Parkinson’s disease or dementia with Lewy bodies. Possibility of suicide attempt in high-risk patients. Orthostatic hypotension, hyperglycemia and pre-existing DM, weight gain, pre-existing hyperprolactinemia and in patients with possible prolactin-dependent tumors. Esophageal dysmotility and aspiration, aspiration pneumonia, may mask signs and symptoms of overdosage of certain drugs or of conditions e.g. intestinal obstruction, Reye’s syndrome and brain tumor due to antiemetic effect, disruption of body temp regulation. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "NMS, tardive dyskinesia, orthostatic hypotension associated with dizziness, tachycardia, syncope, hyperglycemia, weight gain, hyperprolactinemia, priapism, leukopenia, neutropenia and agranulocytosis, dysphagia, hyperthermia or hypothermia. Somnolence, increased appetite, fatigue, rhinitis, URTI, vomiting, cough, urinary incontinence, increased salivation, constipation, fever, Parkinsonism, EPS, dystonia, abdominal pain, anxiety, nausea, dizziness, dry mouth, tremor, rash, akathisia and dyspepsia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Paliperidone, furosemide, centrally acting drugs (e.g. opiates, antihistamines, benzodiazepines) and alcohol, antihypertensives, levodopa and dopamine agonists, cimetidine, ranitidine, CYP2D6 inhibitors e.g. fluoxetine, paroxetine, quinidine. CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. verapamil. Carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, phenobarbital. Clozapine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 1 mg (P46.46), 2 mg (P92.93)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 87,
          "name": "Medichem Pharmaceuticals, Inc."
        },

          },

            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of chronic constipation in adults in whom laxatives fail to provide adequate relief."
          },

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 2 mg once daily. <b>Elderly >65 years:</b> Initially 1 mg once daily, may be increased to 2 mg once daily. <b>Severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>):</b> 1 mg once daily. Taken with or without food."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Renal impairment requiring dialysis.           },

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Decreased appetite; headache, dizziness; nausea, diarrhea, abdominal pain, vomiting, dyspepsia, flatulence, abnormal GI sounds; fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, verapamil, cyclosporine A, quinidine."
          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/fPZUeSoydsh8wPtdfHqOl5lsdkABeOHOOgFnK4QiJjB1ArNgdR.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ceftriaxone sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections caused by respiratory infections e.g. pneumonia, and bronchitis; otorhinolaryngology infections, renal or urinary tract infections, meningitis, peri-op prophylaxis of infections; infection of bone and joint infection of skin, wound, and soft tissue; peritonitis, cholecystitis, cholangitis, GIT infections; genital infections e.g. gonorrhea. Treatment of infections in patients with declined immunologic function."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs or weighing &gt;50 kg</b>: 1-2 g IV/IM once daily, may be increased to 4 g depending on the type and severity of infection. <b>Gonorrhea</b>: 250 mg IM single dose. <b>Prophylaxis of peri-op infections</b>: 1-2 g single dose administered 30-90 mins before surgery. <b>Terminal kidney failure – CrCl 10 mL/min</b>: Max 2 g daily. <b>Childn and neonates (15 days to 12 yrs)</b>: 20-80 mg/kg BW once daily. <b>Neonates (14 days)</b>: 25-50 mg/kg BW once daily. Max 50 mg/kg BW. Meningitis in childn and neonates: Initially 100 mg/kg BW once daily. Max 4 g/daily. Treatment duration depending on causative agent – <i>Neisseria meningitis</i>: 4 days; <i>Haemophilus influenzae</i>: 6 days; <i>Streptococcus pneumoniae</i>: 7 days. Administer doses &gt;50 mg/kg BW for at least 30 mins by intermittent IV injection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to any ingredient of the product, other cephalosporins, penicillin and anilide local anesthetics e.g. lidocaine. Coadministration of aminoglycosides."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of drug allergy, susceptible to cause allergy symptoms e.g. bronchial asthma, eruption and urticaria. Patients with severe renal disorder. Patients who cannot ingest orally (parenteral), and with poor systemic body condition due to avitaminosis K. Perform regular clinical tests (liver, renal, hematologic tests). Neonates and premature infants. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rash, urticaria, erythema, ruber, pruritus, chill, flush, allergic dermatitis, edema, erythema multiforme, anaphylactic or anaphylactoid reaction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Solutions containing calcium. Other cephem series compounds, diuretics e.g. furosemide; aminoglycosides; alcohol; probenecid; chloramphenicol. Pseudopositive reflex; Clinitest except Tes-tape; positive Coombs’ test; pseudopositive response may develop in galactosemia test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for injection (IM/IV) 1 g."
          }

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: 1-2 tabs every 6 hrs, as needed for pain and/or fever. Max 8 tabs/day."

        "content": "Brexpiprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD). Treatment of schizophrenia in adults and childn &ge;13 yrs; agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adjunctive treatment of MDD:</b> Initially 0.5-1 mg once daily then titrate weekly up to target dose of 2 mg once daily. Max 3 mg daily. <b>Treatment of schizophrenia</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 1 mg once daily on days 1-4, titrate to 2 mg on days 5-7, then 4 mg on day 8; <b>Childn 13-17 yrs:</b> Initially 0.5 mg once daily on days 1-4, titrate to 1 mg once daily on days 5-7, then to 2 mg on day 8. Weekly dose increases can be made in 1 mg increments. Max 4 mg daily. <b>Treatment of agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer’s disease:</b> Initially 0.5 mg once daily on days 1-7 then increased to 1 mg once daily on days 8-14, and 2 mg on day 15. Max 3 mg once daily after at least 14 days. <b>Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh score &ge;7)</b> - <b>MDD:</b> Max 2 mg once daily; <b>Schizophrenia:</b> Max 3 mg once daily. <b>Moderate, severe, or ESRD (CrCl < 60 mL/min)</b> - <b>MDD:</b> Max 2 mg once daily; <b>Schizophrenia:</b> Max 3 mg once daily. May be taken with or without food. <b>Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers, patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers:</b> Adjust dose except when used as adjunctive treatment of MDD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for patients with dementia-related psychosis. Suicidal thoughts and behaviors. NMS, tardive dykinesia. DM and dyslipidemia. Low WBC count and absolute neutrophil count (ANC), drug-induced leukopenia or neutropenia. Disruption of body temp regulation. Patients with history of seizures or conditions that lower the seizure threshold, impulse-control disorders, and at risk of aspiration pneumonia. CYP2D6 poor metabolizers, hepatic, and renal impairment. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Patients operating hazardous machinery including motor vehicles. Childn. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "NMS, tardive dyskinesia, stroke in elderly, restlessness, seizure, orthostatic hypotension, syncope, body temp dysregulation, dysphagia, cognitive and motor impairment, metabolic changes e.g. hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia and weight gain, leukopenia, neutropenia, agranulocytosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole, clarithromycin, ketoconazole), strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. paroxetine, fluoxetine, quinidine), strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampin, St. John's wort)."
          },

            "content": "Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) e.g. ear, nose, and throat infections, otitis media; LRTI e.g. acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, lobar and bronchopneumonia; gastrointestinal tract (e.g. typhoid and paratyphoid fever), genitourinary tract (e.g. cystitis, urethritis, pyelonephritis, bacteriuria in pregnancy, septic abortion, puerperal sepsis), skin and soft tissue, biliary tract, bone, and pelvic infections.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 250 mg three times daily. Severe infections: 500 mg three times daily. Max dose: 6 g daily in divided doses; <b>Severe RTI:</b> 3 g twice daily; <b>Acute UTI:</b> Two 3 g doses with 10-12 hrs between doses; <b>Dental abscess:</b> Two 3 g doses with 8 hrs between doses; <b>Gonorrhea:</b> Single 3 g dose; <b>Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i>:</b> Amoxicillin 750 mg to 1 g twice daily in combination with a PPI (e.g. omeprazole, lansoprazole) and another antibiotic (e.g. clarithromycin, metronidazole) for 7 days. <b>Childn < 40 kg:</b> 125 mg three times daily. Severe infections: 250 mg three times daily; <b>Acute otitis media:</b> 750 mg twice daily for 2 days, may be used as an alternative course of treatment. <b>Renal impairment</b> - <b>Adults and childn &gt;40 kg</b> - CrCl >10-30 mL/min: Max 500 mg twice daily. < 10 mL/min and patients receiving peritoneal dialysis or hemodialysis: Max 500 mg/day. 1 additional dose may be administered during and at the end of each hemodialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to beta-lactam antibiotics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Anaphylactic reactions, suspected infectious mononucleosis, pseudomembranous colitis, renal impairment, prolonged use may result in overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Concurrent use of anticoagulants.",

            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea and nausea. Skin rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, oral contraceptives, allopurinol, acenocoumarol or warfarin."
          },

            "content": "Adjunct to diet for reduction of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia.             "content": "Infections caused by susceptible organisms: lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) including bronchitis and pneumonia; skin and soft tissue infections; otitis media; sexually transmitted disease (STD) due to <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>; chancroid due to <i>Haemophilus ducreyi</i>; uncomplicated genital infections due to non-multidrug-resistant <i>Neisseria gonorrhoeae</i>; prophylaxis against <i>Mycobacterium avium-intracellulare</i> complex (MAC) infection alone or in combination with rifabutin in patients with advanced HIV; treatment of disseminated MAC (DMAC) infection in patients with advanced HIV infection in combination with ethambutol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>LRTI and URTI:</b> 500 mg/day for 3 days or 500 mg on day 1 then 250 mg daily on 2-5 days. <b>STD caused by <i>C. trachomatis</i>, <i>H. ducreyi</i>:</b> 1,000 mg as single dose. <b>Susceptible <i>N. gonorrhoeae</i>:</b> 1,000 mg or 2,000 mg in combination with ceftriaxone 250 mg or 500 mg. <b>Prophylaxis against MAC infection in HIV patients:</b> 1,200 mg once per week. <b>DMAC infections in patients with advanced HIV:</b> 600 mg once daily. <b>Childn &gt;45 kg:</b> Max total dose of 1,500 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to azithromycin, erythromycin, other macrolide or ketolide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Allergic reactions, hepatotoxicity, infantile hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, ergotism, <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea, renal impairment, prolonged cardiac repolarization and QT interval, myasthenia gravis. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",

        "brand_name": "Rhea Cefuroxime",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefuroxime (as axetil)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections of the upper respiratory tract, lower respiratory tract, genito-urinary tract, skin and soft tissue; gonorrhea, acute uncomplicated gonococcal urethritis, and cervicitis; early Lyme disease and subsequent prevention of late Lyme disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Most infections, UTI, mild to moderate LRTI, and pyelonephritis:</b> 250 mg twice daily; <b>More severe LRTI or suspected pneumonia:</b> 500 mg twice daily; <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 1 g once daily; <b>Lyme disease in adults and childn >12 yrs:</b> 500 mg twice daily for 14 days (range of 10-21 days). <b>Sequential therapy - Pneumonia:</b> 1.5 g IV/IM cefuroxime sodium thrice or twice daily for 48-72 hrs, followed by 500 mg oral cefuroxime axetil twice daily for 7-10 days; <b>Acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis:</b> 750 mg IV/IM cefuroxime sodium thrice or twice daily for 48-72 hrs, followed by 500 mg oral cefuroxime axetil twice daily for 5-10 days. <b>Childn - Most infections:</b> 125 mg twice daily; <b>Otitis media, more severe infections (if appropriate):</b> 250 mg twice daily; <b>Lyme disease in childn < 12 yrs:</b> 250 mg twice daily for 14 days. <b>Renal impairment:</b> 125-500 mg; <b>CrCl 10-29 mL/min:</b> Every 24 hrs; <b>< 10 mL/min:</b> Every 48 hrs; <b>Hemodialysis:</b> Single additional dose at the end of each dialysis. Do not crush or split tab. Taken after food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Overgrowth of <i>Candida</i> and other non-susceptible organisms (e.g., enterococci and <i>Clostridium difficile</i>), pseudomembranous colitis; Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction during treatment of Lyme disease; false negative result in ferricyanide test. Discontinue if prolonged or significant diarrhea or abdominal cramps occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 3 months. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Overgrowth of <i>Candida</i>, eosinophilia, headache, dizziness, diarrhea, nausea, abdominal pain, transient increase of hepatic enzymes (ALT, AST, LDH)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that reduce gastric acidity, oral contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 500 mg (P45.82)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) e.g. tonsillitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, otitis media and scarlet fever; LRTI e.g. bronchitis, pneumonia, empyema and lung abscess; skin and soft tissue (e.g. acne, furuncles, cellulitis, impetigo, abscesses, and wound infections), bone and joint (e.g. osteomyelitis and septic arthritis), gynecological (e.g. <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i> cervicitis, endometritis, cellulitis, vaginal cuff infection and tubo-ovarian abscess, salpingitis and pelvic inflammatory disease), and intra-abdominal (e.g. peritonitis and abdominal abscess) infections; septicemia and endocarditis, dental infections, toxoplasmic encephalitis in patients with AIDS, <i>Pneumocystis jirovecii</i> (previously classified as <i>Pneumocystis carinii</i>) pneumonia in patients with AIDS, malaria, endocarditis in patients sensitive or allergic to penicillins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 600-1,800 mg/day in 2, 3, or 4 equal doses. <b>Childn &gt;1 month:</b> 8-25 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equal doses. <b><i>C. trachomatis</i> cervicitis:</b> 450-600 mg four times daily for 10-14 days. <b>Toxoplasmic encephalitis in patients with AIDS:</b> Clindamycin 600-1,200 mg every 6 hrs for 2 weeks followed by 300-600 mg every 6 hrs + pyrimethamine 25-75 mg each day for 8-10 weeks and folinic acid 10-20 mg/day should be given with higher doses of pyrimethamine. Total duration: 8-10 weeks. <b><i>P. jirovecii</i> (<i>carinii</i>) pneumonia in patients with AIDS:</b> Clindamycin 300-450 mg every 6 hrs for 21 days + primaquine 15-30 mg once daily for 21 days. <b>Acute streptococcal tonsillitis/pharyngitis:</b> 300 mg twice daily for 10 days. <b>Uncomplicated malaria, <i>Plasmodium falciparum</i></b> - <b>Adults:</b> Quinine sulfate 650 mg three times daily for 3-7 days + clindamycin 20 mg base/kg/day divided three times daily for 7 days; <b>Childn:</b> Quinine sulfate 10 mg/kg three times daily for 3-7 days + clindamycin 20 mg base/kg/day divided three times daily for 7 days. <b>Prophylaxis of endocarditis in patients sensitive to penicillin</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 600 mg 1 hr before procedure; <b>Childn:</b> 20 mg/kg 1 hr before procedure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to clindamycin, lactose, corn starch, talc, magnesium stearate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "<i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Neuropathic pain in adults including neuropathic pain associated with spinal cord injury. Adjunctive therapy in adults with partial seizures, with or without secondary generalization. Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) in adults. Fibromyalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "150-600 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>Neuropathic pain:</b> Initially 150 mg/day, may be increased to 300 mg/day after an interval of 3-7 days. Max 600 mg/day after an additional 7-day interval, if needed. <b>Fibromyalgia:</b> Initially 150 mg/day, may be increased to 300 mg/day in 2 divided doses. May be further increased to 450 mg/day in 2 divided doses and to a max 600 mg/day after an additional week, if needed. <b>Epilepsy:</b> Initially 150 mg/day, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>GAD:</b> Initially 150-600 mg/day given as 2 or 3 divided doses, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 1 week. Max 600 mg/day after an additional week. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl &ge;30-< 60 mL/min: Initially 75 mg/day, max 300 mg/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. &ge;15-< 30 mL/min: Initially 25-50 mg/day, max 150 mg/day as single dose or in 2 divided doses. < 15 mL/min: Initially 25 mg/day, max 75 mg/day as single dose. Supplementary dose of 25-100 mg single dose following hemodialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Adjust hypoglycemic medications in diabetic patients who gain weight during treatment. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema, or transient visual blurring and other changes in visual acuity occur. Withdrawal symptoms. History of drug abuse and observe for signs of misuse or abuse (e.g. development of tolerance, dose escalation, drug-seeking behavior). Renal impairment. CHF. May affect ability to drive or operate machines. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. Childn < 12 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, somnolence. Nasopharyngitis; increased appetite; euphoric mood, confusion, irritability, depression, disorientation, insomnia, decreased libido; ataxia, abnormal coordination, tremor, dysarthria, amnesia, memory impairment, attention disturbance, paresthesia, hypoesthesia, sedation, balance disorder, lethargy; blurred vision, diplopia; vertigo; vomiting, constipation, flatulence, abdominal distension, dry mouth; muscle cramp, arthralgia, back pain, limb pain, cervical spasm; peripheral edema, edema, abnormal gait, fall, feeling drunk, abnormal feeling, fatigue, increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ethanol or lorazepam, oxycodone. Other CNS depressants. Medications that have the potential to produce constipation e.g. opioid analgesics."

        },

        "content": "Rivaroxaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in adults undergoing elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE. <b>15 mg and 20 mg:</b> Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (SPAF)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of stroke and SPAF:</b> 20 mg once daily; Patients with CrCl < 50-30 mL/min: 15 mg once daily; Patients who undergo percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with stent placement: 15 mg once daily (or 10 mg once daily in addition to P2Y12 inhibitor for patients with moderate renal impairment) for a max of 12 months after PCI with stent placement. <b>Prevention of VTE in adults undergoing elective hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> 10 mg once daily with or without food for 5 weeks after major hip surgery, or for 2 weeks after major knee surgery. Administer initial dose within 6-10 hrs after surgery. <b>DVT and PE</b> - <b>Treatment:</b> 15 mg twice daily for the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 weeks, then 20 mg once daily for the remaining treatment. Take with food. <b>Prevention:</b> 10 mg or 20 mg once daily (based on individual risk assessment) with or without food after at least 6 months of treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active bleeding, hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy. Patients with rare hereditary problems of lactose or galactose intolerance. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended for thromboprophylaxis in patients having recently undergone transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Patients with renal impairment, hip fracture surgery, increased bleeding risk. History of thrombosis. Epidural or spinal anesthesia, surgery and interventions, prosthetic heart valves, triple positive antiphospholipid syndrome, acute PE in patients with hemodynamic instability or requiring thrombolysis or pulmonary embolectomy. Concomitant use with azole-antimycotics (e.g. ketoconazole) or HIV protease inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir), NSAIDs, platelet aggregation inhibitors, other antithrombotics, SSRIs, SNRIs. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia; eye hemorrhage; gingival bleeding, GI hemorrhage, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, vomiting; fever, peripheral edema, fatigue, asthenia; post-procedural hemorrhage; increased transaminases; pain in extremity; dizziness, headache; urogenital tract hemorrhage, renal impairment; epistaxis, hemoptysis; pruritus, rash, ecchymosis, cutaneous and SC hemorrhage; hypotension, hematoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers. Pgp inhibitors. Clarithromycin, erythromycin, fluconazole, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbitone or St. John’s wort. Azole-antimycotics (e.g. ketoconazole) or HIV protease inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir), NSAIDs, platelet aggregation inhibitors, other antithrombotics, SSRIs, SNRIs."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2F4DZPrz020VD2rMFg1LCYtMcXvDmcEyXmkaQWJA5m4aflNSag.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cetirizine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Antihistamines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis and urticaria of allergic origin. <b>Tab:</b> Prophylactic and symptomatic treatment of vasomotor rhinitis, pruritus associated with allergic reactions and of mild uncomplicated allergic skin manifestation of urticaria and angioedema, dermatographism, urticaria associated with transfusions, sneezing and rhinorrhoea associated with the common cold. Adjunctive therapy to epinephrine and other standard measures for anaphylactic reactions after the acute manifestation have been controlled, for asthma medication to reduce symptoms and improve bronchodilation in patients with mild atopic asthma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – Adults and adolescents:</b> 5-10 mg once a day. <b>Childn &gt;6 yrs:</b> 5-10 mg once a day. <b>Childn 2-6 yrs:</b> 2.5 mg once a day. <b>Syr – Adult:</b> 1-2 tsp once daily. <b>Childn &gt;6 yrs:</b> 1-2 tsp once daily. <b>Childn 2-6 yrs:</b> &frac;12 tsp daily, may increased to max 1 tsp."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (&lt;10 mL/min CrCl) and hepatic impairment, rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with epilepsy and risk of convulsion. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Drowsiness, dryness of mouth, nose or throat, cardiac arrhythmias, palpitations, tachycardia, cholestasis, hepatitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CNS depressants, alcohol, theophylline, ritonavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg (P16.50). Syrup 5 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P219.00)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For acute treatment of signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and acute gouty arthritis. Management of acute pain associated with inflammation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>OA</b>: 30 mg once daily, may be increased to 60 mg once daily if necessary. <b>RA</b>: 90 mg once daily. <b>Acute gouty arthritis</b>: 120 mg once daily. Max 8 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with IHD, HTN, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, PAD. Smoking. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances e.g. GI discomfort, nausea, diarrhea. Headache, vertigo, dizziness, nervousness, tinnitus, depression, drowsiness, insomnia. Anemia, thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, eosinophilia, agranulocytosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Rifampicin, ethinylestradiol, oral salbutamol, minoxidil."

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/s3Xweal6ah4WxhhJCVBBNM5rS352WK47ys9vdixkoAPjNKEXDg.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dienogest",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: Start on any day of the menstrual cycle. 1 tab daily without break, preferably at the same time each day; must be taken continuously regardless of any vaginal bleeding. When pack is finished, start the next pack without interruption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active venous thromboembolic disorder. Present or history of arterial and CV disease (e.g. MI, CVA, IHD); severe hepatic disease as long as liver function values have not returned to normal; liver tumors (benign or malignant). DM with vascular involvement.  Known or suspected sex hormone-dependent malignancies. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Ocular lesion due to ophthalmic vascular disease (e.g. partial or complete loss of vision or visual field defect). Current or history of migraine with focal aura. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid smoking. Serious uterine bleeding. Risk for osteoporosis and changes in bone mineral density. Women with diabetes; history of chloasma, depression, extrauterine pregnancy or impairment of tube function. May experience changes in bleeding pattern, HTN, recurrence of cholestatic jaundice and/or pruritus, persistent ovarian follicles. Discontinue if there is a presence or suspected arterial or venous thrombotic event. Monitor any irregularity or anomaly of the breast.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Changes in menstrual bleeding pattern (e.g. spotting, irregular bleeding, amenorrhea), headache, breast discomfort, depressed mood, acne."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin) and inhibitors (e.g. azole antifungals, macrolides, diltiazem, verapamil), HIV/HCV protease inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir, saquinavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, boceprevir), NNRTIs (e.g. nevirapine, efavirenz), antacids (e.g. cimetidine, ranitidine), grapefruit juice, St. John’s wort; liver, thyroid, adrenal and renal function parameters, plasma levels of carrier proteins (e.g. corticosteroid-binding globulin and lipid/lipoprotein fractions), carbohydrate metabolism, blood coagulation and fibrinolysis parameters."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2 mg x 28 (P1,865.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3567,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3567,
        "brand_name": "Risponz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Yd3W2xGELBx1I9Wgqjnhs0SExiu8g49owhODJkfa6qIgdvUa9K.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Cefa2xbPYlk2jZvzNJSou2XEKyDTEoqN0Xrq7SS3nYrQEXuL2r.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cqb18fsGktC7uDoKUK90afKDb2GozLoidwLrwpYk346LAeApH2.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Risperidone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia and other psychoses. <b>Tab</b>: Short-term treatment of acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorder. Treatment of irritability associated with autistic disorder. <b>Oral soln</b>: Treatment of moderate and severe manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder. Short-term symptomatic treatment (up to 6 weeks) of persistent aggression in conduct disorder in childn &ge;5 yrs and adolescents with sub-average intellectual functioning or mental retardation diagnosed according to DSM-IV criteria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – Schizophrenia</b>: 2 mg on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, 4 mg on 2<sup>nd</sup> day, and 6 mg on the 3<sup>rd</sup> day; may be given in 1-2 divided doses, may be adjusted with &lt;1 week intervals. Maintenance: 4-8 mg daily. <b>Elderly or patients with renal/hepatic impairment</b>: Initially 0.5 mg twice daily slowly increased by 0.5 mg to dose of 1-2 mg twice daily. <b>Oral soln – Schizophrenia</b> - Adults: 2 mg/day given once or twice daily, may be increased to 4 mg on the 2<sup>nd</sup> day. Elderly: Initially 0.5 mg twice daily, may be increased to 1-2 mg twice daily in increments of 0.5 mg twice daily. <b>Manic episodes in bipolar disorder</b> - Adults: Initially 2 mg/day. Dose intervals: Not &lt;24 hrs in dosage increments of 1 mg/day. Elderly: Initially 0.5 mg twice daily, may be increased to 1-2 mg twice daily in increments of 0.5 mg twice daily. <b>Persistent aggression with moderate to severe Alzheimer’s dementia</b>: Initially 0.25 mg twice daily, may be adjusted by increments of 0.25 mg twice daily not more frequently than every other day. Optimum dose: 0.5 mg twice daily. Duration: Not &gt;6 weeks. <b>Conduct disorder in childn and adolescents 5-18 yrs</b> - BW &ge;50 kg: 0.5 mg/day. Optimum dose: 1 mg/day; &lt;50 kg: 0.25 mg/day. Optimum dose: 0.5 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Tab</b>: Conduct and other disruptive behavioral disorders. Patients with other types of dementia than Alzheimer’s. Childn &lt;5 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Not for the treatment of dementia-related behavioral disturbances. Patients with Parkinson’s disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, history of seizures or other conditions that lower seizure threshold, CV disease. Risk of cerebrovascular adverse events in mixed or vascular type of dementia. May induce orthostatic hypotension, tardive dyskinesia/EPS, NMS, hyperglycemia, hyperprolactinemia, QT prolongation, priapism, disruption of body temp regulation, VTE, weight gain. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Childn and adolescents with conduct disorder. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anxiety, dizziness, headache, NMS, tardive dyskinesia; priapism, weight gain, nausea and vomiting, constipation, EPS. <b>Tab</b>: Insomnia, agitation, sedation for childn and adolescents, somnolence, fatigue, impaired concentration, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, weight gain, blurred vision, erectile dysfunction, ejaculatory dysfunction, orgastic dysfunction, urinary incontinence, rhinitis, rash. <b>Oral soln</b>: Dystonic reactions, abnormal T-waves with prolonged ventricular repolarization, arrhythmias, orthostatic HTN, amenorrhea, galactorrhea, gynecomastia, sexual dysfunction; cholestatic jaundice, agranulocytosis, overflow incontinence, urinary retention, altered temp regulation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diuretics. Class IA and III antiarrhythmics, TCAs (e.g., amitriptyline), tetracyclic antidepressants, some antihistamines, other antipsychotics, some antimalarials; medicines causing electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), bradycardia, or inhibition of risperidone metabolism; alcohol and CNS drugs, levodopa, dopamine, carbamazepine, enzyme inducers, phenothiazines, some beta-blockers, fluoxetine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 1 mg (P27.50), 2 mg (P45.00), 3 mg (P49.50). Oral solution 1 mg/mL x 30 mL (P1,995.00)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/VvPbib6OY7Z7exkfC6QbIg7j3UiKk3JMOdZ5U014OfEaJH2DNf.jpg",

        },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Upper and lower respiratory tract infections (URTI and LRTI) including ear, nose, and throat (ENT) infections (e.g. acute otitis media); gastrointestinal tract, genitourinary tract, skin and skin structure, bone, and gallbladder or biliary tract infections. <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> infections (in combination with other drugs), Lyme disease, dental abscess (as an adjunct to surgical management). Prophylaxis for endocarditis. Step down treatment for severe infections, initially given IV antimicrobial therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "250-500 mg every 8 hrs or 500 mg every 12 hrs. Max 6 g/day in divided doses. <b>ENT, genitourinary tract, skin and skin structure infections</b> - Mild to moderate: 250 mg every 8 hrs or 500 mg ever 12 hrs. Severe: 500 mg every 8 hrs. <b>LRTI:</b> 500 mg every 8 hrs. <b><i>H. pylori</i> to reduce the risk of recurrent duodenal ulcer</b> - Triple therapy regimen: Amoxicillin 1 g + clarithromycin 500 mg + omeprazole 20 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. Dual therapy regimen: Amoxicillin 1 g + lansoprazole 30 mg every 8 hrs fr 14 days. <b>Lyme disease</b> - Isolated erythema chromicum migrans: 4 g/day. Generalized manifestations: 6 g/day. <b>Endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures:</b> 2 g as single dose 30-60 mins before procedure. <b>Adults and childn &ge;40 kg with renal impairment</b> - CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 250 mg or 500 mg every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min and hemodialysis: 250 mg or 50 mg every 24 hrs. <b>Duration of treatment</b> - Most infections: 5-14 days; beta-heolytic streptococcal infections: At least 10 days; Lyme disease: At least 12 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with infectious mononucleosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment. CDAD. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms, including fungi. Maintain adequate fluid intake. Perform periodic assessment of organ system functions (renal, hepatic, hematopoietic) during prolonged therapy. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dermatologic or hypersensitivity reactions, GI, nervous system, hemic and lymphatic system, hepatic, and renal effects. Tooth discoloration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Allopurinol, anticoagulants, bacteriostatic agents (e.g. chloramphenicol, macrolides, sulfonamides, tetracyclines), beta-lactamase inhibitors, digoxin, methotrexate, oral contraceptives, probenecid. False-positive results using Clinitest, Benedict’s soln. May interfere with protein testing using colorimetric methods."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 500 mg (P7.50)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> Initially 50 mg once a day, may be increased to 100 mg once a day. <b>Angina pectoris:</b> Initially 50 mg once a day, may be increased after 1 week to 100 mg once a day or 50 mg twice a day. <b>Cardiac arrhythmias</b> - Maintenance: 50-100 mg once a day. <b>MI:</b> Give 5 mg atenolol by slow IV injection within 12 hrs of onset of chest pain, followed by another 5 mg IV atenolol 10 mins later. May give 100 mg once a day or 50 mg twice a day for 6-9 days or until discharge from hospital. <b>Elderly and patients with renal impairment</b> - CrCl 15-35 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: Max 50 mg/day; < 15 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 25 mg/day or 50 mg on alternate days; hemodialysis: 25 or 50 mg after each dialysis."

Anesthesia with agents that produce myocardial depression (e.g. ether, chloroform cyclopropane)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with CAD, CHF controlled by digitalis or diuretics, bronchospastic disease, labile diabetes, history of spontaneous hypoglycemia, thyrotoxicosis, pheochromocytoma, Prinzmetal angina, 1<sup>st</sup>-degree heart block, severe renal disease, systolic BP < 120 mmHg, atrial fibrillation, history of anaphylactic reaction. Concomitant use with CCBs. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
