        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Captopril",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For hypertension (HTN) as monotherapy or as component of a multiple-drug regimen in the stepped care approach. Treatment of chronic heart failure with reduction of systolic ventricular function, in combination with diuretics, digitalis and beta blockers (when appropriate); macroproteinuric diabetic nephropathy in patients with type 1 diabetes. To improve survival following myocardial infarction (MI) in clinically stable patients with left ventricular dysfunction manifested as ejection fraction &le;40%; to reduce the incidence of overt heart failure and subsequent hospitalizations for congestive heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dose. Take 1 hr before meals. <b>HTN:</b> Initially 25 mg 2-3x a day, may be increased up to 150 mg 2-3x a day (with a diuretic), after 1 or 2 weeks. Max 450 mg/day in divided doses. <b>Heart failure:</b> 25 mg 3x a day. Max: 450 mg/day in divided doses. Patients with normal or low BP, are treated with diuretics and may be hyponatremic or hypovolemic: 6.25 or 12.5 mg 3x a day. <b>Left ventricular dysfunction after MI:</b> After a single dose of 6.25 mg, initiate 12.5 mg 3x a day, may be increased to 25 mg 3x a day after several days. Maintenance dose: 50 mg 3x a day. <b>Diabetic nephropathy:</b> 75-100 mg/day in divided doses. Patients with renal impairment: Initially 12.5 mg 2x a day. <b>Elderly:</b> Initially 6.25 mg 2x a day. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl >40 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 25-50 mg/day. Max 150 mg/day; 21-40 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 25 mg/day. Max 100 mg/day; 10-20 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 12.5 mg/day. Max 75 mg/day; < 10 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 6.25 mg/day. Max 37.5 mg/day. <b>Childn 12-18 yrs:</b> 0.1 mg/kg. Max 6.25 mg (test dose). If tolerated, give 12.5-25 mg 2-3x a day. Max 150 mg/day; <b>1 month-12 yrs:</b> 0.1 mg/kg. Max 6.25 mg (test dose). If tolerated, give 0.1-0.3 mg/kg 2-3x a day. Max 6 mg/kg/day in divided doses; and 4 mg/kg/day in divided doses (1 month-1 yr)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of angioedema associated with previous ACE inhibitor therapy. Hereditary or idiopathic angioneurotic edema. Coadministration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients undergoing desensitization procedures; hemodialyzed with high-flux polyacrylonitrile membranes. Patients with collagen vascular disease, immunosuppressant therapy, pre-existing impaired renal function, bilateral renal artery stenosis or renal artery stenosis of a solitary kidney, heart failure, hepatic failure, renal insufficiency, DM, ischemic CV or cerebrovascular disease, left ventricular valvular and outflow tract obstruction, aortic stenosis. Perform WBC and differential counts before therapy and every 2 weeks during the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months. Dual blockade of RAAS. Correct vol- and sodium depletion before treatment. Coadministration with mTOR, allopurinol or procainamide. Concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes. Surgery; anesthesia use. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Infants. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C for 1<sup>st</sup> trimester and D for 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Angioedema, malaise, fatigue, asthenia, fever; blurred vision, itching or dry eyes, taste impairment, dysgeusia. CV, nervous system, GI, hematologic, musculoskeletal, metabolic or nutritional, respiratory, hepatic, skin and appendages, urogenital or reproductive effects."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Agents affecting sympathetic activity (e.g. ganglionic or adrenergic neuron-blocking agents); nitroglycerin or other nitrates; allopurinol, procainamide, cytostatic or immunosuppressive agents (e.g. azathioprine); antacids, antidiabetics, clonidine, lithium, NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin), probenecid. Other antihypertensive agents (e.g. beta-blockers, long-acting CCBs), potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride) or potassium supplements, TCAs, sympathomimetics. False-positive urine test for acetone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mg (P11.00)."
          }

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/C4Q6syVCADFcBPT8IY7BGpRyRUyurxAQIPZlJzG7NFUh4eTuH4.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OqzJT4szsnC7rCJkER3Jr1EhgNubOGNgRAFa4yT9tcMlyCeQS9.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kLOitgjjRsTA8qv5dtxkIbSIZUySUcD1gUaD2bB4zxwTAhgDzv.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Carvedilol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Essential hypertension (HTN), congestive heart failure, chronic stable angina pectoris and moderate moderate-severe stable chronic heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Essential HTN</b> - Adults: 6.25 mg twice daily, the dose should be maintained for 7-14 days, and then increased to 12.5 mg twice daily can be adjusted to 25 mg twice daily if tolerated and needed; Elderly: 12.5 mg once daily. Max 50 mg/day. <b>Chronic stable angina pectoris</b> - Adults: Initially 12.5 mg twice a day for 1st 2 days, continue at 25 mg twice daily. Max 100 mg/day divided in 2 doses. Elderly: Initially 12.5 mg twice a day for 1st 2 days, continue at max 25 mg twice daily. <b>Heart failure:</b> Initially 3.125 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, may be increased slowly with intervals not < 2 weeks up to 6.25 mg twice a day, then 12.5 mg twice daily and finally up to 25 mg twice daily. Patients < 85 kg BW: Max 25 mg twice daily; >85 kg BW: Max 50 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Unstable or decompensated heart failure, liver dysfunction, 2<sup>nd</sup>- and 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block, severe bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome, severe hypotension, cardiogenic shock, history bronchospasm or asthma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with low BP (systolic BP &lt;100 mmHg), IHD and diffuse vascular disease, underlying renal insufficiency, COPD, DM, PVD, history of serious hypersensitivity, psoriasis, pheochromocytoma, Prinzmetal’s variant angina; undergoing major surgery. Left ventricular dysfunction following acute MI, thyrotoxicosis, bradycardia, contact lenses. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Concomitant use with digitalis glycosides, CCBs (verapamil, diltiazem) or other antiarrhythmic agents. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>Serious infections:</b> 150-300 mg every 6 hrs. <b>More severe infections:</b> 300-450 mg every 6 hrs. <b>Acne:</b> 150 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Bacterial vaginosis:</b> 300 mg every 12 hrs for 7 days. <b>Cervicitis due to <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>:</b> 450 mg every 6 hrs for 10-14 days. <b>PID</b> (inpatient treatment): Initially with IV therapy for at least 4 days and at least 48 hrs after patient improves, then continue with oral therapy 450 mg every 6 hrs for 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of bacterial endocarditis in penicillin-allergic patients:</b> 600 mg single dose 30-60 mins before procedure. <b><i>Pneumocystis jiroveci</i> (<i>carinii</i>) pneumonia in patients with AIDS:</b> 300-450 mg every 6 hrs + primaquine for 21 days. <b>Alternative treatment of multidrug-resistant </i>Plasmodium falciparum</i> infection:</b> 5-10 mg/kg/day twice a day + quinine or amodiaquine for at least 5 days."

            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Overgrowth of <i>Clostridium difficile</i>. Discontinue when hypersensitivity or severe skin reactions occur.           "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gCDOe5w3n8ZAo3nhKFnVckRoskXWwCF4Uf3N9xNv3kQFVhCO7D.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/8L97NKivfLb6kl2Z47bzgeubF5B5rguq89J2GUrwq1yzRM5EGc.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Co-amoxiclav",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) including ear, nose, and throat infections e.g. sinusitis, tonsillitis, otitis media; skin and soft tissue infections e.g. boils/abscesses, cellulitis, wound infections, intra-abdominal sepsis; LRTI e.g. acute and chronic bronchitis, pneumonia, lung abscess; genitourinary tract infections e.g. cystitis, urethritis, pyelonephritis, septic abortion, pelvic infection, gonorrhea; osteomyelitis, septicemia, peritonitis, post-op infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn >12 yrs</b> - <b>Mild to moderate infections:</b> 625 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Severe (including chronic and recurrent UTI and LRTI):</b> 625 mg every 8 hrs or 1 g every 12 hrs. Administer at the start of a meal for better absorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction (e.g. anaphylaxis) to another beta-lactam agent (e.g. cephalosporin, carbapenem, or monobactam). History of jaundice/hepatic impairment due to amoxicillin/clavulanic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Fatal hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylactoid and severe cutaneous adverse reactions. Do not use to treat penicillin-resistant <i>S. pneumoniae</i>. Convulsions in patients with impaired renal function or receiving high doses. Patients with renal impairment. Avoid use if infectious mononucleosis is suspected. Discontinue use if symptoms of acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis occur. Concomitant use with allopurinol or anticoagulants. Prolonged treatment. Hepatic events predominantly in males and elderly. Antibiotic-associated colitis. Periodic assessment of organ system functions during prolonged therapy. Crystalluria in patients with reduced urine output. False positive for Coombs’ test. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea. Mucocutaneous candidosis; nausea and vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants (e.g. acenocoumarol, warfarin), methotrexate, probenecid, mycophenolate mofetil."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 625 mg (P36.75), 1 g (P58.75)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Initially 1 mg followed by 500 mcg every 2-3 hrs until relief of pain is obtained or vomiting or diarrhea occurs. Max 6 mg. Should be taken with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hemodialysis, severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;10 mL/min). Patients with renal or hepatic impairment receiving P-gp or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Childn. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with blood disorders, and cardiac, hepatic, or GI disease. Elderly and debilitated patients. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."

            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN) and heart failure. Prophylaxis to patients with asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction to delay onset of symptomatic heart failure; to reduce incidence of coronary ischemic events, including myocardial infarction (MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> Initially 5 mg/day. 1<sup>st</sup> dose given at bedtime. Elderly: Initially 2.5 mg daily. Maintenance dose: 10-20 mg once daily up to 40 mg daily in severe HTN. May be given in 2 divided doses if control is inadequate with single dose. <b>Patients with renal impairment or receiving diuretics:</b> 2.5 mg daily. If possible, withdraw diuretic 2-3 days before treatment. <b>Heart failure:</b> Initially 2.5 mg daily. Maintenance dose: 20 mg daily as single dose or in 2 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with aortic stenosis or outflow tract obstruction, renovascular disease. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Assess renal function before therapy. Patients with existing renal disease, collagen vascular disorders (e.g. SLE, scleroderma), heart failure, salt or water depletion; receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypotension, dizziness, fatigue, headache, nausea, other GI disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diuretics, other antihypertensives, alcohol; potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes; NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 20 mg (P16.00)."
          }

        },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Low dose (&lt;1,200 mg/day):</b> Symptomatic treatment of fever and pains e.g. headache, toothache, pain of motor system and dysmenorrhea. <b>High dose (&gt;1,200 mg/day):</b> Long-term symptomatic treatment of chronic rheumatoid arthritis: Rheumatoid polyarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, Fiessinger-Leroy-Reiter syndrome, psoriatic arthritis, painful and disable arthrosis; short-term symptomatic treatment of acute phase of periarthritis (scapulohumeral periarthritis, tendinitis, bursitis), lumbalgia, radiculalgia; traumatism; dysmenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Analgesic and antipyretic:</b> Initially 200-400 mg every 4-6 hrs if necessary. Max: 1,200 mg/day (6 caps). <b>Rheumatism - Treatment:</b> 2,400 mg/day; <b>Maintenance:</b> 1,200-1,600 mg/day (6-8 caps). <b>Dysmenorrhea:</b> 400 mg (2 caps) 3-4 times daily. Swallow entire cap with water. Do not chew. Administer during meal."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Gastroduodenal ulcers. Severe hepatic and renal insufficiency. Concomitant use with other NSAIDs including aspirin; oral anticoagulants, heparin, oral sulfonylurea hypoglycemic agents, lithium, ticlopidine. Childn &lt;15 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "CV risk at high doses and long-term treatment. Patients with history of GI disease e.g. ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease. Concomitant use with oral corticosteroids, or anticoagulants e.g. warfarin, SSRIs, or antiplatelet agents e.g. aspirin. Renal papillary necrosis and other renal injury on long-term administration. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, gastralgia, dyspepsia, hemorrhagia, transitory troubles; rash, eruption, pruritus, edema; asthma; headache; hepatic dysfunctions e.g. transient increase in transaminases, renal dysfunctions e.g. oliguria, renal failure, hematologic dysfunctions e.g. agranulocytosis, hemolytic anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other NSAIDs including high-dose salicylates; oral anticoagulants, heparin, ticlopidine; lithium; methotrexate; oral sulfonylurea hypoglycemic agents; antihypertensive agents e.g. beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, diuretics; digitalis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 200 mg (P4.50)."
          }

      "data": {
        "id": 3793,
        "brand_name": "RiteMED Levofloxacin",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/zcBD4GLkriQOSl0C2SdWRTlIbqIxFBFputedGPVz3M9FLUJvZd.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/B2HSqBfDvSV7RbIAOTW3QJ9V7UvAz8xczTh8kFOTf646RkczTt.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qxd1AOHkD2i37hdryrGtArVrD2wpC57gclbGMSVDV2FSvLZVrq.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levofloxacin hemihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of adults (&ge;18 yrs) with mild, moderate, or severe infections caused by susceptible strains of the designated microorganisms for the following conditions: Acute bacterial sinusitis, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections (mild to moderate) including abscesses, cellulitis, furuncles, impetigo, pyoderma, wound infections, complicated urinary tract infections (UTI), chronic bacterial prostatitis. To reduce the incidence or progression of inhalational following exposure to aerosolized <i>Bacillus anthracis</i>. Treatment of plague, including pneumonic and septicemic plague, due to <i>Yersinia pestis</i> and prophylaxis for plague."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Usual adult dose:</b> 500 mg once every 24 hrs. <b>Duration of treatment</b> - <b>Acute bacterial sinusitis:</b> 10-14 days; <b>Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis:</b> 7 days; <b>CAP:</b> 7-14 days; <b>Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections:</b> 7-10 days; <b>Uncomplicated UTI:</b> 10-14 days; <b>Chronic bacterial prostatitis:</b> 28 days; <b>Inhalation anthrax (post-exposure):</b> 60 days; <b>Plague:</b> 10-14 days. <b>Patients with impaired renal function</b> - <b>CrCl 20-49 mL/min:</b> Initially 500 mg, then 250 mg every 24 hrs; <b>10-19 mL/min, hemodialysis, CAPD:</b> Initially 500 mg, then 250 mg every 48 hrs."
          },

            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults, childn and adolescents 6-18 yrs; renal disease in adults with HTN and type 2 diabetes mellitus with proteinuria &ge;0.5 g/day; chronic heart failure in adults when ACE inhibitors is incompatible or contraindicated. Reduce risk of stroke in hypertensive adults with left ventricular hypertrophy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>HTN, reduction of stroke in patients with left ventricular hypertrophy, patients with HTN and DM with proteinuria &ge;0.5 g/day:</b> 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg once daily. <b>Heart failure:</b> Initially 12.5 mg once daily, titrated at weekly intervals up to max 150 mg once daily. <b>Patients with intravascular vol depletion:</b> Initially 25 mg once daily. <b>Childn and adolescents 6-18 yrs</b> - &gt;20-&lt;50 kg BW: 25 mg once daily, may be increased to 50 mg once daily; &gt;50 g BW: 50 mg once daily, may be increased to max 100 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with type 2 DM. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of angioedema, renal (CrCl 30-50 mL/min) and hepatic impairment, heart failure, bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of artery to a solitary kidney, recent kidney transplantation, primary aldosteronism, ischemic CV and cerebrovascular disease, aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; vol- and sodium-depleted. Concomitant use with potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, ACE inhibitors. Dual blockade of RAAS with ACE inhibitors or aliskiren.           },

            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness; vertigo; hyperkalemia. Asthenia, fatigue. Anemia; orthostatic hypotension; renal impairment and failure; increased in blood urea, serum creatinine and serum potassium. Hypoglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors, aliskiren, TCAs, antipsychotics, baclofen, amifostine, fluconazole, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, lithium, NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors."
          },

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hypertension (HTN), angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmias, myocardial infarction (MI). Adjunct treatment of thyrotoxicosis. Prevention of migraine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN and angina pectoris:</b> 50-100 mg daily given in single or divided doses, may be increased at weekly intervals. <b>Cardiac arrhythmias:</b> 100-150 mg/day given in 2 or 3 divided doses, may be increased up to 300 mg/day given in divided doses. <b>MI</b> - <b>Early treatment</b> - Patients who tolerate full IV dose: 50 mg every 6 hrs for 48 hrs, given 15 mins after last IV dose. Maintenance dose: 100 mg twice daily; patients who do not tolerate full IV dose: 25 or 50 mg every 6 hrs, given 15 mins after last IV dose. <b>Late treatment:</b> 100 mg twice daily. <b>Adjunct to treatment of thyrotoxicosis:</b> 150-200 mg/day given in 3 or 4 divided doses, may be increased up to 400 mg. <b>Prevention of migraine:</b> 100 mg/day given as single dose in the morning, may be increased to 200 mg/day in 2 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe bronchial asthma or history of severe bronchospasm, hypotension, metabolic acidosis. Sinus bradycardia, heart block &gt;1<sup>st</sup> degree, cardiogenic shock, overt or decompensated cardiac failure, sick sinus syndrome, severe peripheral arterial circulatory disorders, untreated pheochromocytoma. HR < 45 bpm, 2<sup>nd</sup>- or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree heart block, significant 1<sup>st</sup>-degree heart block (P-R interval &ge;0.24 sec), systolic BP < 100 mmHg, moderate to severe cardiac failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Patients with bronchospastic disease, IHD, DM receiving insulin or oral hypoglycemic agents, thyrotoxicosis, impaired hepatic failure, history of severe anaphylactic reaction; bradycardia, AV block, hypotension. Patients undergoing major surgery. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."

            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Cap 20 mg:</b> short-term treatment and symptomatic relief for heartburn that occurs two or more days per week (frequent heartburn). <b>Delayed-release cap 40 mg:</b> Conditions where inhibition of gastric acid secretion may be beneficial, including aspiration syndromes, dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease (PUD), and the Zollinger-Ellison syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap 20 mg:</b> 1 cap once daily 30 mins to 1 hr before breakfast with full glass of water for 14 days or as prescribed. <b>Delayed-release cap 40 mg</b> - <b>Acid-related dyspepsia:</b> 10-20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>GERD:</b> 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks, followed by 4-8 weeks. <b>Childn >2 yrs:</b> 0.7-1.4 mg/kg daily given for 4-12 weeks. Max 40 mg daily given for 4-12 weeks. <b>Refractory esophagitis:</b> 40 mg daily. <b>Esophagitis:</b> 20 mg once daily. <b>Acid reflux:</b> 10 mg daily. <b>PUD:</b> 20 mg or 40 mg daily as single dose in severe cases. <b>Duodenal ulcer and gastric ulcer:</b> 10-20 mg daily for 8 weeks. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome:</b> 60 mg once daily adjusted as required."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Cap 20 mg:</b> Stomach ulcer and liver problems. <b>Delayed-release cap 40 mg:</b> Gastric ulcers, hepatic impairment, subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal discomfort, headache, dizziness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin, phenytoin, diazepam, digoxin, saquinavir, tacrolimus, cilostazol, iron salts, ketoconazole, clarithromycin, voriconazole, rifampicin, St. John's Wort, atazanivir, nelfinavir and clopidogrel."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 20 mg (P27.00). Delayed-release capsule 40 mg (P39.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 236,

          },
          {

            "content": "150-600 mg/day given in 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>Neuropathic pain:</b> Initially 150 mg/day given as 2 or 3 divided doses, may be increased to 300 mg/day after 3- to 7-day interval. Max: 300 mg; <b>&ge;15-&lt;30 mL/min:</b> 25-50 mg once or twice daily. Max: 150 mg; <b>&lt;15 mL/min:</b> 25 mg once daily. Max: 75 mg. Supplementary dose following hemodialysis: 25 mg single dose. Max 20 mg once daily. <b>Elderly &gt;70 yrs:</b> 10 mg once daily. <b>Mild to moderate renal failure:</b> 10-20 mg once daily. <b>Asians, patients with myopathy:</b> 5 mg once daily."

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Alpha-Adrenoreceptor Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of mild to moderate hypertension. Symptomatic treatment of urinary obstruction caused by benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Starting dose:</b> 1 mg before bedtime. <b>HTN:</b> 1 mg initially, followed by maintenance dose 2 mg daily. Max dose 20 mg. <b>BPH:</b> 1 mg initially for 7 days and should not be exceed during 1<sup>st</sup> week of treatment. Dose can be increased to 2 mg daily for 14 days. Followed by 5 mg daily for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of micturition syncope, dizziness, light-headedness or fainting. Concomitant use of PDE-5 inhibitors. Patients with intraoperative floppy iris syndrome; pulmonary edema due to aortic or mitral stenosis; high-output insufficiency; right ventricular heart failure caused by pulmonary embolism or pericardial effusion; left ventricular heart failure with low filing pressure. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sinusitis, nervousness, headache, dizziness, paresthesia, somnolence, blurred vision, palpitations, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, dyspnea, nasal congestion, nausea, pain in extremities, back pain, erectile dysfunction, asthenia, peripheral edema, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "PDE-5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil). Vasodilators and nitrates, dopamine, ephedrine, epinephrine, metaraminol, methoxamine, phenylephrine, vanillylmandelic acid, clonidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 2 mg (P26.79), 5 mg (P32.14)."
          }

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Trimetazidine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Partial Fatty Acid Oxidation Inhibitors (pFOX inhibitors)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of stable angina pectoris inadequately controlled by 1<sup>st</sup>-line anti-anginal agents. Adjunct treatment of congestive heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 1 tab in the morning and evening during meals. <b>Moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-60 mL/min), elderly:</b> 1 tab in the morning during breakfast. Swallow tab whole with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Parkinson’s disease, parkinsonian symptoms, tremors, RLS, and other movement-related disorders. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not a curative treatment for angina attacks, nor an initial treatment for unstable angina pectoris. Not a treatment for MI. Worsen parkinsonian symptoms especially in elderly. Discontinue therapy in patients who develop movement disorders. Falls related to gait instability or hypotension may occur in patients taking anti-hypertensive drugs. Patients with renal impairment. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea and vomiting, rash, pruritus, urticaria, and asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "MAOIs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Modified-release tablet 35 mg (P15.75)."
          }

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ghQuCGMfj7pputKEoUalsXoxdD2S0A41CN3vdao2BhQmCG73pM.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/h5cWbze4wIVrJlKorVk99Z5arqdjGpRKxH1RlrI844ITEbN7LE.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Valsartan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN) and heart failure. To reduce cardiovascular mortality in clinically stable patients with left ventricular failure or left ventricular dysfunction following myocardial infarction (MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b> - Adults: Initially 80 mg or 160 mg once daily, may be increased up to max 320 mg once a day. Childn 6-18 yrs: Initially 1.3 mg/kg once daily, up to 40 mg total dose. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Max 80 mg. <b>Heart failure:</b> Initially 40 mg twice daily, increase to 80 mg and 160 mg twice daily. Max 320 mg in divided doses. <b>Post-MI:</b> Initially 20 mg twice daily, may be increased within 7 days to 40 mg twice daily, up to 160 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and cholestasis. Co-administration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes and renal impairment (GFR &lt;60 mL/min). Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients who are vol- and sodium-depleted; with mild to moderate hepatic impairment without cholestasis, severe CHF, renal artery stenosis, CKD, primary hyperaldosteronism, aortic or mitral stenosis, or hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Concomitant use with potassium supplements or salt substitutes, potassium-sparing diuretics, or other agents that may increase potassium levels. Childn (GFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, CrCl &lt;30 mL/min, undergoing dialysis). Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dizziness, viral infection, fatigue, abdominal pain; hyperkalemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Rifampin, ciclosporin, ritonavir, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, aliskiren, lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 80 mg (P17.86), 160 mg (P25.00)."
          }
        ],

      "data": {
        "id": 4619,
        "brand_name": "RiteMED Verapamil",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Gy9qUj3DbUl2vzSdjHG0bJwwqh6oYpNRJHqvoGKn8Roci5RUb1.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/fotcjJAGkQDppcjfeeQwxxXVKADSRyzh59AVhv4rbzJqpZoOl3.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/plIOu9iwbF2iocq66dMK8m62D8jGt7AeJhIePlB5voc38qcxOQ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Verapamil HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic coronary heart disease (CHD). Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation or flutter with rapid atrioventricular conduction (except in case of WPW or Lown-Ganong-Levine [LGL] syndrome). Hypertension (HTN)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and adolescents weighing &gt;50 kg - <b>CHD, paroxysmal, supraventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation or flutter:</b> 240-480 mg/day in 2 single doses. <b>HTN:</b> 240-480 mg/day in 1-2 single doses. Max 480 mg/day. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> 40 mg 2-3x daily (equiv to 80-120 mg/day). Do not suck or chew tab."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. CV shock, pronounced conduction disturbances (e.g. SA or AV block degrees II and III), sick sinus syndrome. Cardiac insufficiency with reduced ejection fraction (< 35%) and pulmonary wedge pressure &gt;20 mmHg. Atrial fibrillation or flutter in the presence of an accessory bypass tract (e.g. WPW or LGL syndrome). Combination with ivabradine. Concomitant use with beta-blockers. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not take in a lying position. Do not use in patients with angina pectoris until 7 days after acute MI. Patients with acute MI with complications (e.g. bradycardia, hypotension, left ventricular dysfunction), neuromuscular transmission disorders, hypotension (< 90 mmHg systolic BP), renal and hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with anti-arrhythmics, inhalation anesthetics, digoxin. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dizziness or drowsiness, GI disorders (e.g. nausea, constipation, abdominal disorders), bradycardia, tachycardia, palpitations, hypotension, flushing, peripheral edema, fatigue; nervosity; neuropathy and tremor; development of cardiac insufficiency or exacerbation of pre-existing cardiac insufficiency, excessive fall in BP and orthostatic dysregulation; erythromelalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alpha-blockers, antiarrhythmics, theophylline, anticonvulsants or anti-epileptics, imipramine, glibenclamide, anti-infectives, doxorubicin, azole antifungals, benzodiazepines and other anxiolytics, beta-blockers, cardiac glycosides, cimetidine, immunosuppressives, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, almotriptan, uricosurics, ivabradine, grapefruit juice, St. John’s wort. HIV antiviral agents, lithium, muscle relaxants, aspirin, alcohol, other antihypertensives, diuretics, vasodilators."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sustained-release tablet 240 mg (P42.50)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2XVchj70qsCp7kCgz3C06jwvPr4bFjWV83eQPl9IKyE0d6cLII.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/fwGGPtkSgvTxKhHYa3wN4iDd4SxsaUovl2HHFuvKOoIe9xh1AO.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Nfu0L5TCHP0Gess2OLH9yQZ4ehJiVBq7aB8cigS4shwvhUnQOH.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rosuvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary hypercholesterolemia (type IIa including heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia) or mixed dyslipidemia (type IIb) in adults, adolescents, and childn &ge;6 yrs as adjunct to diet when response to diet and other non-pharmacological treatments is inadequate; homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia as adjunct to diet and other lowering treatments (e.g. LDL apheresis) or if such treatments are inappropriate. Prevention of major cardiovascular (CV) events in patients at high risk for a first CV event."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Hypercholesterolemia:</b> Initially 5 or 10 mg once daily. May be adjusted after 4 weeks if necessary. Max 40 mg in patients with severe hypercholesterolemia at high CV risk (particularly those with familial hypercholesterolemia), when treatment goal is not achieved on 20 mg and requires routine follow-up. <b>Prevention of CV events:</b> 20 mg daily. <b>Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia - Childn 6-9 yrs:</b> 5-10 mg once daily; <b>10-17 yrs:</b> 5-20 mg once daily. <b>Elderly >70 yrs, Asians, predisposing factors to myopathy, moderate renal impairment (CrCl < 60 mL/min):</b> Initially 5 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease, including unexplained, persistent elevations of serum transaminases (e.g. >3x ULN). Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Myopathy. Predisposing to renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Co-administration with ciclosporin. Women of childbearing potential not using contraceptives. Pregnancy and lactation. 40 mg dose: Patients with predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis e.g. moderate renal impairment (CrCl < 60 mL/min), hypothyroidism, personal or family history of hereditary muscular disorders, previous history of muscular toxicity with another HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor or fibrate, alcohol abuse, situations that increases plasma levels, Asians, concomitant use of fibrates."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with predisposing factors for myopathy, excessive alcohol use, history of liver disease, DM. Proteinuria; myalgia, myopathy, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, rhabdomyolysis. Do not measure creatinine kinase (CK) following strenuous exercise or in presence of alternative cause of CK increase. Discontinue therapy if CK >5x ULN or if muscular symptoms are severe and cause daily discomfort; ILD. Co-administration with gemfibrozil, systemic fusidic acid or within 7 days of stopping fusidic acid is not recommended. Monitor liver functions prior to and 3 months after initiation of therapy. Treat hypothyroidism or nephrotic syndrome in patients with secondary hypercholesterolemia prior to initiation of therapy. May affect ability to drive or operate machinery. Asians. Childn < 6 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "DM, headache, dizziness, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, myalgia, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Transporter protein inhibitors (e.g. ciclosporin, protease inhibitors), gemfibrozil and other lipid-lowering drugs, ezetimibe, antacid containing aluminum and magnesium hydroxide, erythromycin, vit K antagonists (e.g. warfarin or other coumarin anticoagulant), oral contraceptive/HRT, fusidic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P15.50), 20 mg (P32.00)."
          }
        ],

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3612,
        "brand_name": "Rocaltrol",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/zHhszWk78WifJsMc8ebgOsauC0FlNo1hYJ1hxAO3OPIZnFUh1n.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LQkhNGR3cR6x5KN3SaHoNvZh2YGTexNjsvPNH2q9WuCNzY81js.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Xj79uLN9QBSzGqtkkbFrRFpHmEtW2dTaixV17564CYasXRNmFr.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Calcitriol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vitamins A, D, & E"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Established postmenopausal osteoporosis. Renal osteodystrophy in patients with chronic renal failure, particularly those undergoing hemodialysis. Secondary hyperparathyroidism in patients with moderate to severe chronic renal failure (pre-dialysis). Postsurgical hypoparathyroidism. Idiopathic hypoparathyroidism. Pseudohypoparathyroidism. Vitamin D-dependent rickets. Hypophosphatemic vitamin D-resistant rickets."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Postmenopausal osteoporosis:</b> 0.25 mcg 2x daily. Determine serum calcium and creatinine at 1, 3, and 6 months and at 6-month intervals thereafter. <b>Renal osteodystrophy (dialysis patients):</b> Initially 0.25 mcg daily; patients with normal or only slightly reduced serum calcium levels: 0.25 mcg every other day. May be increased by 0.25 mcg at 2- to 4-week intervals if no satisfactory response is observed within 2-4 weeks. Determine serum calcium at least 2x weekly. <b>Secondary hyperparathyroidism (pre-dialysis patients i.e. CrCl 15-55 mL/min):</b> Initially 0.25 mcg/day in adults, may be increased to 0.5 mcg/day. <b>Hypoparathyroidism, rickets:</b> Initially 0.25 mcg/day in the morning, may be increased at 2- to 4-week intervals if no satisfactory response is observed. Determine serum calcium at least 2x weekly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. All diseases associated-hypercalcemia. Evidence of vit D toxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Ensure adequate calcium intake at the beginning of therapy. Patients with renal failure; immobilized patients (e.g. undergone surgery). Development of hypercalcemia. Increased serum inorganic phosphate levels. Possible stimulation of intestinal absorption of phosphate on patients with vit D-resistant rickets. Do not give other vit D preparation. Avoid dehydration and maintain adequate fluid intake in patients with normal renal function. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypercalcemia. Headache, abdominal pain, nausea, rash, UTI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Calcium supplements and calcium-containing preparations. Thiazide diuretic, digitalis. Magnesium-containing drugs (e.g. antacids). Phosphate binding agents. Bile acid sequestrants (e.g. cholestyramine, sevelamer)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Softgel capsule 0.25 mcg x 100s (P2,938.00)."
          }
        ],

          {

            "content": "<b>Trichomoniasis – 7-day course - Childn 3-7 yrs (15 mg/kg BW)</b>: 100 mg 3x daily. <b>1-3 yrs</b>: 50 mg 3x daily. <b>Amebiasis – Childn 7-10 yrs (35-50 mg/kg BW)</b>: &frac12; of the adult dose or 35-50 mg/kg/day in divided doses; <b>3-7 yrs</b>: &frac13; of adult dose; <b>1-3 yrs:</b> &frac14; of adult dose. <b>Giardiasis</b>: Same dose as for amebiasis; or 15 mg/kg in divided doses. <b>Anaerobic infections</b>: 7.5 mg/kg/day every 8 hrs."

            "content": "Active liver disease. Monitor leukocyte count (when therapy &gt;10 days). Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

            "content": "Amebiasis, balantidiasis and <i>Blastocystis hominis</i> infection, giardiasis, trichomoniasis, bacterial vaginosis, acute necrosing ulcerative gingivitis, prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infection, peptic ulcer disease (PUD), leg ulcers, pressure sores and anaerobic infections."
          },

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Amebiasis, balantidiasis and <i>Blastocystis hominis</i> infection</b>: 400-800 mg three times daily for 5-10 days or 1.5-2.5 g as single dose daily for 2 or 3 days. <b>Giardiasis</b>: 2 g once daily for 3 successive days or 400 mg thrice daily for 5-10 days or 500 mg twice daily for 7-10 days. <b>Trichomoniasis</b>: 2 g as single dose or 2-day course of 800 mg in morning and 1.2 g in afternoon or 7-day course of 600 mg to 1 g daily in 2 or divided doses. <b>Bacterial vaginosis</b>: 400-500 mg twice daily for 5-7 days or 2 g as single dose. <b>Acute necrosing ulcerative gingivitis</b>: 200 mg every 8 hrs for 3 days. <b>Prevention of post-op anaerobic bacterial infection</b>: 400 mg every 8 hrs, 24 hrs before surgery followed post-op by infusion or rectal administration until oral therapy is possible. <b>PUD</b>: 400 mg twice daily (except when given in combination with omeprazole and amoxicillin) or 400 mg three times daily for 1 week. <b>Leg ulcers, pressure sores</b>: 400 mg every 8 hrs for 7 days. <b>Anaerobic infections</b>: Initially 800 mg then 400 mg every 8 hrs for 7 days or 500 mg every 8 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "An adjunct to diet to reduce elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein-B, non-HDL-C and triglycerides levels; increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and non-familial); mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson Type IIa and IIb); patients with elevated serum triglycerides levels (Fredrickson Type IV); reduce LDL-C, total cholesterol, and apolipoprotein-B in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia as an adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g. LDL-aphresis) or if such treatments are unavailable; slow the progression of atherosclerosis; prevention of cardiovascular events."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Hypercholesterolemia:</b> Initially 5 or 10 mg once daily. <b>Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b> - Childn 10-17 yrs: 5-20 mg once daily; 6-9 yrs: 5-10 mg once daily. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia, prevention of CV events:</b> 20 mg once daily. <b>Severe hypercholesterolemia at high CV risk:</b> Max 40 mg if patients did not achieve goal on 20 mg. Dose adjustment can be made after 4 weeks. Elderly &gt;70 yrs and patients with moderate renal impairment or predisposing factor to myopathy: Initially 5 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease or with unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminase (&gt;3x ULN), severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;60 mL/min), myopathy. Concomitant use with ciclosporin. Women of childbearing potential not using contraception. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with pre-disposing factors for myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, history of liver disease. DM. Concomitant use of systemic fusidic acid, gemfibrozil, lopinavir or atazanavir and ritonavir. Discontinue when creatinine kinase levels &gt;5x ULN. Perform liver function tests before therapy and 3 months after. Asian patients. Elderly &gt;70 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Type 1 DM, headache, dizziness, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, myalgia, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, protease inhibitors, gemfibrozil, other lipid-lowering drugs, ezetimibe, antacid, erythromycin, vit K antagonists, oral contraceptive or HRT, fusidic acid. Alcohol, itraconazole, red yeast rice, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P20.00), 20 mg (P31.63)."
          }

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet when response to diet and exercise is inadequate. Adjunct to diet when response to diet and exercise is inadequate. Prevention of cardiovascular (CV) events in adult patients with increased risk of atherosclerosis and CV disease to reduce total mortality. Reduce elevated LDL-C, total cholesterol, triglycerides and increases HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and non-familial) and mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson types IIa/IIb). Treatment of primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson type III hyperlipoproteinemia), isolated hypertriglyceridemia (Fredrickson type IV hyperlipidemia). Slow or delay atherosclerosis progression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Initial dose</b>: 5-20 mg once daily at night. <b>Maintenance dose</b>: 5-40 mg once daily at night."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Acute liver disease, unexplained persistent raised serum aminotransferase concentrations. Pregnancy.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, myalgia, asthenia, constipation, dizziness, nausea, abdominal pain; pruritus, rash, urticaria, myopathy, hypersensitivity fractions, rhabdomyolysis, pancreatitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fibric acid derivatives e.g. fibrates, gemfibrozil, nicotinic acid, ciclosporin, HIV protease inhibitors."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ezetimibe, rosuvastatin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Lipid Modifying Agent Combination"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Primary hypercholesterolemia</b>: Adjunctive therapy to diet for reduction of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, triglycerides, and non-HDL-C, and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia or mixed hyperlipidemia. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)</b>: For the reduction of elevated total cholesterol-C and LDL-C levels in patients with HoFH."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary hypercholesterolemia</b>: Initially 10 mg/10 mg once daily. <b>Severe hypercholesterolemia or those with aggressive lipid targets</b>: 10 mg/20 mg once daily. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b>: Initially 10 mg/20 mg once a day. <b>For patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) not on hemodialysis</b>: Initially 10 mg/5 mg once daily. Max: 10 mg/10 mg once daily. <b>Asian</b>: Initially 10 mg/5 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended in patients with moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9) or severe (Child-Pugh score &gt;9) liver dysfunction. Discontinue if CK levels elevated (&gt;10x ULN) or if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected. Patients with pre-disposing factors for myopathy. Temporarily withheld in patient with acute serious condition suggestive of myopathy or predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Liver enzyme abnormalities. Patients already at high risk for developing diabetes. Childn. Women of childbearing potential not using appropriate contraceptive measures. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pruritus. Abdominal distension/pain, constipation, dry mouth, nausea; allergic dermatitis, eczema; arthralgia, myalgia; rash; ALT increased."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fibric acid derivatives (e.g. gemfibrozil), nicotinic acid, azole antifungal and macrolide antibiotics. Daptomycin. Other fibrates. Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, other coumarin anticoagulant, fluindione). Antacids, cholestyramine, ciclosporin, fenofibrate, fusidic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg/10 mg, 10 mg/20 mg."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of dyslipidemia. Primary prevention of cardiovascular (CV) disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults </b>- Hyperlipidemia, mixed dyslipidemia, isolated hypertriglyceridemia, slowing of the progression of atherosclerosis: Initially 10 mg once daily. Severe hypercholesterolemia: 20 mg once daily. Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: Initially 20 mg once daily, response to therapy should be estimated from pre-apheresis LDL-C levels. Primary prevention of CV disease: 20 mg once daily. <b>Childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs</b> - Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia: Usual initial dose 5 mg once daily; Usual dose range 5-20 mg once daily. Max 20 mg once daily. Adjustment should be made at intervals of &ge;4 weeks. <b>Asian patients, elderly (>70 yrs), patients taking ciclosporin or with predisposing factors to myopathy, moderate renal impairment:</b> 5 mg once a day. <b>Patients taking gemfibrozil, lopinavir/ritonavir and atazanavir/ritonavir:</b> 10 mg once a day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease, unexplained elevations in serum transaminases >3x ULN, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), myopathy. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with predisposing factors of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Liver enzyme abnormalities. Patients who consume substantial amounts of alcohol and/or have a history of liver disease. Increases in HbA1c and FBS. Risk of DM, ILD. Asian race. Childn < 10 yrs. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, edema, flu syndrome. Undesirable effects on GI, hepatic, metabolic and nutritional, musculoskeletal, nervous, respiratory, skin, and urogenital systems."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, gemfibrozil, protease inhibitors, coumarin anticoagulants, niacin, antacid, erythromycin, oral contraceptives/hormone replacement therapy."
          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rotavirus vaccine, live, oral, pentavalent",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Rotavirus Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of rotavirus gastroenteritis caused by the serotypes G1, G2, G3, G4, and G-serotypes that contain P1A [8] (e.g. G9) in infants (including premature infants) and childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "May be administered as early as 6 weeks old. Administer orally only, without mixing with any other vaccine or solution. <b>1<sup>st</sup> dose:</b> 6-12 weeks old. <b>Subsequent doses:</b> Minimum interval of 4 weeks between each dose. No restrictions on the infant's food or liquid consumption, including breast milk. May be given to pre-term infants according to their chronological age. If an incomplete dose is administered (e.g. infant spits or regurgitates the vaccine), a replacement dose is not recommended; continue to give the remaining doses in the recommended series. Vaccination course has been shown efficacious when administered to infants 6-32 weeks old."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Individuals with SCID."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Serious medical conditions in infants. Patients who are immunocompromised, infected with HIV, or those who received blood transfusion or blood products including immunoglobulin within 42 days. Infants with immunodeficient household members, active GI illness, chronic diarrhea or growth retardation, or a history of congenital abdominal disorders or intussusception, or any acute infection or febrile illness. Infants < 6 weeks. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."

                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."

                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]

          },

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet when response to diet and exercise is inadequate. Adjunct to diet when response to diet and exercise is inadequate. Treatment of primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson type III hyperlipoproteinemia), isolated hypertriglyceridemia (Fredrickson type IV hyperlipidemia). Slow or delay atherosclerosis progression."

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Primary hypercholesterolemia</b>: Adjunctive therapy to diet for reduction of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, triglycerides, and non-HDL-C, and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia or mixed hyperlipidemia. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH)</b>: For the reduction of elevated total cholesterol-C and LDL-C levels in patients with HoFH."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary hypercholesterolemia</b>: Initially 10 mg/10 mg once daily. <b>Severe hypercholesterolemia or those with aggressive lipid targets</b>: 10 mg/20 mg once daily. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b>: Initially 10 mg/20 mg once a day. <b>For patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) not on hemodialysis</b>: Initially 10 mg/5 mg once daily. Max: 10 mg/10 mg once daily. <b>Asian</b>: Initially 10 mg/5 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not recommended in patients with moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9) or severe (Child-Pugh score &gt;9) liver dysfunction. Discontinue if CK levels elevated (&gt;10x ULN) or if myopathy is diagnosed or suspected. Patients with pre-disposing factors for myopathy. Temporarily withheld in patient with acute serious condition suggestive of myopathy or predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Liver enzyme abnormalities. Patients already at high risk for developing diabetes. Childn. Women of childbearing potential not using appropriate contraceptive measures. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pruritus. Abdominal distension/pain, constipation, dry mouth, nausea; allergic dermatitis, eczema; arthralgia, myalgia; rash; ALT increased."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fibric acid derivatives (e.g. gemfibrozil), nicotinic acid, azole antifungal and macrolide antibiotics. Daptomycin. Other fibrates. Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, other coumarin anticoagulant, fluindione). Antacids, cholestyramine, ciclosporin, fenofibrate, fusidic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of rotavirus gastroenteritis caused by the serotypes G1, G2, G3, G4, and G-serotypes that contain P1A [8] (e.g. G9) in infants (including premature infants) and childn."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "May be administered as early as 6 weeks old. Administer orally only, without mixing with any other vaccine or solution. <b>1<sup>st</sup> dose:</b> 6-12 weeks old. <b>Subsequent doses:</b> Minimum interval of 4 weeks between each dose. No restrictions on the infant's food or liquid consumption, including breast milk. May be given to pre-term infants according to their chronological age. If an incomplete dose is administered (e.g. infant spits or regurgitates the vaccine), a replacement dose is not recommended; continue to give the remaining doses in the recommended series. Vaccination course has been shown efficacious when administered to infants 6-32 weeks old."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Individuals with SCID."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Serious medical conditions in infants. Patients who are immunocompromised, infected with HIV, or those who received blood transfusion or blood products including immunoglobulin within 42 days. Infants with immunodeficient household members, active GI illness, chronic diarrhea or growth retardation, or a history of congenital abdominal disorders or intussusception, or any acute infection or febrile illness.             "content": "Symptomatic treatment of seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis and associated ocular symptoms in adults and childn &ge;6 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Intranasal route only. <b>Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs</b>: 2 sprays in each nostril twice daily (morning and evening). <b>Childn 6-11 yrs</b>: 1 spray per nostril twice daily (morning and evening). Shake the bottle well before use. Prime nasal spray before initial use by releasing 6 sprays. When not used for &gt;14 days, re-prime by releasing 2 sprays or until a fine mist appears."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with untreated fungal, bacterial, or TB infections of the respiratory tract."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use nasal corticosteroid in patients with recent nasal surgery or trauma. Instances of nasal ulceration and nasal septum perforation in patients following the intranasal application of antihistamines. Long-term treatment. Transfer from (long-term) systemic corticosteroid to nasal preparation. Systemic corticosteroid withdrawal may result in adrenal insufficiency for a number of months until recovery of HPA axis function. Risk of infection due to potential immunosuppression. Visual disturbances. Growth retardation in pediatric patients. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Women of childbearing age. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dysgeusia; epistaxis, nasal discomfort. Dizziness, headache, somnolence; nasal dryness; dry mouth, abdominal pain, nausea; fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol or other CNS depressants. <b>Mometasone</b>: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, atazanavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, saquinavir, ritonavir, cobicistat-containing products)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension for nasal spray 600 mcg/25 mcg per actuation x 56 actuations (P497.25), 120 actuations (P819.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with activating epidermal-growth factor receptor (EGFR) Exon 20 insertion mutations whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b> Adults (&ge;18 yrs): </b> < 80 kg: 1050 mg; &ge;80 kg: 1400 mg. Dosing schedule: Week 1-4: weekly (total of 4 doses). Week 5 onwards: every 2 weeks. <b> Infusion rates: 1050 mg dose: </b> Week 1 (split dose) – Day 1: 350 mg; Day 2: 700 mg both at 50 mL/hr, increased to 75 mL/hr after 2 hrs if no infusion-related reaction (IRR) occurs. Week 2: 1050 mg at 85 mL/hr. Subsequent weeks: 1050 mg at 125 mL/hr. <b> 1400 mg dose: </b> Week 1 (split dose) – Day 1: 350 mg at 50 mL/hr, increased to 75 mL/hr after 2 hrs if no IRR occurs; Day 2: 1050 mg at 35 mL/hr, increased to 50 mL/hr after 2 hrs if no IRR occurs. Week 2: 1400 mg at 65 mL/hr. Week 3: 1400 mg at 85 mL/hr. Subsequent weeks: 1400 mg at 125 mL/hr. Week 5 onwards: Dosing is every 2 weeks. Dose reduction: Adjustments may be required based on the severity of adverse reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Infusion-related reactions (IRR): Pre-medicate with antihistamines (diphenhydramine), antipyretics (paracetamol), glucocorticoids (dexamethasone, methylprednisolone), and antiemetics to reduce the risk of IRRs. Monitor for symptoms indicative of interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis (e.g., dyspnea, cough, fever). Limit sun exposure during and for 2 months after treatment. Use sun protection and emollients. Monitor for symptoms of eye disorders. Advise against contact lens use until evaluated. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

          },
