        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiarrhythmics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of symptomatic and tachycardiac supraventricular arrhythmias requiring treatment. e.g. supraventricular tachycardia associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. <b>Tab:</b> A-V-junctional tachycardia, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, severe symptomatic tachycardiac ventricular arrhythmias. Patients who were not prescribed with or do not respond to other antiarrhythmics.  <b>IV infusion:</b> For severe rhythm disorders (e.g. supraventricular rhythm disorders, ventricular rhythm disorder) and patients with rhythm disorders requiring rapid response or where oral administration is not possible."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab - Adults - Saturation dose:</b> 600 mg/day given in 3 divided doses for 8-10 days; doses up to 1,200 mg/day (in 6 divided doses) may be necessary in some cases. <b>Maintenance dose:</b> 200 mg for 5 days/week. In some cases, 200-600 mg/day are required during long-term therapy. <b>Childn:</b> Dosage should be adjusted to BSA or BW. <b>IV infusion - Infusion regimen for the first 24 hrs - Loading infusion:</b> Initial rapid infusion phase: 150 mg (3 mL) over 10 mins at a rate of 15 mg/min. Slow infusion phase: 360 mg over 6 hrs at a rate of 1 mg/min. <b>Maintenance infusion:</b> 540 mg over 18 hrs at a rate of 0.5 mg/min. After the first 24 hrs, continue a maintenance infusion rate of 0.5 mg/min. <b>Breakthrough episodes of ventricular fibrillation or hemodynamically unstable ventricular tachycardia:</b> 150 mg for over 10 mins of supplemental amiodarone infusion. Administer through a central venous catheter."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Sinus bradycardia, SA heart block, sinoauricular and nodal conduction delay (e.g. sick sinus syndrome, 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block, bi- and tri-fascicular if no pacemaker is used), thyropathy, preexisting QT prolongation, hypokalemia, circulatory collapse, severe arterial hypotension, and iodine allergy. Concomitant use with MAOIs and drugs that may induce torsades de pointes. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pulmonary toxicity. Severe inflammatory pneumopathy, increased liver enzymes, cholestatic icterus or hepatomegaly, ECG changes, dyspnea or non-productive cough may develop. Discontinue if bradycardia or sinus node arrest occurs. May interfere with radioiodine uptake. Photosensitization; avoid exposure to sun. Perform thyroid function test before therapy. Patients with personal or family history of thyroid disorders. Childn. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hyperthyroidism/hypothyroidism, extrapyramidal tremors, nightmares, dyssomnia, cornea verticillata, impaired vision, atypical pneumonia, nausea, vomiting, constipation, isolated elevation of serum transaminases, acute hepatitis, photosensitisation, eczema, and muscle weakness. Hypotension, asystole/cardiac arrest/electromechanical dissociation (EMD), cardiogenic shock, CHF, bradycardia, ventricular tachycardia, AV block, and liver function test abnormalities."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "HIV protease inhibitors, loratadine, cimetidine, trazodone, ciclosporin, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, antihypertensives, anticoagulants, clopidogrel, antibiotics, fentanyl, lidocaine, dextromethorphan, St. John’s Wort, grapefruit juice. Drugs affecting QT interval, digoxin, antiarrhythmics. Cholestyramine, phenytoin, vincamine, sultopride, sparfloxacin, erythromycin IV, pentamidine. Agents that cause hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia. Methotrexate. Tab: Sofosbuvir and other antivirals for HCV. IV infusion - Incompatibilities: Aminophylline, cefamandole, cefazolin, mezlocillin, sodium bicarbonate, heparin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 200 mg (P56.21). Solution for IV infusion 50 mg/mL x 3 mL (P267.10)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Atorvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduction of LDL-C, apolipoprotein-B, triglycerides and increase HDL-C in treatment of hyperlipidemias (type IIa or IIb hyperlipoproteinemia), hypertriglyceridemia (type IV), and dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10-20 mg once daily; 40 mg daily in patients who require large reduction in LDL-C. Dose may be adjusted at intervals of 4 weeks up to a max 80 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with active liver disease. Risk of myopathy in renal impairment and increased creatinine phosphokinase.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances. Headache; skin rashes; dizziness, blurred vision; dysgeusia. Hypersensitivity reactions e.g. anaphylaxis, angioedema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. ciclosporin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV-protease inhibitors, nefazodone, danazol, amiodarone, and verapamil. Grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P12.64), 20 mg (P16.20), 40 mg (P23.98)."
          }

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduction of LDL-C, apolipoprotein-B, triglycerides and increase HDL-C in treatment of hyperlipidemias (type IIa or IIb hyperlipoproteinemia), hypertriglyceridemia (type IV), and dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10-20 mg once daily; 40 mg daily in patients who require large reduction in LDL-C. Dose may be adjusted at intervals of 4 weeks up to a max 80 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with active liver disease. Risk of myopathy in renal impairment and increased creatinine phosphokinase.",

          },
          {

            "content": "GI disturbances. Headache; skin rashes; dizziness, blurred vision; dysgeusia. Hypersensitivity reactions e.g. anaphylaxis, angioedema."
          },

            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. ciclosporin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV-protease inhibitors, nefazodone, danazol, amiodarone, and verapamil. Grapefruit juice."
          },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Intestinal Anti-Inflammatory Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment or prevention of relapse of ulcerative colitis and proctitis; Crohn’s disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Gastro-resistant tab</b>: 500 mg 3x a day. <b>Granules - Acute episodes of ulcerative colitis</b>: 1-2 sachets once daily for 8 weeks or as prescribed. <b>Maintenance of ulcerative colitis remission</b>: 0.5 g 3x a day (in the morning, midday, and evening) corresponding to a total dose of 1.5 g daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe liver and kidney function disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor patient's pulmonary dysfunctions particularly asthma and patients with known hypersensitivity to sulfasalazine. Hepatic and renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, diarrhea, flatulence, nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, peripheral neuropathy, renal function impairment including acute and chronic interstitial nephritis and renal insufficiency, muscle and joint pain, changes in blood counts and liver function tests, hepatitis, alopecia, oligospermia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine, thioguanine. Anticoagulants."
          },

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute and maintenance treatment of schizophrenia and related psychoses in adults and adolescents 13-17 yrs. Bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed episodes): As monotherapy for acute and maintenance treatment of manic or mixed episodes in adults and adolescents 13-17 yrs. As adjunct to valproate or lithium in the treatment of manic or mixed episodes in adults. For preventing recurrence of manic, mixed, or depressive episodes. In combination with fluoxetine: Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults and childn 10-17 yrs; treatment-resistant depression in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia - Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> Initially, 5-10 mg/day, with target dose of 10 mg/day within several days, adjust dose by 5 mg/day at not &lt;1 week intervals if needed; Maintenance treatment: Reassessment is needed; 10-20 mg/day in patients stable on olanzapine for approx 8 weeks. <b>Adolescents 13-17 yrs:</b> Initially, 2.5 or 5 mg, with target dose of 10 mg/day, adjust dose by 2.5 or 5 mg if needed. <b>Bipolar I disorder (manic or mixed episodes) - Adults &ge;18 yrs - Monotherapy:</b> Initially 10 or 15 mg/day, and adjust dose by 5 mg/day at intervals not &lt;24 hrs if indicated. <b>As adjunct to lithium or valproate:</b> Initially 10 mg/day. <b>Prevention of bipolar I disorder recurrence:</b> 10 mg/day, subsequent adjustment of daily dose should be within 5-20 mg/day. <b>Adolescents 13-17 yrs:</b> Initially 2.5 or 5 mg/day with a target dose of 10 mg/day, adjust dose by 2.5 or 5 mg. <b>Depressive episodes associated with bipolar I disorder - Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> Olanzapine 5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Adjust dose within ranges of olanzapine 5-12.5 mg and fluoxetine 20-50 mg. <b>Childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs:</b> Olanzapine 2.5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. <b>Treatment-resistant depression - Adults &ge;18 yrs:</b> Initially, olanzapine 5 mg and fluoxetine 20 mg once a day in the evening. Adjust dose within ranges of olanzapine 5-20 mg and fluoxetine 20-50 mg. <b>Elderly &ge;65 yrs, debilitated patients, patients with hepatic/renal impairment or a predisposition to hypotensive reaction:</b> 5 mg/day starting dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {

          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/IV0QrKIbTB9bYOFPq5neUNUmnXcD2JaNxBtRyEO0v0cHQw6RlJ.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YhioinnbCrsmcbOpudJrVc0YXfhHbb9evtzStZnkvzi2ssy5EE.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/q3DqSHk6bWKhzociOGEQqgerhvvz29aEtb227qPNZswI9djXrc.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tolvaptan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vasopressin antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct treatment of vol overload in heart failure in combination with other diuretics when adequate response is not obtained with other diuretics (e.g. loop diuretics, thiazides) alone. Treatment of hypervolemic and euvolemic hyponatremia (serum sodium < 125 mEq/L or less marked hyponatremia that is symptomatic and has resisted correction with fluid restriction), including patients with heart failure and syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adjunct treatment of vol overload on heart failure:</b> 15 mg once daily. For patients with serum sodium < 125 mEq/L or &gt;140 mEq/L, or inappropriate rapid vol decrease, elderly: 7.5 mg/day. <b>Hyponatremia:</b> 15 mg once daily, without regard to meals, may be increased to 30 mg once daily after at least 24 hrs. Max 60 mg daily, as needed to achieve desired level of serum sodium. Take in the morning to avoid nocturnal urination."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to benzazepine derivatives. Urgent need to raise serum sodium acutely. Inability to sense or appropriately respond to thirst. Hypovolemic, hyponatremia, anuria. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Hypernatremia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Too rapid correction of hyponatremia (e.g. &gt;12 mEq/L every 24 hrs). Induction of hypernatremia. Potential to cause irreversible and potentially fatal liver injury. For short-term use (< 30 days), perform liver function test, prior to initiation, and frequently at least for the 1<sup>st</sup> 2 weeks in patients with vol overload in heart failure. For long-term use (&gt;30 days), blood testing for hepatic transaminases and bilirubin is required prior to initiation; continue for 18 months at regular intervals (e.g. 3-6 months) thereafter. GI bleeding in patients with cirrhosis; dehydration, and hypovolemia, co-administration with hypertonic saline. Discontinue if serum sodium level increase above the normal range. Concomitant use of CYP3A inducers and P-gp inhibitors. Patients with serum potassium &gt;5 mEq/L or those receiving drugs known to increase serum potassium levels. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dry mouth, constipation, thirst, asthenia, pyrexia, hyperglycemia, anorexia, pollakiuria or polyuria, disseminated intravascular coagulation, intravascular thrombus, ventricular fibrillation, prolonged PT, ischemic colitis, diabetic ketoacidosis, rhabdomyolysis, CVA, urethral hemorrhage, vaginal hemorrhage, pulmonary embolism, respiratory failure, DVT."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole and other strong CYP3A inhibitors. Erythromycin, fluconazole, aprepitant, diltiazem, verapamil. Ciclosporin, rifabutin, rifapentine, barbiturates, phenytoin, carbamazepine, St. John's Wort, digoxin. Grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 15 mg (P693.75)."
          }

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for weight management in adults with an initial BMI of &ge;30 kg/m<sup>2</sup> (obese) or &ge;27-&lt;30 kg/m<sup>2</sup> (overweight) in the presence of at least 1 weight-related comorbidity e.g. dysglycemia (pre-diabetes or type 2 diabetes mellitus), hypertension, dyslipidemia or obstructive sleep apnea, and in childn &ge;12 yrs with BW &gt;60 kg and initial &ge;30 kg/m<sup>2</sup>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC injection. Initially 0.6 mg once daily. Increase dose in increments of 0.6 mg with at least 1-week intervals to maintenance and max dose of 3 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used as a substitute for insulin. Patients treated with weight management products; with obesity secondary to conditions or treatment that cause weight gain; severe renal or hepatic impairment. Patients with CHF NYHA class IV; IBD and diabetic gastroparesis; thyroid disease; type 2 DM receiving sulfonylurea or insulin. Acute pancreatitis. Cholelithiasis and cholecystitis.May cause increased heart rate, dehydration. Monitor INR in patients receiving warfarin. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Elderly &ge;75 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, dry mouth, dyspepsia, gastritis, GERD, upper abdominal pain, flatulence, eructation, abdominal distension, insomnia, dizziness, dysgeusia, cholelithiasis, injection site reactions, asthenia, fatigue, increased lipase and amylase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral medications, insulin secretagogue (e.g. sulfonylurea), or insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) 6 mg/mL x 3 mL (P3,380.00)."

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Secukinumab",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Biologic Response Modifiers (Biologicals)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults, adolescents, and childn &ge;6 yrs who are candidates for systemic therapy; active psoriatic arthritis in adults, alone or in combination with methotrexate, when the response to previous DMARD therapy has been inadequate; active ankylosing spondylitis in adults who have responded inadequately to conventional therapy; adults with active non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis with objective signs of inflammation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC inj. Initial dosing at weeks 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, followed by monthly maintenance dosing. <b>Plaque psoriasis - Adult:</b> 300 mg; <b>Childn < 25 kg BW:</b> 75 mg; <b>25 to < 50 kg BW:</b> 75 mg; <b>&ge;50 kg:</b> 150 mg, may be increased to 300 mg (some patients may derive additional benefit from the higher dose). <b>Psoriatic arthritis:</b> 150 mg, may be increased to 300 mg; <b>Anti-TNF alpha inadequate responders or with concomitant moderate to severe plaque psoriasis:</b> 300 mg. <b>Ankylosing spondylitis:</b> 150 mg, may be increased to 300 mg. <b>Non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis:</b> 150 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with chronic infection or history of recurrent infection; IBD (e.g., Crohn’s disease and ulcerative colitis); latex-sensitive individuals. Not to be given in patients with active TB. Prior initiation of therapy, consider anti-TB therapy in latent TB. Discontinue immediately and initiate appropriate therapy if anaphylactic or other serious allergic reaction occurs. Childn should receive all age-appropriate immunizations. Childn < 6 yrs with plaque psoriasis; < 18 yrs in other indications. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI (e.g. nasopharyngitis, rhinitis, pharyngitis); oral herpes; rhinorrhea; diarrhea; urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Live vaccines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) pre-filled syringe 150 mg/mL, 300 mg/2 mL."
          }

            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 250-500 mg twice daily. <b>Acute exacerbation of cystic fibrosis associated with <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i> infections – Adolescents and childn &gt;5 yrs</b>: 20 mg/kg BW up to max 750 mg twice daily. <b>Acute uncomplicated cystitis in women</b>: 100 mg twice daily. <b>Gonorrhea</b>: 250-500 mg single dose. <b>Prophylaxis of meningococcal meningitis</b>: 500 mg single dose. <b>Surgical infection prophylaxis</b>: 750 mg single dose given 60-90 mins before procedure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic and renal impairment; epilepsy. Ensure adequate fluid intake. Childn and adolescents. Pregnancy and lactation",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea. Headache, dizziness, sleep disorders. Rash, pruritus, anaphylaxis, photosensitivity. Increase in blood urea and creatinine, transient disturbance in liver enzymes and bilirubin, arthralgia, myalgia, blood disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids, theophylline, rifampicin, chloramphenicol."
          },

            "content": "A robust and lightweight (2.3 kg) digital baby scale and floor scale for childn in one, with a breast-milk-intake function (BMIF). Capacity of 20 kg (44 lbs) with fine graduation of 10 g (5 oz); uses batteries."
          },
          {
            "title": "Uses",
            "content": "Used to weigh babies and small childn. Has an auto-HOLD function which enables the baby to be taken care of before reading the result; a tare function used to deduct excess weight present on the scale such as bedding, nappies; and a BMIF to determine how much milk the baby has consumed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Direction",
            "content": "Place the scale on a level and stable surface. Position the tray on the base of the scale, then pull forward until it is heard to snap into place and the release button is in the top position. Press the green key to switch on the scale and wait for the signal tone. <b>Infants:</b> Place the infant on the tray, ensuring that he/she lie as still as possible. <b>Childn (able to stand up):</b> Press the release button and slide back the tray to remove it, then place the child on the scale and make sure he/she keeps still. Read the result. See manual for complete instructions for use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "The accuracy of the differential measurement may be impaired if the infant is kicking vigorously. Never use abrasive or acid materials, white spirit, benzene, or similar substances for cleaning.",

          },

            "content": "<b>Cap – Adult:</b> 250 mg every 6 hrs or 500 mg every 8-12 hrs increased to 1-1.5 g every 6-8 hrs for severe infections. <b>Susp – Childn:</b> 25 mg/kg daily in divided doses, doubled for severe infections, max 100 mg/kg daily. <b>6-12 yrs:</b> 250 mg every 8 hrs; <b>1-5 yrs:</b> 125 mg every 8 hrs; <b> &lt;1 yr:</b> 125 mg every 12 hrs."

        "id": 4189,
        "brand_name": "Seroquel",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nDWqIchFW9Kr1DxuJEQUCduL6LY3Cce3t2mmN1v7dxPUNCKDWC.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qnkboFIeld5eaT8fV5o2t7KKqUFdCHCZnJGEtL61ADAPZoJ2gD.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/732VWUWQS73LY88fhgJECnl7R1EpDQzTMY61RYhzuPzDUus8wO.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Quetiapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute and chronic psychoses including schizophrenia; bipolar disorder including manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder, depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder, preventing recurrence in maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder (manic, mixed or depressive episode) as monotherapy or in combination with mood stabilizers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>Acute and chronic psychoses, including schizophrenia:</b> Total daily dose for the 1<sup>st</sup> 4 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, and 300 mg on day 4. All administered twice daily. From day 4 onwards, titrate dose to the usual effective dose range of 300-450 mg/day, may be adjusted within the dose range of 150-750 mg/day depending on clinical response and tolerability. <b>Manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder:</b> Total daily dose for the 1<sup>st</sup> 4 days of therapy is 100 mg on day 1, 200 mg on day 2, 300 mg on day 3, and 400 mg on day 4. All administered twice daily. Adjust dose up to 800 mg/day by day 6 in increments no >200 mg/day. Dose may be adjusted within the range of 200-800 mg/day depending on clinical response and tolerability. Usual effective dose range: 400-800 mg/day. <b>Depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder:</b> 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, 300 mg on day 4, 400 mg on day 5, and up to 600 mg by day 8. All given once daily at bedtime. <b>Adolescents 13-17 yrs</b> - <b>Schizophrenia:</b> Total daily dose for the 1<sup>st</sup> 5 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, 300 mg on day 4, and 400 mg on day 5. All administered twice or thrice daily. Dose may be adjusted within the effective dose range of 400-800 mg/day after day 5, in increments no >100 mg/day. <b>Childn 10-17 yrs</b> - <b>Manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder:</b> Total daily dose for the 1<sup>st</sup> 5 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, 300 mg on day 4, and 400 mg on day 5. All administered twice or thrice daily. Dose may be adjusted to 400-600 mg/day after day 5 in increments no >100 mg/day. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Initially 25 mg/day, may be increased daily in increments of 25-50 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Suicide/suicidal thoughts or clinical worsening. Neutropenia and agranulocytosis. Hyperglycemia, increase in triglycerides and cholesterol, decrease in HDL, worsening of metabolic factors, pancreatitis. Patients with CV disease, cerebrovascular disease, or other conditions predisposing to hypotension, orthostatic hypotension. History of or at risk for sleep apnea, aspiration pneumonia, constipation, seizures. Concomitant use of CNS depressants and medications with anticholinergic effects. Tardive dyskinesia, EPS, NMS, QT prolongation, cardiomyopathy and myocarditis. SJS, TEN and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS). Withdraw gradually over a period of at least 1-2 weeks. Patients with history of alcohol or drug abuse. Current diagnosis or history of urinary retention, prostatic hypertrophy, intestinal obstruction, increased IOP or narrow-angle glaucoma. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs. Elderly with dementia. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, dizziness, dry mouth, withdrawal symptoms, elevations in triglyceride levels and total cholesterol (predominantly LDL-C), decreases in HDL-C, weight gain, decreased hemoglobin, EPS."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Hepatic enzyme inducers e.g. carbamazepine, barbiturates, rifampicin. CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, protease inhibitors. Other centrally acting drugs and alcohol. Medications with anticholinergic effects. Thioridazine, phenytoin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg. Film-coated tablet 300 mg."
          }
        ],

Major depressive disorder (MDD), preventing relapse in stable MDD patients who have been maintained on quetiapine. Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), preventing relapse in patients with GAD maintained on quetiapine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered once daily. Tabs should be swallowed whole and not split, chewed or crushed. <b>Adults</b> - <b>Schizophrenia and manic episodes associated with bipolar disorder:</b> 300 mg on day 1, 600 mg on day 2, up to 800 mg after day 2. Should be adjusted within the effective dose range of 400-800 mg/day depending on clinical response and tolerability. <b>Depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder:</b> 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, 300 mg on day 4. Administered once daily in the evening. May be titrated to 400 mg on day 5 and up to 600 mg by day 8. <b>Preventing recurrence in maintenance treatment of bipolar disorder:</b> Patients who have responded to quetiapine monotherapy or in combination therapy to a mood stabilizer for acute treatment of bipolar disorder should continue on quetiapine therapy at the same dose. Dose range: 400-800 mg/day (combination therapy); 300-800 mg/day (monotherapy). <b>MDD and GAD:</b> Initially 50 mg on days 1-2, increased to 150 mg on days 3-4. Administered once daily in the evening, may be adjusted upwards or downwards within the dose range of 50-300 mg depending on clinical response and tolerability. Maintenance therapy: Effective dose during the initial treatment should be continued. <b>Switching from quetiapine immediate-release tabs:</b> Patients may be switched to quetiapine extended-release tabs at the equiv total daily dose taken once daily. <b>Elderly:</b> Initially 50 mg/day, may be increased in increments of 50 mg/day to an effective dose. <b>MDD and GAD:</b> 50 mg on days 1-3, may be increased to 100 mg on day 4, 150 mg on day 8, and up to 300 mg depending on clinical response and tolerability. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Initially 50 mg/day, may be increased in increments of 50 mg/day to an effective dose depending on clinical response and tolerability."

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/3wDTwxddRUDDNjSkmVvth936LePBneZBuoMhK6CcUPsretfTNW.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Bk8M6ga4YwKU5LW4XukCayVu1adL1t9IvFI5X9BImQkUOClm1L.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Linezolid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Oxazolidinones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of nosocomial and community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) (including concurrent bacteremia), complicated (including diabetic foot infections without concomitant osteomyelitis) and uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, vancomycin-resistant <i>E. faecium</i> infections (including concurrent bacteremia)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Nosocomial pneumonia, CAP, complicated skin and skin structure infections -</b> Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs: 600 mg oral or IV every 12 hrs; Childn 0-12 yrs: 10 mg/kg oral or IV every 8 hrs. All doses taken for 10-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections -</b> Adults: 400 mg oral every 12 hrs; Adolescents 12-17 yrs: 600 mg oral every 12 hrs; Childn 5-11 yrs: 10 mg/kg oral every 12 hrs; 0-5 yrs: 10 mg/kg oral every 8 hrs. All doses taken for 10-14 days. <b>Vancomycin-resistant <i>E. faecium</i> infections, including concurrent bacteremia -</b> Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs: 600 mg oral or IV every 12 hrs; Childn 0-12 yrs: 10 mg/kg oral or IV every 8 hrs. All doses taken for 14-28 days. <b>MRSA -</b> Adults: 600 mg every 12 hrs via IV infusion for 30-120 mins. <b>Pre-term neonates < 7 days (gestational age < 34 weeks):</b> Initially 10 mg/kg every 12 hrs, may be adjusted to 10 mg/kg every 8 hrs if clinical response is sub-optimal. All neonates should receive 10 mg/kg every 8 hrs by 7 days of life. Patients who started with Servalin IV may switch to oral when clinically indicated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with uncontrolled HTN, pheochromocytoma, thyrotoxicosis, bipolar or schizoaffective disorder, acute confusional state. Concomitant use with MAOIs; direct or indirect-acting sympathomimetic agents (e.g. pseudoephedrine), vasopressors (e.g. epinephrine, norepinephrine), dopaminergic agents (e.g. dopamine, dobutamine). Patients with carcinoid syndrome or those receiving SSRI, TCAs, triptans, meperidine, bupropion, or buspirone, unless clinically appropriate and observed for signs and symptoms of serotonin syndrome or NMS-like reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated for the treatment of G(-) infections; catheter-related infections. Should not be taken >28 days. Patients with preexisting myelosuppression, receiving drugs that produce myelosuppression, chronic infection who received previous or concomitant antibiotics, or those who receive therapy for >2 weeks; severe renal impairment; BW < 40 kg; diabetes. CDAD; hypoglycemia; lactic acidosis; superinfection; peripheral and optic neuropathy; convulsions. Monitor CBC weekly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, headache, nausea. <b>Childn:</b> Fever, sepsis; rash; anemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Adrenergic or serotonergic agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 600 mg (P3,104.14). Solution for injection for IV infusion 2 mg/mL x 300 mL (P4,537.98)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Sevoflurane",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inhalational Anesthetics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Induction and maintenance of general anesthesia in adults and childn, at the discretion of anesthesiologist."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to sevoflurane or other halogenated inhalational anesthetics. Patients with known or suspected genetic susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal and hepatic impairment. Monitor respiration. Respiratory depression may occur. Patients susceptible to developing QT prolongation; childn with Pompe’s disease. Elevation of ICP, in conjunction with ICP-reducing maneuvers (e.g., hyperventilation). Patients with mitochondrial disorders; CAD; at risk for seizures. Stop MAOIs treatment 2 weeks prior to surgery. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Skip breastfeeding for 48 hrs, and discard milk produced, after administration of sevoflurane. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Agitation, bradycardia, hypotension, cough, nausea, vomiting. Somnolence, headache, dizziness, tachycardia, HTN, respiratory disorder, laryngospasm, salivary hypersecretion, chills, pyrexia, abnormal blood glucose, liver function test, WBC count, increased fluoride, hypothermia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Isoprenaline, adrenaline, noradrenaline, non-selective MAOIs, calcium antagonists. Isoniazid, alcohol, nitrous oxide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "100% Liquid for inhalation 250 mL."
          }

  {
    "id": 3572,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3572,
        "brand_name": "Siftus",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5y0FqJL9CYZTxFzlFkY2YPmuV9RbCY8rqcJ4MKBfahvEcgFkrH.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5y0FqJL9CYZTxFzlFkY2YPmuV9RbCY8rqcJ4MKBfahvEcgFkrH.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KY9h6VRVyXxquMCFtEuSjUdV9fP7smhmyF7UNm5CVZS31ZR1kT.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ivabradine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in adults with coronary artery disease with normal sinus rhythm and heart rate (HR) &ge;70 bpm and treatment of chronic heart failure (NYHA class II-IV) with systolic dysfunction in sinus rhythm and HR &ge;75 bpm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Chronic stable angina pectoris</b> - <b>Adults &lt;75 yrs:</b> Should not exceed 5 mg twice daily. If tolerated and HR remains >60 bpm dose may increase to higher dose in patients receiving 2.5 mg or 5 mg twice daily after 3-4 weeks of treatment. Maintenance: Max 7.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue treatment if no improvement of symptoms after 3 months. If HR decreases &lt;50 bpm at rest or the patient experiences symptoms related to bradycardia: Titrate downward to 2.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if HR remains &lt;50 bpm. <b>CHF:</b> Initially 5 mg twice daily. May be increased to 7.5 mg twice daily if resting HR >60 bpm or decreased to 2.5 mg twice daily if resting HR is &lt;50 bpm after 2 weeks. If HR is between 50-60 bpm: 5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if HR remains &lt;50 bpm or bradycardia persist. Elderly >75 yrs: 2.5 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Resting HR &lt;70 bpm prior to treatment, cardiogenic shock, acute MI, severe hypotension (&lt;90 mmHg), severe hepatic insufficiency, sick sinus syndrome, SA block, unstable or acute heart failure, pacemaker dependent, unstable angina, 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Combination with verapamil or diltiazem and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors and nefazodone. Patients with congenital QT syndrome or treated with QT-prolonging medicinal products. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with 2<sup>nd</sup>-degree AV-block, heart failure with NYHA class IV, retinitis pigmentosa, hypotension, renal impairment (CrCl &lt;15 mL/min), moderate hepatic impairment. Not recommended in patients with atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrhythmias that interfere with sinus node function. Not recommended immediately after a stroke. Monitor CHF patients with intraventricular conduction defects and ventricular dyssynchrony. Elderly. Childn and adolescents &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Luminous phenomena. Headache, dizziness; blurred vision; 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block (ECG prolonged PQ interval), ventricular extrasystoles, atrial fibrillation; uncontrolled BP."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of flat urothelial cell carcinoma in situ of urinary bladder. Adjunct therapy after transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) - primary or relapsing superficial noninvasive papillary tumors that are limited to the bladder mucosa (stage Ta or T1)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Intravesical instillation. Perform tuberculin test before 1st instillation. Start treatment 2-3 weeks after TURBT. Treatment schedule is weekly instillation during first 6 weeks, then 3 consecutive weekly instillations at 3 months, at 6 months, and thereafter every 6 months up to 36 months. Total of 27 instillations in 3 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "HIV-positive and immunocompromised patients. Patients with UTI and bladder trauma. Patients with TB or taking anti-TB agents. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for IV, SC, or IM administration. Not intended for immunization. Patient with fever; unhealed traumatic catheterization.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Micturition and dysuria. Cystitis and typical granulomatous inflammation. Malaise and fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anti-TB drugs e.g. streptomycin, isoniazid, ethambutol, rifampicin, and para-aminosalicylic acid."
          },
          {

      "data": {

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sultamicillin (Tab: Tosylate; IM/IV: Sodium)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab:</b> Treatment of gonococcal infections, otitis media, pyelonephritis, upper and lower respiratory tract, urinary tract (UTI), and skin and soft tissue infections. <b>IM/IV:</b> Community-acquired pneumonia, upper UTI, intra-abdominal, gynecological, and skin and soft tissue infections. Prophylaxis to reduce the risk of infections following abdominal surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab:</b> 375-750 mg twice a day. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 2.25 g with probenecid 1 g. <b>IM/IV</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 3-12 g depending on severity of infection, divided into equal single doses every 6-8 hrs. Administer by deep IM injection or slow IV injection over at least 10-15 mins, or IV infusion over 15-30 mins in greater dilutions; <b>Childn weighing &ge;40 kg:</b> Adult dose; <b>&gt;2 yrs, newborn (&gt;2<sup>nd</sup> week of living), toddlers:</b> 150 mg/kg/day (equiv to 100 mg/kg/day ampicillin + 50 mg/kg/day sulbactam) IV given in 3 or 4 divided doses; <b>Newborn (1<sup>st</sup> week of living):</b> 75 mg/kg daily (equiv to 50 mg/kg/day ampicillin + 25 mg/kg/day sulbactam) in 2 divided doses. <b>Acute pelvic inflammatory disease:</b> 3 g (equiv to 2 g ampicillin + 1 g sulbactam) every 6 hrs in conjunction with doxycycline. <b>Prophylaxis of surgical infections:</b> 1.5-3 g injection given at the induction of anesthesia. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl >30 mL/min: 6-8 hrs dose intervals; 15-30 mL/min: 12 hrs dose intervals; 5-14 mL/min: 24 hrs dose intervals; &lt;5 mL/min: 48 hrs dose intervals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mononucleosis, superinfections with mycotic or bacterial pathogens. Hepatic, renal and hematopoietic dysfunction. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms during prolonged use. May reduce effects of oral contraceptives. Antibiotic-associated colitis. Neonates and infants. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B. <b>IM/IV:</b> Concomitant use of oral contraceptives. Patients on controlled sodium diet.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, meteorism, diarrhea. Anaphylactic shock, GI distress, blood dyscrasias, abnormal hepatic function, and jaundice. <b>IM/IV:</b> Pain at injection site, phlebitis (IV)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin and methotrexate. Estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, probenecid, allopurinol, aminoglycosides. Aspirin, indomethacin, phenylbutazone, tetracyclines, erythromycin, sulfonamides, chloramphenicol, anticoagulants. May result in false positive values of glucosuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 750 mg. Powder for injection (IM/IV) 500 mg/250 mg (P450.24), 1 g/500 mg (P739.76)."
          }
        ],

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3882,
        "brand_name": "Ventar",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/b90wDmZKhx3QxB8tHMhOU6u2pCVsmZm1gks1kyJ913dFIu17Ia.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/b90wDmZKhx3QxB8tHMhOU6u2pCVsmZm1gks1kyJ913dFIu17Ia.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/sK5v3dS31dt5ZAl8gun0aMKOJFmJDjXnyWFJBdoZ7Uak18YR1u.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Salbutamol sulfate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic Anti-Asthmatic & COPD Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of bronchospasm in bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis, emphysema and other reversible obstructive pulmonary disease. <b>Soln for inhalation</b>: Treatment of acute severe asthma and routine management of chronic bronchospasm unresponsive to conventional therapy. Symptomatic relief of an acute attack and as part of emergency treatment of acute severe asthma and long-term therapy of chronic asthma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab/Syr – Adults</b>: 4 mg or 10 mL (2 tsp). May be gradually increased to 8 mg or 20 mL (4 tsp) if bronchodilation is inadequate. <b>Childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: 1-2 tabs or 5-10 mL (1-2 tsp). <b>6-12 yrs</b>: 1 tab or 5 mL (1 tsp). <b>2-6 yrs:</b> &frac12; to 1 tab or 2.5-5 mL (&frac12;-1 tsp). To be taken every 6-8 hrs. <b>Neb soln and soln for inhalation – Adults</b>: Initially 2.5-5 mg. May be repeated up to 4 times daily. Max 40 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients suffering from thyrotoxicosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with cardiac arrhythmias, coronary insufficiency, HTN, IHD, DM, hyperthyroidism, ketoacidosis, pheochromocytoma, sensitivity to sympathomimetics and receiving antihypertensive therapy. Patients undergoing anesthesia with cyclopropane or halothane or receiving cardiac glycoside, quinidine, or TCAs. Not recommended for patients under beta-blockers. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tremor; nausea; pounding heartbeat; nervousness and restlessness. Slight tachycardia, peripheral vasodilation, and occasional headache. <b>Soln for inhalation</b>: Hypersensitivity reactions including angioedema, urticaria, bronchospasm, hypotension and collapse. Hypokalemia. Hyperactivity. Cardiac arrhythmia including atrial fibrillation, supraventricular tachycardia and extrasystoles. Peripheral vasodilation, paradoxical bronchospasm. Mouth and throat irritation. Muscle cramps."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Corticosteroids, diuretics, xanthines. <b>Soln for inhalation</b>: Other short-acting sympathomimetic aerosol bronchodilators, epinephrine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Syrup 2 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P81.50). Tablet 2 mg (P2.86). Nebulizing solution for inhalation 1 mg/mL x 30 mL (P155.92). Solution for inhalation 1 mg/mL x 2.5 mL (P26.95)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 5000,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 5000,
        "brand_name": "Ventera",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/EUfRdSxKWEqhHXuqH3bzGkz1vAjB3fiJH0vNgoiAlNNl5ISqJS.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/EFHkkixYqg0IHiOEUhlaWqTyVOxo4Y6IEfxHUpoZReffH28JYH.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dRgQffFGfZPAJqNOWTn7OEED5exIYLvQlxDxajCdWh8O64beiW.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Irinotecan HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Camptothecins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of patients with advanced colorectal cancer. In combination with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and folinic acid (FA) in patients with no prior chemotherapy for advanced cancer. Monotherapy if treatment regimen containing 5-FU has failed. In combination with cetuximab for treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (KRAS wild-type) with expression of epidermal growth factor receptor without prior treatment for metastatic disease or after failure of irinotecan-containing cytotoxic therapy. In combination with 5-FU, FA, and bevacizumab as 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment for colon or rectum metastatic carcinoma. In combination with capecitabine with or without bevacizumab as 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment for metastatic colorectal carcinoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion. Infuse the diluted infusion solution into a peripheral or central vein. <b>Adults - Monotherapy (previously treated patients):</b> 350 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 30-90 mins every 3 weeks; <b>Hepatic impairment (bilirubin 1.5-3x the ULN):</b> 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. <b>Combination therapy (patients not previously treated) - Combination with 5-FU/FA:</b> 180 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once every 2 weeks over 30-90 mins, followed by FA and 5-FU infusion; <b>Combination with cetuximab:</b> Same dose as the previous regimen containing irinotecan given over the last cycles."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "History of severe hypersensitivity. Chronic inflammatory bowel disease and/or bowel obstruction. Bilirubin >3x the ULN. Severe bone marrow failure. WHO performance status >2. Concomitant use with St. John’s wort or live vaccines. Hereditary fructose intolerance. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not give irinotecan before 1 hr after the end of cetuximab infusion. Avoid extravasation. Not recommended in patients with impaired renal function. Patients with congenital deficiency of UGT1A1, asthma, risk factors for interstitial lung disease, diarrhea, or MI. Delayed diarrhea (e.g., >24 hrs of diarrhea), febrile neutropenia, interstitial lung disease, MI, diminished response to killed/inactivated vaccines. Give anti-diarrheal treatment containing high doses of loperamide and broad-spectrum prophylactic antibiotic when diarrhea is associated with severe neutropenia; prophylactic antiemetic before each administration; prophylactic atropine sulphate with subsequent administration of irinotecan if acute and severe cholinergic syndrome occurs. Monitor CBC weekly; liver function prior to each cycle. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Use contraceptives during and for at least 3 months after discontinuation. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neutropenia, anemia, severe delayed diarrhea, febrile neutropenia, infectious episodes (can be associated with severe neutropenia), thrombocytopenia, severe nausea, vomiting, and delayed diarrhea, constipation, alopecia, severe transient acute cholinergic syndrome, asthenia, fever in the absence of infection and without concomitant severe neutropenia, fever in the absence of infection and without concomitant severe neutropenia, transient mild to moderate increased in serum levels of creatinine, transient serum levels (grade 1 and 2) of either ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase or bilirubin without progressive liver metastasis.  <b>Combination therapy:</b> Transient grade 3 serum levels of bilirubin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 strong inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole) and inducers (e.g., rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, St. John’s wort), neuromuscular blocking agents, atazanavir sulfate, vit K antagonist anticoagulants, yellow fever vaccine, other live attenuated vaccines, phenytoin, ciclosporine, tacrolimus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 20 mg/mL (P4,200.00)."
          }
        ],

          "id": 3399,

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2856,
        "brand_name": "Veral",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Verapamil HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic coronary artery disease: Chronic stable angina pectoris (exertion angina), unstable angina pectoris (crescendo angina, angina at rest), vasospastic angina pectoris (Prinzmetal angina, variant angina), angina pectoris in conditions after myocardial infarction in patients without cardiac insufficiency if beta-blockers are not indicated. Disorders in the heartbeat rate in cases of: Paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia, atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter with rapid atrioventricular conduction (except in case of Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or Lown-Ganong-Levine syndrome). Hypertension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and adolescents &gt;50 kg: 240-480 mg/day in 2 divided doses. Take with sufficient quantity of liquid (no grapefruit juice) preferably with or shortly after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with angina pectoris after MI until 7 days after the acute infarction; CV shock; pronounced conduction disturbances (e.g. 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> degree SA or AV block except in patients with artificial pacemaker); sick sinus syndrome; cardiac insufficiency with reduced ejection fraction &lt;35% and/or pulmonary wedge pressure &gt;20 mmHg; atrial fibrillation/flutter in the presence of an accessory bypass tract. Combination with ivabradine, IV beta-blockers. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> trimesters) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not take in lying position.         "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,

          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clozapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of treatment-resistant or negative symptom schizophrenia, serious psychosis with tardive dyskinesia, schizo-affective disorder, severely manic bipolar 1 disorder, and borderline personality disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "12.5 mg once or 2x daily, continued with 25-50 mg/day increments to achieve target dose of 300-450 mg/day at the end of 2 weeks. Subsequent increments may be once or 2x weekly, max 100 mg increments. <b>To minimize risk of hypotension, seizures, and sedation:</b> 300-600 mg/day in divided dosage, max 900 mg/day. <b>Elderly:</b> 12.5 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day with subsequent increments restricted to 25 mg/day. <b>History of seizures, CV, renal or hepatic disorders:</b> 12.5 mg on 1<sup>st</sup> day, increase in slow and small increments."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Myeloproliferative disorders. History of clozapine-induced agranulocytosis or granulocytopenia. Uncontrolled epilepsy. Severe CNS depression or comatose states due to any cause. Concomitant use with other myelosupressants. WBC < 3,500/cu.mm. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Only for severely ill schizophrenic patients. Give each patient at least 2 trials with different antipsychotics prior treatment. Patients with serious underlying medical illness, cachexia, history or predispose to seizures, hepatic, renal, CV or pulmonary disease, prostatic enlargement, narrow angle glaucoma, paralytic ileus, on general anesthesia. Agranulocytosis, seizure, orthostatic hypotension, collapse with respiratory and cardiac arrest, tachycardia, ECG changes, ischemic changes, nonfatal arrhythmia, MI, CHF, myocarditis, tardive dyskinesia, severe hyperglycemia. Discontinue if NMS or fever occurs. Avoid prolonged treatment if significant improvement is not observed. Perform baseline WBC and differential count prior treatment and every week thereafter for 6 months; if acceptable WBC counts have been maintained during 1st 6 months of therapy, monitor every other week; if total WBC count < 2,000/cu.mm or ANC count < 1,000/cu.mm., monitor daily; after discontinuation, monitor weekly for &ge;4 weeks. Assess liver function if patients develop nausea, vomiting, and/or anorexia during treatment. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Women. Elderly. Childn. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Drowsiness/sedation, seizures, dizziness/syncope, vertigo, headache, tremor, salivation, sweating, dry mouth and visual disturbances, hypotension, constipation, nausea/vomiting, leucopenia, granulocytopenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other CNS drugs, alcohol, benzodiazepine, other psychotropics, warfarin, digoxin, cimetidine, erythromycin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline, hypotensive drugs, anticholinergics, adrenaline, antidepressants, propafenone, flecainide, encainide, quinidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg (P47.02)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Naproxen sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx/Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>220 mg</b>: For relief of headache, toothache, muscle aches, minor arthritis pain, back pain, minor aches and pains associated with common cold, and dysmenorrhea. For fever reduction. <b>550 mg</b>: Symptomatic relief of rheumatic arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, tendonitis, bursitis, and acute gout. Management of pain including headache, migraine, post-op pain, post-partum cramping, and primary dysmenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>220 mg tab - Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b>: 1 tab every 8-12 hrs, as needed. Do not exceed 2 tabs in 8-12-hr period, or 3 tabs in 24-hr period. <b>Elderly &gt;65 yrs</b>: Do not exceed 1 tab every 12 hrs. <b>550 mg tab – Adults</b>: 1 tab 2 times a day. Do not exceed 2 tabs in 24-hr period. May be taken with food or milk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of asthma, rhinitis, urticaria, nasal polyps, or allergic reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs; advanced kidney disease. Patients at risk for CV and GI disorders. Pregnancy (last trimester) and lactation. <b>550 mg tab</b>: Patients with active or history of peptic/GI ulcers, bleeding or perforation related to NSAID therapy, chronic dyspepsia; and history of peptic ulcer/hemorrhage unrelated to previous therapy. Severe renal, hepatic, or cardiac failure. Treatment of peri-op pain in the setting of CABG surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use for more than 10 days. Severe allergic reactions/hypersensitivity. Increased risk of serious CV thrombotic events, MI, and stroke. Patients with preexisting or at risk for severe stomach bleeding or history of ulcer disease. Naproxen is not a corticosteroid substitute and should not be used concomitantly. Patients with fluid retention, HTN, or heart failure, restricted sodium intake. Risk for renal toxicity; ophthalmic disturbances. Patients with initial Hgb values of 10 g or less should be monitored periodically. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Stomach ulcers or bleeding, headache, nausea, somnolence, dizziness, vomiting and dyspepsia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cholestyramine, antacids, sucralfate. Aspirin, phenylbutazone, indomethacin, salicylates, and other NSAIDs. Highly protein-bound drugs (e.g. sulfonylureas, hydantoins, and sulfonamides). Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, dicumarol), thrombolytic agents (e.g. streptokinase). Ciclosporin, tacrolimus. Lithium. ACE inhibitors and ARBs. Beta-adrenergic blockers. Diuretics (e.g. furosemide and thiazide). Probenecid. Methotrexate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 220 mg (P9.50). Film-coated tablet 550 mg (Rx) (P20.25)."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ep1A8ZRaeQyIASUWltLNYRQ7FOtrZbXdPWudABCpl3yWxEYPpD.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Naproxen sodium, paracetamol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For relief of mild to moderate pain and inflammation including headache, migraine, backache, muscular aches, menstrual cramps, minor arthritis pain, toothache, and pain associated with the common cold and flu. For fever reduction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults 18-65 yrs</b>: 1 tab every 8-12 hrs, as needed. <b>Elderly &ge;65 yrs</b>: 1 tab every 12 hrs. Take with or after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients who are diagnosed with asthma, urticaria, or other allergic reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs. Active peptic/duodenal/GI ulcers, bleeding or perforation related to previous NSAID therapy. Active recurrent peptic ulcer/hemorrhage (&ge;2 distinct episodes of proven ulceration or bleeding) unrelated to previous NSAID therapy. Cerebrovascular bleeding or other bleeding disorders. IBD, chronic dyspepsia, congestive gastritis, or atrophic gastritis. Hyperkalemia. Severe uncontrolled cardiac failure, liver impairment or active liver disease, or renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min). In treatment of peri-op pain in CABG surgery. Pregnancy (last trimester) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal or hepatic impairment. May mask signs and symptoms of an underlying infectious disease. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Childn &lt;18 yrs. <b>Naproxen</b>: Increased risk of CV thrombotic events (e.g., MI and stroke). Patients with preexisting CV disease or risk factors of CV disease; established IHD, CHF, CHD, PAD, TIA and amaurosis fugax; HTN or at risk of HTN; fluid retention, edema (including peripheral edema), and heart failure. Patients with history of ulcer or GI bleeding, IBD (ulcerative colitis, Crohn’s disease). Patients with conditions that increase risk of renal papillary necrosis and other renal effects (acute interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis, low-grade proteinuria, nephrotic syndrome) and hyperkalemia. Borderline elevations of liver enzymes (ALT, AST, ALP). Patients with coagulation or platelet disorders; monitor hematocrit or Hgb levels of patients on long-term treatment; patients with initial Hgb values of &le;10 g should be checked regularly. Naproxen cannot be corticosteroid substitute nor a treatment for corticosteroid insufficiency. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn. Elderly. May cause reversible infertility. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Risk of hepatotoxicity (&ge;4 g paracetamol/day); alcohol consumption (&gt;3 alcoholic drinks a day). Patients with G6PD; low glutathione levels.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Constipation, nausea, headache. <b>Naproxen</b>: Peptic ulcer, heartburn, constipation, abdominal pain, dizziness, pruritus, ecchymoses, skin eruptions, and tinnitus. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Insomnia, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Naproxen</b>: Albumin-bound drugs (e.g. hydantoins, sulfonamides, sulfonylureas, other NSAIDs); ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, biphosphonates, cholestyramine, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, digoxin, diuretics, antacids, H2-receptor antagonists, lithium, methotrexate, pemetrexed, probenecid, quinolone antibiotics, SSRI, zidovudine. May increase urinary values of 17-ketogenic steroids and interfere with 5-HIAA urinary assays. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Alcohol, anticonvulsants, chloramphenicol, cholestyramine, domperidone, metoclopramide, enzyme-inducing agents, drugs that decrease gastric emptying, hepatotoxic drugs, lamotrigine, oral anticoagulants, phenothiazines, probenecid. May yield false-positive results in 5-HIAA urine test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 275 mg/325 mg."
          }
        ],
