            "content": "Symptomatic short-term treatment of moderate to severe acute pain in adult patients whose pain is considered to require a combination of tramadol and dexketoprofen."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 1 tab daily, additional doses can be taken as needed with minimum dosing intervals of 8 hrs. Max 3 tabs/day. May be taken at least 30 mins before meals. Duration should not be >5 days. <b>Patients with mild or moderate hepatic and renal (CrCl 60-89 mL/min) impairment</b>: Reduce to 2 tabs/day and closely monitor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe hepatic dysfunction and moderate to severe renal dysfunction (CrCl &lt;59 mL/min). History of CVA, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV). Patients with history of GI bleeding or perforation, related to previous NSAID therapy, chronic dyspepsia; active bleedings or bleeding disorders; Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis. Elderly &gt;75 yrs. Childn and adolescents. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, GIT irritation, headache, somnolence. Abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dry mouth, nausea, vomiting. Hyperhidrosis. Fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Tramadol</b>: MAOIs, coumarin derivatives, mixed agonists-antagonists opioid receptors. <b>Dexketoprofen</b>: NSAIDs (including COX-2 selective inhibitors), anticoagulants, heparin, corticosteroids, lithium, methotrexate, hydantoins (including phenytoin) and sulphonamides."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 75 mg/25 mg (P65.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hormonal contraceptive."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Start on 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual bleeding. Take 1 tab daily for 28 consecutive days (1 white active tab daily during the 1<sup>st</sup> 24 days and 1 green inactive tab daily during the 4 following days). Tabs must be taken every day at about the same time of the day. Start next pack immediately without a break."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active VTE disorder, presence or history of severe hepatic disease (with hepatic function insufficiency), severe renal insufficiency or acute renal failure, adrenal insufficiency, known or suspected sex-steroid sensitive malignancies, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal insufficiency, hyperkalemia, HTN, diabetes, history of chloasma gravidarum, rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, GI disturbances. May induce hyperkalemia, increased risk of MI or cerebral thromboembolism, decreased bone mineral density, increased risk of breast cancer, benign or malignant liver tumors, depression, jaundice and/or pruritus related to cholestasis, gallstone formation, porphyria, SLE, HUS, Sydenhams’ chorea, herpes gestationis, otosclerosis-related hearing loss, hereditary angioedema, changes in menstrual bleeding pattern. Ectopic pregnancy. Avoid exposure to sunlight or UV radiation in women predisposed to chloasma. May interfere with laboratory tests. Discontinue if jaundice develops.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Libido disorder, mood disturbances, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, acne, breast discomfort, metrorrhagia, vaginal hemorrhage, irregular menstruation, weight gain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Barbiturates, bosentan, carbamazepine, phenytoin, primidone, rifampicin, ritonavir, nevirapine, efavirenz, felbamate, griseofulvin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, St. John's wort. Boceprevir, telaprevir. Azole antifungals (e.g. fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, voriconazole), verapamil, macrolides (e.g. clarithromycin, erythromycin), diltiazem, grapefruit juice, cyclosporine, and lamotrigine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 4 mg x 28s (24 active tablets + 4 placebo) (P908.00)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "<b>Per 1,000 mL Smofkabiven Peripheral (three-chamber bag) - Glucose 13%:</b> Glucose (as monohydrate) 71 g; <b>Amino acid solution with electrolyte:</b> Alanine 4.4 g, arginine 3.8 g, glycine 3.5 g, histidine 0.93 g, isoleucine 1.6 g, leucine 2.3 g, lysine (as acetate) 2.1 g, methionine 1.3 g, phenylalanine 1.6 g, proline 3.5 g, serine 2.1 g, taurine 0.32 g, threonine 1.4 g, tryptophan 0.63 g, tyrosine 0.12 g, valine 2 g, calcium chloride (as dihydrate) 0.18 g, sodium glycerophosphate (as hydrate) 1.3 g, magnesium sulfate 0.38 g, potassium chloride 1.4 g, sodium acetate (as trihydrate) 1.1 g, zinc sulfate (as heptahydrate) 0.004 g; <b>Lipid emulsion:</b> Refined soya bean oil 8.5 g, medium-chain triglycerides 8.5 g, refined olive oil 7 g, fish oil rich in omega-3-acids 4.2 g",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Parenteral Nutritional Products"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Parenteral nutrition for adults when oral or enteral nutrition is impossible, insufficient, or contraindicated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Infusion rate < 3 mL/kg/hr (corresponding to 0.21 g glucose, 0.1 g amino acids, 0.08 g fat/kg/hr). Recommended infusion period: 14-24 hrs. See product information for complete instructions for use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to any ingredient of the formulation, fish, egg, soya, or peanuts. Hyperlipidemia, severe liver disorder, coagulation disorder, congenital error of amino acid metabolism, severe kidney disease without access to dialysis, acute shock, uncontrolled hyperglycemia, elevated serum levels of the included electrolytes, acute pulmonary edema, hyperhydration, untreated heart failure, hemophagocytic syndrome, unstable conditions (e.g. serious trauma, uncontrolled diabetes, acute heart attack, stroke, blood clot, metabolic acidosis, severe sepsis, coma, hypotonic dehydration). Newborn babies. Childn < 2 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Use continuous and well-controlled infusion to avoid risks associated with too rapid infusion rates. Strict aseptic precautions should be taken to avoid any contamination, especially during catheter insertion and manipulations. Monitor serum glucose, electrolytes, osmolarity, fluid balance, acid-base status, and liver enzyme test. Should not be given simultaneously with blood in the same infusion set due to the risk of pseudoagglutination. Any sign or symptom of anaphylactic reaction (e.g. fever, shivering, rash, or dyspnea) should lead to immediate interruption of the infusion. The catheter insertion site should be evaluated daily for local signs of thrombophlebitis. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thrombophlebitis, slight increase in body temp. High blood (plasma) levels of compounds from the liver, lack of appetite, nausea, vomiting, chills, dizziness, and headache."

            "content": "Emulsion for IV infusion (three-chamber bag) 1,448 mL x box of 4s (P22,562.02), 1,904 mL x box of 4s (P23,457.34)."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Solifenacin succinate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Drugs for Urinary Frequency and Incontinence"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of urge incontinence and/or increased urinary frequency and urgency in patients with overactive bladder syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly:</b> 5 mg once daily, may be increased to 10 mg once daily. <b>Combination with CYP3A4 inhibitors, severe renal (CrCl &le;30 mL/min) and moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B):</b> Max 5 mg once daily. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Urinary or gastric retention. Uncontrolled narrow-angle glaucoma. Childn. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic and renal impairment; bladder outflow obstruction at risk of urinary retention; GI obstructive disorders, decreased GI motility; hiatus hernia/GERD, concomitant use of drugs that can cause or exacerbate esophagitis; autonomic neuropathy; myasthenia gravis; preexisting long QT syndrome, hypokalemia. QT prolongation and Torsade de Pointes. Assess other causes of frequent urination prior to therapy. Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Discontinue if angioedema and anaphylactic reaction occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dry mouth, nausea, blurred vision, constipation, dyspepsia, abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir, nelfinavir, itraconazole)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg (P48.00)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Hydrocortisone sodium succinate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary, secondary or acute adrenocortical insufficiency; pre-op, and in the event of serious trauma or illness, in patients with known adrenal insufficiency or when adrenocortical reserve is doubtful; shock unresponsive to conventional therapy when adrenocortical is present; congenital adrenal hyperplasia; non-suppurative thyroiditis; hypercalcemia associated with cancer. Adjunct for short-term administration in management of acute episode or exacerbation of acute and subacute bursitis, acute gouty arthritis, acute non-specific tenosynovitis, epicondylitis, post-traumatic osteoarthritis (OA), psoriatic arthritis, rheumatic arthritis (RA), including juvenile RA; synovitis of OA. Treatment during an exacerbation or as maintenance of acute rheumatic carditis, systemic dermatomyositis (polymyositis), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Bullous dermatitis herpetiformis; exfoliative dermatitis; mycosis fungoides; pemphigus; severe erythema multifome (SJS), psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis. Control severe or incapacitating allergic conditions intractable to adequate trials of conventional treatment: Acute non-infectious laryngeal edema; atopic, or contact dermatitis; bronchial asthma; drug hypersensitivity or urticarial transfusion reactions; serum sickness. Severe acute or chronic allergic and inflammatory processes involving the eye (ophthalmic diseases): Allergic conjunctivitis; allergic corneal marginal ulcers; anterior segment inflammation; chorioretinitis; diffuse posterior uveitis and choroiditis; herpes zoster ophthalmicus; iritis and iridocyclitis; keratitis; optic neuritis; sympathetic ophthalmia. Manage critical periods of gastrointestinal diseases: Ulcerative colitis; regional enteritis. Aspiration pneumonitis; berylliosis; fulminating or disseminated pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) when used concurrently with appropriate anti-TB chemotherapy; Loeffler’s syndrome not manageable by other means; symptomatic sarcoidosis. Acquired autoimmune hemolytic anemia; congenital erythroid hypoplastic anemia; erythroblastopenia; idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura; secondary thrombocytopenia. Palliative management of neoplastic diseases: Acute leukemia of childhood; leukemia and lymphoma in adults. To induce diuresis or remission of proteinuria in the nephrotic syndrome, without uremia, of the idiopathic type or that due to lupus erythematosus. Shock secondary to adrenocortical insufficiency; acute allergic conditions following epinephrine. Trichinosis with neurologic or myocardial involvement; tuberculous meningitis with subarachnoid block or impending block when used concurrently with appropriate anti-TB chemotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion, or IM inj. 100-500 mg IV over 30 secs-10 mins, may be repeated at intervals of 2, 4, or 6 hrs as required. High-dose corticosteroid therapy is continued not >48-72 hrs only until patients stabilize."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections. Cushing’s disease. Intrathecal route of administration, except as part of certain chemotherapeutic regimens (diluents containing benzyl alcohol must not be used). Epidural route. Administration of live attenuated vaccines in patients receiving immunosuppressive doses of corticosteroids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Not for treatment of traumatic brain injury. Patients with latent TB or tuberculin reactivity, septic shock, hypothyroidism, emotional instability or psychotic tendencies, seizure disorders, myasthenia gravis, ocular herpes simplex, CV risk, CHF, predisposition to thromboembolic disorders, HTN, non-ulcerative colitis, diverticulitis, fresh intestinal perforation, fresh anastomoses, active or latent peptic ulcer, liver disease, renal insufficiency, pheochromocytoma, high risk of tumor lysis syndrome. May mask signs of infection and increase susceptibility; symptoms of peptic ulcer, peritonitis and other GI disorders.  May decrease resistance and inability to localize infection. May diminish effect of killed or inactivated vaccines when co-administered. Restrict use in fulminating or disseminated TB. Karpos’s sarcoma; allergic reactions; hypothalamic-pituitary adrenal suppression and epidural lipomatosis on prolonged use; predisposition or worsening of DM; psychic derangements; ocular effects; venous thromboembolism; acute pancreatitis; hepatobiliary disorders; acute myopathy; osteoporosis. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infections and infestations, neoplasms. Blood and lymphatic system, immune system, endocrine, metabolism and nutrition, psychiatric, nervous system, eye, ear and labyrinth, CV, respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, skin and SC tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, reproductive system, breast disorders. Administration site conditions, injury, poisoning and procedural complications."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, grapefruit juice, aprepitant, fosaprepitant, HIV-protease inhibitors, CCB, estrogens, cyclosporine, clarithromycin, erythromycin, troleandomycin), inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, and phenytoin), and substrates (cyclophosphamide, tacrolimus). Isoniazid, oral anticoagulants, neuromuscular blockers, anticholinesterase, aminoglutethimide, digoxin, high-dose aspirin, potassium-depleting agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sterile powder for injection (IM/IV) 100 mg; act-o-vial 100 mg/2 mL, 250 mg/2 mL, 500 mg/4 mL."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4816,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4816,
        "brand_name": "Somaset",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Somatostatin acetate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Somatostatin and Analogs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute GI hemorrhage, resulting from gastric or duodenal ulcers, hemorrhagic gastritis, and bleeding esophageal varices, intestinal and pancreatic fistulae. Symptomatic treatment of excessive secretion from GIT endocrine tumors. Prevention of complication after pancreatic surgery or endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "3.5 mcg/kg/hr, or usually 6 mg/24 hrs for a 75-kg patient, as continuous infusion of 250 mcg/hr. Adjust the infusion rate for 12 or 24 hours (for 3 or 6 mg respectively). <b>Treatment of GI hemorrhage:</b> Initiate before endoscopy as soon as possible after the first signs of bleeding and continue for 5 days minimum duration of 48 hrs. Additionally, a bolus inj of 3.5 mcg/kg should be given immediately after the start of the continuous infusion and another bolus about 1 min before endoscopy. After endoscopic treatment, similar boluses should be given when patients show clinical signs of bleeding. <b>Fistulae or excessive secretion from endocrine tumors:</b> Infuse &frac12; the dose for the next 48 hrs after healing. <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min):</b> 1.75 mcg/kg/hr for continuous infusion. 1.75 mcg/kg for bolus dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal impairment. Hypoglycemia may occur at the beginning of the infusion, measure blood sugar every 4-6 hrs. May induce transient systemic HTN, transiently reduced cardiac output, increased pulmonary arterial pressure and central venous pressure, systemic hypotension, bradycardia, AV block. Regularly check renal function and plasma electrolytes. Patients with compromised CV status or a history cardiac arrhythmias. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea and vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs that influence blood glucose regulation, plasma renin level, and arterial BP. Any form of sugar (glucose and fructose solutions or total parenteral nutrition)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection 3 mg (P3,571.50)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1101,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1101,
        "brand_name": "Soniphen",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WWDAntzSL1Osvi973p5RP2OFxbrrX04TB0bmRs3r3tPK7Xpg2s.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pknZMZxGGrYOUQLhdBm2O7GpUaK9XYtMS9Mf6XdPHTu6JdrLUT.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tiOoO9XkuL5KL2A09tKTyH4UuLPkgmPz77sChhaDL4pSoMTTGG.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Diphenhydramine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "First Generation Antihistamines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Antihistamine:</b> Relief of symptoms associated with seasonal, perennial, vasomotor rhinitis; for mild, uncomplicated allergic skin manifestations of urticaria and angioedema; dermatographism; as adjunct in anaphylactic reactions; allergic conjunctivitis due to foods; amelioration of allergic reactions to blood or plasma. <b>Antiparkinsonism:</b> Parkinsonism (including drug-induced) in elderly unable to tolerate more potent agents; mild cases of parkinsonism (including drug-induced) in other age groups; other cases of parkinsonism (including drug-induced) in combination with centrally acting anticholinergic agents. <b>Nighttime sleep aid:</b> Short-term management of insomnia. <b>Antitussive:</b> Relief of cough caused by minor throat and bronchial irritation e.g. due to common colds, inhaled irritants, or allergy. <b>Antiemetic or motion sickness:</b> Prevention and treatment of nausea, vomiting, and/or dizziness associated with motion sickness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap</b> - <b>Antihistamine, antiparkinsonism:</b> 1 cap every 6 hrs. Max 300 g/day (antihistamine); <b>Antitussive:</b> 1 cap every 8 hrs. Max 150 mg/day; <b>Motion sickness:</b> 1 cap 30 mins before travel or exposure to motion, subsequent doses may be given every 6 hrs before meals and at bedtime for the duration of the exposure. Max 300 mg/day; <b>Nighttime sleep aid:</b> 1 cap at bedtime as needed. <b>IV/IM</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 10-50 mg at an IV rate not &gt;25 mg/min. Max 400 mg/day; <b>Childn:</b> 5 mg/kg/day or 150 mg/m<sup>2</sup>/day in divided doses given every 6 hrs at a rate not &gt;25 mg/min. Max 300 mg/day. <b>Renal impairment:</b> Increase dosage intervals from 6 hrs to 12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Narrow-angle glaucoma. Stenosing peptic ulcer and pyloroduodenal obstructions. Not be used as a local anesthetic. Asthma attack, prostatic hypertrophy, bladder-neck obstruction, porphyria. Newborn or premature infants. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients taking other products containing diphenhydramine including topical formulations, antihistamines, sedatives, or tranquilizers. Alcohol consumption. Liver and renal impairment, glaucoma, urinary retention, myasthenia gravis, seizure disorders, COPD, hyperthyroidism, CV disease, HTN. Avoid use for &gt;7-10 days. Not be used empirically for premedication. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Agranulocytosis, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia. Anorexia. Confusion, disturbance in attention, euphoria, irritability, paradoxical excitation (e.g. increased energy, restlessness, nervousness). Convulsion, drowsiness, disturbed coordination, dizziness, dyskinesia, euphoria, fatigue, headache, insomnia, neuritis, paresthesia, sedation, sleepiness, tremor, unsteadiness, vertigo. Blurred vision, diplopia. Acute labyrinthitis, tinnitus. Extrasystoles, palpitations, tachycardia. Anaphylactic shock, hypotension. Dryness of the throat, nasal stuffiness, thickening of bronchial secretions, tightness of chest or throat, and wheezing. Constipation, dry mouth, epigastric distress, GI disturbance (e.g. nausea and vomiting). Drug rash, excessive perspiration, photosensitivity reaction. Muscle twitching, muscle weakness. Dysuria, urinary difficulty, frequency, and retention. Early menses. Angioedema, chills, dyspnea, fatigue, urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Atropine, TCAs. Alcohol and other CNS depressants (hypnotics, sedatives, tranquilizers). MAOIs, metoprolol, venlafaxine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 50 mg (P17.93). Solution for injection 50 mg/mL (P169.57)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 87,
          "name": "Medichem Pharmaceuticals, Inc."
        },
        "class": "human",
        "form_class": "3",
        "prescription_class": "Rx",

            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Long term, once daily maintenance treatment of airflow obstruction in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "2 puffs once daily at the same time of the day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Asthma. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not allow the soln or mist into the eyes.             "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis; dehydration; dizziness, insomnia; glaucoma, IOP, vision blurred; atrial fibrillation,  palpitations, supraventricular tachycardia, tachycardia; hypertension; cough, epistaxis, pharyngitis,  dysphonia, bronchospasm, laryngitis, sinusitis; dry mouth, constipation, oropharyngeal candidiasis,  dysphagia, GERD, gingivitis, glossitis, stomatitis, intestinal obstruction; skin and subcutaneous disorders;  arthralgia, joint swelling, back pain; UTI, urinary retention, dysuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other adrenergics; xanthine derivatives, steroids, non-potassium sparing diuretics; beta-blockers;  MAOI, TCA, QTc prolonging drugs."
          },

            "content": "Solution for inhalation 2.5 mcg/2.5 mcg per puff x 60 puffs (equiv to 30 doses) + 1 Respimat reusable inhaler (P2,707.95). 1 cartridge refill pack (P2,599.01)."

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of heart failure. Used for refractory edema associated with liver cirrhosis and in ascites associated with malignancy. Treatment of essential hypertension. Used in the diagnosis and treatment of primary hyperaldosteronism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Edema:</b> Initially 100 mg daily, may increase to 400 mg daily. <b>Hepatic cirrhosis with ascites, edema-  urinary sodium/potassium ratio of &gt;1:</b> Initially 100 mg daily. <b>ratio of &lt;1:</b> Initially 200-400 mg daily. <b>Primary hyperaldosteronism:</b> 400 mg daily. <b>Preoperative management of hyperaldosteronism:</b> 100-400 mg daily.           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe renal impairment. Hyperkalemia; elderly with DM. Serum electrolytes and BUN should be monitored.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

            "content": "Maintenance treatment of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), e.g. chronic bronchitis and emphysema and associated dyspnea. <b>Spiriva:</b> Prevention of exacerbations of dyspnea. <b>Spiriva Respimat:</b> Improvement of COPD-compromised quality of life and reduction of exacerbations.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Spiriva:</b> Inhale contents of 1 cap once a day with the Handihaler device at the same time each day. <b>Spiriva Respimat:</b> 2 puffs once daily at the same time each day. See product insert for complete instructions on use/handling."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for initial treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm, relief of acute symptoms, 1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment of asthma. Do not allow the soln or mist into the eyes. Do not use more than once daily.  Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (CrCl &le;50 mL/min); narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia, or bladder-neck obstruction. May cause inhalation-induced bronchospasm. Advise patient to continue taking anti-inflammatory after initiation of therapy even when symptoms improve. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dehydration; dizziness, insomnia; glaucoma, increased IOP, blurred vision; cough, epistaxis,  pharyngitis, dysphonia, bronchospasm, laryngitis, sinusitis; dry mouth, constipation, oropharyngeal candidiasis, dysphagia, GERD, gingivitis, glossitis, stomatitis, intestinal obstruction; joint swelling, urinary retention, dysuria, UTI. Cardiac, skin, subcutaneous tissue, immune disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other anticholinergics."
          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Spironolactone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Aldosterone Antagonists and Potassium-Sparing Diuretics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of primary aldosteronism, edematous conditions for patients with congestive heart failure (CHF), cirrhosis of the liver associated by edema and/or ascites, nephrotic syndrome, essential hypertension (HTN), hypokalemia, severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV) and pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary hyperaldosteronism</b> - Long test: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks. Correction of hypokalemia and HTN provides presumptive evidence for diagnosis of primary hyperaldosteronism. Short test: 400 mg for 4 days. If serum potassium increases during treatment but drops when discontinued, a presumptive diagnosis should be considered. After definitive diagnosis of hyperaldosteronism: Spironolactone 100-400 mg may be administered daily in preparation for surgery. For patients considered unsuitable for surgery, spironolactone may be employed for long-term maintenance therapy. <b>Edema in adults (CHF, hepatic cirrhosis, or nephrotic syndrome)</b>: Initially 100 mg as single dose or in divided doses. Doses may range from 25-200 mg daily. <b>Essential HTN</b>: Initially 50-100 mg administered in single or divided doses; <b>Hypokalemia</b>: 25-100 mg daily; <b>Severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV)</b> – Serum potassium &le;5.0 mEq/mL and serum creatinine &le;2.5 mg/dL: Initially 25 mg once daily, may be increased to 50 mg once daily if tolerated or reduced to 25 mg every other day if not."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with anuria, acute renal insufficiency, impairment of renal excretory function, or hyperkalemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Potassium supplementation from medications or diet. Patients with severe heart failure, impaired hepatic function. Concomitant use of lithium, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs. Dilutional hyponatremia, transient elevation of BUN, mild acidosis, gynecomastia. Observe for evidence of fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Childn. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Gastric bleeding, ulceration, gastritis, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting. Gynecomastia, inability to achieve or maintain erection, irregular menses or amenorrhea, post-menopausal bleeding. Agranulocytosis, fever, urticaria, maculopapular/erythematous eruptions, vasculitis. Confusion, ataxia, headache, drowsiness, lethargy. Renal dysfunction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors. Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics. Corticosteroids, ACTH, norepinephrine, tubocurarine, lithium, NSAIDs, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mg (P15.00)."
          }

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of HF, to treat refractory edema, and in lower doses as adjunct therapy. Refractory edema associated with liver cirrhosis or nephrotic syndrome and in ascites associated with malignancy. Treatment of essential HTN. Diagnosis and treatment of primary aldosteronism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Edema:</b> Initially 100 mg daily; some may require up to 400 mg daily. <b>Hepatic cirrhosis with ascites and edema:</b> Initially 100 mg daily if urinary sodium/potassium ratio >1; 200–400 mg daily if < 1. <b>Hyperaldosteronism - Presumptive diagnosis:</b> 400 mg daily; <b>Pre-op management:</b> 100-400 mg daily. <b>Severe HF:</b> 25-50 mg with ACE inhibitors and loop diuretics. <b>Idiopathic hirsutism or PCOS:</b> 50-200 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Anuria. Acute renal insufficiency, severe or rapidly progressing renal impairment. Hyperkalemia. Addison’s disease. DM, especially in confirmed or suspected renal insufficiency. Diabetic nephropathy. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; excessive potassium intake; porphyria; menstrual abnormalities or breast enlargement. Reversible BUN increased and hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis associated with hyperkalemia in decompensated cirrhosis. Discontinue if hyperkalemia occurs. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },

            "content": "Headache, drowsiness, cramps, diarrhea, ataxia, mental confusion, skin rashes, gynecomastia, hirsutism, deepening of voice, menstrual irregularities, impotence, transient increase in BUN, mild acidosis, hyponatremia, breast cancer, agranulocytosis, effects on electrolyte balance, increased serum cholesterol, lichen-planus-like skin eruptions, chloasma-like face pigmentation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors, chlorpropamide, ciclosporin, aspirin, norepinephrine, estrogen, warfarin."
          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NlM2c3IkKuuk9FpENpFeBsVOPDbfcA1McTtPkyH36PHM47Lb9i.jpg"

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "NMDA Receptor Antagonist"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with oral antidepressant therapy: for treatment-resistant depression (TRD), a major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults who have not responded adequately to at least two different antidepressants of adequate dose and duration to treat the current depressive episode), or for rapid reduction of depressive symptoms in adult patients with MDD who have acute suicidal ideation or behavior."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "For nasal use only. Single-use nasal spray device delivers a total of 28 mg of esketamine in 2 sprays (one spray per nostril). Do not be prime before use. Use 1 device (for a 28 mg dose), 2 devices (for a 56 mg dose), or 3 devices (for an 84 mg dose), with a 5-mins rest between use of each device. <b>TRD - Induction Phase</b> - Week 1-4 (2 treatment sessions/week): Starting day 1 dose of 56 mg; if &ge;65 yrs: 28 mg. Subsequent doses of 56 mg or 84 mg. <b>Maintenance Phase</b> - Week 5-8: 56 mg or 84 mg once weekly. From week 9: 56 mg or 84 mg every 2 weeks or once weekly. After depressive symptoms improve, treatment is recommended for at least 6 months. <b>MDD with acute suicidal ideation or behavior:</b> 84 mg twice weekly for 4 weeks. Dose reduction to 56 mg may be done based on tolerability."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with increased BP or intracranial pressure; with known aneurysmal vascular disease (including intracranial, thoracic, or abdominal aorta, or peripheral arterial vessels); with known history of intracranial hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Administer under supervision of a healthcare professional. Patients with history of suicide-related events or has significant degree of suicidal ideation; unstable or poorly controlled HTN; with history (within 6 weeks) of CV event including MI, ischemic stroke, or TIA; with hemodynamically significant valvular heart disease e.g. mitral regurgitation, aortic stenosis, or aortic regurgitation; with NYHA class III-IV heart failure of any etiology. Potential for short-term and long-term cognitive impairment and motor impairment. Long-term use. Patients with history of drug abuse or dependence including alcohol. Patients with presence or history of psychosis, mania or bipolar disorder; hyperthyroidism, pulmonary insufficiency, known uncontrolled brady- or tachyarrhythmias. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dissociation, dizziness, nausea, sedation, headache, dysgeusia, hypoesthesia, vertigo, anxiety, increased BP, and vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CNS depressants e.g. benzodiazepines, opioids, and alcohol. Psychostimulants e.g. amphetamines, methylphenidate, modafinil, and armodafinil. MAOIs e.g. tranylcypromine, selegiline, and phenelzine. CYP3A4 inhibitor e.g. clarithromycin (oral). CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 inducer e.g. rifampicin (oral). CYP3A4 substrate e.g. midazolam (oral). CYP2B6 substrate e.g. bupropion (oral). Other nasally administered medicinal products e.g. oxymetazoline and mometasone furoate."
          },

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia in adults and adolescents &ge;15 yrs; moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar I disorder. Prevention of new manic episode in adults with predominant manic episodes and whose episodes responded to aripiprazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia - Adults:</b> Initially 10 mg/day or 15 mg/day. Maintenance: 15 mg/day once daily. Max 30 mg daily; <b>Adolescents &ge;15 yrs:</b> Initially 2 mg for 2 days, titrated to 5 mg for 2 additional days to reach 10 mg/day. May increase subsequent dose in 5 mg increments. Max 30 mg daily. <b>Manic episodes in bipolar I disorder - Adults:</b> Initially 15 mg once daily. Max 30 mg daily; <b>Adolescents &ge;13 yrs:</b> Initially 2 mg for 2 days, titrated to 5 mg for 2 additional days to reach 10 mg/day. Treatment duration: Max 12 weeks. Place the tab on the tongue. Taken with or without liquid or food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for treatment of dementia-related psychosis. Patients with severe hepatic impairment; history of MI or IHD, heart failure, conduction abnormalities, cerebrovascular disease, predisposition to hypotension or HTN; history of QT prolongation; history or conditions associated with seizures; DM, obesity; thyroid disorder, pituitary adenoma; aspiration pneumonia; phenylketonuria. Coadministration with stimulants. May induce suicidal behavior, VTE, tardive dyskinesia, akathisia, Parkinsonism, seizure, hyperglycemia, weight gain, dysphagia, increased and uncontrollable urges, somnolence, postural hypotension, sensory instability. Discontinue if NMS or unexplained high fever without NMS occurs. Not recommended in childn < 15 yrs with schizophrenia; < 13 yrs with manic episodes in bipolar I disorder. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Akathisia, nausea, DM, insomnia, anxiety, restlessness, EPS, tremor, headache, sedation, somnolence, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, dyspepsia, salivary hypersecretion, vomiting, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, HIV protease inhibitors, diltiazem) and inducers (e.g., carbamazepine, rifampicin, rifabutin, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, efavirenz, nevirapine, St John’s Wort), CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, escitalopram), famotidine, SSRI, SNRI, antihypertensives, CNS drugs, QT prolonging drugs, drugs-induced electrolyte imbalance.             "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Nasal Decongestants, Antiallergics & Related Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Sterimar Nose Hygiene and Comfort</b>: For childn and adults to cleanse and eliminate impurities; moisturize and restore the natural moisture of the nasal mucosa; prevent ears, nose and throat disorders by reinforcing the nasal mucosa’s defenses; help improve breathing, contributing to a healthy sleeping pattern.  <b>Sterimar Nose Hygiene Baby</b>: For babies from 0-3 yrs to gently cleanse the nose and eliminate impurities; moisturize and restore the natural moisture of the nasal mucosa; prevent ears, nose and throat disorders by reinforcing the nasal mucosa’s defenses; improve breathing to facilitate a good sleep and bottle or breastfeeding. <b>Sterimar Sensitive Nose</b>: For babies &lt;6 months, childn and adults to cleanse and eliminate impurities, soften mucus or scabs; moisturize, regenerate cells and restores the natural mucosa. <b>Sterimar Blocked Nose</b>: For childn 3 yrs to adults in case of colds, rhinitis, acute or chronic sinusitis to quickly decongest the nasal mucosa; eliminate thick mucus; help to fight colds, sinusitis and limit the risks of secondary infection by washing out nasal cavities; prevent flu infection; improve effectiveness of local medicated treatments to reduce intake."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Spray 2-6 times/day in each nostril. <b>Sterimar Nose Hygiene and Comfort/Sterimar Sensitive Nose</b> – Hygiene and moisturizing of the nasal mucosa: Spray once or twice in each nostril. Let any excess solution flow out and then blow the nose; Deeper cleansing of nasal cavities: Spray once for longer from 2-3 secs. Let any excess solution flow out of the nostrils and then blow the nose. <b>Sterimar Nose Hygiene Baby</b> – Hygiene and moisturizing of the nasal mucosa: Spray briefly 1-2 times in each nostril. Let any excess solution flow out before wiping the nose; Deeper cleansing of nasal cavities: Press the nozzle for approximately 2 secs. Let any excess solution run out of the other nostril then wipe the nose. Repeat to the other nostril if necessary. <b>Sterimar Blocked Nose</b> – Use 2-6 times a day or more until decongestion. Spray once or twice in each nostril. Let any excess solution flow out and then blow the nose; Deeper cleansing of nasal cavities: Spray once for longer from 2-3 secs. Let any excess solution flow out of the other nostril and then blow the nose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sterimar Nose Hygiene and Comfort Sea Water Nasal Spray 50 mL. Sterimar Nose Hygiene Baby Sea Water Nasal Spray 50 mL. Sterimar Sensitive Nose Sea Water Nasal Spray 50 mL.  Sterimar Blocked Nose Sea Water Nasal Spray 100 mL."
          }
        ],

        "id": 4831,
        "brand_name": "Strasimet",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/n5rPjQAfFpeMkhZVDeGDg1l4Iq8m1frCzpLBRjbNUiYRBrJGrp.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/19plGo7ODiTdUe2KZGr4c8I6aTkXICuW2sn63VuEkGoRYo57q5.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/RnR0EiDWweQdqsKvbbxuQwC9BNzopDiaEBCQ4bSm6vZZnNV3y1.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin phosphate monohydrate, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control, in patients inadequately controlled on their max tolerated dose of metformin alone or those already being treated with combination of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs; as triple combination with sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma agonist as adjunct to diet and exercise in patients inadequately controlled on their max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma agonist; as add-on to insulin as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control, stable dose of insulin and metformin alone do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Max for sitagliptin: 100 mg/day. <b>Patients with moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30 to < 50 mL/min):</b> 50 mg sitagliptin once daily. <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis:</b> 25 mg sitagliptin once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis or pre-coma, severe renal failure (GFR< 30 mL/min), dehydration, severe infection, shock, intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents, cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, hepatic impairment, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not to be used for patients with type 1 diabetes or treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis. Acute pancreatitis. Risk of lactic acidosis. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy. Hypoglycemia in combination with a sulfonylurea or with insulin. Hypersensitivity reactions. Bullous pemphigoid. Temporarily discontinue treatment prior to surgery or administration of iodinated contrast agents prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure and not restarted until at least 48 hrs after. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol. Iodinated contrast agents. NSAIDS, COX-2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists, diuretics, ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine, beta-2 agonists, ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin, ciclosporin, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/1 g."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of mild to moderately severe infections (respiratory and genitourinary tract, skin and skin structure infections; oral and dental infections including necrotizing gingivitis) caused by susceptible organisms. Prevention and treatment of secondary bacterial infections in measles, mumps, chickenpox, influenza, and other viral infections. Prophylaxis in recurrent streptococcal infections including prevention of recurrent rheumatic fever and/or Sydenham's chorea; for bacterial endocarditis after tonsillectomy or tooth extraction in patients with history of rheumatic fever and/or congenital heart disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b> - Mild to moderately severe infections: 250-500 mg every 4-6 hrs. Prevention of recurrent rheumatic fever: 250 mg every 12 hrs continuously. <b>Childn 6-12 yrs (who can swallow cap whole)</b>: 250 mg every 6 hrs. All doses taken preferably at least 1 hr before or 2 hrs after meals for 10-14 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with chronic, severe, or deep-seated infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cross-sensitivity with other penicillins and cephalosporins. Patients with renal impairment, history of allergy and/or asthma, nausea, vomiting, gastric dilatation, esophageal achalasia, cardiospasm, intestinal hypermotility. Serious and fatal hypersensitivity (anaphylactoid) reactions, CDAD, and colitis may occur. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms during prolonged use. Use an alternative or additional method of contraception if used concomitantly with an estrogen-containing contraceptive. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions; hematologic and GI effects, hepatotoxicity, nephropathy, neuropathy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminoglycosides, beta-lactam antibiotics, bacteriostatic antibiotics (e.g. erythromycin, chloramphenicol, tetracycline), contraceptives, probenecid, NSAIDs, sulfamethoxypyridazine, sulfaethidole, antacids. Zinc oxide, magnesium carbonate, magnesium oxide, calamine. May interfere with urinary tests for fructose, aminolevulinic acid, estrogens, 17-hydroxycorticosteroids, protein, and sugar. Serum tests for uric acid. Biological thesis for serum folate. Serum electrophoresis. May decrease urinary excretion of PAH and PSP."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 250 mg (P11.66), 500 mg (P17.75)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "4 mL/kg per dose. <b>Prevention</b> – In premature infants < 1,250 g birth weight or evidence of surfactant deficiency: Give as soon as possible, preferably within 15 mins of age. <b>Rescue</b> – Treatment of infants with RDS confirmed by X-ray and requiring mechanical ventilation: Give as soon as possible, preferably by 8 hrs of age.  4 doses can be administered in 1<sup>st</sup> 48 hrs of life; should not be more frequently than every 6 hrs.   {
    "id": 3721,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3721,
        "brand_name": "Sutrip",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/emZKAU7wOpab9dkPvHrSk5720dcvfGyYJuNUgTFD062Br5h5vT.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XSt0GDRiM0XOuniZqWMVrrRZkIBOuryhxlZBBHDeBscdPRibH1.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dtpnYraF6AOX5bS6HRdj1gN9YhB5oISu1L2WVOcBMibaEa4Y6r.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sumatriptan succinate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antimigraine"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute treatment of migraine attacks and cluster headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment of acute migraine</b> - <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs</b>: 50 mg. Administer orally as soon as possible after the onset of the headache phase. If no response is obtained with initial dose by any route, 2<sup>nd</sup> dose should not be given for the same attack. Further doses may be given at minimum 2-hr interval between doses and not >300 mg in the 24-hr period if symptoms recur. Lower dose of 25 mg may be used, although some patients require 50 or 100 mg, followed by a 2<sup>nd</sup> dose of up to 100 mg if the headache returns or the patient has a partial response provided that the total daily dose does not exceed the recommended max of 200 mg and at a min 2-hr interval between doses. <b>Childn 10-12 yrs</b>: 50 mg; <b>6-10 yrs</b>: 25 mg. Repeated once after at least 2 hrs if symptoms recur after an initial response. <b>Hepatic impairment</b>: 50 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with uncontrolled HTN, IHD (CAD), history of MI, coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal’s angina), PVD or previous CVA or TIA. Severe hepatic impairment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use for prophylaxis and in patients with basilar, hemiplegic, or ophthalmoplegic migraine. Should not be given as IV because of the risk of producing coronary vasospasm. Should not be used for prophylaxis and should not be given to patients with basilar, hemiplegic or ophthalmoplegic migraine. Exclude unrecognized CV disease prior to treatment in postmenopausal women, men >40 yrs, patients with risk factors for IHD. Patients with hepatic, renal impairment, or history of epilepsy or conditions predisposing seizures, hypersensitivity to sulfonamides. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, flushing, weakness, drowsiness and fatigue. Nausea and vomiting. Dyspnea and sensory disturbance including paresthesia and hypoesthesia. Pain or sensations of heaviness, heat or cold, pressure or tightness. Transient increase in BP. Hypotension, bradycardia or tachycardia, palpitations, Raynaud’s syndrome and ischemic colitis.           "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xh5Kv4RIZCmIWXkIwisRozbVKpONDs5BtsrFeSfY9JgE1eBKJI.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/IDEqe67fGlwLkMOsnR2RA01WBYReWTd0wEX9ZYZeTVsSkOYqrS.jpg"

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Budesonide, formoterol fumarate dihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inhaled Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Asthma requiring treatment with combination of inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta2-agonist. Moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with frequent symptoms and history of exacerbations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Maintenance therapy - Adults (&ge;18 yrs) and adolescents (12-17 yrs):</b> 2 inhalations of 80 mcg/4.5 mcg or 160 mcg/4.5 mcg once or twice daily, may be increased up to max 4 inhalations twice daily. <b>Childn (6-11 yrs):</b> 2 inhalations of 80 mcg/4.5 mcg twice daily. Max 4 inhalations/day. <b>COPD - Adults (&ge;18 yrs):</b> 2 inhalations of 160 mcg/4.5 mcg twice daily. Max 4 inhalations/day. Shake well before use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Rinse mouth with water after each dose administration. Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Should not be used in severe exacerbations. Patients transferring from oral steroids, taking high emergency dose of corticosteroids, or prolonged therapy at highest recommended dose. Patients with severe liver disease, hepatic or renal impairment, severe CV disorders (e.g. arrhythmias), DM, untreated hypokalemia, thyrotoxicosis. May decrease serum potassium levels, increase risk of pneumonia in COPD patients. If therapy is ineffective or prescribed dose is exceeded, consider increased therapy with corticosteroids. A separate rapid-acting bronchodilator should always be ready for emergency use. Monitor childn’s and adolescents' growth in long-term therapy. Pregnancy (especially 1<sup>st</sup> trimester and before delivery) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Palpitations, <i>Candida</i> infections in oropharynx, pneumonia (in COPD patients), headache, tremor, mild throat irritation, coughing, hoarseness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Budesonide:</b> CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir). <b>Formoterol:</b> Beta-blockers (including eye drops)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Pressurized suspension for inhalation 80 mcg/4.5 mcg per actuation x 120 actuations, 160 mcg/4.5 mcg per actuation x 120 actuations."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>80 mcg/4.5 mcg and 320 mcg/9 mcg:</b> Treatment of asthma where use of a combination (inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta<sub>2</sub>-agonist) is appropriate. <b>160 mcg/4.5 mcg:</b> Treatment of asthma to achieve overall asthma control, including the prevention and relief of symptoms as well as the reduction of the risk of exacerbations and is suitable for any asthma severity, where the use of inhaled corticosteroids is appropriate. <b>160 mcg/4.5 mcg and 320 mcg/9 mcg:</b> Regular treatment of patients with moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), with frequent symptoms and a history of exacerbations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>80 mcg/4.5 mcg - Maintenance therapy - Adults (&ge;18 yrs) and adolescents (12-17 yrs):</b> 1-2 inhalations once or twice daily, may be increased up to max 4 inhalations twice daily. <b>Childn (&ge;4 yrs):</b> 1-2 inhalations twice daily. For symptom relief: 1 inhalation as needed. If symptoms persist, take additional inhalation. Max 6 inhalations per occasion. Max 12 inhalations/day can be used temporarily. <b>Childn (&ge;4 yrs)</b> - Maintenance: 1 inhalation/day. For symptom relief: 1 additional inhalation as needed. If symptoms persist, take additional inhalation. Max 4 inhalations per occasion. Max 8 inhalations/day can be used temporarily. <b>160 mcg/4.5 mcg - Anti-inflammatory reliever therapy (patients with mild disease) - Adults and adolescents (&ge;12 yrs):</b> 1 inhalation as needed, and for prevention of allergen- or exercised-induced bronchoconstriction. Max 6 inhalations per occasion. Max 12 inhalations/day can be used temporarily.  <b>Maintenance therapy - Adults (&ge;18 yrs) and adolescents (12-17 yrs):</b> 1-2 inhalations twice daily, may be increased up to max 4 inhalations twice daily. <b>Childn (&ge;4 yrs):</b> 1 inhalation twice daily. Max 2 inhalations/day. <b>COPD - Adults (&ge;18 yrs):</b> 2 inhalations twice daily. For symptom relief: 1 inhalation as needed, and for prevention of allergen- or exercised-induced bronchoconstriction. If symptoms persist, take additional inhalation. Max 6 inhalations per occasion. Patients transferring from oral steroids, taking high emergency dose of corticosteroids, or prolonged therapy at highest recommended dose. Patients with severe liver disease, hepatic or renal impairment, severe CV disorders (e.g. arrhythmias), DM, untreated hypokalemia, thyrotoxicosis. May decrease serum potassium levels, increase risk of pneumonia in COPD patients. If therapy is ineffective or prescribed dose is exceeded, seek medical attention to consider increased therapy with corticosteroids. Monitor childn’s and adolescents' growth in long-term therapy. Contains lactose. Pregnancy (especially 1<sup>st</sup> trimester and before delivery) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Palpitations, <i>Candida</i> infections in oropharynx, pneumonia (in COPD patients), headache, tremor, mild throat irritation, coughing, hoarseness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Budesonide:</b> CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. ketoconazole. <b>Formoterol:</b> Beta-blockers including eye drops."

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of chronic hepatitis B in adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs with at least 35 kg BW."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents &ge;12 yrs with at least 35 kg BW:</b> 1 tab once daily with food. <b>Treatment duration - HBeAG-positive without cirrhosis:</b> at least 6-12 months after HBe seroconversion (HBeAg loss and HBV DNA loss with anti-HBe detection) is confirmed or until HBs seroconversion or until there is loss of efficacy; <b>HBeAG-negative without cirrhosis:</b> at least until evidence of loss of efficacy occurs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Does not prevent risk of transmission of HBV through sexual contact or contamination with blood. Patients with decompensated liver disease and have a Child-Pugh score >9 (e.g. class C), cirrhosis, renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min), co-infected with HBV and hepatitis C or D virus or HIV, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Acute exacerbations of hepatitis after treatment discontinuation. Monitor hepatic function at least 6 months after treatment discontinuation. Potential risk of nephrotoxicity. Childn < 12 yrs or weighing < 35 kg. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain/distension, flatulence; fatigue; headache, dizziness; rash, pruritus; increased ALT; arthralgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Products containing tenofovir alafenamide, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or adefovir dipivoxil. P-gp inducers (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John's wort). Strong P-gp inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole and ketoconazole). Phenobarbital, oxcarbazepine, phenytoin. Rifampicin, rifapentine, rifabutin. Atazanavir/cobicistat, atazanavir/ritonavir, darunavir/cobicistat, darunavir/ritonavir, lopinavir/ritonavir, tipranavir/ritonavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

            "content": "Treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and childn &ge;6 yrs who are candidates for systemic therapy.           },
          {

If no response is shown after 16-20 weeks, consider discontinuing treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active infections (e.g. active TB). Concomitantly with live vaccines. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {

            "content": "Avoid injecting in areas of skin with psoriasis. Hypersensitivity.           "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LT8XKL2gI8fLbta53jxvTmBkxJ3wMI1OfHQTIW1Dt6TbIm0gPe.png",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/3AbZwszr3xLObD5qiQD0ulRziW9hDmllbhPLpEImaQ7UAne59t.png"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Flecainide acetate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiarrhythmics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardias, including atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter. Symptomatic sustained ventricular tachycardia, premature ventricular contractions and/or non-sustained ventricular tachycardia causing disabling symptoms in patients resistant to or intolerant of other therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Ventricular arrhythmias</b>: 100 mg twice daily. Max 400 mg daily. After 3-5 days, adjust the dose to the lowest level that maintains control of arrhythmia. <b>Supraventricular arrhythmias</b>: 50 mg twice daily. Max 300 mg daily. <b>Elderly</b>: 1 tab twice daily. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl &le;35 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>)</b>: Max 100 mg daily. Concomitant use of amiodarone: Reduce by 50% of usual dosage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Cardiac failure. Should not be given to patients with sinus node dysfunction, atrial conduction defects, second-degree or greater AV block, bundle branch block or distal block; asymptomatic premature ventricular contractions and/or asymptomatic non-sustained ventricular tachycardia in patients with a history of MI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Electrolyte disturbances, hepatic impairment. Patients with permanent pacemakers or temporary pacing electrodes, predisposition to cardiac failure. Renal impairment. Concomitant use of other antiarrhythmics, disopyramide, amiodarone or verapamil. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, giddiness, light-headedness, visual disturbances, nausea, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other sodium channel blockers, digoxin, beta-blockers and other cardiac depressants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg (P108.00)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of moderate to severe symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH); reduction in the risk of acute urinary retention and surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly:</b> 1 cap once daily, approx 30 mins after the same time of meal. Swallow whole. Do not chew or open."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to soya, peanut, drug components, and other 5-alpha reductase inhibitors. History of orthostatic hypotension. Severe hepatic impairment. Childn < 18 yrs. Adolescents. Women."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild to moderate hepatic and severe renal impairment. CV adverse events, male breast cancer, orthostatic hypotension, reduction in semen volume, sperm count, and motility. Coadministration with PDE5 inhibitors. Not recommended for patients scheduled for cataract surgery. Avoid contact with leaking caps by women, childn, and adolescents; exposure of semen to pregnant women. Evaluate patients regularly for prostate cancer.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, impotence, decreased libido, ejaculation, and breast disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Dutasteride:</b> CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, ritonavir, nelfinavir, itraconazole). <b>Tamsulosin:</b> Anesthetics, PDE5 inhibitors, other alpha-adrenoceptor antagonists, ketoconazole, paroxetine, cimetidine, diclofenac, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 500 mcg/400 mcg (P39.00)."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qgomzwzCUqQGHHimi8rgIMvtlRRP8a0BLYI6DRgiSPCPdpNymv.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Methimazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-Hyperthyroidism Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of hyperthyroidism, including treatment of Graves’ disease. Preparation of hyperthyroid patients for thyroidectomy. Adjunct to radio-iodine therapy and treatment of thyroid storm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult</b>: Initially 15-60 mg/day in single or divided doses (usually with 8-hr intervals). Maintenance: 5-15 mg/day. <b>Euthyroid patients</b>: 5-15 mg/day. <b>Childn</b>: Initially 400 mcg/kg BW daily. For maintenance, dose may be halved."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor for evidence of illness (i.e. mouth ulcers, sore throat, fever, bruising, malaise) occurs. Withdraw treatment upon occurrence of neutropenia and liver damage. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, gastric discomfort, skin rashes, pruritus, hair loss, headache, aplastic anemia, isolated thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, taste disturbance, arthralgia, myopathy, vasculitis, nephritis, lupus-like syndrome, neutropenia, liver damage (usually cholestatic jaundice)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, beta-blockers, digitalis glycosides, theophylline."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 5 mg (P7.25), 20 mg (P27.50)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Urinary Alkalinizers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of renal tubular acidosis with calcium stones; hypocitraturic calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis; uric acid lithiasis with or without calcium stones. Prevention of stone relapse after extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy or lithotomy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – Severe hypocitraturia (urinary citrate &lt;150 mg/day)</b>: 60 mEq/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. <b>Mild to moderate hypocitraturia (urinary citrate &gt;150 mg/day)</b>: 30 mEq/day in 2 or 3 divided doses. Take tab 30 mins after meals. Limit salt intake. Increase fluid intake."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hyperkalemia or who have conditions predisposing to hyperkalemia; slow gastric emptying time, esophageal compression, intestinal obstruction or stricture; anticholinergic therapy; active PUD; active UTI; renal insufficiency (GFR &lt;0.7 mL/kg/min); respiratory or metabolic acidosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with chronic renal failure or any other condition which impairs potassium excretion e.g. severe myocardial damage or heart failure; cardiac or renal disease, or acidosis. Discontinue immediately in the event of severe vomiting, abdominal pain or GI bleeding. Regular serum potassium monitoring is recommended. Discontinue in the occurrence of hyperkalemia when a significant rise in creatinine, or a significant fall in hematocrit or Hgb. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
