                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal discomfort, vomiting, diarrhea, loose bowel movements, nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. triamterene, spironolactone or amiloride). Drugs that slow GI transit time (e.g. anticholinergics)."
          },

            "content": "<b>Cap</b>: Individualized dose. 50-100 mg every 4-6 hrs.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;10 mL/min), acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotics, analgesics, opioids, or other psychotropic agents; receiving MAOIs. Pregnancy."

          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal or liver impairment, history of epilepsy or susceptibility to seizures. Do not administer during light planes of general anesthesia. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, constipation, drowsiness and confusion, tolerance (long-term use), respiratory depression, hypotension, hypertension, anaphylaxis, hallucinations"
          },
          {

            "content": "Carbamazepine, noradrenaline and serotonin, lithium, TCAs and SSRIs. <b>IM/IV incompatibilities</b>: Diazepam, diclofenac sodium, indomethacin, midazolam, piroxicam."

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily. Initial therapy: 40/5 mg or 80/5 mg. The maximum recommended dose is 80/10 mg once daily. <b>Replacement therapy from separate tablets:</b> 1 tab containing the same component doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },

            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },

            "content": "Peripheral edema, dizziness, hypotension. Impotence, increased sweating, flushing; fever, leg pain, malaise. Palpitations, angina pectoris, tachycardia, leg edema.           },

            "content": "<b>Telmisartan:</b> Digoxin, lithium, NSAIDs. <b>Amlodipine:</b> Simvastatin, grapefruit juice, cimetidine."

      "data": {
        "id": 4148,
        "brand_name": "Telarb Plus",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Telmisartan, hydrochlorothiazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension. For adults whose BP is not adequately controlled on telmisartan alone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once daily or as prescribed. May be increased if necessary."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active ingredients, any of the excipients, or sulfonamide-derived drugs. Patients with cholestasis and biliary obstructive disorders; refractory hypokalemia and hypercalcemia. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use of aliskiren-containing products in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR &lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose and/or galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with cholestasis, biliary obstructive disorders or severe hepatic insufficiency, impaired hepatic function or progressive liver disease, bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min), vol- and sodium depletion, primary hyperaldosteronism, aortic and mitral valve stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Dual blockade of RAAS. Increased risk for renovascular HTN. May impair glucose tolerance or cause hypoglycemia in diabetic patients. Electrolyte imbalance (e.g. hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hypercalcemia, hypomagnesemia), choroidal effusion, acute myopia, angle-closure glaucoma, and non-melanoma skin cancer. Severe CHF, ischemic cardiomyopathy or ischemic CV disease. History of allergy or bronchial asthma. Photosensitivity. Hypertensive black patients. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, dose-related orthostatic hypotension, impaired renal function, elevation of liver enzymes, hyperkalemia and myalgia, respiratory tract disorders, back pain, GI disturbances, fatigue, neutropenia, headache, photosensitivity reactions, paresthesia, impotence, xanthopsia, cholestatic jaundice, pancreatitis, and blood dyscrasias. <b>HCTZ</b>: hypokalemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Lithium, medicinal products associated with potassium loss and hypokalemia (e.g. kaliuretic diuretics, laxatives, corticosteroids, ACTH, amphotericin, carbenoxolone, penicillin G sodium, salicylic acid and derivatives), digitalis glycosides, class Ia and III antiarrhythmics, some antipsychotics (e.g. thioridazine, chlorpromazine, levomepromazine, trifluoperazine, cyamemazine, sulpiride, sultopride, amisulpride, tiapride, pimozide, haloperidol, droperidol, cholestyramine, colestipol resins, antidiabetic agents (e.g. oral agents, insulin, metformin), other antihypertensives, NSAIDs, noradrenaline, tubocurarine, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, allopurinol, calcium salts, atropine, biperiden, amantadine, cyclophosphamide, and methotrexate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 40 mg/12.5 mg x 30s (P472.50)."
          }

            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults. Reduction of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity with atherothrombotic CV disease e.g., history of coronary heart disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial disease  or type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) with targeted organ damage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Essential HTN:</b> 40 mg once daily. Some patients benefit from 20 mg daily. Max of 80 mg once daily. CV prevention: 80 mg once daily. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: </b>Max 40 mg once daily. <b>Severe renal impairment or hemodialysis:</b> Initially 20 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment. Cholestasis. Biliary obstructive disorder. Concomitant use with aliskiren-containing products or ACE-inhibitors in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment; recent kidney transplantation; vascular tone and renal function depend predominantly on RAAS activity; aortic or mitral stenosis or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Diabetic patients treated with insulin or antidiabetics. Not recommended in patients with primary aldosteronism. Increased risk of severe hypotension and renal insufficiency in patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney. Hyperkalemia. MI or stroke in patients with ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic CV disease. Monitor potassium and creatinine serum levels periodically in patients with renal impairment. Correct volume and/or sodium depletion prior to administration of therapy. Black population. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >70 yrs. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, UTI (e.g., cystitis), anemia, hyperkalemia, depression, insomnia, syncope, vertigo, bradycardia, hypotension, orthostatic hypotension, dyspnea, cough, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, hyperhidrosis, pruritus, rash, myalgia, back pain, muscle spasms, renal impairment (e.g., ARF), chest pain, asthenia, increased blood creatinine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Digoxin, potassium sparing, thiazide, or loop diuretics, potassium supplements, lithium, NSAIDs, baclofen, amifostine, alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, antidepressants, systemic corticosteroids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 40 mg (P14.00), 80 mg (P19.50)."

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension. Prevention of CV morbidity and mortality in patients &ge;55 yrs at high risk of CV disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Essential HTN:</b> 40 mg once daily. Max 80 mg once daily if target BP is not achieved. <b>Severe HTN:</b> Max 160 mg alone, or in combination with HCTZ 12.5-25 mg daily; <b>CV morbidity and mortality:</b> 80 mg once daily. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Max 40 mg once daily. Take with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Biliary obstructive disorders. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Rare hereditary fructose intolerance. Pregnancy 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters, and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to single functioning kidney; recent kidney transplant; vascular tone and renal function depend on RAAS activity; suffering from aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; heart failure; hepatic impairment; DM and additional CV risk; ischemic cardiomyopathy or CV disease. Not recommended in patients with primary aldosteronism. Correct vol and/or sodium depletion prior to therapy.           },

            "content": "UTI including cystitis, URTI, sepsis. Anemia, eosinophilia, thrombocytopenia. Hyperkalemia, hypoglycemia. Anxiety, insomnia, depression. Syncope. Visual disturbances. Vertigo.           },

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents for treatment of hypertension (HTN). <b>20 mg tab/80 mg tab</b>: Reduction of risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular (CV) events in patients &ge;55 yrs at high risk of CV events who are unable to take ACE inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: Individualized dosage. Initially, 40 mg once daily. Max 80 mg/day. <b>CV risk reduction</b>: 80 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>40 mg tab</b>: Biliary obstructive disorders. Hepatic impairment. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Concomitant use with aliskiren-containing products in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors in patients with diabetic nephropathy. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with cholelithiasis, bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, impaired renal function, recent kidney transplant, renal replacement therapy, vol- and/or sodium depletion, dehydration, acute cardiac decompensation, metabolic acidosis, worsening of renal condition, cellular lysis (e.g. acute limb ischemia, rhabdomyolysis), severe CHF or underlying renal disease, primary aldosteronism, aortic or mitral stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, diabetes (treated with insulin or antidiabetics), ischemic cardiopathy or CV disease. Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aliskiren, drugs that increase potassium levels. Black population. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Elderly &gt;70 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>20 mg tab/80 mg tab</b>: GI disturbances, pharyngitis, back pain. <b>40 mg tab</b>: Acute renal failure; anaphylactic reaction, angioedema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Digoxin, lithium, ramipril, ramiprilat. <b>40 mg tab</b>: Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, NSAIDs, thiazide or loop diuretics; ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aliskiren, other anti-HTN drugs; baclofen, amifostine, alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, antidepressants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 20 mg (P12.50), 40 mg (P14.50), 80 mg (P19.50)."
          }

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Imidazotetrazine"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of malignant gliomas e.g. glioblastoma multiforme and anaplastic astrocytoma, and malignant melanoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma multiforme</b>: Concomitant 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily for 42 days with focal radiotherapy, monotherapy 4 weeks after completing concomitant phase, administered for up to 6 cycles of monotherapy treatment. <b>Cycle 1</b>: 150 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily for 5 days followed by 23 days without treatment; <b>Cycle 2</b>: Escalate dose to 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily, once escalated, the dose remains at 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily for the 1<sup>st</sup> 5 days of each subsequent cycle except if toxicity occurs. <b>Adults and childn &ge;3 yrs with recurrent or progressive malignant glioma:</b> Treatment cycle is 28 days. <b>Patients previously untreated with chemotherapy</b>: 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily for the 1<sup>st</sup> 5 days followed by 23-day treatment interruption; <b>Patients previously treated with chemotherapy</b>: 150 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily, may be increased in the 2<sup>nd</sup> cycle to 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily for 5 days if there is no hematological toxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May experience myelosuppression. Prior to dosing, patients must have absolute neutrophil count (ANC) &ge;1.5 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L and platelet count &ge;100 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L. CBC should be obtained on day 22 (21 days after 1<sup>st</sup> dosing) or within 48 hrs of that day, and weekly until ANC is above 1.5 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L and platelet count exceeds 100 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, headache, fatigue, myelosuppression. May induce hypercoagulability."
          },

      "data": {
        "id": 215,

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Em1eb9L4lCLiN34W8vXKgvgDaHdjzTjYFt6xtX5KM43wRUVftq.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LBHYZo7wGxPwDz9MVggkJwnyZDLQxJjCwyvEUixpAZMzzHlmAt.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yNL7LsozgzwLvKf2DVqMijNdE8SGmHHOZ7gteAxspnFYjTeOhV.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefixime",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections due to susceptible microorganisms: acute bronchitis, acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis with infection, secondary infections in chronic respiratory tract disease, pneumonia; urinary tract infection (UTI) including pyelonephritis, cystitis, and cystourethritis; uncomplicated cervical/urethral gonorrhea; cholecystitis, cholangitis; scarlet fever; sinusitis, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, otitis media; typhoid fever including multi-drug resistant typhoid fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn >12 yrs (or weighing >50 kg):</b> 400 mg once daily or 200 mg every 12 hrs; <b>Childn 7-12 yrs (who can swallow cap whole):</b> 200-300 mg once daily or 100 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Uncomplicated cervical/urethral gonococcal infections:</b> 400 mg as a single dose. <b>Uncomplicated UTI:</b> 100 mg twice daily or 200 mg once daily for 7-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated cystitis:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs or 400 mg once daily for 3 days. <b>Uncomplicated acute pyelonephritis:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs or 400 mg once daily for 14 days. <b>Typhoid fever:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs or 400 mg once daily for 7-14 days. <b>Renal impairment -</b> CrCl 20-40 mL/min: Reduce dose to 75% (i.e. 300 mg/day); < 20 mL/min, CAPD, hemodialysis: Reduce dose to 50% (i.e. 200 mg/day at usual dosing interval)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia or colitis. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (including TEN, SJS, DRESS), CDAD, hemolytic anemia, acute renal failure, fall in prothrombin activity, and seizure may occur. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms including fungi during prolonged use. Monitor for signs and symptoms of hemolytic anemia periodically, including measurement of hematological parameters or drug-induced antibody testing. Infants < 6 months. Childn with renal impairment. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI, dermatologic/hypersensitivity, hepatic, renal/GUT, nervous system, and hematologic reactions. Hyperbilirubinemia. Increased serum amylase concentrations, dyspnea, respiratory distress."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbamazepine, chloramphenicol, nifedipine, probenecid, salicylates, warfarin, and other anticoagulants. False positive reaction on Nitroprusside and Coombs’ test, Clinitest, Benedict’s and Fehling’s soln."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P94.00), 200 mg (P155.25)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefixime",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections due to susceptible microorganisms: acute bronchitis, acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis with infection, secondary infections in chronic respiratory tract disease, pneumonia; urinary tract infection (UTI) including pyelonephritis, cystitis, and cystourethritis; uncomplicated cervical/urethral gonorrhea; cholecystitis, cholangitis; scarlet fever; sinusitis, tonsillitis, pharyngitis, otitis media; typhoid fever including multi-drug resistant typhoid fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn >12 yrs (or weighing >50 kg):</b> 400 mg once daily or 200 mg every 12 hrs; <b>Childn 7-12 yrs (who can swallow cap whole):</b> 200-300 mg once daily or 100 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Uncomplicated cervical/urethral gonococcal infections:</b> 400 mg as a single dose. <b>Uncomplicated UTI:</b> 100 mg twice daily or 200 mg once daily for 7-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated cystitis:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs or 400 mg once daily for 3 days. <b>Uncomplicated acute pyelonephritis:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs or 400 mg once daily for 14 days. <b>Typhoid fever:</b> 200 mg every 12 hrs or 400 mg once daily for 7-14 days. <b>Renal impairment -</b> CrCl 20-40 mL/min: Reduce dose to 75% (i.e. 300 mg/day); < 20 mL/min, CAPD, hemodialysis: Reduce dose to 50% (i.e. 200 mg/day at usual dosing interval)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia or colitis. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (including TEN, SJS, DRESS), CDAD, hemolytic anemia, acute renal failure, fall in prothrombin activity, and seizure may occur. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms including fungi during prolonged use. Monitor for signs and symptoms of hemolytic anemia periodically, including measurement of hematological parameters or drug-induced antibody testing. Infants < 6 months. Childn with renal impairment. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI, dermatologic/hypersensitivity, hepatic, renal/GUT, nervous system, and hematologic reactions. Hyperbilirubinemia. Increased serum amylase concentrations, dyspnea, respiratory distress."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbamazepine, chloramphenicol, nifedipine, probenecid, salicylates, warfarin, and other anticoagulants. False positive reaction on Nitroprusside and Coombs’ test, Clinitest, Benedict’s and Fehling’s soln."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 400 mg (P202.35)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Human tetanus immunoglobulin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "DPT Immunoglobulins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Immediate prophylaxis after tetanus-prone injuries in patients who are not adequately vaccinated, with unknown immunization status, or with severe deficiency in antibody production."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IM inj. <b>Prophylaxis for tetanus-prone wounds</b>: 250 IU, may be increased to 500 IU. <b>For extensive burns</b>: Administer 2<sup>nd</sup> inj of 250 IU after exudative phase of burn has subsided (about 36 hrs after onset of burns). <b>Therapy of clinically manifest tetanus</b>: 3,000-6,000 IU given as single dose. May be administered in divided doses at different sites if a large total vol is required (&gt;2 mL for BW &le;20 kg or 5 mL for BW &gt;20 kg)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for IV administration. Monitor patients for at least 20 mins after administration or longer term (at least 1 hr) in case of accidental IV inj. Vaccinations with live attenuated virus vaccines (e.g., rubella, mumps, and varicella vaccines) should be done after at least 3 months. May interfere with some serological test for red cell allo-antibodies (e.g. Coombs’ test). May be given SC if IM is contraindicated. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fall in BP, dyspnea, cutaneous reactions. Chills, fever, headache, malaise, nausea, vomiting, arthralgia, moderate back pain. Local pain, tenderness, swelling."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IM) 250 IU/mL in pre-filled syringe (P1,060.00)."
          }

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Tetracyclines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections due to microorganisms sensitive to tetracyclines. Treatment of acne."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Indications other than acne:</b> 600 mg/day. <b>Acne:</b> 300 mg/day for 12 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concurrent treatment with oral retinoids. Childn &lt;8 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Take with adequate fluid to avoid esophageal irritation and ulceration. Renal or hepatic impairment. Hepatotoxicity (overdosage, nephrotoxicity (high doses). Avoid exposure to direct sunlight and UV light. Discontinue use if erythematous cutaneous manifestations occur. Use of expired tetracyclines can lead to renal tubular acidosis (pseudo-Fanconi syndrome). Discontinue if any evidence of raised intracranial pressure develops. May result in the appearance of resistant organisms and superinfection in prolonged use. Patients with myasthenia gravis. False positive urine glucose determinations. Interfere with fluorometric determinations of urine catecholamines resulting in falsely increased values (Hingerty’s method).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea. Dental dyschromia and/or enamel hypoplasia if administered in childn < 8 yrs. Extra-renal hyperazotemia linked to an anti-anabolic effect which may be intensified by the association with diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral retinoids, vit A, iron preparations; antacids e.g. magnesium or aluminum and calcium hydroxides; oxides, salts and activated charcoal, cholestyramine, bismuth chelates and sucralfate. Products that increase gastric pH. Enzyme inducers e.g. barbiturates, carbamazepine, phenytoin; oral coumarin-type anticoagulants, penicillins, methoxyflurane, didanosine, lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 300 mg x 28s (P3,085.00)."
          }

        "content": "Diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (acellular component), and poliomyelitis (inactivated) vaccine (adsorbed)",

            "content": "Rx"
          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Combined prevention of diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, and poliomyelitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary vaccination:</b> 2 doses with an interval of 2 months, 1 at the age of 2 months and 1 at the age of 4 months, followed by 1 booster inj at the age of 6 months and another booster at the age of 6 yrs; or 3 inj at an interval 1-2 months, followed by 1 booster one yr after primary vaccination. <b> Booster vaccination:</b> Between 11-13 yrs of age for childn who received a vaccine containing the pertussis valence at reduced concentration at the age of 6 yrs."
          },

        "content": "Levothyroxine sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-Hypothyroidism Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism). Treatment of other types of thyroid disorders e.g. certain types of goiters, thyroid nodules, thyroiditis, and thyroid cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Initially 50-100 mcg, increased by 25-50 mcg at 3-4 week intervals to maintain max 150-300 mcg daily. <b>Childn:</b> Initially 25-150 mcg with 25 mcg increments every 2-4 weeks; <b>Childn >1 yr with juvenile myxedema:</b> Initially 2.5-5 mcg/kg per day. Take on an empty stomach 30-60 mins before breakfast. Take at the same time each day. Tabs may be crushed and mixed with 1 or 2 tsps of water and taken immediately."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Thyrotoxicosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "CHD, ECG changes of MI. Give corticosteroid therapy first followed by thyroxine in patients with adrenal insufficiency. Do not use either alone or in combination with diet pills to treat obesity or for weight loss. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Palpitation, osteoporosis, angina, tremors, thyrotoxicosis, allergic reaction, headache, tachycardia, diarrhea, restlessness, sweating, weight loss and muscle weakness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, phenytoin, anticonvulsants e.g. carbamazepine, cardiac glycosides, sympathomimetic agents, TCAs, cholestyramine, bile acid sequestrants (e.g. colestipol), anion/cation exchange resins (e.g. kayexalate, sevelamer), sucralfate, calcium carbonate, and ferrous sulfate, oral contraceptives, estrogen, tamoxifen, clofibrate, methadone, and 5-fluorouracil, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins), androgens and anabolic steroids, tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g. imatinib and sunitinib), amiodarone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 50 mcg x 100s (P710.00), 100 mcg x 100s (P1,134.00)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tadalafil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Drugs Used in Erectile Dysfunction"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult males."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 10 mg taken prior to sexual activity. In patients in whom tadalafil 10 mg does not produce adequate effect: 20 mg may be taken 30 mins prior to sexual activity. Max once per day. If frequent use (i.e. at least twice weekly) is anticipated: Use lower doses. <b>Patients with hepatic or severe renal impairment</b>: 10 mg taken with or without food and prior to anticipated sexual activity. Film should be placed on tongue, allow to dissolve and swallow the residue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with MI (within last 90 days), unstable angina or angina occurring during sexual intercourse, heart failure NYHA class 2 or greater (within last 6 months), uncontrolled arrhythmias, hypotension (&lt;90/50 mmHg) or uncontrolled HTN. Patients who have loss of vision in one eye due to NAION. Patients taking organic nitrates. Coadministration with guanylate cyclase stimulators e.g. riociguat. Women. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Serious CV events e.g. MI, sudden cardiac death, unstable angina pectoris, ventricular arrhythmia, stroke, TIA, chest pain, palpitations, tachycardia. Patients with severe hepatic insufficiency (Child-Pugh Class C). Patients with deformation of penis (e.g. angulation, cavernosal fibrosis or Peyronie’s disease) or patients who have conditions which predispose priapism (e.g. sickle cell anemia, multiple myeloma, leukemia). Concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitors.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, flushing, nasal congestion, dyspepsia, backpain, myalgia, pain in extremity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ritonavir, saquinavir, ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, grapefruit juice. Rifampicin, phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine. Nitrates, doxazosin. Antihypertensives, alpha-reductase inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Orodispersible film 10 mg, 20 mg."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Initially 50 mg once daily. Maintenance dose: 25-100 mg daily. <b>HTN:</b> 50-100 mg daily. <b>Angina pectoris:</b> 100 mg daily as a single or in divided doses, may be increased to 200 mg if needed. <b>MI:</b> 100 mg daily as single or in divided doses is recommended for long-term prophylaxis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Shock, CHF, hypotension, sick sinus syndrome, sinus bradycardia, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree heart block, significant right ventricular hypertrophy, right ventricular failure secondary to pulmonary HTN, bronchospasm, metabolic acidosis, and untreated pheochromocytoma. Concurrent use anesthetic agents that produce myocardial depression (e.g. ether, chloroform, cyclopropane)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt discontinuation. May precipitate severe heart failure and thyroid storm. May mask signs of acute hypoglycemia i.e. tachycardia. Use with caution during anesthesia and major surgery. May increase serum free-thyroxine levels. May impair peripheral circulation and renal function. Patients with bronchospastic diseases, Prinzmetal angina, 1<sup>st</sup> degree heart block, MI with < 120 mmHg systolic BP, atrial fibrillation after MI, bradycardia, history of anaphylaxis, eye and skin reactions.           "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ToJPAItAhh50lqLZQ05HXYozpJIiioG4CjnBWffM6E421JcRIy.jpg"

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-Hypothyroidism Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Replacement therapy for, or as adjuvant, to prevent hypothyroidism. Suppression of TSH in simple non-toxic goiter (e.g. thyroid nodules and Hashimoto’s thyroiditis) and post-therapeutic treatment for radiological or surgical operation. Concomitantly given in patients undergoing thyroid suppression test and in patients taking drugs with goitrogenic effects e.g. lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - Hypothyroidism: Initially 50-100 mcg increased by increments of 25-50 mcg every 14 days. Maintenance dose: 100-200 mcg daily. Suppression of TSH: 2.6 mcg/kg daily. <b>Elderly with cardiovascular disorder</b>: Initially 12.5 mg increased by increments of 12.5-25 mcg every 4 weeks. <b>&gt;60 yrs</b>: Maintenance dose is 25% lower than adult dose. <b>Childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: 2-3 mcg/kg. Usual dose: 100-200 mcg daily. <b>6-12 yrs</b>: 4-5 mcg/kg; Usual dose: 100-150 mg daily. <b>1-5 yrs</b>: 5-6 mcg/kg. Usual dose: 75-100 mcg daily. <b>6-12 months</b>: 6-8 mcg/kg. Usual dose: 50-75 mcg daily. <b>&lt;6 months</b>: 8-10 mcg/kg. Usual dose: 25-50 mcg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used for treatment of obesity or weight loss. Patients with CV disease, myxedema. Perform TSH test to check T3 and T4 levels for dose titration. Institute corticosteroid replacement therapy prior to levothyroxine replacement therapy in pituitary hypothyroidism. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Vomiting, diarrhea, tachycardia, arrhythmia, angina pectoris, HTN, muscular weakness and cramps, headache, benign intracranial disorder, weight loss, hyperhidrosis, hyperthyroidism, restlessness, insomnia, tremors, palpitations, flushing, fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cholestyramine, aluminum, magnesium, and ferrous preparations, ciprofloxacin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, barbiturates, estrogens, lithium, iodide, propranolol, amiodarone, X-ray imaging fluids, dexamethasone, antidiabetics, anticoagulants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 12.5 mcg (P6.00), 25 mcg (P6.00), 50 mcg (P7.00), 100 mcg (P12.00), 150 mcg (P18.00)."

  {
    "id": 4786,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4786,
        "brand_name": "Thyroxil",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/r1NOyQ22IRM3KsTbpXhvlOnHfPkk6b7coUlMQLEcL7ggddF35o.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QCA6RPhQBdeRUjOCDO46ZwvWxLpvGCRi4dkuMmwyiSd6zgSPI8.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tcy9bEJCe7ZZPePMScs6o9k7jycA2zXvDWBRIQVAGKfOMoKCzC.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levothyroxine sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-Hypothyroidism Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For control of hypothyroidism, congenital hypothyroidism in infants. Treatment for acquired hypothyroidism in children and juvenile myxedema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Initially 50-100 mcg daily, preferably taken before breakfast or first meal of the day, adjust by 50 mcg at 3-4 weeks intervals until normal metabolism is steadily maintained. Final dose 100-200 mcg. <b>Elderly >50 yrs:</b> Max 50 mcg, the daily dose may be increased by 50 mcg at 3-4 weeks intervals, until stable thyroxine levels are attained. Final dose 50-200 mcg daily. <b>Patients >50 yrs with cardiac disease:</b> 25 mcg or 50 mcg on alternate days, may increased daily dose by 25 mcg at 4-week intervals. Final daily dose 50-200 mcg. <b>Child:</b> 100-150 mcg<sup>2</sup> BSA. <b>Acquired hypothyroidism:</b> Initially 12.5-50 mcg/day, increased gradually every 2-4 weeks according to clinical findings and thyroid hormones and TSH values. <b>Juvenile myxedema:</b> Initially 25 mcg daily, may be increased by 25 mcg at 2-4 weeks until mild symptoms of hyperthyroidism are seen, then reduce the dose slightly. <b>Infants and neonates - Congenital hypothyroidism:</b> Initially 10-15 mcg/kg/day for the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months, adjust dose individually according to clinical findings and thyroid hormone and TSH values."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Thyrotoxicosis. Adrenal gland disorder or adrenal insufficiency."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with panhypopituitarism or other causes predisposing to adrenal insufficiency, initiate corticosteroid therapy first. Patients with cardiac symptoms, DM, diabetes insipidus, angina, arrhythmias, MI, cardiac failure. Should not be used for the treatment of obesity and weight loss. Larger doses may produce serious or life-threatening manifestations of toxicity, particularly when given in association with sympathomimetic amines. Patients with myxedema have an increased sensitivity to thyroid hormones. In women, long-term levothyroxine has been associated with increased bone resorption. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased appetite, abnormal loss of weight. Hyperthyroidism. Abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. Headache, tremors, seizures. Anginal pain, cardiac arrthyhmias, palpitations, tachycardia, increased blood pressure, heart failure, MI. Dyspnea, sweating, alopecia, flushing. Anxiety, emotional lability, nervousness, excitability, insomnia, restlessness. Menstrual irregularity, impaired fertility. Fatigue, heat intolerance, fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticonvulsants (e.g. carbamazepine and phenytoin), rifampicin, barbiturates, cardiac glycosides. Cholestyramine, calcium, aluminum, magnesium, iron supplements, aluminum hydroxide, polystyrene sulfonates, sucralfate, lanthanum, bile acid sequesterants (e.g. colestipol), calcium carbonate, ferrous sulfate, PPIs. Oral contraceptives, estrogens, tamoxifen, clofibrate, methadone, 5-fluorouracil. Propanalol, amiodarone, lithium, iodide, oral contrast agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 50 mcg, 100 mcg."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 215,
          "name": "The Cathay YSS Distributors Co., Inc."
        },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiplatelets"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "To reduce risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction (MI), and stroke in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or history of MI. To reduce rate of stent thrombosis in patients who have been stented for treatment of ACS."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Management of ACS:</b> Initially 180 mg. <b>During 1<sup>st</sup> yr after an ACS event:</b> 90 mg twice daily. <b>After 1 yr:</b> 60 mg twice daily. Use with a maintenance dose of aspirin 75-100 mg daily. Tabs can be crushed and mixed with water for patients with swallowing difficulties."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe hepatic impairment, history of intracranial hemorrhage and active pathological bleeding e.g. peptic ulcer, intracranial hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "If therapy must be temporarily discontinued (e.g. treat bleeding, significant surgery), restart as soon as possible; or interrupt therapy for 5 days prior to surgery with major risk of bleeding and resume as soon as hemostasis is achieved. Patients with history of sick sinus syndrome, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block or bradycardia-related syncope not protected by a pacemaker. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bleeding, dyspnea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A inhibitors and inducers. Opioids, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 90 mg (P49.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3115,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3115,
        "brand_name": "Tidomet",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ESmHtxH4tcnmtTw49jue8W9809hA8rjanKFvU0irgY3QeP3Flv.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/CaILSelj7R6JqwJHdU8gVR4sy9R3cWWRQGYJczHuX9yaArMIla.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/E8WhmjeFZNl3nU1doD9jLONBioKOkg3udmZe91KtB7F8ukxvgU.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levodopa, carbidopa",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptoms of idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (paralysis agitans), post-encephalitic parkinsonism, which may follow injury to nervous system by carbon monoxide intoxication and manganese intoxication."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Tidomet 100 mg/25 mg tab – Patients not previously treated with levodopa</b>: Initially 1 tab 3x daily, increased gradually in increments of carbidopa 12.5 mg with levodopa 50 mg or carbidopa 25 mg with levodopa 100 mg every day or on alternate days. Maintenance: Carbidopa 75-200 mg with levodopa 750 mg-2 g daily in divided doses. Max Carbidopa 200 mg daily. <b>Patients previously treated with levodopa</b>: Initially &frac14; of dose previously taken. <b>Patients taking &lt;1.5 g or &gt;1.5 g levodopa daily</b>: Initially 1 tab 3-4 times daily. <b>Tidomet 250 mg/25 mg tab</b>: Initially 1 tab 3x a day, may be increased by 1 tab a day or every other day as necessary, up to 8 tabs/day. <b>Tidomet CR tab – Patients already receiving levodopa and currently receiving levodopa alone</b>: Initially 1 tab twice daily adjusted according to response at intervals of not &lt;3 days. <b>Patients not already receiving initial dose</b>: Should not exceed 600 mg levodopa. <b>Patients already receiving conventional preparation</b>: Initially similar to that of conventional preparation but dosing intervals should be prolonged and normally between 4-12 hrs. Alter doses and intervals according to response, allowing at least 3 days between adjustments. Maintenance: Carbidopa 100 mg with levodopa 400 mg to carbidopa 400 mg with levodopa 1.6 g."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Narrow-angle glaucoma, patients with suspicious undiagnosed skin lesions or a history of melanoma. Concomitant use with MAOIs. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with open-angle glaucoma, CV or pulmonary disease, endocrine disorders, psychiatric disturbances, osteomalacia, hepatic or renal disease or history of peptic ulceration, malignant melanoma. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI effects (e.g. nausea, vomiting and anorexia), GI bleeding; orthostatic hypotension; psychiatric symptoms; abnormal involuntary movements or dyskinesias; positive response to the direct Coombs’ test; transient increase in liver enzymes, BUN and serum uric acid concentrations; discoloration of urine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antihypertensives, tricyclics, phenothiazines and butyrophenones, phenytoin and papaverine. Drugs affecting gastric emptying."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 100 mg/25 mg (P33.50), 250 mg/25 mg (P53.00). Controlled-release tablet 200 mg/50 mg (P74.30)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Thromboembolic disorders. Prophylactic in atherosclerosis with risk of thromboembolic disorders (e.g., MI, PAD, and stroke). In combination with aspirin in acute coronary syndromes (e.g., acute MI and unstable angina), and coronary stenting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prophylaxis of thromboembolic events:</b> 75 mg once daily. <b>Acute ST-elevation MI:</b> 75 mg once daily; <b>Elderly < 75 yrs:</b> 300 mg. Treatment is continued for at least 4 weeks. <b>Unstable angina and non-Q wave MI:</b> Single dose of 300 mg, followed by 75 mg once daily. <b>Childn:</b> 1-3 mg/kg once daily; <b>1.5-17 yrs with arterial ischemic stroke:</b> 0.5-2.4 mg/kg (target dose 1 mg/kg)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active pathological bleeding (e.g., peptic ulcer or intracranial hemorrhage)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of bleeding or at risk of increased bleeding from recent trauma, surgery, or other pathological conditions; impaired CYP2C19 function. Recent TIA or stroke.  Avoid concomitant use with omeprazole or esomeprazole. Platelet transfusion may be used when quick reversal is needed. May induce TTP. Rhabdomyolysis in combination with ciclosporin and statins. Childn. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Serum sickness, interstitial pneumonitis, erythema multiforme, SJS, lichen planus, myalgia, loss of taste, angioedema, fever rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants, other antiplatelets, NSAIDs, ketoconazole, ciclosporin, statins, omeprazole, esomeprazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 75 mg (P24.00)."
          }

          {

            "content": "1 drop in the affected eye(s) once daily in the morning. If intraocular pressure (IOP) is not at satisfactory level, concomitant therapy with other IOP-lowering agents can be used."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Existing or history of bronchial asthma, severe COPD, sinus bradycardia, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block, overt cardiac failure, or cardiogenic shock."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Remove contact lenses prior to administration and reinsert after 15 mins. May cause systemic effects of beta-blockers. Concomitant use with other topical beta-blockers. Reduced blood flow, bacterial keratitis, choroidal detachment, muscle weakness consistent with certain myasthenic symptoms (e.g. diplopia, ptosis, generalized weakness). Discontinue treatment at the first sign of cardiac failure. Gradual withdrawal prior to surgery. May mask signs and symptoms of acute hypoglycemia and hyperthyroidism. Childn.                 },

                  "title": "X",

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduction of intraocular pressure (IOP) in adults with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension insufficiently responsive to topical beta-blockers or prostaglandin analogues."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults including elderly: 1 drop in the affected eye once daily at the same time each day. Close eyelids and gently press against the corner of the eye (nasolacrimal occlusion) for 2 mins after administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Reactive airway disease (i.e. bronchial asthma or history of, severe COPD). Sinus bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome, SA block, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block uncontrolled with pacemaker, overt cardiac failure, and cardiogenic shock."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with CV diseases and hypotension therapy with beta-blockers; 1<sup>st</sup> degree heart block; hepatic and renal impairment; severe peripheral circulatory disturbance; and mild/moderate COPD; corneal diseases; history of atopy or anaphylactic reactions; active intraocular inflammation.             "content": "Conjunctival hyperemia. Headache, dizziness, rhinitis, blepharal pigmentation, hirsutism, skin hyperpigmentation (periocular), and  visual disturbances/eye disorders."
          },

    "id": 3104,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3104,
        "brand_name": "Tolanz",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tlGi00q989Jmwx3Fk7S6DQ7QGht2QBaYhAWHBv90DLOgbFvq3m.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DWNY9i9W1r73coRSJLiZgFT4x6mXOayTIG6Y1yyUKOz1LKXo4C.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tk0J5HkNCIzEsjXguVPGAorcovtFcHHPI07UU3bENXd0i6wNxJ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Olanzapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of schizophrenia and for the treatment of moderate to severe mania associated with bipolar disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia</b>: Initially 10 mg daily. <b>Acute manic episodes</b>: Initially 10-15 mg daily as monotherapy or 10 mg as part of combination therapy. May be adjusted in dosage of 5 mg at intervals of not &lt;24 hrs if necessary within 5-20 mg daily. <b>Prevention of recurrence</b>: Initially 10 mg daily. <b>Patients with moderate hepatic and/or renal impairment</b>: Initially 5 mg daily. <b>Female, elderly, or non-smoking patients</b>: If more than 1 factor is present, 5 mg daily escalated gradually. Tab should be placed in the mouth, where it will rapidly disperse in saliva, so it can be easily swallowed. Alternatively, it may be dispersed in a full glass of water or other suitable beverage (orange juice, apple juice, milk or coffee) immediately before administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Known risk for narrow-angle glaucoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with DM, risk factors for DM (e.g. obesity, family history of diabetes), hyperglycemia; prostatic hypertrophy or paralytic ileus and related conditions; elevated ALT and/or AST, signs and symptoms of hepatic impairment, pre-existing conditions associated with limited hepatic functional reserve, and treated with potentially hepatotoxic drugs; low leukocyte and/or neutrophil counts, history of drug-induced bone marrow depression/toxicity, bone marrow depression caused by concomitant illness, radiation therapy or chemotherapy, and with hypereosinophilic conditions or with myeloproliferative disease; history of seizure or risk factors that may lower seizure threshold. NMS. Not for treatment of dopamine agonist associated psychosis in patients with Parkinson’s disease. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. May affect ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence and weight gain; hyperprolactinemia. Increased appetite, dizziness, elevated plasma glucose, triglyceride and liver enzyme values, eosinophilia, edema, orthostatic hypotension, and mild transient antimuscarinic effects e.g. constipation and dry mouth. Speech difficulty."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other CNS depressants including alcohol; dopaminergics; valproate; other drugs that may cause QT prolongation. CYP1A2 inhibitors, inducers or substrate; fluvoxamine, tobacco smoking and carbamazepine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Orodispersible tablet 5 mg (P73.21), 10 mg (P131.25)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 1246,
          "name": "Torrent Pharma Philippines, Inc."
        },

          },
          {

            "content": "Isolated or predominant endogenous hypertriglyceridemia in patients at risk of ischemic heart disease and or pancreatitis.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 2 caps daily, may be increased to 4 caps."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active substances, soya and peanut. Exogenous hypertriglyceridemia (type I hyperchylomicronemia)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitive or allergic to fish. Fall in thromboxane A2 production treatment. Monitor patients receiving anticoagulant therapy. Childn and adolescents. Elderly &gt;70. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal distension, abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, eructation, GERD, nausea, vomiting."

            "title": "Drug Interactions",

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TejYrwfBxIDSMbgH3WUWRqvHNYl0w8oB9EaAXNPAmsOC1pLrkt.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yjp8Bc2hklpNnhHcAul5qKPt6iD0KMfqzHCBgffYfAZ8V6Ltjb.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults; stroke and systemic embolism in adults with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), with one or more risk factors, e.g., prior stroke or transient ischemic attack, elderly &ge;75 yrs, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class &ge;II), and patients unstable for warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment of DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment. <b>Prevention of VTE - Elective hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily. Initial dose taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. <b>Treatment duration - Hip replacement surgery:</b> 32-38 days; <b>Knee replacement surgery:</b> 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily; elderly &ge;80 yrs, &le;60 kg BW, serum creatinine >1.5 mg/dL: 2.5 mg twice daily. Taken with or without food. Tabs may be crushed and mixed with water, D5W, apple juice, or apple puree for patients unable to swallow whole tabs. May be mixed with water or D5W and administered via nasogastric tube."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active bleeding. Concomitant anticoagulants. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment (Child Pugh A or B); increased risk of bleeding. Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment; hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and bleeding risk; undergoing dialysis; renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min); prosthetic heart valves, with or without atrial fibrillation. Discontinue at least 24 hrs (low risk of bleeding) or 48 hrs (moderate or high risk of bleeding) prior to elective surgery or invasive procedures; severe hemorrhage occurs. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Eye hemorrhage, GI (e.g., hematemesis, melena), rectal, and other hemorrhage, hematoma, hematuria, epistaxis, gingival bleeding, menorrhagia, confusion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole, ritonavir), inducers (e.g., rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John’s Wort), antiplatelets, NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin), other platelet aggregation inhibitors, antithrombotics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg (P23.00), 5 mg (P33.00)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Candesartan cilexetil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults. Treatment of adult patients with heart failure and impaired left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 40%) as add-on therapy to ACE inhibitors or when ACE inhibitors are not tolerated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: Initially 8 mg once daily, can be increased to 16 mg once daily. Max 32 mg once daily. <b>Patients with intravascular volume depletion, renal (including on hemodialysis) or mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: Initially 4 mg once daily. <b>Heart failure</b>: Initially 4 mg once daily. Max 32 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment and/or cholestasis. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Periodic monitoring of serum potassium and creatinine levels in patients with renal impairment. Assess renal function periodically. Concomitant therapy with ACE inhibitor in heart failure. Monitor BP in patient on hemodialysis. Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a solitary kidney; heart failure, intravascular vol depletion, receiving high-dose diuretics, during anesthesia and surgery. Aortic or mitral valve stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Not recommended in primary hyperaldosteronism. Hyperkalemia. Excessive BP decrease in patients with ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic cerebrovascular disease could result in MI or stroke. Galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Respiratory infection; leucopenia, neutropenia and agranulocytosis; hyperkalemia, hyponatremia; dizziness/vertigo, headache; hypotension; cough; nausea; increased liver enzymes, abnormal hepatic function or hepatitis; angioedema, rash, urticaria, pruritus; back pain, arthralgia, myalgia; renal impairment including renal failure in susceptible patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potassium-diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium or other medicinal products that may increase potassium levels (e.g. heparin). Lithium; NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 8 mg (P15.50)."
          }

      "success": true,
