        "id": 5022,
        "brand_name": "Torsit",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4RFqQJAwKhFgU0qmIRF6LnD5FYFG1RmYnLyK3sFFDVzbIDOym7.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/3myjldDFQhlge4IZJc416ijEdarGJpO66pzBGARjPEwvcNrWHf.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/iaAxzS2ZKNiFQv36GViPZO5LQ2O3ozLhPoS0B9BDx1Xa0Rl78O.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), to improve glycemic control as monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone, and for whom metformin is inappropriate. As dual therapy in combination with metformin, or sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist (e.g., thiazolidinediones), when as a single agent, with diet and exercise, does not provide adequate glycemic control. As triple oral therapy in combination with sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma and metformin, when diet and exercise plus dual therapy with these agents do not provide adequate glycemic control. As add-on to insulin (with or without metformin) when diet and exercise plus stable dose of insulin do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "100 mg once daily. <b>Renal impairment - Moderate (CrCl &ge;30 to < 50 mL/min):</b> 50 mg once daily; <b>Severe (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or ESRD requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis:</b> 25 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for patients with type 1 DM or diabetic ketoacidosis. Patients with history of pancreatitis. Hypoglycemia. Discontinue if acute pancreatitis or hypersensitivity reaction is suspected. Consider lowering the dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when used concomitantly. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, nasopharyngitis, osteoarthritis, pain in extremity. <b>Combination with sulfonylurea and metformin:</b> Hypoglycemia; <b>With insulin:</b> Influenza; <b>With metformin:</b> Nausea and vomiting; <b>With metformin or pioglitazone:</b> Flatulence; <b>With sulfonylurea and metformin:</b> Constipation; With pioglitazone (with or without metformin): Peripheral edema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P30.00), 100 mg (P25.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4584,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4584,
        "brand_name": "Torsit-M",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dTp2oszXvuW4nSlL78R79MraW6T5sLCtxzPMzcwqqVsdBmitvT.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/VRbc1CIcHStDXNcI0RIG86lmLvPY2M7KXR4w4O3vf3GpOertv2.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/m18PCyUmT3j1mQS3tlEtRNg5dzu2BRaVlwUJQvdHTGml6FzGyn.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients inadequately controlled on their maximal tolerated dose of metformin alone or those already being treated with a combination of sitagliptin and metformin. In triple combination with a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist (i.e. a thiazolidinedione) as adjunct to diet and exercise in patients inadequately controlled on maximal tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist. Add-on to insulin as adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients when stable dose of insulin and metformin alone do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Initially sitagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus dose of metformin already being taken. Max daily sitagliptin dose 100 mg. <b>Renal impairment</b> – GFR 60-89 mL/min: Max metformin 3,000 mg/day, sitagliptin 100 mg/day. 45-59 mL/min: Max metformin 2,000 mg/day, sitagliptin 100 mg/day. 30-44 mL/min: Max metformin 1,000 mg/day, sitagliptin 50 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Type 1 diabetes. Hepatic impairment. Patients with any type of acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma, severe renal failure (GFR &lt;30 mL/min), acute conditions with potential to alter renal functions e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock, intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents, acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia such as cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, acute alcohol intoxication; alcoholism. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk of acute pancreatitis, lactic acidosis. Hypoglycemia when used in combination with a sulfonylurea or insulin. Concomitant use of antihypertensive, diuretics and NSAIDs. Discontinue use if bullous pemphigoid is suspected; or at the time of surgery under general, spinal or epidural anesthesia or prior to or at the time of imaging procedure with intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents and not restarted until at least 48 hrs after. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, nausea, flatulence, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Iodinated contrast agents. Alcohol. NSAIDs e.g. selective COX-2 inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics (loop diuretics). Drugs that interfere with common renal tubular transport systems (e.g. OCT2/multidrug and toxin entrusion such as ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine). Glucocorticoids, beta2-agonists, diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/1 g (P19.50)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rosuvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunctive therapy to diet to reduce elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, non-HDL-C and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in adults with primary hyperlipidemia or mixed dyslipidemia; to reduce total cholesterol, LDL-C and apolipoprotein B in adolescent boys and girls (who are at least 1 yr post-menarche) 10-17 yrs with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (LDL-C &gt;190 mg/dL or &gt;160 mg/dL and positive family history of premature cardiovascular (CV) disease or &ge;2 other CV disease risk factors); patients with hypertriglyceridemia; primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III hyperlipoproteinemia); in combination with other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g. LDL apheresis) or alone if such treatments are unavailable to reduce LDL-C, total cholesterol and apolipoprotein B in adult patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia; to slow the progression of atherosclerosis in adults, as part of a treatment strategy to lower total cholesterol and LDL-C. To reduce risk of stroke, myocardial infarction and arterial revascularization procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Hypercholesterolemia</b>: 5 or 10 mg once daily, may be adjusted after 4 weeks if necessary. Patients with severe hypercholesterolemia at high CV risk: Final titration to max 40 mg if treatment goal is not achieved at 20 mg. <b>Prevention of CV events</b>: 20 mg daily. <b>Childn and adolescent 10-17 yrs (boys Tanner stage &ge;2 and girls at least 1 yr post-menarche) - Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b>: Initially 5 mg daily. Dose range: 5-20 mg once daily. <b>Elderly &gt;70 yrs, Asian ancestry, patients with predisposing factors myopathy or moderate renal insufficiency</b>: 5 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease, severe renal impairment, myopathy. Concomitant use of ciclosporin. 40 mg dose is contraindicated in patients with predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal effects (e.g. proteinuria). Monitor liver function tests. Patients who consume excessive alcohol, with history of liver disease, secondary hypercholesterolemia caused by hypothyroidism or nephrotic syndrome. Skeletal muscle effects, predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis; DM. Concomitant use of protease inhibitors. ILD may develop. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Asian race. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dizziness, constipation, nausea, abdominal pain, myalgia, asthenia, DM."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, protease inhibitors, gemfibrozil, ezetimibe, antacid, erythromycin, vitamin K antagonists, oral contraceptives, hormone replacement therapy, transporter protein inhibitors, fusidic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P30.50), 20 mg (P37.80)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN) in adults and childn 6-18 yrs. Treatment of heart failure (NYHA class II-IV) in patients receiving standard therapy e.g. diuretics, digitalis and either ACE inhibitors or beta-blockers. To improve survival following myocardial infarction (MI) in clinically stable patients with evidence of left ventricular failure and/or with left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Adjunct to lifestyle modifications to delay the progression to type 2 diabetes in hypertensive adult patients with impaired glucose intolerance at CV risk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – HTN</b>: 80 mg-160 mg once daily, may be increased to 320 mg if BP is not adequately controlled. <b>Heart failure</b>: 40 mg twice daily, may be titrated to 80 mg-160 mg twice daily. Max 320 mg in divided doses. <b>Post-MI</b>: May be initiated as early as 12 hrs after MI. Initially 20 mg twice daily, and titrated to 40 mg, 80 mg, and 160 mg twice daily over the next few weeks. Patient must achieve a dose level of 80 mg twice daily for 2 weeks after initial treatment and target max dose achieved by 3 months depending on the patient’s tolerability to valsartan during titration. <b>Patients with HTN and impaired glucose tolerance at CV risk</b>: 80-160 mg once daily. <b>Childn and adolescents 6-18 yrs and &ge;35 kg BW</b>: 80 mg once daily. <b>&lt;35 kg BW</b>: 40 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of  aliskiren in patients with type 2 diabetes or severe renal impairment (GFR &lt;30 mL/min). Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal and hepatic impairment. Patients with sodium and/or vol depletion, renal artery stenosis, biliary obstructive disorders, heart failure or post-MI. May cause angioedema. Dual blockade of RAAS with ACEs or aliskiren. Childn with GFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup> or undergoing dialysis. Childn and adolescents &le;18 yrs. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Angioedema. Dizziness, hypotension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 80 mg (P26.80), 160 mg (P43.00)."
          }

    "id": 1496,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1496,
        "brand_name": "Trajenta Duo",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9w90UhJZ2xXWOBm8gerCMQsoqto4dAHr2D2coRRzWBD0RodDBC.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Bvj6QbLxlL7QuA1CvEqq3MnePFkDq9OSp1779QnIeSwTxDWON5.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6IIewjnTf9r9xtpxDnL1UiFi9h9mkHtqXcn0Q4TtaYfRVRYjsf.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Linagliptin, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) when both linagliptin and metformin are appropriate. Patients inadequately controlled on metformin alone or those already being treated and well-controlled with separate tabs of linagliptin and metformin. In combination with a sulfonylurea or an SGLT2 inhibitor (triple combination therapy) in patients inadequately controlled on max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or an SGLT2 inhibitor.  Add-on to insulin in patients inadequately controlled with insulin and metformin alone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Linagliptin 2.5 mg and metformin 500 mg, 850 mg, or 1 g 2x daily. Individualized dose.Max 5 mg/2 g  daily. <b>Patients currently not treated with metformin:</b> Initially 2.5 mg/500 mg 2x daily. <b>Inadequately controlled on max tolerated dose of metformin monotherapy:</b> Initially 2.5 mg linagliptin 2x daily with dose of metformin already being taken. <b>Switching from co-administration to fixed-dose combination:</b> Initiate treatment at the doses already being taken. <b>Inadequately controlled on dual combination therapy with max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or insulin:</b> 2.5 mg linagliptin 2x daily with dose of metformin already being taken. Lower dose of sulfonylurea or insulin when combined with therapy. <b>Renal impairment:</b> No dose adjustment for linagliptin; <b>GFR 60-89 mL/min:</b> Max 3 g metformin daily, may reduce in relation to declining renal function; <b>45-59 mL/min:</b> Max 2 g metformin  daily (starting dose: most &frac12; max dose); <b>30-44 mL/min:</b> Max 1 g metformin daily (starting dose: most &frac12; max dose). Taken with meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis).  Diabetic pre-coma. Severe renal failure (CrCl < 30 mL/min or eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function (e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock, IV iodinated contrast agents). Diseases which may cause tissue hypoxia, especially acute disease or worsening of chronic disease (e.g. decompensated heart failure, respiratory failure, recent MI, shock). Hepatic impairment. Acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM. Pancreatitis, hypoglycemia, bullous pemphigoid. Coadministration with sulfonylureas or insulin. Inform patients of risk of lactic acidosis (e.g. acidotic dyspnea, abdominal pain,  muscle cramps, asthenia, hypothermia followed by coma). Discontinue if dehydration and symptoms of lactic acidosis occurs; prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure or surgery under general, spinal or epidural anesthesia until &ge;48 hrs after, provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable. Assess GFR prior initiation of treatment and regularly after. Monitor vit B<sub>12</sub> levels periodically. May be used with regular monitoring of cardiac and renal function in patients with stable chronic heart failure.  Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Planning pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, lactic acidosis, decreased vit B<sub>12</sub>, hypoglycemia, taste disturbance, cough,  decreased appetite, diarrhea, constipation (combination with insulin), nausea, pancreatitis, vomiting,  pruritus, abdominal pain, mouth ulceration, abnormal liver function test, hepatitis, bullous pemphigoid,  pruritus, erythema, rash, increased lipase and amylase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, iodinated contrast agents, NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists and diuretics, verapamil, cimetidine, dolutegravir, ranolazine, trimethoprim, vandetanib, crizotinib, olaparib."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg/500 mg (P24.44), 2.5 mg/850 mg (P24.24), 2.5 mg/1,000 mg (P24.32)."
          }
        ],

          },

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of moderate to severe pain requiring a combination of tramadol and paracetamol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs</b>: Initially 2 tabs, additional doses may be given with intervals &ge;6 hrs. Max 8 tabs/day. <b>Elderly &gt;75 yrs</b>: Minimum dose interval should be at least 6 hrs. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl 10-30 mL/min)</b>: Increase dose interval to 12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotic drugs, centrally acting analgesics, opioids, or psychotropic drugs. Patients receiving MAOIs or within 2 weeks of withdrawal. Epilepsy not controlled by treatment. Severe renal and hepatic impairment. Severe respiratory insufficiency. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Moderate renal, and hepatic impairment. Patients with non-cirrhotic alcoholic liver disease. Epileptic patients controlled by treatment or patients susceptible to seizures or taking other medication that lowers seizure threshold. Not to be used as substitute in opioid-dependent patients, or used concomitantly with opioid agonists-antagonists. Patients with cranial trauma, prone to convulsive disorder, biliary tract disorders, problems affecting respiratory function, and increased intracranial pressure. Withdrawal symptoms.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, dizziness, headache, trembling, confusion, mood changes, anxiety, nervousness, euphoria, sleep disorder, vomiting, constipation, dry mouth, diarrhea, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, flatulence, sweating, pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "SSRIs, triptans, TCAs, antipsychotics, centrally acting analgesics, local anesthesia, opioids agonists-antagonists (e.g. nalbuphine, buprenorphine, pentazocine), MAOIs, alcohol, carbamazepine and other enzyme inducers, other opioids derivatives (e.g. antitussives), sedative antihistamines, neuroleptics, thalidomide, baclofen, warfarin, CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, erythromycin), metoclopramide, domperidone, cholestyramine, ondansetron."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 37.5 mg/325 mg (P25.00)."

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hemostatics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of painful bleeding. Short-term treatment for hemorrhage or risk of hemorrhage in conditions associated with increased fibrinolysis or fibrinogenolysis. Management of local fibrinolysis occurs in: prostatectomy and bladder surgery, menorrhagia, epistaxis, conization of the cervix, traumatic hyphaema, hereditary angioneurotic edema, dental extraction in hemophiliacs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 1-1.5 g (or 15-25 mg/kg BW) 2-4x daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "<b>Tranexamic</b>: Acquired defective color vision, subarachnoid hemorrhage, active intravascular clotting. <b>Mefenamic</b>: Hypersensitivity. Patients with asthma, urticaria or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or NSAIDs. Active ulceration or chronic inflammation of either upper or lower GIT, renal disease with impaired renal or hepatic function and epileptics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal insufficiency, previous history of thromboembolic disease, disseminated intravascular coagulation. Ureteral obstruction. Venous and arterial thrombosis or thromboembolism. Risk of GI ulceration, bleeding and perforation. Concomitant use with Factor IX Complex concentrations or anti-inhibitor coagulant concentrates. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B for tranexamic; Category C for mefenamic.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, tinnitus, headache. <b>Tranexamic</b>: Cramps, transient disturbance in color vision, musculoskeletal malaise, weakness, fatigue, elevated serum enzymes e.g. creatinine phosphokinase, rhabdomyolysis, dizziness, delirium, auditory, visual and kinesthetic hallucinations, miscellaneous conjunctival suffusion, nasal stiffness, skin rash, reversible acute renal failure, thrombophlebitis. <b>Mefenamic</b>: Abdominal pain, constipation, dyspepsia, flatulence, gross bleeding/perforation, heartburn, GI ulcers (gastric/duodenal), abnormal renal function, anemia, dizziness, edema, elevated liver enzymes, increased bleeding time, pruritus, rashes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg/250 mg."
          }

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Guselkumab",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Biologic Response Modifiers (Biologicals)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of plaque psoriasis, active psoriatic arthritis, and palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP) in adult patients with inadequate response to conventional therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC injection. <b>Adults &ge;18 yrs – Plaque psoriasis and PPP:</b> 100 mg at week 0, week 4 and every 8 weeks thereafter. <b>Psoriatic arthritis:</b> 100 mg at week 0, week 4 and every 8 weeks thereafter; or 100 mg at week 0 and every 4 weeks thereafter. May be taken alone or in combination with a conventional synthetic DMARD e.g. methotrexate. <b>Switching from other biologics:</b> In patients with inadequate response to ustekinumab or adalimumab, when switching to guselkumab, administer at week 0, week 4 and every 8 weeks thereafter."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with clinically important active infection; history of active or latent TB. Evaluate patients for TB;  initiate latent TB treatment prior to therapy. Avoid use of live vaccines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTIs, herpes simplex infections, tinea infections, gastroenteritis, increased transaminases, headache, diarrhea, arthralgia, injection site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Live vaccines or therapeutic infectious agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) 100 mg/mL (P117,000.00)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Insulin degludec",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Long-acting Insulins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Diabetes mellitus (DM) in adults and childn &ge;1 yr."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC administration once daily preferably at the same time every day. <b>Type 1 DM</b>: Initially once daily with meal-time insulin followed by individual dosage adjustments. <b>Type 2 DM</b>: Initially 10 IU followed by individual dosage adjustments."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For SC use only. Inadequate dosing or discontinuation of treatment may lead to hyperglycemia and diabetic ketoacidosis. Omission of meals or unplanned strenuous physical exercise may lead to hypoglycemia. Transferring from other types of insulin should be done under strict medical supervision. Concomitant infections or diseases in the kidney, liver, and those affecting the adrenal, pituitary, and thyroid gland may require changes in the insulin dose. Risk of heart failure with concomitant use of pioglitazones. Diabetic retinopathy. Weight gain. Glucose monitoring should be intensified and the dosage should be adjusted for elderly and patients with renal or hepatic impairment. May form insulin antibodies. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, injection site reactions, rarely hypersensitivity, urticaria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral antidiabetics, GLP-1 receptor agonists, MAOIs, beta-blockers, ACE inhibitors, salicylates, anabolic steroids and sulfonamides. Oral contraceptives, thiazides, glucocorticoids, thyroid hormones, sympathomimetics, growth hormone and danazol. Octreotide/lanreotide. Alcohol."
          },
          {

            "content": "Solution for injection (SC) (FlexTouch, Pre-filled pen) 100 IU/mL x 3 mL (P763.00)."

  {
    "id": 4999,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4999,
        "brand_name": "Trexed",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/o4K59ReAqWfK5UZTIhxazkIY3kDZRJaKFXjYFdIkkU7vzq5o1z.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/D7xwG3UVv0kWrsa8Sb8H2Sw5uOSjMjaUXxgMn8WbYpoMAu7BNH.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/sfi4p6FKtEUninMvU89y8li3JXgoKaNsyeQG9PQOzorArW8wjZ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Pemetrexed",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Folic Acid Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in combination with cisplatin as initial treatment or monotherapy after prior chemotherapy. In combination with cisplatin for treatment of patients with malignant pleural mesothelioma whose disease is unresectable or who are not candidates for curative surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion. <b>Combination with cisplatin:</b> 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 10 mins on day 1 of each 21-day cycle, 30 mins before 2 hrs infusion of 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> cisplatin. Give appropriate hydration prior to and/or after receiving cisplatin. <b>Monotherapy:</b> 500 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 10 mins on day 1 of each 21-day cycle. <b>Pre-medication regimen:</b> Low-dose oral folic acid (350-1000 mcg) or multivitamin with folic acid daily at least 5 daily doses for 7 days prior to 1<sup>st</sup> dose of treatment, continued throughout the therapy and for 21 days after last dose; 1,000 mcg vit B<sub>12</sub> IM during the week prior to 1<sup>st</sup> dose of treatment and every 3 cycles thereafter; 4 mg oral dexamethasone 2x daily prior to, the same day and the day after pemetrexed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "History of severe hypersensitivity. Renal impairment (CrCl < 45 mL/min). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not a treatment for squamous cell non-small cell lung cancer. Coadministration with NSAIDs to patients with mild to moderate renal impairment (CrCl 45-79 mL/min). Patients should have ANC &ge;1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>, platelet count &ge;100,000, and CrCl 45 mL/min prior to the start of new cycle. Bone marrow suppression, myelosuppression. Consider draining the effusion in patients with a third-space fluid collection prior to treatment. Monitor CBC (e.g., platelet counts) and renal function. Use effective contraceptives. Childn. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy:</b> Fatigue, nausea, anorexia. <b>Combination with cisplatin:</b> Vomiting, neutropenia, leukopenia, anemia, stomatitis/pharyngitis, thrombocytopenia, constipation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Nephrotoxic drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for IV infusion 500 mg (P40,000.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3399,
          "name": "Bio-Onco, Inc."
        },

            "content": "Fibric Acid Derivatives & Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of mixed hypercholesterolemia, hypertriglyceridemia; dyslipidemia associated with metabolic syndrome; diabetes when response to diet and lifestyle modification is inadequate. Correction of low HDL in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 1 tab once daily. <b>Patients with renal impairment:</b> Lower doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic insufficiency (including biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormality), severe CKD, chronic or acute pancreatitis except acute pancreatitis due to severe hypertriglyceridemia, history of fibrate or ketoprofen-associated photoallergy or phototoxicity or pre-existing gallbladder disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic or renal impairment. Treat secondary causes of hyperlipidemia (e.g. uncontrolled type 2 DM, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, dysproteinemia, obstructive liver disease, alcoholism) prior to treatment initiation. Monitor transaminase and creatinine levels every 3 months during the 1<sup>st</sup> 12 months of treatment and periodically thereafter; discontinue treatment if AST/ALT levels increase to >3x ULN, if hepatitis occurs, and if creatinine levels increase 50% ULN. Increased risk of muscle toxicity in patients with predisposing factors for myopathy and/or rhabdomyolysis, hereditary muscular disorders, renal impairment, hypothyroidism, high alcohol intake and concomitant use with other fibrates or HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors, especially in cases of pre-existing muscular disease; discontinue treatment if muscle toxicity occurs. Pancreatitis. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, flatulence. Increased transaminase levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, ciclosporin, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors and other fibrates, glitazones. Drugs metabolized by CYP2C19, CYP2A6, and CYP2C9."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the symptomatic relief of severe chronic spasticity. To reduce muscle spasm and pain especially in spinal cord lesions in conditions e.g. muscle sclerosis, paraplegia. For spasticity of cerebral origin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Initially 5 mg, may be increased to 10 mg 3x daily for 3 days.           {

            "content": "Maintenance treatment in adult patients with moderate to severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who are not adequately treated by a combination of an inhaled corticosteroid or a long-acting muscarinic antagonist and a long beta2-agonist. Maintenance treatment of asthma, in adults not adequately controlled with a maintenance combination of long-acting beta2-agonist and medium dose of inhaled corticosteroids, and who experienced one or more asthma exacerbations in the previous year."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "2 inhalations twice daily. Max 2 inhalations twice daily. Patients should be regularly reassessed so that their doses remain optimal and are only changed on medical advice.             "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm or acute disease exacerbation. Paradoxical bronchospasms. Sudden or progressive deterioration of symptoms. Patients with CV diseases, known or suspected QTc interval prolongation. Patients with thyrotoxicosis, DM, pheochromocytoma, and untreated hypokalemia. Increased incidence of pneumonia. Systemic corticosteroid effects (e.g. Cushing’s syndrome, Cushingoid features, adrenal suppression, growth retardation, decrease bone mineral density). Patients with active or quiescent pulmonary tuberculosis or with fungal and viral infection in the airways. Hyperglycemia. Patients with narrow-angle glaucoma, prostatic hyperplasia or urinary retention. Severe renal or hepatic impairment. Oropharyngeal infections, visual disturbance. Patients taking disulfiram or metronidazole. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of candidal vulvovaginitis due to <i>Candida albicans</i>, bacterial vaginosis due to anaerobic bacteria and <i>Gardnerella vaginalis</i>, trichomonal vaginitis due to <i>Trichomonas vaginalis</i>, mixed vaginal infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult and elderly (&gt;65 yrs) – Vaginitis</b>: Insert 1 vaginal suppository at night and in the morning for 7 days, or insert 1 vaginal suppository at night for 14 days. <b>Vaginitis resistant to other treatments or recurrent vaginitis</b>: Insert 1 vaginal suppository at night and in the morning for 14 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe liver problems, nervous system diseases, disturbances in hematopoiesis. Childn. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Liver impairment (e.g. porphyria), nervous system diseases, hematopoiesis. May be used after the 1<sup>st</sup> trimester if considered necessary. Disulfiram-like effects with alcohol intake. Concurrent use of rubber or latex products (e.g. vaginal contraceptive diaphragms, condoms). Sexual partners of patients with <i>Trichomonas vaginalis</i> should be treated at the same time. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain or cramps, metallic taste, constipation, dry mouth, seldom diarrhea, lack of appetite, vomiting, nausea, decreased WBC, musculoskeletal cramps, headache, movement disorders, dizziness, mental changes, peripheral neuropathy after overdose or long period of usage, vaginal irritation (burning, itching), rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Astemizole, terfenadine, phenytoin, carbamazepine, ciclosporin, oral anticoagulants (acenocoumarol, anisindione, dicoumarol, phenindione, warfarin). Barrier contraceptives. <b>Metronidazole</b>: Alcohol, amiodarone, disulfiram, phenobarbital, fluorouracil, lithium, cimetidine, theophylline, procainamide. <b>Miconazole</b>: Cisapride, fosphenytoin, fentanyl, glimepiride, oxybutynin, oxycodone, pimozide, tolterodine, trimetrexate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Vaginal suppository 500 mg/100 mg (P115.00)."

            "content": "Treatment of infections due to susceptible microorganisms: Upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) e.g. bacterial pharyngitis, tonsillitis, otitis media, sinusitis; and LRTI e.g. acute bronchitis and acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis; urinary tract infections (UTI) e.g. acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, cystourethritis; bronchiectasis with infection, secondary infections in chronic respiratory tract diseases, uncomplicated gonorrhea, cholecystitis and cholangitis, scarlet and typhoid fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 200-400 mg daily as single dose or in 2 divided doses. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea:</b> 400 mg as a single dose. <b>Childn &gt;6 months and weighing &lt;50 kg:</b> 8 mg/kg/day as single dose or in 2 divided doses. <b>Typhoid fever:</b> 15-20 mg/kg. Dose may be given as a single daily dose or 2 divided doses given every 12 hrs. Duration of treatment: 5-14 days. Max 400 mg/day. <b>Patients with renal impairment:</b> Reduce dosage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Tab:</b> Patients with renal impairment (CrCl &lt;60 mL/min)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Penicillin-sensitive patients. History of allergy; colitis; cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia. <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Fall in prothrombin activity especially in patients with kidney or liver impairment and poor nutritional state. Patients receiving a protracted course of antimicrobial therapy and previously stabilized on anticoagulant therapy. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms (long-term use). Alcohol consumption.                 },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },

                  "title": "X",

                }

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions, skin rashes, urticaria, fever, pruritus, arthralgia, angioedema, facial edema, erythema multiforme, SJS, TEN, serum sickness-like reactions, diarrhea, abdominal pain, anorexia, flatulence, dry mouth, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, transient elevation of ALT, AST, ALP, BUN or creatinine levels, hepatitis, jaundice, headache, dizziness, nervousness, insomnia, somnolence, malaise, fatigue, seizures, transient thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, neutropenia, and eosinophilia."
          },

            "title": "Drug Interactions",

False-positive results in Nitroprusside test, Coombs’ test, Clinitest, Benedict’s or Fehling’s soln."

  {

      "data": {
        "id": 1813,
        "brand_name": "Triplixam",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/y5GU3iM8m6YdUSSN3GrJg2DAjR1GGbi5yHvCouDpnmHnlgg0Dw.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wQo6OCC8LRLbkRD54amvfBNoRNuipVVliYmdHLA63Zhw8bLaqi.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/mQBqompsieDHz481NdShymeO2zuhu5jtBXCRdqojDBWHlE1Pl7.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Perindopril arginine, indapamide, amlodipine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Substitute therapy for essential hypertension in patients already controlled with perindopril/indapamide fixed-dose combination and amlodipine taken at the same dose level."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab/day, preferably in the morning before meals. If change of dosage is required, titration should be done with individual components."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe renal (CrCl < 30 mL/min) and hepatic impairment, history of ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema (Quincke’s edema), hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, significant bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, hepatic encephalopathy, hypokalemia, untreated decompensated heart failure, severe hypotension, shock including cardiogenic shock, obstruction of the outflow of left ventricle (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis), hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI, those receiving extracorporeal treatments leading to contact of blood with negatively charged surfaces, or on hemodialysis. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>); sacubitril/valsartan (therapy must not be initiated until after 36 hrs of last dose). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters) and lactation. <b>10 mg/2.5 mg/10 mg:</b> Patients with moderate renal impairment (CrCl < 60 mL/min)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not suitable for initial therapy. Patients with mild to moderate renal and hepatic impairment, heart failure, receiving desensitization treatment (e.g. hymenoptera venom), primary hyperaldosteronism, diabetes, hyperuricemia, HTN without pre-existing apparent renal lesions and for whom renal blood tests show functional renal insufficiency, risk of arterial hypotension and/or renal insufficiency, IHD; choroidal effusion with visual field defect, transient myopia, and acute angle-closure glaucoma.           {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension and/or stable coronary artery disease, in association with primary hypercholesterolemia or mixed hyperlipidemia, as substitution therapy in adults adequately controlled with atorvastatin, perindopril, and amlodipine given concurrently at the same dose level as in the combination."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab/day in the morning before meals. If change of dosage is required, titration should be done with individual components. <b>Patients with renal impairment (CrCl < 60 mL/min):</b> Titrate dose of components individually."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases >3x ULN, severe hypotension, shock including cardiogenic shock, obstruction of the outflow tract of left ventricle, hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI, history of ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema (Quincke’s edema), hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, significant bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, or those receiving extracorporeal treatments leading to contact of blood with negatively charged surfaces. Concomitant use with hepatitis C antivirals (e.g. glecaprevir, pibrentasvir); aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>); and sacubitril/valsartan. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not suitable for initial therapy. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, heart failure, substantial alcohol consumption and/or history of liver disease, hypothyroidism, personal or familial history of hereditary muscular disorders, history of muscular toxicity with a statin or fibrate, aortic or mitral valve stenosis, primary hyperaldosteronism, galactose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, total lactase deficiency, at high risk to develop DM, receiving desensitization treatment (e.g. hymenoptera venom), or those on hemodialysis. Perform liver function tests periodically. Recent kidney transplantation. Concomitant use with CYP3A4 inhibitors or transport proteins, gemfibrozil and other fibric acid derivatives, erythromycin, niacin, ezetimibe, fusidic acid (systemic), mTOR inhibitors, lithium, ARBs. LDL-apheresis with dextran. Cholestatic jaundice that may progress to fulminant hepatic necrosis and sometimes death; myalgia, myositis, and myopathy that may progress to rhabdomyolysis; ILD, DM, hypotension, hyperkalemia, neutropenia/agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, anemia. Non-productive, persistent cough. Discontinue treatment 1 day prior to surgery. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Black patients. Elderly >70 yrs. Childn and adolescents.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, hypersensitivity, hyperglycemia, headache, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, constipation, flatulence, dyspepsia, nausea, diarrhea, change of bowel habit, myalgia, arthralgia, extremity pain, muscle spasms, joint and ankle swelling, back pain, abnormal liver function test, increase blood creatinine kinase, somnolence, dizziness, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, edema, fatigue, paresthesia, visual impairment, diplopia, tinnitus, vertigo, hypotension, cough, dyspnea, vomiting, dysgeusia, rash, pruritus, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Immunosuppressants (e.g. ciclosporin, tacrolimus), antifungals, antibiotics, colchicine, lipid-regulating drugs (e.g. gemfibrozil, other fibrates, colestipol, ezetimibe), CCBs (e.g. diltiazem), antiarrhythmics (e.g. digoxin, verapamil, amiodarone), anti-HIV medicines (e.g. delavirdine, efavirenz, ritonavir, lopinavir, atazanavir, indinavir, darunavir, etc), warfarin, oral contraceptives, stiripentol, cimetidine, phenazone, antacids, St. John’s Wort, dantrolene (infusion), antihypertensives including aliskiren, ARBs (e.g. valsartan), potassium-sparing drugs (e.g. triamterene, amiloride, eplerenone, spironolactone), potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes. Grapefruit juice, grapefruit. Alcohol."

  {
    "id": 4275,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4275,
        "brand_name": "Trokendi XR",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9O4v0d1x74DfYZr6uI7LBaTmXLCrnUgfREGbLgVUNFHHDuASVy.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/n3vUHVscRECi4paz7dDGplHO1yfR0huEn991LhFfNgwOcTG6vi.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HP4mrLyQNVdZpH0D6yztHoZe3L3d5BRqdR1teGgu6ZC2geFnyZ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Topiramate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dioxolopyran"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Initial monotherapy for treatment of partial-onset or primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures in patients >6 yrs; adjunctive therapy for the treatment of partial-onset seizures, primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures and seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome in patients >6 yrs. Prophylaxis of migraine headache in patients >12 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy: Monotherapy - Adults and childn >10 yrs with partial onset or primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures:</b> 400 mg once daily, titrated according to the following schedule - Week 1: 50 mg once daily; week 2: 100 mg once daily; week 3: 150 mg once daily; week 4: 200 mg once daily; week 5: 300 mg once daily; week 6: 400 mg once daily. <b>Childn 6-9 yrs:</b> 25 mg/day, given at night, for the first week and can be increased to 50 mg/day based upon tolerability. Dose can be increased by 25-50 mg each week as tolerated. <b>Target total daily maintenance dosing for childn 6-9 yrs - BW up to 11 kg</b> - Minimum 150 mg/day; max: 250 mg/day, <b>12-22 kg</b> - minimum 200 mg/day; max 300, <b>23-31 kg</b> - minimum 200 mg/day; max 350, <b>32-38 kg</b> - minimum 250 mg/day; max 350 mg/day, <b>>38 kg</b> - minimum 250 mg/day; max 400 mg/day. <b>Adjunctive therapy - Adults &ge;17 yrs:</b> Initially 25-50 mg once daily followed by titration effective dose in increments of 25-50 mg every week. 200 mg-400 mg once daily for partial-onset seizures or Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and 400 mg once daily for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures. <b>Childn 6-16 yrs:</b> 5-9 mg/kg once daily. Begin titration at 25 mg once daily, given nightly for the first week. Then increase the dosage at 1- or 2-week intervals by increments of 1-3 mg/kg/day. Max 400 mg/day. <b>Migraine prophylaxis:</b> Initially 100 mg once daily, titrated to the following schedule - week 1: 25 mg/day; week 2: 50 mg/day; week 3: 75 mg/day; 100 mg/day. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl >70 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>):</b> Half of usual adult dose. Supplemental dose may be required for patients undergoing hemodialysis. Swallow cap whole and intact. Do not sprinkle on food, chew, or crush."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Recent alcohol use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid alcohol use 6 hrs before and after administration. Acute myopia and secondary angle closure glaucoma. Visual field defects. Oligohydrosis and hyperthermia. Concomitant use of drugs that predispose patients to heat-related disorders. Metabolic acidosis. Suicidal behavior and ideation. Cognitive-related dysfunction. Psychiatric/ behavioral disturbance. Somnolence fatigue. Hyperammonemia and encephalopathy. Gradually withdraw to minimize the potential for seizures or increased seizure frequency. Moderate to severe renal/hepatic impairment. Kidney stones. Hypothermia with concomitant valproic acid use. Patients undergoing hemodialysis. Elderly. Childn < 6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased risk of bleeding. <b>Adults:</b> Paresthesia, weight loss, anorexia; difficulty with memory, fatigue, asthenia, insomnia, somnolence; dizziness, speech disorders/related speech problems, nervousness, psychomotor slowing, abnormal vision; taste perversion, diarrhea, hypoesthesia, nausea. <b>Childn:</b> Fever, weight loss; difficulty with concentration/attention, flushing, confusion; fatigue somnolence; paresthesia, URTI, anorexia, abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol. Phenytoin, carbamazepine. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (zonisamide, acetazolamide). CNS depressants. Oral contraceptives. HCTZ. Pioglitazone. Lithium. Amitriptyline. Sumatriptan."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended release capsule 25 mg (P41.25)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Contraception. Treatment of menstrual disorders e.g. dysmenorrhea, premenstrual syndrome, and menorrhagia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Take 1 tab daily, beginning on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual bleeding or any day as long as not pregnant for 28 days. Start with the tab marked number '1' and follow the arrows indicated on the pack. The interval between 2 pills should be 24 hrs, should be taken at the same time everyday, preferably at the time of the evening meal. A pack is good for 28 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Liver disorders, clotting disorders, breast and cervical cancer, sickle-cell anemia, hormone-active tumors, hyperlipidemia, severe CV diseases, previous or existing thromboembolic diseases and idiopathic jaundice. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "DM, high BP, varicose veins, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, migraine, ophthalmological problems and tetany. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, gastric upsets, nausea, vomiting, change in appetite, breast tenderness, changes in body weight and libido, depressive moods or interference with liver functions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Analgesics, anti-migraine and tranquilizer. Ampicillin, chloramphenicol, neomycin, penicillin V, nitrofurantoin, sulfonamides, tetracycline and isoniazid. Clarithromycin, erythromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir, or grapefruit juice. Carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, felbamate, topiramate, phenytoin, griseofulvin, troglitazone, phenylbutazone, rifampicin and troleandomycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "<b>Each 21 ochreous tablet</b>: Ethinylestradiol 30 mcg, levonorgestrel 125 mcg; <b>Each 7 brown tablet</b>: Ferrous fumarate 75 mg (equiv to 24.75 mg elemental iron) x 28s."
          }

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduce the risk of myocardial infarction and stroke. Reduce the risk for revascularization procedures and angina in patients with type-2 diabetes, and without clinically evident CHD, but multiple risk factors for CHD (e.g. retinopathy, albuminuria, smoking, or HTN). Reduce risk of non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal stroke, angina. Adjunct therapy to diet or reducing elevated total-C, LDL-C, apo B and TG levels and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia, mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson type IIa and IIb), elevated serum triglyceride levels (Fredrickson type IV), primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson type III)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevation in hepatic transaminases. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe obstructive coronary artery disease; duration of angina or acute MI on starting CCB therapy. Patients with severe aortic stenosis. Severe hepatic impairment. Liver dysfunction. Patients who consumed substantial quantities of alcohol and have history of liver disease; with recent stroke or TIA. Concomitantly taken with ketoconazole, spironolactone, and cimetidine.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, flushing, headache, edema, palpitation, fatigue, abdominal pain, somnolence. Nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, pain in extremities, UTI, dyspepsia, nausea, muscle spasm, myalgia, insomnia, pharyngolaryngeal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors."
          },
          {

            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg/10 mg (P15.00), 5 mg/20 mg (P16.00), 10 mg/10 mg (P18.00)."

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antitussives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For relief of cough, clogged nose, postnasal drip, headache, body aches, and fever associated with common cold, allergic rhinitis, sinusitis, flu, and other minor respiratory tract infections. Management of congested sinus openings and passages."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs: 1 cap every 6 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe liver impairment and at risk of developing respiratory failure. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with HTN or severe heart disease, anemia, arrhythmia, toxic goiter, BPH, glaucoma, and kidney disease. Patients on warfarin therapy. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.",

            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, constipation, dizziness, drowsiness, excitation, mental confusion."

          },

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Telmisartan, amlodipine besilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension in patients already receiving same dose of individual components as separate tabs or whose BP is not adequately controlled on telmisartan or amlodipine monotherapy. Initial therapy in patients who are likely to need multiple drugs to achieve BP goals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily. <b>Initial therapy:</b> 40 mg/5 mg or 80 mg/5 mg. May increase up to max 80 mg/10 mg. <b>Replacement therapy for separate tabs:</b> 1 tab containing same component doses. <b>Patients treated with 10 mg amlodipine experiencing dose-limiting adverse reactions (e.g. edema):</b> 40 mg/5 mg. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Max 40 mg Telmisartan."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active components, excipients, and dihydropyridine. Biliary obstructive disorders. Severe hepatic impairment. Severe hypotension. Shock (e.g. cardiogenic shock). Obstruction of the outflow tract of the left ventricle (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis). Hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI. Concomitant use of aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60  mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with vol and/or sodium depletion; hepatic insufficiency; renal impairment, kidney transplant; bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney; whose vascular tone and renal function depend largely on RAAS; suffering from aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; unstable angina and during or within 1 month of MI; heart failure; DM and coexistent CAD. May induce hyperkalemia, renovascular HTN, acute/symptomatic/severe hypotension, changes in renal function, hyperazotemia, oliguria; risk of fatal MI and unexpected CV death in concomitant use with ARBs or ACE inhibitors; MI or stroke in excessive BP reduction in patients with ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic CV disease. Not recommended in patients with primary aldosteronism; dual blockade of RAAS; hereditary fructose intolerance. Black hypertensive people. Monitor BP, serum creatinine, and potassium. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs. Women planning pregnancy. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "UTI, cystitis, depression, anxiety, confusional state, insomnia, altered mood, insomnia, syncope, somnolence, dizziness, migraine, headache, peripheral neuropathy, paresthesia, hypoesthesia, dysgeusia, tremor, vertigo, tinnitus, visual impairment, diplopia, MI, ventricular tachycardia, arrhythmia,  atrial fibrillation, bradycardia, tachycardia, palpitations, hypotension, orthostatic hypotension, flushing,  vasculitis, dyspnea, cough, rhinitis, GI disorders, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, renal and urinary, reproductive system and breast, general disorders and administration site conditions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other antihypertensives, baclofen, amifostine; alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, antidepressants. Corticosteroids (systemic); digoxin, lithium, NSAIDs; grapefruit and grapefruit juice; CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g protease inhibitors, azole antifungals, erythromycin, clarithromycin, verapamil, diltiazem; inducers (e.g. rifampicin, <i>Hypericum perforatum</i>); dantrolene; tacrolimus; ciclosporin; simvastatin; MTOR inhibitors  (e.g. sirolimus, temsirolimus, everolimus); potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 40 mg/5 mg (P18.66), 40 mg/10 mg (P18.66), 80 mg/5 mg (P26.64), 80 mg/10 mg (P26.64)."
          }

  {
    "id": 3927,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3927,
        "brand_name": "Tykinib",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TVsDIpVGgnbBJOLHlKdoLSpo64JeaN1RRderD7dFC1ECtelMRj.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ItZjBrYkPZfbOxZRgL7IPg40i8fwfprBZ9jnSALj2tZFt6wqCT.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/AwcBPhOYBwdULA1WfzXN0s8cbnXLmsSGR0jcO7wkYWB5XmG0sX.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Imatinib mesilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Protein Kinase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn</b>: Treatment of newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome (bcr-abl) positive (Ph+) chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) for whom bone marrow transplantation is not considered as the 1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment; Ph+ CML in chronic phase after failure of interferon-alpha therapy, or in accelerated phase or blast crisis; newly diagnosed Philadelphia chromosome positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia (Ph+ ALL) integrated with chemotherapy. <b>Adults</b>: Treatment of relapsed or refractory Ph+ ALL as monotherapy; myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative diseases (MDS/MPD) associated with platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) gene re-arrangements; advanced hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) and/or chronic eosinophilic leukemia (CEL) with FIP1L1-PDGFR-alpha rearrangement; unresectable dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans (DFSP) and with recurrent and/or metastatic DFSP who are not eligible for surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – CML</b> - Chronic phase: 400 mg/day, may be increased to 600 or 800 mg/day; Accelerated phase or blast crisis: 600 mg/day, may be increased to max 800 mg (400 mg twice daily); <b>Ph+ ALL</b>: 600 mg/day; <b>MDS/MPD</b>: 400 mg/day; <b>HES/CEL</b>: 100 mg/day, may be increased to 400 mg; <b>DFSP</b>: 800 mg/day. <b>Childn – CML</b> - Chronic and advanced phase: 340 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once daily or may be divided into two doses (one in the morning and one in the evening), may be increased to 570 mg/m<sup>2</sup> daily. Max 800 mg; <b>Ph+ ALL</b>: 340 mg/m<sup>2</sup> daily. Max 600 mg. <b>Hepatic impairment</b>: 400 mg/day, may be reduced if not tolerated. <b>Renal impairment</b>: Initially 400 mg/day, may be reduced if not tolerated or increased for lack of efficacy. For patients unable to swallow tabs, tabs may be dispersed in sufficient vol of water or apple juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic dysfunction, cardiac dysfunction or disease, risks for cardiac failure, history of renal failure. Thyroidectomy patients on levothyroxine replacement therapy. May induce hypothyroidism, liver injury, severe fluid retention, GI and intra-tumoral hemorrhages in patients with GIST, gastric antral vascular ectasia, TLS, reactivation of HBV in chronic carriers. Concomitant use with protease inhibitors, azole antifungals, certain macrolides, CYP3A4 substrates with a narrow therapeutic window (e.g. cyclosporine, pimozide, tacrolimus, sirolimus, ergotamine, diergotamine, fentanyl, alfentanil, terfenadine, bortezomib, docetaxel, quinidine) or warfarin, other coumarin derivatives, CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. dexamethasone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenobarbital, St. John’s wort). Perform ECG and determine serum troponin in patients with HES/CEL and MDS/MPD before treatment. Correct clinically significant dehydration and treat high uric acid levels prior to treatment. Avoid exposure to direct sunlight. Discontinue if thrombotic microangiopathy develops. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>CML</b>: Childn &lt;2 yrs. <b>Ph+ ALL</b>: Childn &lt;1 yrs. <b>MDS/MPD, DFSP, HES/CEL</b>: Childn &lt;18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, headache, nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, periorbital edema, dermatitis/eczema/rash, muscle spasm and cramps, musculoskeletal pain (e.g. myalgia, arthralgia, bone pain), fluid retention and edema, fatigue, increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (protease inhibitors e.g. indinavir, lopinavir/ritonavir, ritonavir, saquinavir, telaprevir, nelfinavir, boceprevir; azole antifungals e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole, voriconazole; macrolides e.g. erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin) and inducers (e.g. dexamethasone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, phenobarbital, fosphenytoin, primidone, St. John’s wort). Ciclosporin, pimozide, tacrolimus, sirolimus, ergotamine, diergotamine, fentanyl, alfentanil, terfenadine, bortezomib, docetaxel, quinidine. Triazolo-benzodiazepines, dihydropyridine CCBs, statins. Metoprolol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 100 mg (P97.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ursodeoxycholic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of primary biliary cirrhosis without decompensated hepatic cirrhosis. Dissolution of cholesterol gallstones in gallbladder. Hepatobiliary disorders associated with cystic fibrosis in childn 6-18 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary biliary cirrhosis:</b> 14 ± 2 mg/kg/day (1&frac12;–3&frac12; tablets daily). Divide daily dose into 2-3 doses for the first 3 months. May be taken once daily in the evening once liver values improve. <b>Dissolution of cholesterol gallstones:</b> Taken in the evening at bedtime. <b>>100 kg:</b> 2&frac12; tabs; <b>81-100 kg:</b> 2 tabs; <b>61-80 kg:</b> 1&frac12; tab; <b>&le;60 kg:</b> 1 tab. <b>Hepatobiliary disorders associated with cystic fibrosis in childn 6-18 yrs:</b> 20 mg/kg/day in 2-3 divided doses, may be increased to 30 mg/kg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute inflammation of gallbladder or biliary tract. Occlusion of common bile duct or cystic duct. Frequent episodes of biliary colic. Radio-opaque calcified gallstones. Impaired contractility of gallbladder. Unsuccessful portoenterostomy or without recovery of good bile flow in childn with biliary atresia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor hepatic function parameters during first 3 months of treatment every 4 weeks and every 3 months thereafter. Decompensation of hepatic cirrhosis; worsening of clinical symptoms at the beginning of treatment (e.g., increased itching). Discontinue if persistent diarrhea occurs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pasty stools, diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Colestyramine, colestipol, antacids containing aluminum hydroxide and aluminum oxide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P74.00)."
          }
        ],
