        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ursodeoxycholic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the dissolution of cholesterol-rich gallstones in patients with functioning gallbladders. Primary biliary cirrhosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 300 mg thrice daily with meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Complete obstruction of biliary tract, fulminant hepatitis, radiopaque cholelithiasis, non-functioning gallbladder or acute cholecystitis, renal disease, gastric ulcers, colitis or enteritis e.g. Crohn’s disease. PUD, IBD. Childn. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Jaundice, hepatic cirrhosis. Severe pancreatic disease, choledocholithiasis, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, ascites. Regularly monitor liver enzymes. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, abdominal pain, heartburn, epigastric discomfort, hypersensitivity, intestinal pneumonia, fever, cough, dyspnea, general malaise, dizziness, calcification of cholelithiasis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Tolbutamide, cholestyramine, colestipol, charcoal, aluminum hydroxide and magnesium-based antacid, oral contraceptives containing estrogen, clofibrate. Hepatotoxic drugs."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",

      "data": {
        "id": 5053,
        "brand_name": "Udcapro",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ursodeoxycholic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Dissolution of cholesterol-rich gallstones in the gallbladder. Biliary reflux gastritis. Cholestatic liver diseases (e.g., PBC)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>300 mg - Dissolution of cholesterol gallstones:</b> Taken once daily. >100 kg BW: 5 caps; 81-100 kg: 4 caps; 61-80 kg: 3 caps; &le;60 kg: 2 caps. <b>Biliary reflux gastritis:</b> 1 cap daily. Treatment duration: 10-14 days. <b>Symptomatic treatment of PBC - 300 mg:</b> >110 kg: 2 tabs AM, noon, and PM; 86-110 kg: 1 tab AM; 2 tabs noon and PM; 66-85 kg: 1 tab AM and noon, 2 tabs PM; 51-65 kg: 1 tab AM, noon, and PM; 34-50 kg: 1 tab AM and PM. <b>500 mg:</b> 13-15 mg/kg/day in two to four divided doses with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy. <b>300 mg:</b> Acute inflammation of gallbladder and bile ducts. Biliary tract obstruction (common bile duct or gallbladder). Inflammatory disorders of the small and large intestines. Patients with a non-visualized or non-functioning gallbladder, calcified (radio-opaque) stones, impaired gallbladder contractility, frequent biliary colic, chronic liver disease, severe renal impairment, or PUD. <b>500 mg:</b> Complete biliary obstruction of extrahepatic origin. Widespread intrahepatic obstruction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated for treatment of decompensated cirrhosis. Patients with partial biliary obstruction of extrahepatic origin. Maintain bile flow during therapy. Discontinue treatment if gallstones have not reduced in size after 12 months. Monitor liver function (gamma-GT, alkaline phosphatase, AST, ALT) and bilirubin levels every month for three months after start of therapy and every six months thereafter. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Calcification of gallstones. Pasty stools/diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>300 mg:</b> Cholestyramine, colestipol, aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids, clofibrate, oral contraceptives (estrogen), activated charcoal. <b>500 mg:</b> Ciclosporin, ciprofloxacin, nitrendipine, dapsone, rosuvastatin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 300 mg. Film-coated tablet 500 mg."
          }
        ],

      "data": {
        "id": 216,
        "brand_name": "Ultraxime",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/bV8zzqo8Gd2c7vowg0qprmhCL5w9jF5fY55WxvZvFbyQp4SaTO.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HHUUtQSh958kdnUFZC7GztELXDrPQ6m18k5fDPmWIg9U33Th2G.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/uFm3uOQa2dBP82VXaZ7cZq2mHXWWogdKQHDemHWnPatWPL38zK.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefixime",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Third Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute bronchitis, acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, bronchiectasis with infection, secondary infections in chronic respiratory tract diseases, pneumonia, urinary tract infections (e.g. pyelonephritis, cystitis, cystourethritis), uncomplicated cervical/urethral gonorrhea, cholecystitis, cholangitis, scarlet fever, sinusitis, tonsilitis, pharyngitis, otitis media, and typhoid/enteric fever including multidrug-resistant typhoid fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Usual dose in childn:</b> Total daily dose of 8 mg/kg. <b>Susp -</b> Adults and childn >12 yrs or >50 kg: 20 mL; Childn 7-12 yrs: 10-15 mL; 3-6 yrs: 5-10 mL; 1-2 yrs: 5 mL. All doses taken once daily or in 2 divided doses every 12 hrs. <b>Oral drops -</b> Childn 1-2 yrs: 5 mL; Infants 6-11 months: 2.5-5 mL. <b>Usual treatment duration -</b> Most infections: 7-14 days; <i>Streptococcus pyogenes</i> infections: At least 10 days. <b>Typhoid fever:</b> 15-20 mg/kg. Max 400 mg/day. Shake well before use. <b>Adults with renal impairment -</b> CrCl 20-40 mL/min: 75% of the standard dosage (i.e. 300 mg/day); < 20 mL/min: 50% of the standard dosage (i.e. 200 mg/day)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Penicillin-sensitive patients; possible cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics. History of colitis and cephalosporin-associated hemolytic anemia. Fall in prothrombin activity in patients with kidney/liver impairment, poor nutritional state, receiving protracted course of antimicrobial therapy, or previously stabilized on anticoagulant therapy. Patients with renal impairment. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms during prolonged therapy. Childn < 6 months. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Severe cutaneous adverse reactions, CDAD, acute renal failure, hyperbilirubinemia. GI, dermatologic, hepatic, renal/genitourinary, nervous system, and hematologic reactions. Increased serum amylase concentration, dyspnea, respiratory distress."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbamazepine, chloramphenicol, nifedipine, probenecid, salicylates, warfarin and other anticoagulants. False positive in nitroprusside test, Coombs’ test, Clintest, Benedict’s, and Fehling’s soln."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Granules for suspension 100 mg/5 mL x 30 mL (P706.00), 60 mL (P999.00). Granules for suspension (oral drops) 20 mg/mL x 10 mL (P296.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For relief from pain or abdominal cramps e.g. menstrual cramps and urinary tract spasm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 1-2 tabs 3x daily. Max 6 tabs/day. Tabs should be swallowed whole with a sufficient amount of water."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Nephropathy associated with excessive use of analgesics. Severe liver impairment. Glaucoma. Myasthenia gravis. Bowel blockade (paralytic or obstructive ileus), megacolon. Childn &lt;10 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "G6PD deficiency, hepatic or renal dysfunction. Gilbert’s syndrome. Patients prone to narrow-angle glaucoma, intestinal or urinary outlet obstruction, or tachyarrhythmia. Patients &gt;40 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

  {
    "id": 1022,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1022,
        "brand_name": "Ural",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sodium bicarbonate, sodium citrate, citric acid, tartaric acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Urinary Alkalinizers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Urinary alkalinizer:</b> As supportive therapy for urinary tract infection to relieve symptoms of painful urination and improve the action of certain antibiotics (e.g. some sulfonamides). As anti-urolithic to reduce and prevent crystallization of calcium oxalate and cysteine. For the treatment and prevention of uric acid stones (in certain conditions e.g. gout). <b>Gastric alkalinizer:</b> For symptomatic treatment of gastric hyperacidity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 4-8 g (1-2 sachets) dissolved in half glass of cold water, given 3-4x daily or as prescribed. <b>Childn 6-12 yrs:</b> 4 g (1 sachet), given 2-3x daily. Taken on empty stomach. Additional water (approx &frac12; glass) should be subsequently ingested."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Renal failure or hypernatremia, overt and occult cardiac failure; concomitant use with quinolone antibiotics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Low sodium diet. Patients with cardiac failure, HTN, impaired renal function, peripheral and pulmonary edema, pre-eclampsia. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Systemic alkalosis or hypernatremia. Mild laxative effect."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Chlorpropamide, lithium, salicylates, tetracyclines, amphetamines, ephedrine or pseudoephedrine, antacids, quinolones, laxatives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Effervescent granules 1.76 g/630 mg/720 mg/890 mg per 4 g sachet (P29.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 10,
          "name": "Abbott Laboratories"
        },

  {
    "id": 4810,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4810,
        "brand_name": "Urania",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DSC9SVSVQ4mFcgvDuu0VLMrA7GgejGaAZ1rMB29jG0CooL182m.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Cu8ru2XrcK8tCzg5pcAm1cFMIMDDojuCGc2nbneZ3bMsX0jIQb.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OMkInB2XiNOpXUWya1jCxzbf75kpnBieMVKIUWbgVLS4tqk8TG.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), with &ge;1 risk factor such as prior stroke or transient ischemic attack, &ge;75 yrs, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class &ge;II). Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily. In patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: age &ge;80 yrs, BW &le;60 kg, or serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL (133 &#181;mol/L): 2.5 mg twice daily  <b>Treatment of acute DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for the first 7 days followed by 5 mg twice daily. Max 20 mg for the first 7 days; 10 mg thereafter. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT/or PE:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily should be initiated following the treatment completion of 6 months. Max 5 mg twice daily. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active clinically significant bleeding. Hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk. Lesion or condition considered at significant risk for major bleeding. Concomitant treatment any other anticoagulant agents e.g., unfractionated heparin (UFH), low molecular weight heparins, heparin derivatives, oral anticoagulants except under specific circumstances of switching anticoagulant therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hemorrhage risk. Surgery and invasive procedures. Patients with prosthetic heart valves, active cancer, renal and hepatic impairment. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, thrombocytopenia, hemorrhage (including GI, mouth, and eye), hematoma, hypotension, epistaxis, nausea."

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 40 mg once daily, may be increased to 80 mg in patients who do not achieve serum uric acid of < 6 mg/dL after 2 weeks of therapy with 40 mg. May be taken without regard to food or antacid use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients whose rate of urate formation is greatly increased (e.g. malignant disease and its treatment, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome). Concurrent treatment with azathioprine, mercaptopurine, or theophylline."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Gout flares, CV thromboembolic events, liver enzyme elevations. Patients with severe renal and hepatic impairment. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

            "content": "Drugs for Urinary Frequency and Incontinence"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of overactive bladder symptoms e.g. urinary urgency and frequency, urge urinary incontinence."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab twice daily after breakfast and dinner. Dose may be increased to 2 tabs twice daily if insufficient efficacy. <b>Severe hepatic and renal impairment</b>: 1 tab twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Urinary retention; occluded pyloric region, duodenum, intestine, or paralytic ileus; decreased GI motility; angle closure glaucoma; myasthenia gravis; severe heart disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with dysuria, arrhythmia, hepatic and renal dysfunction, dementia or cognitive dysfunction, Parkinsonian symptoms or cerebrovascular disorder, ulcerative colitis, and hyperthyroidism; lower urinary tract obstructive disease.           },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thirst, dry mouth, constipation; QT prolongation, ventricular tachycardia; GI disturbances; pharyngolaryngeal pain, cough, dry throat, hoarseness; hematologic effects; photophobia, blurred vision, abnormal sensation in eye, xeropthalmia, asthenopia, eyelid edema, diplopia; increased liver enzymes, bilirubin, creatinine, triglycerides, LDH, cholesterol; malaise, weakness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Itraconazole, erythromycin, and clarithromycin; anticholinergic and antihistaminic agents, TCAs, phenothiazines, MAOIs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 100 mcg (P39.75)."
          }

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Patients with radiolucent, non-calcified gallbladder stones &lt;20 mm in greatest diameter in whom elective cholecystectomy would be undertaken, except for the presence of increased surgical risk due to systemic disease, advanced age, idiosyncratic reaction to general anesthesia, or for patients who refuse surgery. Prevention of gallstone formation in obese experiencing rapid weight loss."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly: </b> 10-15 mg/kg/day in 2-4 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with calcified and pigment gallstones, radio-opaque gallstones, non-functioning gallbladders, chronic liver disease and PUD, inflammatory disease of colon and small intestine. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver function parameters every 4 weeks during the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months, then every 3 months thereafter. Patients with primary biliary cirrhosis. Do not use if gallbladder cannot be visualized on x-ray images or in cases of calcified gallstones, impaired contractility of gallbladder or frequent episodes of biliary colic. Women of childbearing potential should be treated only if they use reliable (non-hormonal) contraception.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pasty stools or diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cholestyramine, charcoal, aluminum-based antacids, estrogens, clofibrate, ciclosporin, dapsone, ciprofloxacin, nitrendipine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 300 mg (P57.00)."
          }

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Dissolution of cholesterol-rich gallstones in the gallbladder, biliary reflux gastritis and cholestatic liver diseases."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cap</b> - Approx 10 mg/kg BW - <b>BW &gt;100 kg</b>: 5 caps; <b>up to 100 kg</b>: 4 caps; <b>up to 80 kg</b>: 3 caps; <b>up to 60 kg</b>: 2 caps. <b>Biliary reflux gastritis</b>: 1 cap daily at bedtime for 10-14 days. <b>Childn 6-18 yrs - Cystic fibrosis</b>: 20 mg/kg/day in 2-3 divided doses, may increase to 30 mg/kg/day. <b>FC tab</b> - Approx 10 mg/kg BW - <b>BW &gt;100 kg</b>: 2&frac12; tabs; <b>81-100 kg</b>: 2 tabs; <b>61-80 kg</b>: 1&frac12; tab; <b>up to 60 kg</b>: 1 tab. <b>Symptomatic treatment of primary biliary cirrhosis</b>: Daily dose depends on BW and ranges from 1&frac12; to 3&frac12; tabs (14 &plusmn; 2 mg/kg BW). For first 3 months of treatment, 500 mg should be taken, divided over the day. When the liver function parameters improve, daily dose may be taken once daily in the evening."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute inflammation of the gallbladder and bile ducts, obstruction of the biliary tract, inflammatory disorders of the large and small intestine. Should not be taken where the gallbladder cannot be visualized at X-ray, by patients with calcified gallstones disturbed contractility of the gallbladder or frequent biliary colic. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Calcification of gallstones, stool may become doughy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cholestyramine, colestipol, aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 250 mg (P50.00). Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P103.50)."
          }

  {
    "id": 1416,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1416,
        "brand_name": "Utrogestan",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XvGnwOwz0c9MIU1EpW6nfY9uyx7HLFAE5LRd15mzOQsX1bfg7e.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/vadNMU9KMLIGkeNFnxQhNgJnnLKe78wAlPg4I7nG0Wb7vyKbh3.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/BQ6y8S8AtPBdWJ4yESEHMgJw56mTKtyj2sA02fJNC2Duaxc5Dp.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Progesterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Menace of abortion or prevention or recurrent spontaneous abortions due to diagnosed luteal phase defect; preterm delivery. <b>Oral cap:</b> Treatment of disorders associated with progesterone deficit e.g. pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), menstrual irregularity, benign breast disease, pre-menopause; infertility caused by luteal phase defect. Adjunct to estrogen therapy in the treatment of menopause. <b>Vaginal cap:</b> During In Vitro Fertilization (IVF) cycles."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Threatened abortion or prevention of LPD-related recurrent spontaneous abortions:</b> 200-400 mg in 2 divided doses, taken up until gestation week 12. <b>Oral cap -</b> usually 200-300 mg daily as a single or in 2 doses (i.e. 200 mg in the evening at bedtime and 100 mg in the morning, if needed). <b>Luteal phase defect (PMS, menstrual irregularity, pre-menopause, benign breast disease):</b> Administered for 10 days/menstrual cycle, usually from cycle days 17-26. <b>Menopause (as adjunct to estrogen):</b> Given during last 2 weeks of the treatment sequence, followed by 1-week suspension of all HRT. <b>Threatened pre-term delivery:</b> 400 mg every 6-8 hrs, followed by a maintenance dose (e.g. 3 x 200 mg/day) taken up until gestation week 36. <b>Vaginal cap -</b> usually 200 mg daily as a single dose or in 2 divided doses, taken in the morning and evening. To be inserted deep into vagina with or without applicator. <b>Partial luteal phase defect (dysovulation, irregular menstrual cycles):</b> 200 mg for 10 days/menstrual cycle, usually from cycle days 17-26. <b>Infertility associated with total luteal phase defect (oocyte donation):</b> Initially 100 mg on days 13-14 of the transfer cycle, then 100 mg in the morning and evening on cycle days 15-25. From cycle day 26, in the event of conception, increase dose in weekly increments of 100 mg/day up to max 600 mg given in 3 divided doses. Dose is maintained up until day 60. <b>Luteal phase supplementation during IVF:</b> Initiate treatment in the evening of the transfer at a rate of 600 mg given in 3 divided doses (morning, noon, evening). <b>Threatened pre-term delivery:</b> 200-300 mg 2-3x a day for 3 days, followed by a maintenance dose of 100-200 mg/day until suppression of contraction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe changes in hepatic function."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not a contraceptive. Shortened menstrual cycle and/or bleeding may occur if treatment is initiated too early, i.e. before cycle day 15. Patients with uterine bleeding, history of thrombophlebitis. Suspend treatment if eye disorder (e.g. vision loss, diplopia, vascular lesions of the retina), VTE or thrombotic events regardless of territory, or severe headache develops. Administration of progesterone during HRT involving estrogens over a minimum of 12 days/cycle is strongly recommended in non-hysterectomized women. May cause a reduction in glucose tolerance, which increases the need for insulin and other antidiabetics in diabetic patients. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Lactation. <b>Vaginal cap:</b> Contains soya lecithin.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Altered menstrual cycles, amenorrhea, intermenstrual bleeding, headache. <b>Vaginal cap:</b> Local irritation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Barbiturates, antiepileptics (e.g. phenytoin), rifampicin, phenylbutazone, spironolactone, griseofulvin; antibiotics (e.g. ampicillin, tetracycline)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral softgel capsule 100 mg (P38.00), 200 mg (P73.75). Vaginal softgel capsule 200 mg (P73.75)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        "content": "Estradiol hemihydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of atrophic vaginitis due to menopause."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially, 1 vaginal tab daily for 2 weeks then 2 vaginal tab twice weekly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Known or history of breast cancer, estrogen-dependent malignant tumors (e.g. endometrial cancer); undiagnosed genital bleeding, untreated endometrial hyperplasia. Previous or current VTE (DVT, PE); known thrombophilic disorders (e.g. protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency); active or recent arterial thromboembolic disease (e.g. angina, MI). Acute or history of liver disease. Porphyria. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Periodic check-ups are recommended during treatment. Breast and ovarian cancer. Conditions that may recur or be aggravated during treatment: leiomyoma (uterine fibroids) or endometriosis; risk factors thromboembolic disorders, estrogen-dependent tumors; HTN, liver disorders, DM, cholelithiasis, migraine or severe headache, history of endometrial hyperplasia, epilepsy, asthma, otosclerosis. Discontinue if jaundice or deterioration in liver function, significant increase in BP, new onset of migraine-type headache occurs. Patients with cardiac or renal impairment. Women who have risk factors for VTE; undergone hysterectomy because of endometriosis.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, abdominal pain, vaginal hemorrhage or discomfort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of hypertension (HTN) and heart failure. Reduction of cardiovascular mortality in patients with left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction (MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b> - Adults: Initially, 80 mg once daily; may be increased to 160 mg/day. Max 320 mg/day. Childn 6-16 yrs: 1.3 mg/kg once daily. Max 40 mg/day. <b>Heart failure</b>: Initially 40 mg twice daily, may be increased to 80 mg and 160 mg twice daily as tolerated. <b>Post-MI</b>: Start 12 hrs after the infarction in clinically stable patients with an initial dose of 20 mg twice daily, may be uptitrated within 7 days to 40 mg twice daily and subsequently to 160 mg twice daily as tolerated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and cholestasis. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with vol and salt depletion receiving high doses of diuretics, heart failure, history of MI, impaired hepatic and renal function. May cause hypotension. Childn and neonates. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypotension, headache, dizziness, flu symptoms, tiredness, abdominal pain, diarrhea, joint and back pain, elevated blood potassium, cough and blood creatinine (decreased kidney function), rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Atenolol, OATP1B1 inhibitors (e.g. rifampin, cyclosporin), MRP2 inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir), potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, or salt substitutes containing potassium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 40 mg (P16.00), 80 mg (P23.57), 160 mg (P35.36)."
          }

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the secondary prevention of atherothrombotic events, non-ST segment elevation acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina or non-Q-wave myocardial infarction) including patients undergoing a stent placement following percutaneous coronary intervention."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 cap once daily."
          },

          },

          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs. <b>Clopidogrel:</b> Heparin, warfarin. <b>Aspirin:</b> Corticosteroids, carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, antacids and adsorbents, mifepristone, antimetabolites, alcohol, antiemetics, ACE inhibitors."

            "content": "Melatonergic Agonist"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of major depressive episodes (MDE) and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "25 mg/day at bedtime for at least 6 months, may be increased to 50 mg/day if there is no improvement of symptoms 2 weeks after initial treatment in MDE and 4 weeks in GAD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic impairment (i.e. cirrhosis or active liver disease) or transaminases exceeding 3x ULN. Concomitant use with potent CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform liver function tests prior treatment. Do not initiate treatment if transaminases exceed 3x ULN. Monitor transaminases periodically after around 3 weeks, 6 weeks (end of acute phase), 12 weeks, and 24 weeks (end of maintenance phase), and thereafter. Patients with moderate or severe renal impairment, hepatic injury risk factors (e.g. obesity/overweight, NAFLD, diabetes, alcohol use disorder, and/or substantial alcohol intake), ALT and/or AST values of >3x ULN, pretreatment elevated transaminases (>ULN and &le;3x ULN); history of bipolar disorder, mania, or hypomania; history of suicide-related events; galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption. Concomitant use with moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors (e.g. propranolol, enoxacin). Increased risk of suicidal thoughts, self-harm, and suicide. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly &ge;75 yrs and with dementia. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache. Anxiety; dizziness, somnolence, insomnia; nausea, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, vomiting; increased ALT and/or AST; back pain; fatigue; weight gain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP1A2 and CYP2C9 inducers (e.g. rifampicin) or inhibitors (e.g. fluvoxamine, ciprofloxacin, estrogen; alcohol."

  {
    "id": 4761,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4761,
        "brand_name": "Valheart",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ivabradine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channel blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in coronary artery disease adults with normal sinus rhythm and HR &ge;70bpmin adults unable to tolerate or with a contraindication to the use of beta-blockers or in combination with beta-blockers in patients inadequately controlled with an optimal beta-blocker dose. Treatment of stable chronic heart failure NYHA II to IV class with systolic dysfunction, in adult patients who are in sinus rhythm with HR &ge;75 bpm, in combination with standard therapy including beta-blocker therapy or when beta-blocker therapy is contraindicated or not tolerated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Chronic stable angina - Adults < 75 yrs:</b> Initially, 5 mg twice daily. If tolerated and resting HR remains >60 bpm dose may increase to the next higher dose in patients receiving 2.5 mg or 5 mg twice daily. Maintenance: Max 7.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if no improvement of symptoms after 3 months. If HR decreases < 50 bpm at rest, titrate the dose downward including the lowest dose of 2.5 mg twice daily. Discontinue if HR remains < 50 bpm. <b>CHF:</b> Initially 5 mg twice daily. If resting heart rate >60 bpm: increase dose by 2.5 mg twice daily with max 7.5 mg twice daily. If HR is 50-60 bpm: Maintain dose. If heart rate is < 50 bpm: decrease dose by 2.5 mg twice daily or discontinue if current dose is 2.5 mg. <b>Elderly >75 yrs:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily initially."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Resting heart rate < 70 bpm prior to treatment, cardiogenic shock, acute MI, severe hypotension (< 90/50 mmHg), severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C), sick sinus syndrome, SA block, unstable or acute heart failure, pacemaker dependent, unstable angina, 3rd-degree AV block. Patients with existing prolonged QT interval. Concomitant use with verapamil or diltiazem and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors and nefazodone. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor HR and ECG. Patients with 2nd-degree AV-block, CHF, atrial fibrillation or other cardiac arrhythmias that interfere with sinus node function. Not recommended immediately after a stroke. Moderate hepatic impairment, severe renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min). Retinitis pigmentosa. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Luminous phenomena (phosphenes) and bradycardia. Eosinophilia. Hyperuricemia, hypokalemia; Headache, dizziness, vertigo, tinnitus, dyspnea; Eye, cardiac, vascular, skin, and GI disorders; arthralgia, muscle cramps; asthenia, fatigue, malaise."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. azole antifungals, macrolide antibiotics, HIV protease inhibitors) and nefazodone. Moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. diltiazem or verapamil). CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. St. John’s Wort, rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin). QT-prolonging medications (e.g. quinidine, disopyramide, bepridil, sotalol, ibutilide, amiodarone); pimozide, ziprasidone, sertindole, mefloquine, halofantrine, pentamidine, cisapride, erythromycin IV. Digoxin, beta-blockers. Furosemide, HCTZ, indapamide. Omeprazole, lansoprazole. Sildenafil. HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (e.g. simvastatin); dihydropyridine CCBs (e.g. amlodipine, lacidipine); aspirin, warfarin. Grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg (P23.58), 7.5 mg (P24.53)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dZiW1pVAhe015WwXTJ044eAzXVQndFIhnjrIEc7dp2Nx1MxQJT.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ShDPBGGNU17RqTYDPWuG0g6HAtA77nucnT6Cd1f7DRc1thrE1w.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Diazepam",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anxiolytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx, Exempt Dangerous Drug"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b>: Symptomatic relief of anxiety, tension, and other somatic or psychological complaints associated with anxiety syndrome. Adjunct in treatment of anxiety or excitation associated with psychiatric disorders, and relief of muscle spasm due to local trauma (injury, inflammation). <b>IM/IV</b>: Management of conscious sedation. Premedication and induction of anesthesia. Treatment of excitation states associated with psychiatric disorders e.g. acute anxiety and panic, motor unrest and delirium tremens; status epilepticus and other convulsive states. 2<sup>nd</sup>-line treatment of eclampsia. Adjunct in the relief of reflex muscle spasm (including tetanus) due to local trauma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – Adults</b>: Initially 5-10 mg daily. Max 10 mg once daily. Tabs may be divided into equal halves to facilitate dosing. <b>IM/IV</b>: Individualized dosage. <b>Adults and adolescents</b>: 2-20 mg IM/IV. If IV, should be administered slowly approx. 0.5-1 mL/min. <b>Anesthesia - Premedication anesthesia</b>: 10-20 mg IM. 0.1-0.2 mg/kg BW in childn. Administer 1 hr before induction of anesthesia. <b>Induction of anesthesia</b>: 0.2-0.5 mg/kg BW IV. <b>Conscious sedation</b>: 10-20 mg IV and 30 mg IV for heavy patients; 0.1-0.2 mg/kg BW in childn. <b>Eclampsia – For actual or threatened convulsions where magnesium sulfate is unavailable</b>: 10-20 mg IV; additional doses either IV or by continuous infusion (up to 100 mg in 24 hrs). <b>If seizure continue despite administration of magnesium sulfate</b>: 5-10 mg IV. <b>Tetanus</b>: 0.1-0.3 mg/kg BW given IV in intervals at 1-4 hrs or 3-4 mg/kg BW in 24 hrs or by continuous infusion or gastric tube. <b>Status epilepticus</b>: 0.15-0.25 mg/kg BW IV repeated as necessary after 10-15 mins. Max: 3 mg/kg BW in 24 hrs. <b>Excitation states associated with psychiatric disorders</b>: Initially 0.1-0.2 mg/kg BW IV repeated at 8-hrly intervals until acute symptoms subsides then continue with oral treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. <b>Tab</b>: Patients with severe respiratory insufficiency, severe hepatic impairment, sleep apnea syndrome, myasthenia gravis. Not for primary treatment of psychotic illness. Not be used alone in treating depression or anxiety with depression. <b>IM/IV</b>: Use of PVC-containing bags and infusion set."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Respiratory insufficiency. Mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Concomitant use of alcohol or CNS depressants. History of alcohol or drug abuse. Adverse behavioral effects and anterograde amnesia may occur. Tolerance, dependence. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Childn &lt;6 months. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Tab</b>: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. <b>IM/IV</b>: Patients with myasthenia gravis; limited pulmonary reserve, sleep apnea. Contains benzyl alcohol.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fatigue, drowsiness, muscle weakness. <b>IM/IV</b>: Injection site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors and inducers. Grapefruit juice, omeprazole, esomeprazole, disulfiram, INH, diltiazem, idelalisib, modafinil, armodafinil. Alcohol, olanzapine, methadone, levodopa, theophylline and caffeine, ketamine. Rifampicin, carbamazepine. <b>Tab</b>: Food and antacids, prokinetic drugs, metoclopramide IV, narcotics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 5 mg, 10 mg. Solution for injection (IV/IM) 5 mg/mL x 2 mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Treatment of generalized epilepsy particularly with absence, myoclonic, tonic-clonic, atonic and mixed patterns of seizures, and partial epilepsy particularly with simple or complex, secondary generalized, specific syndromes (Lennox-Gastaut). Treatment and prevention of mania associated with bipolar disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy – Adults</b>: 600 mg in 2 divided doses. May be increased by 200 mg every 3 days to 1-2 g daily (20-30 mg/kg daily) up to a max of 2.5 g/day. <b>Childn</b>: 20-30 mg/kg daily, may be increased to 40 mg/kg daily in severe cases. <b>Combination with anticonvulsants (phenytoin, phenobarbital and carbamazepine)</b>: Initiation therapy should be gradual to raise dose by 5-10 mg/kg/day and achieve target dose after 2 weeks. <b>Bipolar</b>: Initially 20 mg/kg/day. Max 3,000 mg/day. Maintenance: 1,000-2,000 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute and chronic hepatitis, family history of severe hepatitis, porphyria. Patients known to have mitochondrial disorders caused by mutations."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Liver damage, renal impairment. Cell and platelet count, bleeding time and coagulation test are recommended before initiating therapy and surgery. Potential risk in patients with SLE. Hyperammonemia or hypothermia may occur. False interpretation of urine ketone test. Monitor signs of suicidal ideation and behaviors. Women with childbearing potential. Infants. Childn &lt;3 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",

            "content": "GI disturbances, hair loss, fine postural tremor, weight gain, amenorrhea, menstrual disturbances, increase bleeding time, decrease fibrinogen, thrombocytopenia. Confusion, convulsion, isolated hyperammonaemia."

          {

            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension. May be used as an initial therapy in patients who are likely to need multiple drugs to achieve BP goals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab/day. Take at the same time (morning) every day. Adjust dose with individual components (amlodipine or valsartan). <b>Mild to moderate hepatic disorder</b>: Max 80 mg valsartan."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to amlodipine, valsartan, or dihydropyridine derivatives.           },

            "title": "Precautions",

            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, influenza. Headache. <b>Valsartan</b>: Edema, pitting edema, face edema, peripheral edema, fatigue, blush, asthenia, hot flush."

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/niH4nS7299CxFpSRkrwgSlHkHthgE9LWernNXFJ4TeM8T8Utet.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nQxlFJSvwOZxSNFtH9cTwJIf6GYgdD3QmTlREHQ32nshjvZrPk.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Valproic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fatty Acid Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy and adjunctive therapy treatment in patients with complex partial seizures that occur in either isolation or in association with other types of seizures; sole and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of simple and complex absence seizures and adjunctively in patients with multiple seizure types (e.g. absence seizure)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Complex partial seizures</b> - Adults and childn &ge;10 yrs: Initially 10-15 mg/kg daily, increase by 5-10 mg/kg/week. Max 60 mg/kg/day. <b>Simple and complex absence seizures</b>: Initially 15 mg/kg/day, increasing at 1-week intervals by 5-10 mg/kg/day. Max 60 mg/kg/day. If total daily dose exceeds 250 mg, give in divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction, urea cycle disorders, porphyria, mitochondrial disorders caused by mutations in mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma (POLG; e.g. Alpers-Huttenlocher syndrome); use in prophylaxis of migraine headaches in pregnant women."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of hepatic disease, encephalopathy. Hepatotoxicity. Pancreatitis. Urea cycle disorders. Suicidal behavior and ideation. Concomitant use with carbapenems; topiramate (associated with hyperammonemia with or without encephalopathy). May cause hypothermia, brain atrophy. Patients should be monitored for platelet count and coagulation parameters prior to surgery. Patients with DM, rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, or sucrose-isomaltase insufficiency; fructose intolerance. Contains sorbitol and methylhydroxybenzoate. May impair ability to operate machinery. Childn &lt;2 yrs. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, asthenia, fever, back pain, chest pain, malaise. Tachycardia, HTN, palpitation. GI disturbances. Thrombocytopenia weight gain/loss, peripheral edema, SGOT increased, SGPT increase. Myalgia, twitching, arthralgia, leg cramps, myasthenia. Somnolence, tremors, dizziness, diplopia, blurred vision nystagmus, ataxia, emotional liability, thinking abnormal, amnesia, nervousness, depression, anxiety, confusion, abnormal gait, paresthesia, hypertonia, incoordination, abnormal dreams, personality disorder. Rash, pruritus, dry skin, alopecia. Tinnitus, taste perversion, deafness, otitis media. Urinary incontinence and frequency, vaginitis, dysmenorrhea, amenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aspirin, carbapenem antibiotics (e.g. ertapenem, imipenem, meropenem), felbamate, rifampin, amitriptyline/nortriptyline, carbamazepine/carbamazepine-10,11-epoxidase, clonazepam, diazepam, ethosuximide, lamotrigine, phenobarbital, primidone, phenytoin, tolbutamide, topiramate, warfarin, zidovudine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Syrup 250 mg/5 mL x 100 mL (P330.00)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Lowering BP reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal CV events, primarily strokes and myocardial infarction. Initial therapy in patients likely to need multiple antihypertensive agents to achieve their BP goals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Taken once daily. <b>Initial therapy:</b> 40 mg/5 mg or 80 mg/5 mg once daily.           },

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Do not co-administer with aliskiren with in patients with diabetes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults and childn 6-18 yrs. Treatment for adults with symptomatic heart failure or asymptomatic left ventricular systolic dysfunction of recent myocardial infarction (MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b> - <b>HTN</b>: 80 mg once daily, may be increased to 160 mg once daily. Max 320 mg once daily.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and with cholestasis, primary hyperaldosteronism. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal impairment (CrCl &lt;10 mL/min) and undergoing dialysis, hepatic impairment, bilateral renal artery stenosis, aortic or mitral stenosis, hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy, recent MI, heart failure, history of angioedema; recent kidney transplantation. Correct sodium- and/or vol-depletion before therapy. Concomitant use with potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics, and salt substitutes. Combination with ACE inhibitors. Childn. Pregnancy.",

          },

            "title": "Side Effects",

          },

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension in adults whose BP is not adequately controlled on amlodipine or valsartan monotherapy."

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab/day, with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis or cholestasis, renal impairment and patients undergoing dialysis.           },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Correct sodium- and/or vol-depletion before therapy. Concomitant use with potassium supplements, potassium-sparing diuretics and salt substitutes.             "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, influenza, hypokalemia, headache, asthenia, fatigue, edema, flushing or hot flush. <b>Amlodipine:</b> Somnolence, palpitations, flushing, upper abdominal pain and discomfort, nausea, ankle swelling."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alpha-blockers, diuretics, TCAs, CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers, lithium, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplement and salt substitutes, NSAIDs. Grapefruit or grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

  {
    "id": 4438,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4438,
        "brand_name": "Vancolife",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HY4v4lUKAWih9aIYkENRbvNGX5F8Cu8IW4n967y2rONi2CiNJW.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9w8aWNCcOteAwbULPQd8JQCKPnwcP5UoEnllUpFxH1XlHt2PJF.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/z9xbvk6DzlCmSnNBP2H4mdbeAAFpJDv7GWRU67tqdlVOBnK3WY.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Vancomycin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Glycopeptide Antibiotic"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of secondary superficial infections (e.g. endocarditis, osteomyelitis, arthritis, meningitis, burn, operative wound); pneumonia, sepsis, pulmonary pyosis, empyema thoracis; severe infections which have failed to respond to penicillins or cephalosporins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administer via intermittent IV infusion at a rate of &le;10 mg/min for at least 60 mins. Alternatively, administer slowly for >24 hrs via continuous IV infusion. <b>Adults:</b> 500 mg every 6 hrs or 1 g every 12 hrs. <b>Childn:</b> 10 mg/kg every 6 hrs; <b>Young infants and neonates:</b> Initially 15 mg/kg, then 10 mg/kg every 12 hrs in the 1<sup>st</sup> week of life, and every 8 hrs thereafter until 1 month of age; <b>Renal impairment, elderly:</b> CrCl 100 mL/min: 1,545 mg/day. Dose is reduced by 155 mg/day for every 10 mL/min decrease in CrCl. Dose is given every several days; <b>For functionally anephric patients:</b> Initially 15 mg/kg; <b>Anuria:</b> 1 g every 7-10 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of shock with vancomycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not active against G(-) bacilli, mycobacteria, or fungi. Cross-sensitivity with teicoplanin. Patients with auditory disorder caused by peptide and aminoglycosides or with other auditory disorder; renal (including acute urinary retention) and hepatic impairment; cochlea or vestibular organ damage. Prolonged use may result in overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms. Serial tests of auditory function may be helpful to minimize risk of ototoxicity. Perform blood level tests, urinalysis, and renal function tests regularly. Premature infants, newborn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Auditory function disturbances. Elevated bilirubin, AST, ALT, and ALP; renal failure; exfoliative or bullous dermatitis; SJS, TEN."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anesthetics, neurotoxic or nephrotoxic drugs (e.g. amphotericin B, aminoglycosides, bacitracin, polymyxin B, cloistin, viomycin, cisplatin, nedaplatin), anticoagulants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection for IV infusion 1 g (P2,044.00)."
          }
        ],

          "name": "United American Pharmaceuticals, Inc."
        },

    "id": 23,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 23,
        "brand_name": "Varivax",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Varicella virus vaccine, live",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Varicella Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Vaccination against varicella in individuals >1 yr."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "0.5 mL SC in the outer aspect of the upper arm (deltoid). <b>Adults and adolescents >13 yrs - 1<sup>st</sup> dose:</b> At elected date; <b>2<sup>nd</sup> dose:</b> 4-8 weeks after. <b>Childn 1–12 yrs:</b> Single dose; at elected date. If a 2<sup>nd</sup> dose is to be administered, there should be a minimum of 3 month interval."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Anaphylactoid reactions to neomycin. Any febrile respiratory illness or active febrile infection; active untreated TB. Patients receiving immunosuppressive; with malignant neoplasms affecting the bone marrow or lymphatic systems (e.g. blood dyscrasias, leukemia, lymphoma of any type). Primary and acquired immunodeficiency states, including immunosuppressed patients with HIV or AIDS, cellular immune deficiencies, hypogammaglobulinemia and dysgammaglobulinemia. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for IV. Risk of transmission of virus from vaccine recipients to susceptible high-risk individuals which include: Immunocompromised individuals, pregnant women and/or newborn infants of mothers without documented history of chickenpox or laboratory evidence of prior infection. Childn and young adults. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fever, rashes or injection site complaints (pain/soreness, swelling and/or erythema, rash, pruritus, hematoma, induration, stiffness). Anaphylaxis (including anaphylactic shock) and related phenomena e.g. angioneurotic, facial and peripheral edema; necrotizing retinitis; nausea, vomiting; aplastic anemia, thrombocytopenia, lymphadenopathy; varicella; encephalitis, CVA, transverse myelitis, Guillain-Barre syndrome, Bell's palsy, ataxia, febrile and non-febrile seizures, aseptic meningitis, dizziness, paresthesia, irritability; pharyngitis, pneumonia/pneumonitis, URTI, SJS, erythema multiforme, Henoch-Schonlein purpura, bacterial infection including impetigo and cellulitis; herpes zoster."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Vaccination should be deferred for at least 5 months after blood or plasma transfusions, administration of immune globulin, or varicella-zoster immune globulin (VZIG). Following vaccination, VZIG should not be given for 2 months. Avoid use of salicylates for 6 weeks after vaccination."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for solution for injection 1,350 PFU/0.5 mL (P2,710.40)."
          }

            "content": "1 tab twice daily, taken in the morning and evening with meals.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min); Parkinson's disease, parkinsonian symptoms, tremors, restless legs syndrome, and other related movement disorders."
          },
          {

            "content": "Not a curative treatment for angina attacks nor an initial treatment for unstable angina pectoris or MI nor in the pre-hospital phase or during the first days of hospitalization.             "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache; abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting; rash, pruritus, urticaria; asthenia."

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Pre- or post-exposure prophylaxis against rabies."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Pre-exposure vaccination</b>: 1 dose (1 mL) IM on days 0, 7, and 21 (or 28) into deltoid, or in the anterolateral thigh in small childn. <b>Post-exposure in incomplete or unvaccinated persons – Active vaccination</b>: 1 dose (1 mL) on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28 into deltoid, or in the anterolateral thigh in small childn, or 0.1 mL intradermally at 2 sites on days 0, 3, 7 and 28; Initiate with 20 IU/kg human rabies immunoglobulin. <b>Post-exposure immunization in previously vaccinated persons</b>: 1 mL IM on days 0 and 3.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Use rabies vaccines derived from non-avian sources for persons with known sensitivity to avian proteins. If such vaccines are not available, all necessary preparations should be made to treat complications which might arise in the event of anaphylactic reaction. Do not administer as intravascular injection. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Active immunization for the prevention of invasive disease, pneumonia, and acute otitis media caused by <i>Streptococcus pneumonia</i> serotypes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F, 22F, 23F and 33F in individuals >6 weeks old. Active immunization for the prevention of invasive disease and pneumonia caused by <i>Streptococcus pneumonia</i> serotypes 1, 3, 4, 5, 6A, 6B, 7F, 9V, 14, 18C, 19A, 19F, 22F, 23F and 33F in adults &ge;18 years old."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IM:</b> Each dose is 0.5 mL. <b>Adults >18 yrs:</b> Single dose. <b>Infants/toddlers - 3-dose regimen:</b> Primary 2 dose series followed by a toddler dose consists of 3 doses (1<sup>st</sup> dose given as early as 6-12 weeks of age, 2<sup>nd</sup> dose 8 weeks later, 3<sup>rd</sup> dose to be administered approx. 11-15 months of age); <b>4-dose regimen:</b> Primary 3 dose series followed by a toddler dose consists of 4 doses (1<sup>st</sup> dose given as early as 6-12 weeks of age with interval of 4-8 weeks between doses in the primary series, followed by a 4<sup>th</sup> dose to be administered approx 11-15 months of age and at least 2 months after the 3<sup>rd</sup> dose). <b>Pre-term infant < 37 week gestation:</b> Primary 3 dose series followed by a toddler dose consists of 4 doses with 1<sup>st</sup> dose given as early as 6-12 weeks of age, with interval of 4-8 weeks between doses in primary series, followed by 4<sup>th</sup> dose to be administered approx 11-15 months of age and at least 2 months after 3<sup>rd</sup> dose. <b>Catch-Up Vaccination - 7-11 months:</b> 3 doses, 1<sup>st</sup> 2 doses given at least 4 weeks apart, 3<sup>rd</sup> dose given after one-year birthday, and at least 2 months after the 2<sup>nd</sup> dose; <b>12-23 months:</b> 2 doses given at least 2 months apart; <b>2-17 yrs:</b> 1 dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to any component of Vaxneuvance or to diphtheria toxoid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For IM injection only. Individuals with altered immunocompetence, including those receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Premature infants. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Childn:</b> Irritability, somnolence, fever, decreased appetite, myalgia, headache. Injection site pain, induration, erythema, swelling. <b>Adults:</b> Fatigue, myalgia, headache, arthralgia. Injection-site pain, swelling, and erythema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Immunosuppressive therapies (irradiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, corticosteroids, therapeutic proteins and targeted immunomodulators)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension for injection (IM) 0.5 mL (P4,189.00)."

    "id": 2913,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2913,
        "brand_name": "Velmetia",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YK8l9pix4YJ07C0AbeqyIfLHkAGwiVocgv6lgo4vQG6WG6CQQB.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MfAegOCDjAB4UPqqu8FyRXMty2fA1I5HdciAo2PIriCi2YAF4A.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/FbrWuIwNkebZEYh4GUMz2iuoqkNvmhGQYC9OWvK6TuDE6hSy2n.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin (as monohydrate phosphate), metformin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Initial therapy in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control when diet and exercise do not provide adequate glycemic control. Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients with inadequately controlled type 2 DM: on metformin or sitagliptin (alone or in combination); as part of triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist (i.e. thiazolidinediones); or in combination with insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Max recommended daily dose: 100 mg sitagliptin. <b>Initial therapy</b>: 50 mg/500 mg twice daily, may be titrated up to 50 mg/1 g twice daily. <b>Patients with inadequately controlled DM on metformin monotherapy</b>: Sitagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus the dose of metformin already being taken; <b>on sitagliptin monotherapy</b>: 50 mg/500 mg twice daily, may be increased up to 50 mg/1 g twice daily; <b>as part of dual combination therapy with sitagliptin, metformin, or PPAR-gamma agonist, or sulfonylurea, or insulin</b>: Sitagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus metformin dose based on glycemic control and current metformin dose (if any) being taken. Consider gradual dose escalation to reduce GI side effects. Patients currently on or initiating a sulfonylurea or insulin doses may require lower doses of sulfonylurea or insulin to reduce risk of hypoglycemia. <b>Switching from co-administered sitagliptin with metformin</b>: May be initiated at the dose of sitagliptin and metformin already being taken."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment (eGFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including diabetic ketoacidosis, with or without coma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Type 1 DM, treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis, acute pancreatitis. Assess renal function prior to initiation of therapy and at least annually after. Hypoglycemia in combination with a sulfonylurea or with insulin; in patients with deficient caloric intake, or during concomitant use with other glucose-lowering agents (e.g. sulfonylureas, and insulin) or ethanol, elderly, debilitated or malnourished, and those with adrenal or pituitary insufficiency or alcohol intoxication. Bullous pemphigoid. Lactic acidosis, patients with unstable or acute CHF who are at risk of hypoperfusion and hypoxemia, renal dysfunction, excessive alcohol intake. Temporarily discontinue treatment prior to any surgical procedure until the patient’s resumption of oral intake or in patients undergoing radiologic studies involving intravascular administration or iodinated contrast imaging with an eGFR &ge;30-&lt;60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>, with a history of hepatic impairment, alcoholism or heart failure, or in patients who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast. Hypoxic states. Impaired hepatic function. Routinely monitor vitamin B<sub>12</sub> levels at 2-3-yrs intervals. Evaluate serum electrolytes and ketones, blood glucose, blood pH, lactate, pyruvate, and metformin levels. Exposure to stress (e.g. fever, trauma, infection, or surgery). Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, diarrhea, nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, headache, abdominal pain, constipation, URTI, cough, fungal skin infection, peripheral edema, asthenia, indigestion, hypersensitivity reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Furosemide, nifedipine. OCT2 or multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) inhibitors e.g. ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine. Thiazides and other diuretics, corticosteroids, phenothiazines, thyroid products, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, sympathomimetics, CCBs, isoniazid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P22.07), 50 mg/1 g (P22.20)."
          }
        ],
