        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sofosbuvir, velpatasvir",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) in adults and childn &ge;3 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once daily with or without food. Do not chew or crush tab. <b>Treatment duration - Adults - without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis:</b> 12 weeks, may add ribavirin for genotype 3 infected patients with compensated cirrhosis; <b>decompensated cirrhosis:</b> 12 weeks (plus ribavirin). <b>Ribavirin dose - Child-Pugh-Turcotte Class B cirrhosis pre-transplant:</b> 1,000 mg/day (weighing < 75 kg) or 1,200 mg/day (weighing &ge;75 kg); <b>CPT Class C cirrhosis pre-transplant and CPT Class B or C post-transplant:</b> Initially 600 mg, can be titrated up to max 1,000 mg (weighing < 75 kg) or 1,200 mg (weighing &ge;75 kg); <b>genotype 3 infected with compensated cirrhosis:</b> 1,000 mg (weighing < 75 kg) or 1,200 mg (weighing &ge;75 kg). <b>Previously failed therapy with an NS5A-containing regimen:</b> 24 weeks (plus ribavirin). <b>Childn 3 to < 18 yrs with &ge;30 kg BW:</b> 1 tab once daily for 12 weeks; <b>17 to < 30 kg BW:</b> 200 mg/50 mg tab once daily for 12 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Co-administration with strong P-gp or CYP450 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, St. John’s wort, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin). Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients who have previously failed therapy with an NS5A-containing regimen; severe renal impairment (GFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) or ESRD requiring hemodialysis; HCV/HBV co-infection; diabetes; CPT Class C cirrhosis; post-liver transplant. Co-administration with moderate P-gp or CYP inducers (e.g. oxcarbazepine, modafinil, efavirenz) and certain HIV antiretroviral regimens. Severe bradycardia and heart block with amiodarone. Monitor glucose levels within the first 3 months. Childn and adolescents < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, rash."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids (e.g. aluminum or magnesium hydroxide, calcium carbonate); H2-receptor antagonists (e.g. famotidine, cimetidine, nizatidine, ranitidine); PPIs (e.g. omeprazole, lansoprazole, rabeprazole, pantoprazole, esomeprazole); anti-arrhythmics (e.g. amiodarone; digoxin); anticoagulants (e.g. dabigatran, vit K antagonists); anticonvulsants (e.g. carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, oxcarbazepine); antifungals (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, voriconazole, posaconazole, isavuconazole); antimycobacterials (e.g. rifampicin; rifabutin, rifapentine); HIV antiviral agents (e.g. tenofovir, efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir); St. John’s wort; rosuvastatin, other statins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 400 mg/100 mg."
          }

            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents (&ge;12 yrs with BW &ge;35 kg):</b> 1 tab once daily with meals. Patients receiving chronic hemodialysis. Administer after completion of hemodialysis treatment."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients."
          },

            "content": "Does not prevent the risk of transmission HBV through sexual contact or contamination with blood. Coadministration with other medicinal products (e.g. tenofovir, adefovir, carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, rifampicin, rifabutin, rifapentine, St. John’s wort, itraconazole and ketoconazole).         "content": "Norepinephrine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inotropic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Secondary treatment of acute hypotension or shock according to different diseases (shock due to MI, and septicemia caused by shock, anaphylactic shock, hypotension or shock, according to the decreased circulating blood vol, acute hypotension during anesthesia), and cardiac arrest."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute hypotension or shock:</b> Individualized dosing IV infusion rate of 2-3 mL/min. Maintenance: 0.5 mL- 1 mL/min. </b>Cardiac arrest:</b> IV inj for acute hypotension or shock."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with low BP due to lack of blood vol, high BP, hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma, renal dysfunction, pulmonary heart disease, severe arrhythmia, anesthesized fingers, toes, or nose. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to sodium sulfite. Patients with cocaine poisoning, ventricular tachycardia, atherosclerosis, heart disease, bradycardia, coronary, mesenteric, peripheral vascular thrombosis, hypotension due to MI. Prinzmetal angina. Monitor BP and administration rate. Lactation. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Ischemic injury due to potent vasoconstrictor action, tissue hypoxia, cardiogenic shock, arrhythmia, anxiety, transient headache, respiratory difficulty, extravasation necrosis at inj site."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cyclopropane and halothane anesthetics. MAOIs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection 1 mg/mL x 4 mL, 10 mL."
          }
        ],

    "detail": {

        "id": 30,

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Rabies Vaccine (Inactivated) (Wistar strain rabies)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Rabies Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Pre- and post-exposure immunization against rabies, as a primary vaccination or as a booster dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>IM inj - Pre-exposure:</b> 0.5 mL on days 0, 7, and 28 or 21; booster after 1 yr then subsequent booster vaccination depending on exposure to risks. <b>Post-exposure:</b> In subjects unvaccinated against rabies, 5 doses of 0.5 mL IM on days 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28. Administer into the deltoid area in adults or the anterolateral aspect of the thigh in infants and toddlers. <b>Intradermal inj:</b> May be used as an alternative, on upper or forearm. One intradermal dose comprises 0.1 mL of reconstituted vaccine e.g. 1/45 of the IM dose. <b>Non-immunized individuals:</b> 1 inj of 0.1 mL at 2 sites on days 0, 3, 7, and 28. <b>Fully immunized individuals:</b> 2 inj on days 0 and 3."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe febrile infection, acute disease. Do not use intradermal route for individuals receiving long-term corticosteroid or other immunosuppressive therapy or chloroquine, immunocompromised individuals, with severe wounds especially to the head and neck or presenting late for consultation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not administer IV. Cases of true allergy to polymyxin B, streptomycin or neomycin. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Local minor reactions e.g. inj site pain, erythema, edema, pruritus, and induration. General reactions e.g. moderate fever, shivering, malaise, asthenia, headaches, dizziness, arthralgia, myalgia, GI disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for suspension for injection (IM/ID) 0.5 mL."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/406WJRPXyyaedEj5xWNenpfmafMaoSWCG4sOWvyP1883fCifha.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OjqvTzTYAtt49rQF7bDSg0tp0haUMhjMIGAoinDIQqC5K35rwJ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Felodipine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Calcium Channel Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hypertension (HTN), either alone or with other antihypertensive agents. Chronic stable angina pectoris, either alone or with other antianginal agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosing and adjusted according to patient response. <b>HTN</b>: Initially 5 mg once daily. Dose may be decreased to 2.5 mg once daily, increased to 10 mg once daily, or another antihypertensive agent added. Dose adjustment should occur at intervals of not &lt;2 weeks. Usual maintenance dose: 5-10 mg once daily. Recommended dose range: 2.5-10 mg once daily. Elderly: 2.5 mg once daily. <b>Angina pectoris</b>: Initially 5 mg once daily, dose may be increased to 10 mg once daily if needed. <b>Elderly</b>: Consider an alternative if 5 mg is not well tolerated. <b>Hepatic impairment</b>: 2.5 mg once daily. Extended-release tab should be swallowed whole with a glass of water."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of previous allergic reaction to other dihydropyridine CCBs. Clinically significant aortic stenosis. Uncompensated heart failure. Acute MI. Unstable angina pectoris. Discontinue if cardiogenic shock develops. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypotension. Patients with heart failure or compromised ventricular function. Peripheral edema. Ensure good dental hygiene. Childn. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypotension, mild gingival hyperplasia (gum swelling), peripheral edema. CV, endocrine/metabolic, GI, hematologic, musculoskeletal, nervous system, respiratory, skin, eyes, and urogenital disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Beta-blockers (e.g. metoprolol). CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin, cimetidine). Anticonvulsant and other enzyme inducers (e.g. phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital). Tacrolimus. Grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 5 mg (P17.65), 10 mg (P31.56)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Cholinesterase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of mild to moderately severe Alzheimer's dementia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly</b>: 5 mg daily in the evening, prior to retiring. Maintain dose for at least 1 month. May increase to 10 mg daily, following a 1-month clinical assessment with 5 mg treatment. Max: 10 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Childn and adolescents &lt;18 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May exaggerate succinylcholine-type muscle relaxation during anesthesia. Important actions with sick sinus syndrome or other supraventricular cardiac conduction conditions e.g. SA or AV block. Syncope and seizures. Increased risk for developing ulcers. May cause bladder outflow obstruction. May cause generalized convulsions. May exacerbate or induce EPS. Discontinue treatment if patient develops signs and symptoms indicative of NMS, or presents with unexplained high fever without additional clinical manifestations of NMS. History of asthma or obstructive pulmonary disease. Avoid concomitant administration with other acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, agonist or antagonists of the cholinergic system. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, muscle cramps, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, insomnia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, quinidine, CYP3A4 inhibitors, CYP2D6 inhibitors, rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, alcohol, anticholinergic, succinylcholine, other neuromuscular blocking agents or cholinergic agonists or beta-blocking agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg, 10 mg."

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/khleA9w4urZgWQ65LbfJhIsyIL8Gh98lA6ey8cMJ3WlNwUqTId.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/X2tyfeWw3pjrgtm5y81x8vx8WCAzdj3addI7L6BLVghXl3Nipj.jpg"
        },

        "content": "Docetaxel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Taxanes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment for breast cancer, non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), hormone-refractory prostate cancer (HRPC), gastric adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinomas (SCC) of the head and neck cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Breast cancer</b>: Premedicate with an oral corticosteroid for 3 days starting 1 day before docetaxel administration. IV infusion in glucose 5% or sodium chloride 0.9% at concentration not >0.74 mg/mL over 1 hr. <b>Monotherapy after failure of previous chemotherapy</b>: 60-100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once every 3 weeks; <b>In combination with doxorubicin or capecitabine or as adjunct therapy with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once every 3 weeks. <b>NSCLC (both 1<sup>st</sup>-line combination therapy and monotherapy after failure of previous chemotherapy)</sup></b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once every 3 weeks. <b>Gastric adenocarcinoma</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> before cisplatin and fluorouracil, treatment is repeated every 3 weeks. <b>SCC of the head and neck cancer</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> before cisplatin and fluorouracil given every 3 weeks for 3 cycles followed by chemoradiotherapy, or for 4 cycles when followed by radiotherapy alone. <b>HRPC</b>: 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> once every 3 weeks with prednisone or prednisolone 5 mg orally twice daily continuously. <b>Elderly with poor performance status or refractory disease</b>: 30-40 mg/m<sup>2</sup> weekly. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment</b>: Monotherapy should be reduced from 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> to 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to polysorbate 80. Hepatic impairment, tumor lysis syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infections, neutropenia, anemia, skin reactions, fluid retention, GI effects, thrombocytopenia, neuropathy, asthenia, pain, myalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antineoplastics that have immunosuppressant effects, antifungals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 20 mg/0.5 mL, 80 mg/2 mL."
          }
        ],

      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3724,
        "brand_name": "Vexdopa",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xSLfdM3WXgInK9bSk9IRdBOmOTwDVQP5UsdUNaE4cD8xafgo6V.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nLe2WCc3wbyNhwzi302f7vEsrihEcqe41XSjAASiZNxCaBogjS.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0vZBB3xZE6JJAIMzfBWyFjl9T0R7XwMwibKaFHnO5Gxg0qaoFX.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Levodopa, carbidopa monohydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of symptoms of idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (paralysis agitans), post-encephalitic parkinsonism, and symptomatic parkinsonism which may follow injury to the nervous system by carbon monoxide or manganese intoxication."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Discontinue levodopa 12 hrs prior to initiation of carbidopa-levodopa therapy. <b>Patients taking &lt;1,500 mg levodopa a day</b>: Initially carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg 3-4x daily. Patients taking >1,500 mg levodopa a day: Initially carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg 3-4x daily. Maintenance: Individualized and adjusted according to desired therapeutic response. At least 70-100 mg carbidopa per day. When greater proportion of carbidopa is required, 1 tab of carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg may be substituted for each tab of carbidopa 10 mg/levodopa 100 mg. Carbidopa 25 mg/levodopa 100 mg may be increased by &frac12; or 1 tab every day or every other day to max 8 tabs/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with non-selective MAOIs. Patients with narrow-angle glaucoma, suspicious and undiagnosed skin lesions or history of melanoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Development of depression with concomitant suicidal tendencies. Patients with past or current psychoses, CV or pulmonary disease, bronchial asthma, renal, hepatic or endocrine disease, history of MI who have residual atrial, nodal or ventricular arrhythmias, sporadic cases of a symptom complex NMS, chronic wide-angle glaucoma. May increase possibility of upper GI hemorrhage in patients with history of peptic ulcer. Sporadic cases of a symptom complex resembling NMS. Periodic evaluations of hepatic, hematopoietic, CV and renal function, and periodic skin examinations. High protein diet and excessive acidity may delay absorption. Sudden onset of sleep during daily activities. Elevations of liver function tests e.g. alkaline phosphatase, SGOT (AST), SGPT (ALT), lactic dehydrogenase, and bilirubin. Abnormalities in BUN and positive Coombs’ test, creatinine, and uric acid are lower. False positive reaction for urinary ketone bodies. False negative tests may result with the use of glucose-oxidase methods of testing for glucosuria. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dyskinesias (e.g. choreiform, dystonic, other involuntary movements), nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antihypertensive drugs, MAOIs (type A or B), TCAs, D2-receptor antagonists (e.g. phenothiazines, butyrophenones, risperidone) and INH, phenytoin and papaverine, iron salts, metoclopramide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 250 mg/25 mg."
          }
        ],

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/FLxoAev0DS0Wh8JPv6f4pqqdr2syJy66Jhoib6GynRevEfDLhi.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TjAqcHI5SVKDtL5uB7RfycTzk9yRiInWyyTFyW2jC9TkmEg7P5.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YmQy0ZqEsn2v6cb6dhgIe3HLklaJ5KZLl7eDui5K12KovzQ205.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paclitaxel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Taxanes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy in ovarian cancer for the treatment of advanced disease or a residual disease >1 cm after the initial laparotomy, in combination with cisplatin and as 2<sup>nd</sup>-line in the treatment of metastatic carcinoma of ovary after failure of standard platinum-based therapy. Adjuvant treatment in node-positive breast carcinoma following anthracycline and cyclophosphamide therapy. Initial treatment of locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer either in combination with an anthracycline, or in combination with trastuzumab in patients over-express HER-2 at 3+ level for whom an anthracycline is not suitable. Treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment of ovarian cancer</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 3 hrs or 135 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV infusion over 24 hrs followed by 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> cisplatin, therapy repeated at 3-weeks intervals. <b>2<sup>nd</sup>-line treatment of ovarian cancer</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs with 3 weeks interval between courses. <b>1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma in combination with doxorubicin (50 mg/m<sup>2</sup>)</b>: Recommended dose 220 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs, with a 3-week interval between courses, should be given 24 hrs after doxorubicin. <b>1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma in combination with trastuzumab</b>: Recommended dose 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs with a 3-week interval between courses, infusion may be started the day following the 1<sup>st</sup> dose of trastuzumab or immediately after subsequent doses of trastuzumab. <b>2<sup>nd</sup>-line chemotherapy of breast carcinoma</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs with 3-week intervals between courses. <b>Advanced NSCLC</b>: 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, followed by 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup> of cisplatin with 3-week intervals between courses. <b>AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma</b>: Recommended dose 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 3 hrs IV infusion every 2 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients must be pre-treated with corticosteroids, antihistamines and H2-antagonists. Impaired hepatic function. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yeFjmANFMsroNewNBkG3JBPGIp7DgC0IgVk6lmEbvWpiXK24vP.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Perindopril, amlodipine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 3.5 mg/2.5 mg once daily, may be increased to 7 mg/5 mg once daily after at least 4 weeks. <b>Patients with moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-60 mL/min):</b> Initially 3.5 mg/2.5 mg every other day, may be increased to 3.5 mg/2.5 mg once daily. Taken preferably in the morning before meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min); history of ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema; hereditary or idiopathic angioedema; severe hypotension; shock including cardiogenic shock; obstruction of the outflow tract of left ventricle; hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI; significant bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney; or those receiving extracorporeal treatments leading to contact of blood with negatively charged surfaces. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), and sacubitril/valsartan (therapy must not be initiated until after 36 hrs of last dose). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe hepatic impairment; heart failure; dialyzed with high flux membranes; receiving desensitization treatment (e.g. hymenoptera venom); underwent kidney transplantation; galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption. Concomitant use with NEP inhibitors (e.g. racecadotril), mTOR inhibitors (e.g sirolimus, everolimus, temsirolimus), gliptins, oral antidiabetic agents or insulin, potassium-sparing drugs, potassium supplements, potassium-containing salt substitutes. LDL-apheresis with dextran. Neutropenia/agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, anemia, hyperkalemia. Non-productive, persistent cough. Discontinue treatment 1 day prior to surgery. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Black patients. Elderly with renal impairment. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache, visual impairment, dyspnea, abdominal pain, nausea, dyspepsia, diarrhea, constipation, muscle spasms, cough, peripheral edema, asthenia. <b>Amlodipine:</b> Diplopia, palpitations, flushing, bowel habit changes, joint swelling, fatigue. <b>Perindopril:</b> Dysgeusia, paresthesia, tinnitus, vertigo, hypotension, vomiting, rash, exanthema, pruritus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aliskiren. Sacubitril/valsartan. Potassium salts, potassium-sparing diuretics, NSAIDs, heparin, immunosuppressants (e.g. ciclosporin, tacrolimus), trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole. Estramustine, lithium, dantrolene (infusion). Antidiabetics, baclofen, non-potassium sparing diuretics, racecadotril, mTOR inhibitors, gliptins, CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors. TCAs, antipsychotics, anesthetics, sympathomimetics, corticosteroids, tetracosactide, alpha-blockers, amifostine, injectable gold (sodium aurothiomalate), grapefruit, grapefruit juice."

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1984,
        "brand_name": "Victus",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/lo4j2QoDODUgPVsEFZCwPIwEOrT1bLACNr6s0Xtke2GWybYvbr.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/lo4j2QoDODUgPVsEFZCwPIwEOrT1bLACNr6s0Xtke2GWybYvbr.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cEanyR9plthz5cRpexlHDcBeQY9uAcONd0U0U5f9FIaCmAjOJJ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Quetiapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute and chronic psychoses including schizophrenia in adults and adolescents 13-17 yrs. Acute treatment of manic episodes associated with bipolar I disorder both as monotherapy and adjunct to lithium or divalproex in adults, adolescents (10-17 yrs) and childn. Acute treatment of depressive episodes associated with bipolar disorder in adults. Maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder and adjunct to lithium and divalproex in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 25 mg twice daily, increase in increments of 25-50 mg divided 2 or 3x on days 2 and 3 to a target dose 300-400 mg by day 4. Usual dose after day 4 is 300-450 mg/day; adjust dose within 150-750 mg/day. Max 750 mg/day; <b>Adolescents 13-17 yrs</b> - Total daily doses for initial 5 days of therapy - Day 1: 50 mg; Day 2: 100 mg; Day 3: 200 mg; Day 4: 300 mg; Day 5: 400 mg. Max 800 mg/day. Daily doses should be administered in 2 or 3 divided doses based on response and tolerability. Maintenance - Adults and adolescents: 400-800 mg/day. Max 800 mg/day. <b>Acute treatment of manic episodes in bipolar I disorder</b> - <b>Adults:</b> As monotherapy or adjunct therapy (with lithium or divalproex) initiate twice daily with total daily doses of - Day 1: 100 mg; Day 2: 200 mg; Day 3: 300 mg; Day 4: 400 mg; Day 5: up to 600 mg; Day 6: up to 800 mg with increments of not >200 mg/day. Usual dose range is 400-800 mg/day. Max 800 mg/day; <b>Childn 10-17 yrs</b> - Total daily doses for initial 5 days of therapy - Day 1: 50 mg; Day 2: 100 mg; Day 3: 20 mg; Day 4: 300 mg; Day 5: 400 mg. After Day 5, adjust dose within 400-600 mg/day by not &gt;100 mg/day increments. Max 600 mg/day. Daily doses should be administered in 2 or 3 divided doses based on response and tolerability. <b>Acute treatment of depressive episodes in bipolar I disorder</b> - <b>Adults</b> - Day 1: 50 mg; Day 2: 100 mg; Day 3: 200 mg; Day 4: 300 mg. Max 300 mg/day. All doses to be given once daily at bedtime. Maintenance: 400-800 mg/day in 2 divided doses or continue dose which stabilized the patient in stabilization phase as adjunct to lithium or divalproex. <b>Elderly and debilitated patients or those with predisposition to hypotensive reactions:</b> 50 mg/day starting dose. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> 25 mg/day. Dose can be increased in increments of 25-50 mg/day depending on response and tolerability."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased mortality in elderly with dementia-related psychosis. Suicidality. Conditions that may contribute to an elevation in core body temp. Withdrawal. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Withdrawal symptoms, fatigue; tachycardia, palpitations, postural hypotension; dizziness, somnolence; rash; elevations in non-fasting serum triglyceride levels, total cholesterol, decreased HDL, weight gain; dry mouth; decreased hemoglobin; elevations in ALT, AST, GGT levels; increased cough, dyspnea, pharyngitis, nasal congestion; blurred vision, amblyopia, conjunctivitis, abnormal vision, dry eyes, blepharitis, eye pain, tinnitus, ear pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, anticholinergics, grapefruit juice, hepatic CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors, antihypertensives, lorazepam, thioridazine, levodopa and dopamine antagonist, divalproex, cimetidine, lithium, fluoxetine, antipyrine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mg (P26.35), 300 mg (P68.51)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections caused by <i>Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i> and other susceptible bacteria; used in immunocompromised or neutropenic patients; for biliary tract (cholangitis), lower (cystic fibrosis) and upper (otitis media) respiratory tract, skin (burns, ecthyma gangrenosum, ulceration), urinary tract, bone and joint, gynecological including postpartum endometritis and pelvic inflammatory disease, and intra-abdominal infections; surgical infection prophylaxis, septicemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Administered by slow IV injection over 3-5 mins and by IV infusion over 20-40 mins. <b>Adults</b> - <b>Serious or complicated infections:</b> 200-300 mg/kg daily in divided doses. Usual dose: 4 g every 6-8 hrs. <b>Life-threatening infections caused by <i>Klebsiella</i> spp. or <i>Pseudomonas</i>:</b> Not < 16 g daily. Max 24 g/day. <b>Mild or uncomplicated infections:</b> 100-150 mg/kg daily. Usual dose: 2 g every 6-8 hrs, or 4 g every 12 hrs IV. <b>Prophylaxis during surgery:</b> 2 g before procedure or when the umbilical cord is clamped in cesarean section, followed by at least 2 doses of 2 g at intervals of 4-6 hrs within 24 hrs of procedure. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl 20-80 mL/min: 12 g/1.5 g per day in divided doses or 4 g/500 mg every 8 hrs; &lt;20 mL/min: 8 g/1 g per day in divided doses or 4 g/500 mg every 12 hrs. Hemodialysis - All indications: Max 2.25 g every 12 hrs (every 8 hrs for nosocomial pneumonia), and additional 0.75 g after each dialysis period. <b>Childn 1 month-12 yrs:</b> 100-300 mg/kg daily in 3 or 4 divided doses; <b>Neonates &gt;7 days or weighing &gt;2 kg:</b> 300 mg/kg daily in 3-4 divided doses; <b>&lt;7 days or weighing &lt;2 kg:</b> 150 mg/kg daily in 3 divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of hypersensitivity to penicillins, cephalosporins, beta-lactamase inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue if serious hypersensitivity reactions and bleeding manifestations occur. Prolonged use may lead to superinfection, leukopenia, and neutropenia. Assess organ system functions (e.g. renal, hepatic, hematopoietic) periodically. Fever and rash in cystic fibrosis patients. Patients with low potassium reserves. Evaluate patients with gonorrhea for syphilis before initiating treatment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, indigestion, vomiting and diarrhea, constipation, rash, itchy or red skin, urticaria, difficulty sleeping, headache, dizziness and superinfection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, aminoglycosides, vecuronium, anticoagulants, methotrexate. <b>Incompatibilities:</b> Other antibiotics, Lactated Ringer’s soln, solns containing only sodium bicarbonate or alkaline solns, blood products, or albumin hydrolysates."
          },

            "content": "For adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) to improve glycemic control: As monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone and metformin is inappropriate.           {

        "content": "Vildagliptin, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control not adequately controlled on metformin or vildagliptin alone or who are already treated with the combination of vildagliptin and metformin HCl, as separate tabs. In combination with an insulinotropic (i.e. triple combination therapy) as an adjunct to diet and exercise in patients inadequately controlled with metformin and a sulfonylurea (SU). Add-on to insulin as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients when stable dose of insulin and metformin alone do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Max 100 mg daily dose of vildagliptin. <b>Adults - Inadequately controlled on metformin monotherapy:</b> Initially 50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg or 50 mg/1,000 mg twice a day, one tab in the morning and one tab in the evening. <b>Switching from combination therapy of vildagliptin + metformin as separate tabs: </b>50 mg/500 mg, 50 mg/850 mg, or 50 mg/1,000 mg based on the dose of vildagliptin or metformin already being taken. <b>In combination with a SU or with insulin: </b>50 mg vildagliptin twice a day (100 mg total daily dose) and a dose of metformin already being taken."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with renal failure or dysfunction (GFR < 60 mL/min), hepatic impairment, diabetic ketoacidosis or diabetic pre-coma, acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function such as dehydration, severe infection, shock, intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents, acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia such as cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, shock, acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use as substitute for insulin in insulin-requiring patients or with type 1 DM, renal failure or dysfunction. Risk of lactic acidosis. Perform liver function tests (LFTs) prior to the initiation of treatment; monitor LFTs during treatment at 3-month intervals during the first year and periodically thereafter. Monitor skin disorders such as blistering or ulceration. Preexisting CHF NYHA class IV. Risk to acute pancreatitis, hypoglycemia. Discontinuation 48 hrs before elective surgery. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, tremor, headache, dizziness, nausea, hyperhidrosis, asthenia, decreased blood glucose, chills, GERD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Thiazides, corticosteroids, thyroid products, sympathomimetics. <b>Metformin:</b> Furosemide, nifedipine, cationic drugs, diuretics, phenothiazines, estrogens, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, nicotinic acid, isoniazid, CCB drugs. Alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P23.75)."

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/w6l5P3FgeJx0cwxBgkiJKxxv9PQcaIvYsqlBPcOWfUXFuqZOnq.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tTKwAwqdASu4rxoZqjolpawwO3ObAnsikODe1Vjcf5jxME2man.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Vildagliptin, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) as adjunct to diet and exercise in patients inadequately controlled with metformin alone, or who are already treated with the combination of vildagliptin and metformin as separate tabs; in combination with other antidiabetic agents, including insulin, when these do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dose. Max 100 mg/day. <b>Patients inadequately controlled on metformin monotherapy, and in combination with sulfonylurea or insulin and metformin:</b> Vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus metformin dose already taken. Administer lower dose of sulfonylurea. <b>Switching from co-administration of vildagliptin and metformin as separate tabs:</b> Initiate at the dose of vildagliptin and metformin already taken."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis), diabetic pre-coma, severe renal failure (GFR &lt;30 mL/min), type 1 DM, hepatic impairment, pre-treatment ALT or AST &gt;3x ULN. Acute conditions that alter renal function e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock, intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents. Acute or chronic disease which may cause hypoxia e.g. cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, shock. Hepatic impairment, acute alcohol intoxication or alcoholism. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concomitant use with antihypertensives, diuretics, NSAIDs. Lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia. Perform liver function tests before therapy and monitor at 3-month intervals during the 1<sup>st</sup> yr and periodically thereafter. Discontinue when AST or ALT &gt;3x ULN, or when jaundice or other signs of liver dysfunction develop. Monitor for skin disorders (e.g. blistering or ulceration). Patients with history of pancreatitis. Discontinue at the time of imaging procedure using iodinated contrast media, or surgery under general, spinal or epidural anesthesia, and restart not &lt;48 hrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors. <b>Vildagliptin:</b> Thiazides, corticosteroids, thyroid products, sympathomimetics. <b>Metformin:</b> Alcohol, iodinated contrast media agents, NSAIDs, COX-2 inhibitors, ARBs, loop diuretics, glucocorticoids, beta2-agonists, ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/500 mg (P23.00)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dienogest",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of endometriosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Start on any day of the menstrual cycle. 1 tab daily without any break, taken preferably at the same time each day; must be taken continuously without regard to vaginal bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active venous thromboembolic disorder. Present or in history of arterial and CV disease (e.g. MI, IHD). DM with vascular involvement. Presence or history of severe hepatic disease as long as liver function values have not returned to normal. Presence or history of liver tumors (benign or malignant). Known or suspected sex hormone-dependent malignancies. Undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated in childn prior to menarche. Decrease in bone mineral density over a treatment of 12 months in adolescents. Women with history of extrauterine pregnancy or impaired tube function. Increased risk of MI and cerebral thromboembolism. Affects menstrual bleeding pattern. May aggravate uterine bleeding in women and adenomyosis uteri or uterine leiomyomata. Patients with history of depression. Withdraw if sustained clinically significant HTN develops. Discontinue if recurrence of cholestatic jaundice and/or pruritus occurred during pregnancy or previous use of sex steroids. Slight effect on peripheral insulin resistance and glucose tolerance. Diabetic women especially with history of gestational DM. Chloasma especially in women with history of chloasma gravidarum. Persistent ovarian follicles may occur. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Increased weight, depressed mood, sleep disorder, nervousness, loss of libido, altered mood, headache, migraine, nausea, abdominal pain, flatulence, abdominal distension, vomiting, acne, alopecia, back pain, breast discomfort, ovarian cyst, hot flushes, uterine or vaginal bleeding including spotting, asthenic conditions, and irritability."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors/inducers, phenytoin, barbiturates, primidone, carbamazepine, rifampicin, oxcarbazepine, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, products containing St. John's Wort, HIV/HCV protease inhibitors and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, azole antifungals (e.g. itraconazole, voriconazole, fluconazole), verapamil, macrolides (e.g. clarithromycin, erythromycin), diltiazem, grapefruit juice, ketoconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 2 mg x 28s (P1,860.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3144,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3144,
        "brand_name": "Vinrab",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Anti-rabies serum (Equine)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Rabies Immunoglobulins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Passive immunization against rabies."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Perform a skin test before administration. <b>First-aid treatment:</b> Thorough flushing and washing of wound with soap and water, detergent or other substance of proven lethal effect on rabies virus. Inject immunoserum as soon as possible after exposure. <b>Nibbling of uncovered skin, minor scratches or abrasions without bleeding, licks on broken skin:</b> Administer vaccine immediately. Discontinue if animal remains healthy throughout 10-day observation or if animal is killed humanely and found negative for rabies. Administer anti-rabies serum along with anti-rabies vaccine for immunocompromised patients. <b>Single or multiple transdermal bites or scratches, contamination of mucous membrane with saliva (e.g. licks):</b> Administer immunoserum and rabies vaccine immediately. Discontinue if animal remains healthy throughout 10-day observation or if animal is killed humanely and found negative for rabies. <b>Prevention of rabies:</b> 40 IU/kg for childn and adults. Infiltrate dose around wounds. Administer the remainder intramuscular (gluteal region) as a single dose. Inoculate 1st dose of vaccine at the same time as immunoglobulin, but in different parts of the body. When indicated, administer anti-tetanus and antimicrobials to control other infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform a skin test before administration. A positive result is a warning, not a contraindication for serotherapy. Administer only after ensuring facility to overcome anaphylactic shock. A negative result is not guaranteed for absence of an immediate allergic type reaction. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anaphylactoid reactions with hypotension, dyspnea, urticaria, inflammatory reaction, fever, pruritus, rash, adenopathy, arthralgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Simultaneous inoculation of immunoglobulin and vaccine to be done in different parts of the body. Do not administer the antiserum from the same syringe as the vaccine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IM) 200 IU/mL x 5 mL."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab:</b> Systemic treatment of varicella-zosters (Chicken pox shingles) and the systemic and topical treatment of herpes simplex infections of the skin and mucous membranes. <b>Cream:</b> Treatment of herpes simplex infections of the skin including initial and recurrent genital herpes and herpes labialis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab – Adults - Genital herpes infection:</b> Initial therapy: 200 mg 5x daily for 10 days. Intermittent therapy: 200 mg 5x daily for 5 days. Chronic suppressive therapy: 400 mg 2x a day or 200 mg 2-5x a day. CrCl >10 mL/min: 400 mg 2x a day. CrCl 0-10 mL/min: 200 mg 2x a day. <b>Herpes zoster:</b> 800 mg 5x daily for 7-10 day. CrCl >25 mL/min: 800 mg 5x a day for 7-10 days. CrCl 10-25 mL/min: 800 mg 3x a day for 7-10 days. CrCl 0-10 mL/min: 800 2x a day for 7-10 days. <b>Varicella:</b> 20 mg/kg, up to 800 mg per dose 4x a dy for 5 days. Initiated at earliest sign of chickenpox. Herpes simplex: 200-400 mg 5x a day for 10 days. <b>Childn 2-12 yrs – Varicella:</b> 20 mg/kg up to 800 mg per dose 4x a dy for 5 days. Initiated at earliest sign of chickenpox. <b>Cream:</b> Apply every 3 hours 6 times daily for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to acyclovir or ganciclovir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Women with herpes genitalis may have an increased risk of developing cervical cancer. <b>Tab:</b> Dehydration or renal function impairment. Neurological abnormalities or prior to neurologic reaction to cytotoxic medications. <b>Cream:</b> Avoid contact with eyes. Do not apply in the mouth, eyes or vagina, as it may be irritant.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Tab:</b> Acute renal failure, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, lightheadedness, skin rashes, increase values for liver enzymes, increase in blood concentrations of urea and creatinine, hematological changes, encephalopathic changes (e.g. lethargy, confusion, tremors, seizures). <b>Cream:</b> Mild pain, burning, stinging, pruritus, skin rash, erythema or mild drying and flaking of skin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 400 mg (P105.00), Cream 50 mg/g (5% w/w) (P690.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Potassium-Competitive Acid Blockers (P-CABs)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Gastric or duodenal ulcer, reflux esophagitis, prevention of recurrence of gastric or duodenal ulcer during low-dose aspirin or NSAID administration. Adjunct to <i>Helicobacter pylori</i> eradication in gastric or duodenal ulcer, gastric MALT lymphoma, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, in stomach after endoscopic resection of early stage gastric cancer, or <i>H. pylori</i> gastritis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Gastric or duodenal ulcer:</b> 20 mg once daily for up to 6 weeks for duodenal ulcer or 8 weeks for gastric ulcer; <b>Reflux esophagitis:</b> 20 mg once daily for up to 4 weeks or 8 weeks if effect is insufficient. Maintenance dose (repeat recurrence and relapse only): 10 mg or 20 mg once daily if effect is insufficient. <b>Prevention of recurrence of gastric or duodenal ulcer during low-dose aspirin or NSAID administration:</b> 10 mg once daily. <b>Adjunct to <i>H. pylori</i> eradication:</b> Administered at the same time, twice daily for 7 days: 20 mg vonoprazan, 750 mg amoxicillin, and 200 mg (max 400 mg) clarithromycin; alternatively, 20 mg vonoprazan, 750 mg amoxicillin and 250 mg metronidazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with atazanavir sulfate or rilpivirine HCl."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic or renal impairment and advanced stage of gastric MALT lymphoma. Long-term treatment. Discontinue in evidence of liver function abnormalities or develop signs or symptoms of liver dysfunction; abdominal pain and frequent diarrhea. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Constipation or diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. clarithromycin), digoxin, methyldigoxin, itraconazole, gefitinib, nilotinib, erlotinib, nelfinavir mesylate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg, 20 mg."
          }

        "brand_info": [

            "content": "Prokinetic Drugs & Antiflatulents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of dyspepsia syndrome accompanied by delayed gastric-emptying; nausea and vomiting due to various causes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Susp - Chronic dyspepsia – Adults</b>: 10 mg 3x daily. <b>Childn</b>: 2.5 mg/10 kg BW 3x daily. <b>Nausea and vomiting – Adults</b>: 10-20 mg 3-4x daily before meals. <b>Childn</b>: 2.5-5 mg/10 kg BW 3-4x daily. <b>Oral drops – Nausea and vomiting – Childn</b>: 2.5-5 mg/10 kg BW or 0.3-0.6 mL/5 kg BW 3-4x daily. All doses are to be taken 15-30 mins before meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with prolactin-releasing pituitary tumor (prolactinoma); moderate or severe hepatic impairment; conditions wherein stimulation of gastric motility is dangerous (e.g. presence of GI hemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation). Concomitant administration of potent CYP3A4 inhibitors associated with QT-prolongation; antacids or antisecretory agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for ventricular arrhythmias. Patients with existing prolongation of cardiac conduction intervals particularly QTc; bradycardia; significant electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, hypomagnesemia); cardiac diseases (CHF). Concomitant administration of drugs associated with QT-interval prolongation. Contains sorbitol. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rash and urticaria. Hyperprolactinemia (breast tenderness and enlargement, galactorrhea, and gynecomastia)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sustained-release and enteric-coated formulations. Anticholinergics (e.g. dextromethorphan, diphenhydramine), antacids, and antisecretory drugs. Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, erythromycin, telithromycin, itraconazole, oral ketoconazole, posaconazole, voriconazole, ritonavir, saquinavir, telaprevir)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral drops 5 mg/mL x 10 mL (P330.00). Suspension 5 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P330.00)."
          }

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OLnIcJiavkTXkeeIiucOn9BXKNACQg7t0qxOsSzSQGr9Hldu23.jpg"
        },

        "content": "Sacubitril-valsartan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin Receptor Neprilysin Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduce risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure especially in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below normal. Administered in place of an ACE inhibitor or ARBs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 100 mg twice daily. Double the dose at 2-4 weeks to target dose of 200 mg twice daily as tolerated. <b>Patients not currently on ACE inhibitors or ARBs or previously taking low doses of these agents:</b> Start at 50 mg twice daily and slow dose titration (doubling every 3-4 weeks). <b>Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) and moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Initially 50 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with an ACE inhibitor (do not start Vymada for at least 36 hrs after discontinuing ACE inhibitor therapy) or ARBs. History of angioedema related to ACE inhibitor or ARBs therapy, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or with renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and cholestasis. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Sodium and/or sodium depletion should be corrected before treatment. Hypotension, impaired renal function, hyperkalemia, angioedema. Patients with renal artery stenosis, CHF NYHA class IV, hepatic impairment. Not suitable with B-type natriuretic peptide as biomarker for heart failure. Psychiatric disorders (e.g. hallucination paranoia, and sleep disorders). Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal impairment,  cough, dizziness, diarrhea, anemia, fatigue, renal failure, hypokalemia, headache, syncope, asthenia, nausea, orthostatic hypotension, gastritis, vertigo, hypoglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates (e.g. statins), PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil), lithium, furosemide, metformin, potassium-sparing diuretics including mineralocorticoid antagonists (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, or salt substitutes containing potassium, NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors, nitrates, inhibitors of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT3 (e.g. rifampin, ciclosporin) or multidrug resistance-associated protein (e.g. ritonavir)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg, 100 mg, 200 mg (Varied Pricing at Government institutions and selected TGO)."
          }
